signals.text: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch We're having a good KV-cache compressor base on the paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.03462 Example we can compress the KV-cache of 2048 tokens into the KV-cache of 512 special tokens, so we need a manual way to feed it into the generate function. ### Alternatives _No response_ ### Additional context _No response_ ### Before submitting a new issue... - [X] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Feature]: Improve DCP error messages
signals.text: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch Currently if a backend doesn't support DCP we get the following error message ``` AssertionError: DCP requires attention impls to return the softmax lse for decode, but the impl FlashInferImpl does not return the softmax lse for decode. ``` It would good to suggest to the user to try an alternative backend using `VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND` ### Alternatives _No response_ ### Additional context _No response_ ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Feature]: Enable LoRA support for tower and connector in more MM models
signals.text: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch Regarding multi-modal models, we have supported adding LoRA to the tower encoder and connector,see: #26674, but have only implemented it for a few models (`Qwen VL series` and `idefics3`). There is no reason not to support other multi-modal models. ### Solution For the remaining models we want to support adding LoRA to the tower encoder and connector, we need to implement the following 2 functions: `get_num_mm_encoder_tokens` `get_num_mm_connector_tokens` **The root cause we need to implement these two functions is:** the number of multi-modal tokens represented in the language model does not necessarily match the input length required by the linear layers in the vision tower or connector. Since the lora_mapping requires the precise input token length prior to activation, these helper functions are necessary to bridge the discrepancy and calculate the correct lengths. ### List of models that are completed or WIP - Qwen VL series: #26674 - idefics3: #26674 - LLaVA: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/31513 - BLIP2: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/31620 - GLM4 : https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/31652 - PaliGemma https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/31656 - H2OVL https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/31696 - Pixtral https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/31724 - DotsOCR https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/31825 - InternVL2 https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/32397 - Gemma3 https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/32764 - Llama 4 Vision https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/35147 - Gemma4 https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39291 ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Feature]: Get latency and tpot per request in vLLM benchmark
signals.text: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch Today ttft and itls are provided but I think that some users would prefer to have the end-to-end latency of the request for a more realistic number in their environments. Also, tpot per request should bring a better idea of the performance that happened on a particular request. It's cool to have it for the whole run but per request might bring a more granular perspective and can help debugging ### Alternatives I haven't seen options to get the requested features ### Additional context nothing additional ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

num_speculative_tokens=2 ### Benchmark Results **Baseline (no MTP, no prefix caching):** ```bash vllm bench latency --model Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8 \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 --max-model-len 262144 ``` - Avg latency: 0.894s - P50: 0.895s, P90: 0.901s, P99: 0.907s **With MTP:** ```bash vllm bench latency --model Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8 \ --tensor-parallel-size signals.title: Hybrid KV offload: MultiConnector + planner for mamba+attention models
signals.text: ## Problem Hybrid models like Qwen3.5 (mamba + attention layers) can't use external KV cache offloading out of the box. The stock offload path requires LCM of all group block sizes, which is impractical for hybrid models where mamba groups have very different block sizes than attention groups. ## What we built A working hybrid offload stack for Qwen3.5-4B-FP8 (24 mamba + 8 attention layers), validated on RTX 4080 Super with `max_model_len=98304`: 1. **HybridOffloadPlanner** (`vllm/v1/kv_offload/planner.py`): configurable `hybrid_chunk_size` splits groups where `gpu_block_size % chunk_size == 0`, with per-group coverage tracking and binary search for efficient chunk counting. 2. **MultiConnector** (`multi_connector.py`): wraps multiple KV connectors (e.g., LMCache CPU + llm-d disk) with weighted load selection, HMA support (`SupportsHMA`), and preemption compatibility with stock vLLM's `set[str]` signature. 3. **Metrics safety**: clamp negative `prompt_tokens_by_source` values in `loggers.py` that crash Prometheus counters under high concurrency with external cache hits. ## Results - 79% cross-restart cache hit rate (llm-d disk, `PYTHONHASHSEED=0`) - 97% same-session hit rate (vLLM APC + LMCache CPU) - 50 concurrent requests stable at 1061 tok/s, 95% external hit rate - Identified and fixed garbled output bug in LMCache hybrid support (LMCache/LMCache#2879) ## Branch `malaiwah/vllm:codex/hybrid-kv-offload` — 261 files changed (includes upstream merge), key changes in `v1/kv_offload/`, `v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`, `distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/`. Related: LMCache/LMCache#2879, LMCache/LMCache#2845 > AI-assisted: developed with Claude. All changes reviewed and tested by a human.
signals.author: malaiwah

signals.title: [Feature]: DeepSeek-V4 Flash sm_80 (A100/A800) support
signals.text: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch I am trying to run DeepSeek-V4-Flash on NVIDIA A800 GPUs, which are sm_80 / Ampere GPUs. Currently, using `vllm/vllm-openai:deepseekv4-cu129`, the model fails during initialization with: ```text RuntimeError: Assertion error (.../deepgemm-src/csrc/apis/hyperconnection.hpp:56): Unsupported architecture ``` This still happens with --enforce-eager, so it seems related to the DeepGEMM / HyperConnection kernels rather than torch.compile. Are there any plans to support sm_80 GPUs such as A100/A800 for DeepSeek-V4, possibly with a slower fallback path? A100/A800 GPUs are still widely used in many research and production clusters, so even a functional fallback would be very helpful. ### Alternatives The current alternatives seem to be: 1. Use newer GPUs such as H100/H200/B200. 2. Wait for a backend/kernel fallback that supports sm_80. I am not sure whether sm_80 support is planned or whether it should currently be considered unsupported for this model. ### Additional context Environment: - GPU: NVIDIA A800, sm_80 / Ampere - vLLM image: `vllm/vllm-openai:deepseekv4-cu129` - Model: `DeepSeek-V4-Flash` - Single node, 8 GPUs Simplified command: ```bash docker run -d --gpus all \ -e CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 \ -v /path/to/models:/workspace \ -p 39001:8000 \ --ipc=host \ vllm/vllm-openai:deepseekv4-cu129 \ /workspace/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --served-model-name dsv4-flash \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --enable-expert-parallel \ --data-parallel-size 4 \ --enforce-eager ``` ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Bug]: Latest Nightly build with TurboQuant KV cache crashes on large chunked continuation prefill after workspace lock ( testing PR #39931 implementing TQ on Hybrid Attention Models e.g Qwen3.5-9B)
signals.text: ### Your current environment ### Environment - vLLM: `0.20.2rc1.dev35+g4845aee6b` - Python: `3.12.13` - Torch: `2.11.0+cu130` - CUDA driver/runtime: NVIDIA driver `595.71.05`, CUDA `13` - GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 - FlashInfer: `0.6.8.post1` - Transformers: `5.7.0` ### 🐛 Describe the bug ### Summary Testing latest commit #39931 turbo --kv-cache-dtype can crash at runtime when chunked prefill resumes a long prompt. The failure happens in TurboQuant attention’s large continuation-prefill path after the global workspace has already been locked. This appears TurboQuant-specific. ### Model Model: NVFP4 quantization of Qwen3.5-9b Relevant config: architectures: Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration model_type: qwen3_5 text_config.hidden_size: 4096 text_config.num_attention_heads: 16 text_config.num_key_value_heads: 4 text_config.head_dim: 256 text_config.num_hidden_layers: 32 text_config.full_attention_interval: 4 quantization_config.quant_method: modelopt quantization_config.quant_algo: NVFP4 Startup logs detect the TurboQuant hybrid layers: TQ hybrid: full-attention layers [3, 7, 11, 15, 19, 23, 27, 31] Using TURBOQUANT attention backend out of potential backends: ['TURBOQUANT']. ### Command vllm serve /home/yk/AI/Models/models/qwen3.5-9b-nvfp4-ptq \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \ --kv-cache-dtype turboquant_4bit_nc \ --max-model-len 102400 \ --enable-chunked-prefill \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \ --language-model-only \ --max-num-seqs 1 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": true}' ### What happened The server started successfully and the first few OpenAI-compatible chat completion requests succeeded. The failure occurred later from Open WebUI during a conversation with tools/web-search enabled, after toolschemas and/or tool results made the prompt larger. The failing request appears to have crossed a chunked-prefill boundary: SchedulerOutput( scheduled_new_reqs=[], scheduled_cached_reqs=CachedRequestData( req_ids=['chatcmpl-8cab1ba7625a3c7c-9669f94e'], ... num_computed_tokens=[4096], ... ), num_scheduled_tokens={chatcmpl-8cab1ba7625a3c7c-9669f94e: 3497}, total_num_scheduled_tokens=3497, ... ) So vLLM had already computed the first 4096 prompt tokens and then resumed the same request with another 3497 prompt tokens. ### Error AssertionError: Workspace is locked but allocation from 'turboquant_attn.py:720:_continuation_prefill' requires 16.00 MB, current size is 1.02 MB. Workspace growth is not allowed after locking. Full relevant stack: EngineCore encountered a fatal error. File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 4089, in execute_model model_output = self._model_forward(...) File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 3562, in _model_forward return self.model(...) File ".../vllm/compilation/cuda_graph.py", line 254, in __call__ return self.runnable(*args, **kwargs) File ".../vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_5.py", line 695, in forward hidden_states = self.language_model.model(...) File ".../vllm/compilation/decorators.py", line 520, in __call__ return self.aot_compiled_fn(self, *args, **kwargs) File ".../vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_next.py", line 495, in forward File ".../vllm/compilation/caching.py", line 215, in __call__ return self.optimized_call(*args, **kwargs) File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/attention.py", line 723, in unified_attention_with_output self.impl.forward(...) File ".../vllm/v1/attention/backends/turboquant_attn.py", line 438, in forward attn_out = self._prefill_attention(...) File ".../vllm/v1/attention/backends/turboquant_attn.py", line 669, in _prefill_attention out = self._continuation_prefill(...) File ".../vllm/v1/attention/backends/turboquant_attn.py", line 720, in _continuation_prefill k_buf, v_buf = current_workspace_manager().get_simultaneous(...) File ".../vllm/v1/worker/workspace.py", line 110, in get_simultaneous current_workspace = self._ensure_workspace_size(total_bytes) File ".../vllm/v1/worker/workspace.py", line 157, in _ensure_workspace_size raise AssertionError( AssertionError: Workspace is locked but allocation from 'turboquant_attn.py:720:_continuation_prefill' requires 16.00 MB, current size is 1.02 MB. Workspace growth is not allowed after locking. ### Suspected root cause TurboQuant attention has a special continuation-prefill path for chunked-prefill resumes. In turboquant_attn.py, small continuation chunks use the decode kernel: _CONTINUATION_DECODE_THRESHOLD = 128 if q_len <= _CONTINUATION_DECODE_THRESHOLD: out = triton_turboquant_decode_attention(...) else: out = self._continuation_prefill(...) The failing request had: cached_len = 4096 q_len = 3497 Since q_len > 128, TurboQuant entered _continuation_prefill(). That path dequants the previously cached TurboQuant K/V into shared workspace: alloc_len = math.ceil(cached_len / block_size) * block_size buf_shape = (1, Hk, alloc_len, D) k_buf, v_buf = current_workspace_manager().get_simultaneous( (buf_shape, torch.float16), (buf_shape, torch.float16), ) For this model/settings: cached_len = 4096 block_size = 2048 Hk = 4 D = 256 dtype = fp16 buffers = K + V Required workspace: 2 * 4096 * 4 * 256 * 2 bytes = 16 MB But vLLM had locked the global workspace after warmup/CUDA graph capture with only ~1.02 MB reserved. The workspace lock is intentional in vLLM: gpu_model_runner.py: Lock workspace to prevent resizing during execution, Max workspace sizes should have been captured during warmup/profiling. The issue appears to be that TurboQuant’s startup warmup/profiling does not exercise or reserve the large continuation-prefill workspace shape, so the first real long chunked-prefill continuation tries to grow the workspace after it has been locked. ### Why this edge case was triggered This did not happen on short initial requests. It happened after Open WebUI with tools/web-search produced a larger prompt/conversation context. Once the prompt exceeded --max-num-batched-tokens 4096, vLLM resumed prefill for the same request: num_computed_tokens=[4096] num_scheduled_tokens=3497 That combination caused TurboQuant to enter the large continuation-prefill path and request a 16 MB workspace. prefix caching does not seem to be the cause. The scheduled_cached_reqs here appears to refer to an internally resumed chunked-prefill request with already-computed KV, not prefix-cache reuse. ### Expected behavior TurboQuant should either: 1. reserve/profile enough workspace before lock_workspace(), or 2. avoid using a workspace path that can require larger allocations after lock ### Suggested root fix TurboQuant should reserve/profile worst-case continuation-prefill workspace before workspace locking. Possible approaches: - During warmup/profiling, exercise a dummy TurboQuant continuation prefill where: - cached_len > 0 - q_len > _CONTINUATION_DECODE_THRESHOLD - cached_len is at least one chunk, e.g. max_num_batched_tokens - Or expose TurboQuant continuation-prefill workspace requirements to the global workspace profiler. - At minimum, reserve enough for: 2 * ceil(max_cached_len / block_size) * block_size * num_kv_heads * head_dim * sizeof(fp16) For this model and one previous chunk: 2 * 4096 * 4 * 256 * 2 = 16 MB A more conservative reservation would scale with the maximum possible chunked continuation cached length, but that could become large for very long context, so the policy likely needs to be tied to scheduler/chunking limits. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [ROCm/MI325X] DeepSeek-V4-Flash: Triton fp8_mqa_logits kernel requires 96KB shared memory, MI325X limit is 64KB
signals.text: ## Environment - **Hardware**: AMD MI325X × 8 (255.98 GiB HBM each) - **vLLM version**: 0.20.2rc1.dev90+g7a576e2c7 (rocm/vllm-dev:nightly, 2026-05-06) - **Model**: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash - **Config**: TP=8, EP=8, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--enforce-eager` ## Bug At inference time, the first request fails with a Triton shared memory OOM: ``` triton.runtime.errors.OutOfResources: out of resource: shared memory, Required: 98304, Hardware limit: 65536. Reducing block sizes or `num_stages` may help. ``` Call stack: ``` rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py:538 → rocm_fp8_mqa_logits aiter/ops/triton/attention/fp8_mqa_logits.py:53 → _fp8_mqa_logits_kernel ``` ## Root Cause The Triton kernel `_fp8_mqa_logits_kernel` in `aiter/ops/triton/attention/fp8_mqa_logits.py` is configured with block sizes that require **96 KB** of LDS (Local Data Share / shared memory). The AMD MI325X GPU supports a maximum of **64 KB** per workgroup. The PR #40871 was developed and tested exclusively on **MI355X**, which appears to support the larger shared memory configuration required by this kernel. ## Impact DeepSeek-V4-Flash is completely non-functional for inference on MI325X. The model loads correctly but crashes on the first forward pass. ## Suggested Fix Add a hardware-capability check before launching the kernel, and reduce `BLOCK_SIZE` or `num_stages` for GPUs with ≤64 KB shared memory. The fix should be in `aiter` (the AITER library used by vLLM ROCm). ## Related - PR #40871 "Add AMD support for DeepSeek V4" (merged 2026-05-05) — tested on MI355X only - Issue #41961: `mul_cuda` not implemented for `Float8_e8m0fnu` (MI325X) - Issue #41962: OOM in `rocm_dequantize_blocked_k_cache` + CUDAGraph incompatibility

signals.title: [RFC]: Logprobs/Logits Semantics and Determinism Across the vLLM Ecosystem
signals.text: Related: #45585 (RL CI Matrix) ## Scope This issue tracks open logits/logprobs correctness, determinism, API, and material memory problems that affect Model Runner V2 (MRV2), including shared sampler, frontend, model, and distributed paths used with MRV2. MRV1-only problems, merged fixes, closed/superseded PRs, and reports without a reproducible MRV2 or shared-path failure are intentionally excluded. ## Motivation The remaining open reports point to gaps in the semantics and determinism of returned logits/logprobs: - duplicated sampled tokens in `top_logprobs` - batch-size-dependent sampling when logits are tied - invalid token IDs when a logits tile contains only `-inf` - streaming/frontend paths that drop, misalign, or fail to validate logprobs - backend-specific mode propagation gaps - batch-invariance gaps across async scheduling, TP collectives, attention, convolution, and speculative decoding - rollout/trainer logprob mismatch in downstream RL frameworks These can produce user-visible wrong values, crashes, non-deterministic scoring, and corrupted policy-gradient signals. ## Proposed Contract Define and test a shared contract for: - `logits` - `logprobs` - `prompt_logprobs` - `top_logprobs` The contract should cover: - raw vs processed semantics - behavior across batch size, request order, async scheduling, TP/DP/EP, and speculative decoding - streaming delta behavior - de-duplication rules for sampled token vs top-k output - validation and non-finite-value behavior - backend parity across core vLLM, vLLM-Ascend, and RL rollout paths ## Open MRV2 / Shared-Path Bugs and PRs ### Sampling and returned-value semantics Bug | Fix PR | Status | Description --- | --- | --- | --- #36660 (stale-closed) | #36746 | OPEN | MRV2 `top_logprobs` can contain the sampled token twice; the open fix changes `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/logprob.py`. #37037 (stale-closed) | — | OPEN IN CODE | `FlatLogprobs` empty slices can crash and delta-mode `logprobs[-0:]` can return stale data; these are shared output paths. — | #50843 | OPEN | MRV2 sampling/spec-decode kernels can emit an out-of-vocabulary ID when the final logits tile contains only `-inf`. — | #50979 | OPEN | PyTorch top-k retains more than `k` tied logits while the Triton path keeps exactly `k`, making sampling batch-size dependent. ### Determinism / batch invariance Bug | Fix PR | Status | Description --- | --- | --- | --- — | #45683 | OPEN | MoE combine (`reduce_scatterv`) is non-deterministic under DP+EP with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`. #50136 | #50505 | OPEN | Custom all-reduce kernel selection depends on token count, so reduction order changes with batch composition. — | #51287 | OPEN | Async scheduling makes batch membership timing-dependent even when batch-invariant kernels are enabled. #51290 | #51292 | OPEN | Fused all-reduce + RMSNorm is non-deterministic with TP > 1 under batch-invariant mode. #51902 | #48694 / vllm-project/flash-attention#169 | OPEN | FA3 changes tiling when an unrelated prefill changes shape, altering the same decode row on H100. — | #52421 | OPEN | cuDNN convolution algorithm selection remains non-deterministic under batch-invariant mode. — | #52522 | OPEN | Seeded stochastic speculative decoding is not yet invariant to batching, scheduling, and preemption. ### Frontend, streaming, and validation Bug | Fix PR | Status | Description --- | --- | --- | --- — | #37738 | OPEN | Streaming tool parsing can drop logprobs when a control-token delta is suppressed. — | #47815 | OPEN | Streamed completion logprob `text_offset` is wrong with `echo=True`. — | #47838 | OPEN | Chat/Responses can silently omit logprobs when `top_logprobs` is JSON `null`. #49319 | #49320 | OPEN | `logprob_token_ids=[]` bypasses validation due to truthiness checks. — | #48585 | OPEN | Python OpenAI serving can fail or emit invalid JSON for `None`/NaN/Inf logprobs. — | #51026 | OPEN | A NaN logprob rank can permanently fail the Rust engine-core client. #51420 | #51474 | OPEN | Rust frontend aborts the process when prompt logprobs are decoded for a zero-token prompt. — | #51846 | OPEN | Shared frontend checks mishandle `prompt_logprobs=0`; chat echo can also request prompt logprobs unintentionally. ### Model-specific MRV2 paths Bug | Fix PR | Status | Description --- | --- | --- | --- #45689 | #45754 | OPEN | DiffusionGemma can consume a co-batched request's pending logprobs and crash when that request later commits. — | #51953 | OPEN | DiffusionGemma MRV2 can OOM from a concurrency-sized full logits projection; the fix tiles logits projection. ### Performance PR | Status | Description --- | --- | --- #42283 | OPEN | Optimize shared `FlatLogprobs` tail slices used by delta output. #50581 | OPEN | Avoid copying Rust frontend logprobs auxiliary frames. #53090 | OPEN | Fuse target-temperature scaling in the MRV2 rejection sampler to avoid a full FP32 target-logits temporary. ### Downstream (not core vLLM bugs) Issue | Framework | Description --- | --- | --- volcengine/verl#6240 | verl | Processed vs raw `logprobs_mode` mismatch in async RL. volcengine/verl#6280 | verl | Rollout vs actor micro-batch differences produce nonzero on-policy `pg_clipfrac`. NovaSky-AI/SkyRL#877 | SkyRL | Propagate top-p/top-k sampling masks for trainer replay. NovaSky-AI/SkyRL#1776 | SkyRL | Investigate LoRA + MoE training/inference mismatch. ### Ascend parity Bug | Fix PR | Status --- | --- | --- vllm-project/vllm-ascend#7218 | vllm-project/vllm-ascend#8643 | OPEN ## Rollout Plan 1. Land MRV2/shared-path correctness and regression tests. 2. Close batch-invariance gaps in shared kernels and distributed paths. 3. Propagate the same contract into vLLM-Ascend. 4. Align downstream rollout/trainer behavior with the same definitions. 5. Keep this issue as the working tracker for open items only. ## Acceptance Criteria - Returned logits/logprobs have documented, consistent semantics. - `top_logprobs` never duplicates the sampled token and contains exactly the requested number of alternatives when possible. - MRV2 results are deterministic under the documented batch-invariance scope. - Streaming and frontend paths preserve, align, and validate logprobs. - MRV2 model-specific paths do not return stale logprobs or materialize avoidable full-vocabulary temporaries. - Ascend and downstream RL integrations follow the same contract or document explicit deviations. ## Feedback Period At least one week.

signals.title: [Bug]: v0.21.0 release notes claim 'DeepSeek V4: AMD/ROCm support' but stock vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.21.0 fails to bring up DeepSeek-V4-Flash on MI350X (mhc_post_tilelang → PDL is not supported); the official recipes YAML marks every AMD SKU as unsupported
signals.text: ## Your current environment The reproduction pod has been reclaimed by other workloads, so a fresh `python collect_env.py` is not available; relevant fields gathered in-pod during the run: <details> <summary>Environment (captured in-pod during the failing run)</summary> ```text Container image: vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.21.0 (official vllm-project release image) vllm: 0.21.0 (/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/__init__.py) PyTorch: 2.10.0+git8514f05 HIP runtime: 7.2.53211 Platform: ROCm 7.2.53 GPU: 8x AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950) 288 GiB HBM each (294592 MiB) 256 CUs, 160 KiB shared_memory_per_block current_platform: is_rocm()=True, is_fp8_fnuz()=False, fp8_dtype()=torch.float8_e4m3fn, capability=(9, 5) Tokenizer: deepseek_v4 (per --tokenizer-mode) Model: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash (canonical HF repo, 46 shards / ~159 GB, FP4+FP8 mixed per the model card) Cluster: Kubernetes (DigitalOcean DOKS), MI350X partition. ``` </details> ## 🐛 Describe the bug ### Summary The v0.21.0 release notes list **"DeepSeek V4: AMD/ROCm support (#40871)"** under Model Support, but on the official `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.21.0` image, attempting to serve `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` on MI350X (gfx950) fails during `profile_run` in the `mhc_post_tilelang` op with a hard TVM/TileLang `LogFatal`: ``` tvm.error.InternalError: Check failed: (!mutator.has_trigger_launch_ && !mutator.has_grid_sync_) is false: PDL is not supported ``` PDL = NVIDIA Hopper's Programmatic Dependent Launch — a CUDA-only feature. The TileLang pass `MarkCudaSyncCalls` refuses an IR that emits `trigger_launch` / `grid_sync` ops when targeting AMD. The path is reached from the DSv4 model's `forward` → `torch.ops.vllm.mhc_fused_post_pre` → `mhc.py:717 mhc_post_tilelang` → TileLang JIT compile. Additionally, the canonical recipe source backing [recipes.vllm.ai](https://recipes.vllm.ai) marks **every AMD SKU as `unsupported`** for both DSv4-Pro and DSv4-Flash (see [`DeepSeek-V4-Flash.yaml`](https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes/blob/main/models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash.yaml) and [`DeepSeek-V4-Pro.yaml`](https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes/blob/main/models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro.yaml)): ```yaml hardware: h200: verified b200: verified gb200: verified b300: verified gb300: verified mi300x: unsupported mi325x: unsupported mi355x: unsupported ``` So the release notes claim AMD/ROCm support, while the official recipes — same project — say it is `unsupported`. As a user reading the release notes first, this contradiction is the actual cost: ~half a day of triage on real hardware before discovering it. There is already a merged main-branch PR that adds AMD MHC support (#41946 "[Bugfix] [ROCm] [DSV4] [Perf] Add aiter mhc support", merged 2026-05-13), but it **did not make the v0.21.0 cut** at commit `ad7125a` (`git log v0.21.0 --grep="(#41946)"` returns nothing). The remaining AMD fallbacks for the rest of the Flash variant are in **open PR #41136** (`lcskrishna/vllm:deepseekv4-rocm`, currently `state=open, mergeable_state=dirty`). ### Reproduction Launch command (adapted from the only recipe-shaped doc that exists for AMD, [`wuhuikx/recipes#433`](https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes/pull/433) — unmerged PR self-labeled `[Do not merge]`; the official YAML provides no AMD command since AMD is `unsupported`). The `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` is required because `vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_v4.py:1636` asserts on it: ```bash export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \ --dtype auto --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --max-num-seqs 16 --max-num-batched-tokens 1024 \ --distributed-executor-backend mp \ --trust-remote-code \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.35 \ --moe-backend triton_unfused \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \ --async-scheduling --enforce-eager ``` ### What works Everything up to the first forward pass succeeds: - Engine config wires up cleanly: `quantization=deepseek_v4_fp8`, `kv_cache_dtype=fp8`, `tensor_parallel_size=4`, `enforce_eager=True`, `moe_backend='triton_unfused'`, `tokenizer_mode='deepseek_v4'`. - All 4 TP workers spawn, NCCL/RCCL collectives initialize, `aiter` imports. - 46/46 safetensors shards load in 233 s (`default_loader.py:397 "Loading weights took 233.04 seconds"`). - KV cache backend registers as `fp8_ds_mla` (`deepseek_v4_attention.py:714 "Using DeepSeek's fp8_ds_mla KV cache format."`). ### What fails `gpu_worker.determine_available_memory` → `model_runner.profile_run` → dummy forward: ```text File "vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_v4.py", line 1235, in forward residual, post_mix, res_mix, x = torch.ops.vllm.mhc_fused_post_pre(...) File "vllm/model_executor/layers/mhc.py", line 717, in mhc_fused_post_pre mhc_post_tilelang(...) File "tilelang/jit/__init__.py", line 465, in __call__ kernel = self.compile(*args, **kwargs) File "tilelang/engine/lower.py", line 311, in lower mod = OptimizeForTarget(mod, target) File "tilelang/engine/phase.py", line 272, in OptimizeForTarget mod = tilelang.transform.MarkCudaSyncCalls(have_pdl(target))(mod) ... tvm.error.InternalError: Check failed: (!mutator.has_trigger_launch_ && !mutator.has_grid_sync_) is false: PDL is not supported ``` All 4 workers crash identically. EngineCore then raises: ```text RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'Check failed: (!mutator.has_trigger_launch_ && !mutator.has_grid_sync_) is false: PDL is not supported' ``` No tokens are ever generated. ### Why this is a bug worth reporting (not "your hardware is unsupported") The hardware-unsupported signal exists in `recipes.vllm.ai`, but **not** in the v0.21.0 release notes, which read "DeepSeek V4: AMD/ROCm support (#40871)" — a phrase a downstream reader will reasonably interpret as "Flash on at least one MI3xx SKU runs in 0.21.0". The two sources contradict each other. Additionally, the user-facing failure is a TVM C++ `LogFatal` deep in TileLang lowering, with no actionable up-front platform check. There is no message saying "DSv4 MHC has no AMD fallback in this build; see #41136" — the user has to dig into the stack to discover that. ### Suggested fixes (any one of these would help) 1. **Reconcile the docs.** Either narrow the release-notes claim (e.g., "initial AMD/ROCm enablement landed in #40871; functional Flash support on MI3xx requires fallbacks that are still in flight in #41136 and were not all included in 0.21.0"), or — if the intent was that Pro on MI355X is actually verified — update the recipes YAMLs to reflect a `preview` / `partial` status rather than `unsupported`. 2. **Add an explicit platform check at `mhc_post_tilelang` entry** so users on ROCm get a clear error pointing to #41136 and #41946, rather than a TVM C++ check failing inside TileLang IR lowering. 3. **Consider a v0.21.1 cut that picks up #41946** (which is already merged on main but missed the 0.21.0 tag), so the gap between "release notes says supported" and "Flash runs on AMD" shrinks. ### Related - Release notes for v0.21.0: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/releases/tag/v0.21.0 - Base AMD enablement PR cited in release notes: #40871 (merged, in 0.21.0) - AMD MHC support: #41946 (merged on main 2026-05-13, **not in v0.21.0**) - Remaining AMD fallbacks for DSv4-Flash: #41136 (open, dirty) - Tracking issue for DSv4 ROCm: #41820 - Existing AMD-specific DSv4 bugs (separate failure modes, not duplicates): #41961, #41962, #41963, #41027 - NVIDIA SM12x equivalent of this MHC issue (closed via a different code path): #40991 - Recipes YAMLs claiming AMD unsupported: - https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes/blob/main/models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash.yaml - https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes/blob/main/models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro.yaml cc @hongxiayang @tjtanaa @vllmellm @lcskrishna (per the auto-cc ROCm group).

signals.title: [Bug]: Cross-node CUDA graph capture fails (illegal memory access at capture_end) — host-staged NCCL all-reduce captured by `breakable_cudagraph` on GB10 (no GPUDirect); `splitting_ops` not honored
signals.text: ## Summary On a 2-node **NVIDIA GB10 (DGX Spark)** cluster (TP=2 across nodes), PIECEWISE CUDA-graph capture dies with `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` at `capture_end()`. Root cause: the **cross-node `vllm::all_reduce` collective is captured inside a piecewise cudagraph segment**. GB10 has **no GPUDirect RDMA**, so NCCL falls back to a host-staged transport (host bounce buffers + CPU-side progress); such a collective is not CUDA-graph-capturable, and capture finalization faults. `--enforce-eager` works fine. The model is otherwise correct. This makes large MoE / TP models on multi-node GB10 permanently eager-bound (no cudagraph), which is a large decode-throughput loss. ## Environment - **Hardware:** 2× NVIDIA GB10 (DGX Spark), aarch64, Blackwell **sm_121a (cc 12.1)**. Inter-node = dual ConnectX-7 200G RoCE, direct-cabled. **GPUDirect RDMA disabled / unavailable** → NCCL host-staged (`ib_write_bw` healthy ~13 GB/s, but collectives bounce through host). - **vLLM:** `0.23.1rc1.dev197+g01192139b` (nightly), **torch 2.11.0+cu130**, CUDA 13.0, **NCCL 2.28.9**. - **Parallelism:** `--tensor-parallel-size 2` (+`--enable-expert-parallel`) across the 2 nodes, native multi-node (no Ray), `--disable-custom-all-reduce` (custom all-reduce is single-node/NVLink only). - **Attention backend:** `TRITON_ATTN`. **Model:** a cross-node MoE (MiniMax-M3-class). ## Symptom / stack (capture phase) ``` vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py profile_cudagraph_memory → _warmup_and_capture vllm/compilation/breakable_cudagraph.py __call__ → _capture → _end_segment → self._current_graph.capture_end() torch/cuda/graphs.py capture_end → super().capture_end() torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered # (an NCCL error appears earlier in the same multi-rank trace) ``` `cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` and `PIECEWISE` both fail identically. `cudagraph_mode=NONE` / `--enforce-eager` are stable. ## Root cause (verified by stack trace) The fault is a **host-staged NCCL `ncclAllReduce` captured into a CUDA graph**. The crashing all-reduce is reached via: ``` minimax_m3/nvidia/model.py:723 fused_allreduce_gemma_rms_norm(hidden_states, residual, post_attention_layernorm) model_executor/layers/fused_allreduce_gemma_rms_norm.py:142 distributed/communication_op.py:14 tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce distributed/parallel_state.py:627 torch.ops.vllm.all_reduce(...) → pynccl ncclAllReduce → NCCL_CHECK (NCCL error) torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered (at capture_end()) ``` Two facts make this hard to avoid via config: 1. **The collective is fused.** The M3 model calls `fused_allreduce_gemma_rms_norm(...)`, which performs the cross-node all-reduce **inside** a fused all-reduce+RMSNorm op. So it is **not** a standalone `vllm::all_reduce` node at the graph level — adding `vllm::all_reduce` to `splitting_ops` does **not** exclude it (we tried; capture still faults identically). 2. **`splitting_ops` isn't even consulted on this path.** For this model (custom quant / not fully torch.compile-traceable) vLLM **auto-enables `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1`** ("Auto-enabling VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 … disabling vLLM's torch.compile pipeline. Equivalent to -cc.mode=none"). The `breakable_cudagraph` capturer wraps the **eager** forward and does not segment on `splitting_ops` (a torch.compile/FX concept), so the fused all-reduce is captured. On single-node TP this is fine (custom all-reduce over NVLink is graph-safe); **cross-node on GB10 it's host-staged NCCL** (host bounce + CPU-side progress) → illegal during capture. Consistent with the platform report "NCCL all-reduce deadlock on dual DGX Spark" (forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/.../366127, affects TRT-LLM too) — capture turns the latent host-staged-collective incompatibility into a hard `illegal memory access` rather than a hang. ## Workarounds tried - `splitting_ops += vllm::all_reduce,reduce_scatter,all_gather` (PIECEWISE): **no effect** — the all-reduce is fused (point 1) and `breakable_cudagraph` ignores `splitting_ops` (point 2). - `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` + the split set (force the torch.compile piecewise path so `splitting_ops` applies): **fails at init** with `AssertionError: Compilation mode should be CompilationMode.VLLM_COMPILE when cudagraph_mode piecewise cudagraphs is used … cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE, compilation_mode=3`. The custom-quant model can't run the VLLM_COMPILE piecewise path (which is *why* breakable was auto-enabled), so `splitting_ops` is effectively unavailable for it. ⟹ on this model, **all three cudagraph routes are blocked**. - `--enforce-eager` / `cudagraph_mode=NONE`: stable, but no cudagraph (decode launch-overhead bound). ## Fix validation (we prototyped it) We monkeypatched the cross-node collectives to be **eager break points** via vLLM's own `eager_break_during_capture` (the mechanism already used for attention): wrapped `tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce` to run NCCL eagerly and write the result back **in place**, and routed `fused_allreduce_gemma_rms_norm` through it. **Result: PIECEWISE/breakable capture SUCCEEDS** — "Graph capturing finished in 1 secs" — i.e. the host-staged all-reduce no longer blocks capture (attention, MoE expert + shared-expert collectives all eager-break cleanly). So the fix direction is confirmed. **Two compounding caveats we hit (so this is not yet a usable build):** - *Replay correctness:* with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` (needed to capture at all, see next), capture succeeds but **replay produces ~zero logits / garbage**. Tried two all-reduce impls (out-of-place+copy, and true in-place `torch.distributed.all_reduce`) — both garbage, so the all-reduce wrapper is not the cause; the captured decode compute is producing zeros. Getting correct replay needs the collective output AND the surrounding captured segments to share **static** buffers across the break. - *Capture-time deadlock without CLB:* with `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH` and no `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING`, capture **deadlocks** — `shm_broadcast: No available shared memory broadcast block found in 60 seconds` (lazy Triton-JIT / NCCL desync between ranks during capture; same as the dual-DGX-Spark NCCL all-reduce deadlock report). CLB serializes the ranks and avoids it, but cripples throughput. So `breakable_cudagraph` should own BOTH: (a) eager-break collectives with guaranteed static buffering, and (b) pre-compile/warm all Triton kernels (incl. spec-decode/sampling) before capture so a lazy JIT can't desync the ranks mid-capture on a host-staged-NCCL multi-node setup. ## Proposed fix For host-staged cross-node collectives (multi-node + `disable_custom_all_reduce` + no NVLink + GPUDirect unavailable), either: - make **`breakable_cudagraph` segment at communication ops** (break around `vllm::all_reduce` and around fused all-reduce ops like `fused_allreduce_gemma_rms_norm`), running the collective eagerly between captured compute segments (the "compute–comm–compute" pattern); and/or - **disable the all-reduce+RMSNorm fusion** when the collective isn't graph-capturable, so the all-reduce becomes a standalone splittable node; and/or - a capability probe at init (is this collective graph-capturable on this transport?) selecting the split set. ## Repro (minimal) 1. 2× GB10, native multi-node, TP=2, NCCL on RoCE (no GPUDirect), `--disable-custom-all-reduce`. 2. Serve any TP-sharded model with default `cudagraph_mode` (PIECEWISE/compiled), `--no-async-scheduling`. 3. Engine dies during cudagraph capture with `illegal memory access` at `capture_end()`. 4. Add the collectives to `splitting_ops` (above) → capture succeeds, serves. ## Ask - Confirm the intended behavior for host-staged cross-node collectives under piecewise cudagraph. - Auto-split at collectives (or document the `splitting_ops` requirement) for GB10 / no-GPUDirect multi-node.

signals.title: [RFC]: PyTorch vLLM correctness audit
signals.text: ### Motivation #### Fix coincidentally correct tests flagged by numeric stability audit Our goal is to smoothen the handoff between PyTorch and vLLM during release. Some tests in vllm may either expect a guarantee in correctness from PyTorch that is not valid causing misleading test failures that aren't true failures or they do not verify the property they intend to. This can lead to hard to debug failing tests against new releases costing significant development time and CI costs. The audit identifies tests that are **coincidentally correct** (CC) — tests that pass today but rely on unstated numeric assumptions that a PyTorch update could silently break. These patterns are identified as a contract of correctness between PyTorch and vLLM, which is documented at [correctness-contract](https://github.com/morrison-turnansky/vllm-test-audit/blob/main/skills/audit-contract/SKILL.md). While we believe that these tests can be identified automatically via agents, we first want to introduce the idea to the community. All issues and PRs involved with this audit will be reviewed and verified during this initial phase. If the community finds value in this, we can consider adding this agentic linting to the CI or run at regular intervals (nightly, monthly, etc.). We will present evaluation metrics of our agents performance before anything is exposed to upstream CI. ### Proposed Change. This issue tracks incremental PRs that fix individual CC-flagged tests. Each PR will reference this issue, cite the specific audit clause, and make the test compliant. If a test is made compliant and is now failing that is useful signal, but we should separate source code fixes from test code fixes during out initial pass. ### Feedback Period. _No response_ ### CC List. @zou3519 @dougbtv ### Any Other Things. _No response_ ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Feature] Support `extract_hidden_states` on Model Runner V2
signals.text: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch ### Feature Add Model Runner V2 support for `extract_hidden_states`, so the existing hidden-state extraction path works when MRv2 is enabled (ideally via an `ExtractHiddenStatesSpeculator` registered in `init_speculator()`), with the same core semantics as Model Runner V1: - extract configured intermediate-layer `aux_hidden_states` - write them into `HiddenStateCache` through the cache-only extract model - remain compatible with hidden-states KV connectors (e.g. `ExampleHiddenStatesConnector`) - return sampled tokens as draft tokens so verification always accepts ### Motivation `extract_hidden_states` is already supported on Model Runner V1 (`ExtractHiddenStatesProposer`) and documented for draft-model data generation / analysis. MRv2 is becoming the default path for more models, but today MRv2 `init_speculator()` does not register extract and raises: ```python NotImplementedError(f"{speculative_config.method} is not supported yet.") ``` ### Pitch Porting extract to MRv2 would: 1. keep feature parity with MRv1 as MRv2 adoption grows 2. avoid long-lived out-of-tree forks just to preserve an already-supported speculative method 3. reuse the existing extract model / cache-spec / connector stack, mainly adding the missing MRv2 Speculator wiring ### Alternatives 1. **Maintain an out-of-tree / backend-specific MRv2 Speculator** Unblocks local users quickly, but risks divergence from upstream semantics and higher maintenance cost. 2. **Build a separate non-speculative hidden-state export API** Cleaner long-term API maybe, but much larger scope than porting the already accepted extract method to MRv2. 3. **Do nothing / wait without tracking** Leaves a growing MRv1/MRv2 feature gap with no clear roadmap signal for downstream projects. ### Additional context #### Current status on recent `main` - **Model Runner V1**: supported in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py` via `ExtractHiddenStatesProposer`, with `use_aux_hidden_state_outputs = True`. - **Model Runner V2**: `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/__init__.py` `init_speculator()` currently registers only `dflash` / `dspark` / Gemma4 MTP / `mtp` / eagle-family (`use_eagle()`). Other methods, including `extract_hidden_states`, fall through to `NotImplementedError`. - There is no `ExtractHiddenStatesSpeculator` (or equivalent) under `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/`. So with MRv2 enabled, a config like: ```python speculative_config = { "method": "extract_hidden_states", "num_speculative_tokens": 1, "draft_model_config": { "hf_config": { "eagle_aux_hidden_state_layer_ids": [1, 2, 3, 4], }, }, } ``` fails at speculator initialization instead of using the existing V1 extract path. #### Related prior art I searched existing issues/PRs for an MRv2 port of `extract_hidden_states` and did **not** find a dedicated tracking issue/PR. Closest related work: - Original RFC: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/33118 - Initial feature: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/33736 - Docs: `docs/features/speculative_decoding/extract_hidden_states.md` - Follow-up MRv1 / connector / hybrid work (not MRv2 port), e.g.: - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39949 - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43869 - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49301 There are active MRv2 speculative-decoding efforts (Eagle/MTP/draft-model, etc.), but none appear to cover `extract_hidden_states` specifically. #### Why this matters As MRv2 becomes the default for more models, lacking extract support creates a feature gap for draft-model data generation and for out-of-tree backends that are migrating users to MRv2 while still needing hidden-state export. #### Questions for maintainers 1. Is it correct that MRv2 does not support `extract_hidden_states` yet? 2. Is there already a tracking issue/PR that I missed? 3. Is there a rough priority or timeline for an MRv2 port (e.g. an `ExtractHiddenStatesSpeculator`)? Happy to help prototype or review an in-tree MRv2 implementation if that matches upstream direction. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Bug][Spec Decode] DSpark speculative decoding broken on H200 nightly
signals.text: ## Summary DSpark speculative decoding (`method: "dspark"`) is non-functional on current main. Multiple code paths assume only `"dflash"` when DSpark reuses the same proposer/speculator infrastructure (`DSparkSpeculator` extends `DFlashSpeculator`, both use `DFlashProposer`). The result is that DSpark either crashes at startup or produces wrong results at inference time. Tested on GLM-5.2-FP8 (753B MoE) with `RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-speculator.dspark` on multi-node Wide-EP H200 clusters. ## Bugs ### 1. `use_dflash()` excludes DSpark — model runner never creates `DFlashProposer` **File:** `vllm/config/speculative.py` (line ~1395) ```python def use_dflash(self) -> bool: return self.method == "dflash" # BUG: excludes "dspark" ``` `use_dspark()` exists (line ~1398) but is never checked in the model runner's drafter initialization elif chain (`gpu_model_runner.py`). DSpark falls through without getting `DFlashProposer` or `use_aux_hidden_state_outputs = True`, so the target model doesn't extract multi-layer aux hidden states. **Fix:** `return self.method in ("dflash", "dspark")` ### 2. `DFlashProposer.__init__` asserts `method == "dflash"` **File:** `vllm/v1/spec_decode/dflash.py` ```python assert vllm_config.speculative_config.method == "dflash" ``` Even after fixing #1, this assert rejects DSpark at proposer creation time. **Fix:** `assert method in ("dflash", "dspark")` ### 3. `llm_base_proposer.py` missing "dspark" in method lists **File:** `vllm/v1/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py` Three locations where DSpark needs to be included alongside DFlash: - **`model_returns_tuple()`** (~line 1015): exclusion list `("mtp", "draft_model", "dflash")` missing `"dspark"` → `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2)` at line ~591 - **`combine_hidden_states` gate** (~line 526): inclusion list `("eagle3", "dflash")` missing `"dspark"` → aux hidden states not combined for the drafter - **`parallel_drafting_token_id` ValueError** — raises for unknown method instead of setting a default for DSpark ### 4. FA3 AOT scheduler head count mismatch (separate PR) Already addressed in #50694 — the FA3 AOT scheduler reads head counts from the target model config, but the draft model may have a different GQA ratio. ## Error Traces ### Without any hotfixes — `model_returns_tuple` crash: ``` ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2) File "vllm/v1/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py", line 591 ``` ### After adding "dspark" to `model_returns_tuple` but not fixing routing — `combine_hidden_states` dimension mismatch: ``` ValueError: DFlash drafter expects 30720 concatenated aux hidden features but received 6144 File "vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_dflash.py", line 761 File "vllm/v1/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py", line 536 ``` (30720 = 5 layers × 6144 hidden_size — target model only outputs last hidden state because `use_aux_hidden_state_outputs` was never set) ## Environment - vLLM nightly (`vllm/vllm-openai:nightly`, v0.26.1rc1.dev255) - Model: `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8` + `RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-speculator.dspark` - Config: `--speculative-config {"model":"...","num_speculative_tokens":5,"method":"dspark"}` - Multi-node Wide-EP with H200 GPUs, DP=16, EP enabled

### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Summary For a `Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration` checkpoint (Ministral-3 family) in HF format, vLLM produces deterministic gibberish (grammatically-plausible, real-vocabulary, multi-language tokens with no coherent meaning) regardless of prompt, while plain `transformers.generate()` on the identical checkpoint is fully coherent. No error or warning is raised at load time. Root cause: `transformers`' own `Mistral3Config.__init__` (the top-level composite-wrapper config class) hardcodes `tie_word_embeddings: bool = True` as its own signature default and never reads/syncs it from `text_config` -- while `Ministral3Config` (the nested `text_config` class actually used for the language model) independently defaults to `tie_word_embeddings=False`. These are two different classes with two different hardcoded defaults, so any checkpoint whose `config.json` doesn't explicitly pin both fields (e.g. the pristine base model itself) loads with a latent conflict between them -- before any merge/export/fine-tuning is involved. `transformers`' own weight-tying logic uses `text_config` (confirmed: `transformers.generate()` is coherent, and the checkpoint's `lm_head.weight`/`embed_tokens.weight` are verifiably distinct tensors, see below), so the top-level field is functionally vestigial there and the mismatch is invisible to `transformers` itself. vLLM appears to resolve tying from the top-level field instead, silently discards the checkpoint's real, correctly-trained `lm_head.weight`, and computes output logits through `embed_tokens.weight` instead -- explaining the exact symptom (valid vocabulary, incoherent output) with no load-time error, since a redundant `lm_head` tensor under an assumed-tied model is normally dropped silently by vLLM's weight loader rather than flagged. ## Environment - vLLM 0.25.1 - Checkpoint: HF-format LoRA-merge of `mistralai/Ministral-3-8B-Base-2512` (`architectures: ["Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration"]`, `model_type: "mistral3"`, nested `text_config.model_type: "ministral3"`) - Reproduced under both vLLM's native `Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration` implementation and `model_impl="transformers"` (the generic Transformers-modeling-backend fallback) -- **identical** gibberish output under both, including in `enforce_eager=True` mode (CUDA graphs ruled out). This points to the bug being in something vLLM's engine does identically across both model-implementation backends (weight-tying resolution), not in either backend's own forward-pass/kernel code. ## Relevant config.json fields ```json { "architectures": ["Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration"], "model_type": "mistral3", "tie_word_embeddings": true, "text_config": { "model_type": "ministral3", "tie_word_embeddings": false, ... }, ... } ``` The base model (`mistralai/Ministral-3-8B-Base-2512`) itself has no `tie_word_embeddings` field at either level in its raw `config.json` -- the conflict above only becomes visible once the config is loaded into Python objects (`Mistral3Config`/`Ministral3Config`'s differing defaults fill it in) and then re-serialized, e.g. by a LoRA-merge/export step's `save_pretrained()` call (LLaMA-Factory's `llamafactory-cli export` in our case). That serialization step isn't introducing the conflict -- it's faithfully writing out a conflict that already exists in `transformers`' own class defaults for this model family, latent in the base model from the moment its config is parsed. So this isn't specific to merged/fine-tuned checkpoints: any HF-format Mistral3/Ministral3-family checkpoint without both fields explicitly pinned could hit this in vLLM. ## Verified NOT the cause (ruled out before landing on this) - **Corrupted/incomplete merge weights**: `transformers.generate()` on the identical checkpoint is coherent. - **Weights silently left at random init / silently-skipped checkpoint tensors**: checked `vllm/model_executor/model_loader/default_loader.py`'s `DefaultModelLoader` and `AutoWeightsLoader` -- both raise `ValueError` if any model parameter never receives a checkpoint tensor, or if an unexpected/unmapped checkpoint tensor doesn't match a model parameter (unless explicitly allowlisted, e.g. `.bias`). Loading succeeds without error here, so this isn't a plain missing/unmapped-weight situation. - **CUDA graph / kernel-fusion corruption**: reproduced identically with `enforce_eager=True`. - **RoPE (YaRN) `rope_parameters` handling**: this checkpoint's `text_config.rope_parameters` uses `rope_type: "yarn"` with `mscale`/ `mscale_all_dim` fields vLLM's YaRN implementation doesn't extract (confirmed via `vllm/model_executor/layers/rotary_embedding/__init__.py`'s `get_rope()` allowlist) -- flagged and tested as a hypothesis, but injecting a corrective `attn_factor` (computed to cancel the resulting ~1.277x default mscale back to the reference implementation's 1.0) produced byte-for-byte near-identical gibberish, ruling this out as the (or at least the primary) cause. - **vLLM's own `Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration` implementation specifically**: `model_impl="transformers"` (bypassing vLLM's hand-written `mistral3.py` entirely) reproduces the identical output. ## Confirmed: lm_head and embed_tokens are genuinely untied in this checkpoint ```python from safetensors import safe_open import torch with safe_open("model-00001-of-00004.safetensors", framework="pt") as f: lm_head = f.get_tensor("language_model.lm_head.weight") embed = f.get_tensor("language_model.model.embed_tokens.weight") torch.equal(lm_head, embed) # False (lm_head.float() - embed.float()).abs().max().item() # 0.32110595703125 ``` ## Fix that resolves it (tested) Patching only the top-level `tie_word_embeddings` field to match the nested `text_config.tie_word_embeddings` (leaving everything else, including the actual weights, untouched) fully resolves the issue. Validated end-to-end: ran the same checkpoint through a full production evaluation harness (37 real judge-classification datasets, full sample counts, not a toy subset) both before and after the patch -- before: uniform incoherent gibberish regardless of dataset; after: real, varied, discriminating metrics (accuracy 0.65-1.0, F1 0.46-1.0, sensible TP/TN/FP/FN splits) closely matching a known-good `transformers.generate()`-based baseline run on the same checkpoint/datasets. ## Suggested root-cause fix For composite VLM wrapper classes like `Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration`, `vllm/model_executor/models/mistral3.py`'s `__init__` already passes `hf_config=config.text_config` (not the top-level composite config) when constructing the inner language model via `init_vllm_registered_model(...)` -- i.e. vLLM already treats `text_config` as authoritative for that submodel's architecture/layer construction. Whatever resolves the weight-tying decision for that inner language model should be consistent with this and also read `tie_word_embeddings` from that same `text_config`, rather than (apparently) falling back to the top-level `vllm_config.model_config.hf_config.tie_word_embeddings`. We haven't pinpointed the exact line responsible -- happy to help narrow it down further if useful, but wanted to report given how solid the repro/diagnosis is and how easy the corruption is to miss (no error, no warning, output is merely wrong rather than absent). ## Practical workaround for anyone else hitting this Before loading via vLLM, patch the checkpoint's `config.json`: ```python import json with open("config.json") as f: cfg = json.load(f) cfg["tie_word_embeddings"] = cfg["text_config"]["tie_word_embeddings"] with open("config.json", "w") as f: json.dump(cfg, f, indent=2) ``` ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Bug]: seed is ignored on CPU when another request in the batch has no seed
signals.text: FYI: Work for this is already in progress and the issue is already claimed ### Your current environment ``` vllm 0.26.0+cpu (vllm-0.26.0+cpu-cp38-abi3-manylinux_2_34_x86_64.whl from the v0.26.0 release) torch 2.11.0+cpu Python 3.12, x86_64 Linux, no GPU ``` ### Describe the bug `SamplingParams(seed=...)` is not respected on CPU when the batch also contains a request without a seed. I'm running two requests together. The first has `seed=42`, the second has no seed. I expected the first request's output to be identical every time I run this, and it isn't — it comes out different on every iteration. If I give the *second* request a seed as well, without touching the first request at all, the first request suddenly becomes reproducible. So whether my seeded request is deterministic seems to depend on the sampling params of the other requests it happens to be batched with. ### 🐛 Describe the bug ```python from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams MODEL, ITERS = "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", 4 PROMPTS = ["The capital of France is", "The capital of Germany is"] def run(llm, second_seeded: bool): params = [ SamplingParams(seed=42, temperature=0.8, max_tokens=16, ignore_eos=True), SamplingParams(seed=(7 if second_seeded else None), temperature=0.8, max_tokens=16, ignore_eos=True), ] return [tuple(llm.generate(PROMPTS, params)[0].outputs[0].token_ids) for _ in range(ITERS)] def main(): llm = LLM(model=MODEL, enforce_eager=True, max_model_len=256) mixed = run(llm, second_seeded=False) # request 1 has no seed control = run(llm, second_seeded=True) # request 1 also seeded print("req1 unseeded -> distinct outputs for req0:", len(set(mixed))) for t in mixed: print(" ", t) print("req1 seeded -> distinct outputs for req0:", len(set(control))) for t in control: print(" ", t) if __name__ == "__main__": main() ``` Request 0 has `seed=42` in both halves, so I'd expect one distinct output in both. What I get: ``` req1 unseeded -> distinct outputs for req0: 4 (12095, 13, 1416, 279, 5590, 3349, 3349, 374, 220, 23, 11, 323, 279, 3349, 315, 1008) (12095, 323, 279, 6722, 315, 32961, 374, 37169, 13, 576, 6722, 315, 33311, 374, 80701, 13) (12095, 13, 576, 6722, 315, 9625, 374, 9625, 13, 576, 6722, 315, 9625, 374, 9625, 13) (12095, 11, 323, 1181, 7772, 3283, 13, 78639, 315, 279, 3639, 4180, 315, 5159, 9270, 1599) req1 seeded -> distinct outputs for req0: 1 (12095, 11, 323, 12095, 374, 279, 6722, 315, 1181, 7772, 3283, 304, 9625, 11, 892, 374) (12095, 11, 323, 12095, 374, 279, 6722, 315, 1181, 7772, 3283, 304, 9625, 11, 892, 374) (12095, 11, 323, 12095, 374, 279, 6722, 315, 1181, 7772, 3283, 304, 9625, 11, 892, 374) (12095, 11, 323, 12095, 374, 279, 6722, 315, 1181, 7772, 3283, 304, 9625, 11, 892, 374) ``` **Expected:** one distinct output in both halves — request 0's seed should make it "mostly" reproducible regardless of what else is in the batch. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the documentation and examples for help.

signals.title: [RFC]: DP pause/sleep correctness: coordinator latch, request admission, device-idle completion, and sleep/pause layering
signals.text: ### Motivation. Pause and sleep are the control plane RL post-training stands on: every weight sync is a pause → (trainer work) → sleep → wake → resume cycle. This RFC tracks four separable problems on that path. They are one topic: **what each call claims versus what it actually guarantees.** | # | Problem | Status | |---|---|---| | 1 | Coordinator's `engines_running` latches `True`; drain can only time out | **Fixed** — #51481 (merged) | | 2 | Per-mode request admission during pause was specified (#32103) but never implemented | #51488 (draft) | | 3 | Pause completion is CPU-only: the future resolves while the device is still busy — and in DP the pause path itself manufactures the GPU work it fails to wait for | #52914, #52957 (in review) | | 4 | `sleep` embeds request-fate policy (`mode`, default `abort`) that belongs to `pause`, and the pause→sleep flow runs the quiescence consensus twice | #53082 (draft, the end-state implementation) — seeking consensus | --- **1. The coordinator latch (fixed by #51481).** After a pause, a single request arriving from a front-end set the DP coordinator's `engines_running` to `True` permanently: `True` was a *prediction* made when forwarding a wake, while `False` was an *observation* requiring the engines to actually step — and paused engines never step, so `wave_complete` was never produced and `True` had no path back. `wait_for_requests_to_drain` could then only reach its 300 s timeout, and the stale `True` published to front-ends made them skip the `FIRST_REQ` notification, so after `resume` nothing woke the engines. All pause modes were affected. The merged fix reports both edges from the engines (rank 0 reports the `False→True` transition, guarded by `not pending_pause` so the pause kick-start is not misreported) and stops predicting in the coordinator. No new fields or message types; the decision stays in the single coordinator process, so ranks cannot diverge (the failure mode that sank #38009). **2. Per-mode admission: specified, never implemented (#51488).** #32103 specified "Frontend blocks new requests" for all modes; the implementation instead queues late arrivals into the scheduler's waiting queue regardless of mode — `mode` only describes requests already in flight. One rule generates the intended behavior: > **`mode` says who keeps custody of a request during the pause.** > `keep` — the engine carries requests across, so late arrivals are held too. > `abort` / `wait` — the pause is a generation boundary, so late arrivals are rejected. Today `abort` says "custody is yours" and then silently keeps late arrivals: a request accepted under old weights executes under new ones; reschedule-style partial rollout gets a **second rollout for the same sample**; and none of it is observable, because the request is excluded from `get_num_unfinished_requests()` under `PAUSED_NEW` and a paused engine publishes no stats. #51488 implements the custody rule at the front-end (`EnginePausedError`, admission closed *before* the pause is requested, reopened if the pause fails; `keep` still accepts). A front-end guard cannot be airtight — each front-end's view of "paused" is a lagging replica — which is why (1) had to land first: with it, the residue is untidy rather than fatal. **3. Pause completion is not a device barrier — and in DP, pause *creates* GPU work (#52914, #52957).** Reported from production: pause + `wait_for_requests_to_drain` before `sleep` does not guarantee an idle GPU; the flow survives on the incidental ~0.5 s between pause and sleep. Verified against main: - The pause future resolves off `has_work()` — a pure CPU predicate — and the DP pause consensus is a **gloo CPU** all-reduce. Nothing on the pause path touches a CUDA stream. - In DP the situation is stronger than "no barrier": `DPEngineCoreProc._pause_complete` unconditionally kick-starts idle engines so every rank reaches the consensus all-reduce, and the fixed every-32-step sync cadence makes each pause call manufacture **32 dummy forwards per rank**. The consensus iteration launches its final dummy batch *before* the all-reduce and nothing ever waits on it (not in `batch_queue`, invisible to `has_work()`); the future resolves one iteration later while that forward can still be executing. - Drain cannot compensate: the coordinator only tracks request-driven waves, so during the burst it publishes "not running" and drain returns immediately — a structural false positive, not a race. - `sleep()` itself is safe only because `GPUWorker.sleep` synchronizes the device before unmapping. Bare pause is sleep minus the synchronizing half; callers that run their own kernels or NCCL between pause and sleep race the in-flight dummy-batch collectives. Measured (DP=2 + EP, PowerMoE-3b, dummy batch inflated to ~110 ms to model a large-MoE step): `pause_generation()` on an **idle** engine takes **3.4 s** and returns with the device still busy; drain returns in 0.00 s during the burst while `pause_done=False`. Fixes, split into two independent PRs (repro scripts in the #52914 description): - **#52914** — resolve the pause future only after `collective_rpc("synchronize_device")` on every worker, in all three pause completion paths (in-proc, fast path, deferred idle callback). Makes pause completion honest regardless of in-flight work. - **#52957** — sync DP state on the first step of a wave as well as every 32nd, so an idle-engine pause reaches consensus after **one** dummy forward instead of 32 — measured 3.4 s → 0.17 s. Also caps the cost of the re-pause `sleep()` runs internally (problem 4). **4. Sleep's semantics are entangled with pause's.** `sleep` was born pure: #12987 introduced it as a memory-state transition only (`executor.sleep(level)` — offload/discard, `wake_up` restores). #33195 routed level 0 through `pause_scheduler()`, and #34528 completed today's shape: ``` sleep(level, mode) = pause_scheduler(mode, clear_cache=level>=1) # request fate + quiescence + executor.sleep(level) # memory release ``` The memory layer is cleanly unaware of requests (`executor.sleep` has no `mode`). The entanglement is at the engine API: `sleep` answers "what happens to the requests" — a question that belongs to `pause` — through a duplicated `mode` vocabulary with a policy default (`abort`), and `sleep(level=0)` is simply a pause under another name. Concrete costs of the entanglement, observed in review and production flows: - The standard RL flow pause → sync → sleep runs the DP quiescence consensus **twice**; the second run kick-starts all ranks again for up to 32 dummy forwards (~3.4 s measured, reduced to ~0.2 s by #52957 — mitigated, not removed). - The internal re-pause cannot be guarded with "already paused → skip": the guard would read a local snapshot of a global in-flight property (`pending_pause` / `engines_running` / `ignore_start_dp_wave` all flip inside the consensus iteration, while the sleep RPC arrives at each rank at an unsynchronized time), and ranks landing on opposite sides of the flip deadlock the gloo rendezvous — one rank enters the all-reduce, the other never does. The unconditional kick-start is what makes the current protocol safe. - `sleep(mode="keep", level>=1)` has compound semantics that surprise callers: requests survive but their KV is preempted and recomputed from scratch after wake — "keep the request, drop the compute" — expressible, but not discoverable from a memory API. ### Proposed Change. Problems 1–3 have concrete fixes (merged / in review, linked above). The new proposal is for problem 4: **restore the layering so that `pause` owns request fate and quiescence, and `sleep` owns memory state — each call guaranteeing exactly what its name claims.** Target end state: - `pause(mode)` — request fate (custody rule from problem 2) + group quiescence + device barrier (#52914). Its completion means: no request needs the GPU, and the GPU is idle. - `sleep(level)` — memory release only. **Precondition: the engine is paused**; raises (`EngineNotPausedError`) otherwise. No `mode` parameter. - `wake_up(tags)` — memory restore only; full wake resumes the scheduler as today, partial wake keeps it paused. Why a *raise* is distributively safe where a *skip* is not: a failed precondition check never enters a collective — every rank either proceeds into the same protocol or errors out to the client, so local-snapshot divergence produces a retryable error instead of a hung all-reduce. The fan-out does need to be all-or-nothing (check on all ranks before any rank releases memory) to avoid partial sleep; that check-then-commit shape is an open design point below. Migration (non-breaking, phased): 1. **Now**: document the layering (`sleep = pause + release`; `level 0` is an alias of pause), land #52914/#52957/#51488. 2. **Deprecation period**: `sleep` called on an un-paused engine keeps today's behavior (internal pause, `mode` honored) but emits a `DeprecationWarning` steering callers to explicit `pause(mode)` → `sleep(level)`; `mode` on `sleep` is marked deprecated. 3. **After the period**: un-paused `sleep` raises; `mode` is removed; `sleep(level=0)` is removed or kept as a documented alias of `pause`. ### Open questions. 1. Direct-`sleep` users (e.g. SPMD colocate frameworks call `llm.sleep()` without a prior pause): is a deprecation cycle across two releases enough runway? 2. Should the sleep fan-out be made check-then-commit (verify all ranks paused, then release), or is raise-and-retry on partial failure acceptable? 3. `sleep(level=0)`: deprecate in favor of `pause`, or keep as an alias? 4. Does anyone depend on `wait` queuing new requests during a pause (problem 2's custody rule aligns it with `abort`)? 5. For `keep`, what shape should the client-visible "paused, not finished" marker take — a `RequestOutput` field, or a protocol-level event in the OpenAI-compatible layer? ### Feedback Period. One week. ### CC List. @njhill @markmc (DP coordinator) @hao-aaron (#37024, #39366) @kouroshHakha (#32103) @junjzhang (#36594) ### Any Other Things. Background findings that constrain the fixes, kept for the record: - Wave coordination is MoE-only (`enable_wave_coordination = model_config.is_moe`); dense DP never reaches this code. - The coordinator cannot infer a pause: pause is a client→engine utility RPC that bypasses it, and a paused engine publishes no stats — observability is lowest exactly in the state drain cares about. - The scheduler keeps two disagreeing ledgers for requests queued during a pause: visible in `len(self.waiting)` for stats, hidden from `get_num_unfinished_requests()` under `PAUSED_NEW`. Count-based drain predicates are therefore not viable. - `keep` + `clear_cache=True` already preempts running requests and recomputes after resume; what is missing is the client-visible pause signal (open question 5). - Fix history before this RFC was engine-side only (#37024, #39366); #38009 was rejected because per-engine checks make ranks diverge and break the all-reduce rendezvous. AI assistance was used while investigating and drafting this RFC; all code references were traced and verified by hand against `main`.

signals.title: [New Model]: nvidia/LocateAnything-3B (slow autoregressive mode first)
signals.text: ### The model to consider. ### The model to consider https://huggingface.co/nvidia/LocateAnything-3B The model architecture is `LocateAnythingForConditionalGeneration`. It consists of: - MoonViT vision encoder - MLP multimodal projector - Qwen2.5-3B language model - custom Parallel Box Decoding (PBD) ### The closest model vLLM already supports `KimiVLForConditionalGeneration` is probably the closest reference for the multimodal path because it also uses MoonViT. The language model can reuse vLLM's existing Qwen2 implementation. ### What's your difficulty of supporting the model? The standard autoregressive `generation_mode="slow"` appears compatible with vLLM's normal one-token decoding loop. However, the model's default hybrid mode uses Parallel Box Decoding: - predicts a six-token box block in parallel - uses a custom block attention mask - switches dynamically between PBD and autoregressive decoding - requires special KV-cache commit/truncation behavior ### Proposed scope For the initial PR, I propose to support: - image preprocessing and multimodal input - MoonViT vision encoder - multimodal projector - Qwen2 language decoder - weight loading - `generation_mode="slow"` only - correctness tests against the Hugging Face slow-mode reference - offline inference and OpenAI-compatible serving PBD fast/hybrid decoding would be implemented in a follow-up PR. Would maintainers accept slow autoregressive mode as the initial model support scope, or is PBD/hybrid decoding required for the first PR? I would also be happy to work on the implementation if this scope is acceptable. ### The closest model vllm already supports. _No response_ ### What's your difficulty of supporting the model you want? _No response_ ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

============================== PYTORCH_NVML_BASED_CUDA_CHECK=1 TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPILE_THREADS=1 TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/torchinductor_nvidia ### 🐛 Describe the bug ### Summary Filed as a code-inspection issue, not a field-crash report. The narrow `except ImportError` in `CudaPlatform.get_valid_backends` and the selected-backend branch of `get_attn_backend_cls` under-implements the probe loop's contract ("mark unavailable, keep going") — any non-`ImportError` raised while importing or validating a backend propagates out and terminates engine init, regardless of whether the underlying cause is filesystem, CUDA runtime, version drift, or anything else the loop cannot enumerate in advance. ### Where - `vllm/platforms/cuda.py:378-394` — `get_valid_backends` enumeration path - `vllm/platforms/cuda.py:407-423` — `get_attn_backend_cls` selected-backend path Both wrap probing in `try: ... except ImportError:` and record `invalid_reasons = ["ImportError"]` — a string that also loses the actual failure detail on the paths it does catch. ### Synthetic reproducer ```python from unittest.mock import patch from vllm.platforms.cuda import CudaPlatform for exc in [ ImportError("baseline: currently handled"), PermissionError(13, "not writable", "/root/.cache/flashinfer"), RuntimeError("CUDA runtime mismatch"), OSError("libcuda.so.1: cannot open shared object file"), AttributeError("api drift"), ]: with patch("vllm.platforms.cuda._get_attn_backend_class", side_effect=exc): try: CudaPlatform.get_valid_backends( device_capability=(9, 0), attn_selector_config=<minimal AttentionSelectorConfig>, num_heads=32, ) print(f"{type(exc).__name__}: recovered") except BaseException as e: print(f"{type(exc).__name__}: PROPAGATED " f"({type(e).__name__}: {e})") On v0.26.0: ImportError recovers; the four others propagate out, killing whatever engine init called into the probe. Fix direction Broaden the catch at both sites to except Exception as e:, log with exc_info=True, and record [f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"] so the existing "No valid attention backend found" error surfaces the root cause per backend instead of the losslessly uninformative literal "ImportError". On the selected-backend path, raise ValueError(...) from e to preserve the exception chain. BaseException (KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit) deliberately not caught. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Bug]: Inkling-Small structured-output request returns 500 ("grammar rejected tokens [200028]")
signals.text: ### Your current environment vLLM recent main, https://huggingface.co/thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small-NVFP4, H100 ### 🐛 Describe the bug A `/v1/chat/completions` request with a JSON-schema `response_format` on `thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small-NVFP4` fails with a 500 Internal Server Error. The engine log shows the grammar rejecting token `200028` right after the JSON payload is complete: ``` (APIServer pid=9419) INFO: 127.0.0.1:37932 - "POST /v1/chat/completions HTTP/1.1" 200 OK (EngineCore pid=10458) ERROR 08-09 09:58:19 [scheduler.py:1841] Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens [200028] for request chatcmpl-8da6fc665494abe1-b5b27872. Terminating request. (APIServer pid=9419) ERROR 08-09 09:58:19 [serving.py:175] Request chatcmpl-8da6fc665494abe1 failed with an internal error during generation (APIServer pid=9419) INFO: 127.0.0.1:37932 - "POST /v1/chat/completions HTTP/1.1" 500 Internal Server Error ``` ### Reproducer: Run the model (4xH100 in my case): ``` VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 \ FLASH_ATTENTION_CUTE_DSL_CACHE_ENABLED=1 \ vllm serve \ --model thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small-NVFP4 \ --trust-remote-code \ --tokenizer-mode inkling \ --kernel-config.enable_flashinfer_autotune=False \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.75 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --tool-call-parser inkling \ --reasoning-parser inkling ``` Send a structured output request: ```bash curl -s http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{ "model": "thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small-NVFP4", "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"Give me a person as JSON."}], "response_format": {"type":"json_schema","json_schema":{"name":"p","schema": {"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string"},"age":{"type":"integer"}}, "required":["name","age"]}}} }' ``` I originally found this via [tool-eval-bench](https://github.com/SeraphimSerapis/tool-eval-bench), and can be reproduced with this command: ``` tool-eval-bench --scenarios TC-65 ```
