signals.title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 intermittently emits malformed DSML tool-call start wrapper on v0.27.1 + DSpark
signals.text: ## Summary With **DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731** on **vLLM v0.27.1** with **DSpark enabled**, we have intermittently observed malformed DSML tool-call output where the opening wrapper is corrupted from: ```text <｜DSML｜tool_calls> ``` to something like: ```text <｜DSML｜toolcalls> ``` while the rest of the DSML block remains structurally close to valid and the closing wrapper is still emitted as: ```text </｜DSML｜tool_calls> ``` This causes the tool-call parser to miss the call and surface the DSML as assistant content instead of producing `tool_calls`. This report intentionally uses a **synthetic example** and does not include the original production prompt, tool names, arguments, paths, or other private information. ## Environment - vLLM: **v0.27.1** - Model: **deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731** - Speculative decoding: **DSpark enabled** - Tool-call parser: DeepSeek V4 / DSML path - Observed intermittently rather than deterministically ## Synthetic example Expected model output: ```text <｜DSML｜tool_calls> <｜DSML｜invoke name="get_weather"> <｜DSML｜parameter name="city" string="true">Seoul</｜DSML｜parameter> </｜DSML｜invoke> </｜DSML｜tool_calls> ``` Malformed output observed in the same class of failure: ```text <｜DSML｜toolcalls> <｜DSML｜invoke name="get_weather"> <｜DSML｜parameter name="city" string="true">Seoul</｜DSML｜parameter> </｜DSML｜invoke> </｜DSML｜tool_calls> ``` The difference is only the opening wrapper (`tool_calls` -> `toolcalls`), but that is enough for strict DSML parsing to fail. ## Expected behavior If the model emits an otherwise complete DSML invoke block for a tool that is actually declared in the request, vLLM should ideally either: 1. recover the tool call safely, or 2. at minimum detect the malformed DSML as a protocol error instead of silently returning the whole block as ordinary assistant content. Any recovery should remain conservative and validate the recovered tool name against the tools declared in the request. ## Relation to existing issues This appears related to #48931 and #49117, but it is a **different malformed-output variant**. - #48931 covers the case where the `<｜DSML｜tool_calls>` opening wrapper is **completely omitted**. - This case has an opening wrapper, but it is **corrupted/misspelled** (`tool_calls` -> `toolcalls`). - Therefore, recovery logic that only handles a fully missing wrapper may not cover this case as-is. It would be useful to add parser regression coverage for malformed opening wrappers in both streaming and non-streaming paths, especially with DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731. ## DSpark note This was observed with DSpark enabled. I do **not** have enough evidence yet to claim that DSpark is the cause. A DSpark ON/OFF comparison would be useful because speculative decoding should not materially change protocol correctness if rejected draft tokens are handled correctly. The main issue here is that a small model-side DSML formatting error currently turns into a complete tool-call failure at the serving layer.

signals.title: [Bug]: draft_model speculative decoding crashes at init under TP>1 when draft hidden_size > target (TRT-LLM fused allreduce+RMSNorm workspace sized from target only)
signals.text: ### Summary With `draft_model` speculative decoding under tensor parallelism (`TP>1`), the engine crashes at init when the **draft model's `hidden_size` is larger than the target model's**. The `fuse_allreduce_rms` compilation pass builds the FlashInfer TRT-LLM fused allreduce+RMSNorm workspace with a token budget derived from the **target** model's `hidden_size` only. When the draft model then runs its own forward under TP, its larger `hidden_size` overflows that workspace and `check_trtllm_allreduce_fusion_workspace_metadata` raises, aborting startup. `draft_hidden < target_hidden` and `TP=1` both work; the crash is specific to **`draft_hidden > target_hidden` AND `TP>1`**. ### Environment - vLLM `v0.27.1`, V1 engine, `dtype=torch.bfloat16` - 2×H100 PCIe (80GB), `tensor_parallel_size=2` - `compilation_config.pass_config.fuse_allreduce_rms: True` (default), FlashInfer allreduce backend - Full raw server logs for all arms (`collect_env` included): https://github.com/seongyun1104/depthchart/tree/39b1557/draft_model_tp_bug ### Reproduction | Arm | target (TP) | draft | draft_hidden vs target_hidden | result | |-----|-------------|-------|-------------------------------|--------| | A | Qwen3-30B-A3B (**TP=1**) | Qwen3-4B | **2560 > 2048** | OK (acceptance 83.8%, normal) | | B | Qwen3-30B-A3B (**TP=2**) | Qwen3-4B | **2560 > 2048** | **CRASH** at init | | C | Qwen3-30B-A3B (TP=2) | Qwen3-0.6B | 1024 < 2048 | OK (acceptance 73.1%, coherent) | Arm A vs B isolates the trigger to **`TP>1`**: same `draft_hidden > target_hidden` pair, only the parallelism differs. Arm C shows the same TP=2 target is fine when `draft_hidden < target_hidden`. Arm B command (greedy): ``` vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B \ --tensor-parallel-size 2 \ --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-seqs 8 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \ --override-generation-config '{"do_sample": false}' \ --speculative-config '{"method": "draft_model", "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-4B", "num_speculative_tokens": 1}' ``` (Qwen3-4B `hidden_size=2560` as draft; Qwen3-30B-A3B `hidden_size=2048` as target.) ### Traceback (arm B, verbatim) ``` File ".../vllm/compilation/passes/fusion/allreduce_rms_fusion.py", line 265, in call_trtllm_fused_allreduce_norm ... check_trtllm_allreduce_fusion_workspace_metadata( File ".../flashinfer/comm/trtllm_ar.py", line 1026, in check_trtllm_allreduce_fusion_workspace_metadata raise ValueError(error_msg) ValueError: Workspace validation failed: - token_num (8192) * hidden_dim (2560) exceeds workspace max_token_num (8192) * hidden_dim (2048). This may cause Illegal Memory Access. ``` `hidden_dim (2560)` is the draft (Qwen3-4B); the workspace budget `hidden_dim (2048)` is the target (Qwen3-30B-A3B). ### Where it comes from The fused-allreduce workspace token budget is `max_token_num = max_size // (hidden_dim * element_size)`, and `hidden_dim` is taken from the target model config in the pass. The draft model's forward under TP issues the same fused allreduce with its own (larger) `hidden_size`, exceeding the target-sized budget. Note (not a proposed fix): patching the pass `__init__` to use `max(target_hidden, draft_hidden)` did **not** resolve it — the run still reports `hidden_dim (2048)` in the validation error, so the workspace metadata that is actually checked is created upstream of that pass field. A correct fix has to reach the workspace **creation** site so its stored `hidden_dim` accounts for the draft model. ### Relationship to #50877 / #50932 Same theme (FlashInfer allreduce workspace/buffer under a draft model that adds allreduce traffic), but a **distinct backend**: - #50877 / PR #50932 — the **MNNVL** path (`trtllm_mnnvl_ar`, Lamport buffer rotation); #50932 touches `flashinfer_all_reduce.py` / `fused_allreduce_gemma_rms_norm.py` and adds an `is_buffer_size_sufficient` admission guard. - This report — the **TRT-LLM fused allreduce+RMSNorm** compilation-pass path (`allreduce_rms_fusion.py` → `flashinfer/comm/trtllm_ar.py`), which #50932 does not touch. Filing separately so the TRT-LLM path is tracked; happy to fold into #50877 if maintainers prefer a single tracking issue.

signals.title: [Bug][ROCm/gfx942]: GLM-5.2-FP8 — first request after GPU idle emits garbage; piecewise CUDA graph cold replay corrupts the request's own prefill (workaround: cudagraph_mode=FULL_DECODE_ONLY)
signals.text: ## Environment - 8× AMD Instinct MI325X (gfx942), ROCm 7.14.0, amdgpu 6.19.14 - Images: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` 2026-08-12 (v0.26.1rc1.dev668+g3ee2df303) **and** 2026-08-13 (`8f515d1d`) — both reproduce - Model: `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8`, TP=8, `--kv-cache-dtype auto`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 4096`, MoE backend AITER blockscale-FP8 (`fmoe_bf16_a16_blockscaleFp8...`) - Reproduces identically at `--max-model-len` 131072 and 1048576 ## 🐛 Describe the bug After the engine sits idle for ≥ ~20–50 s, the **next** request returns garbage from its very first sampled token, e.g. `'!0.1.5,0.1 and1.1.1.0 21.1.'` (token-0/digit noise). Requests sent immediately afterwards are correct. Reproduction probability rises with idle time (~50–100 % at ≥ 50 s idle; back-to-back requests never fail, dozens of samples). Key observations: 1. **The corrupt request never self-heals**: with `max_tokens=300` the output is noise from token 1 through token 300, while a request issued ~0.5 s later is clean — i.e. the corrupt request's *own prefill* wrote garbage into its KV/indexer cache, and every decode step then consumes that poisoned context. 2. `temperature=0`; prompts are ~6–10 tokens (below the 16-token block size, so prefix caching is not involved). 3. No errors in the server log, container healthy, RAS/ECC counters unchanged. 4. Not JIT/autotune related: Triton JIT warnings (`_cp_gather_indexer_quant_cache_kernel`, `_fp8_mqa_logits_kernel`) appear only on the very first request after startup; later corrupt events have no JIT activity. 5. A 25 s-interval keepalive (unique prompts forcing real prefills, all HTTP 200) does **not** reliably prevent it. ## Bisection | config | result | |---|---| | defaults (FULL_AND_PIECEWISE graphs), 131k & 1M, nightly 08-12 & 08-13 | ❌ corrupt | | `--enforce-eager` | ✅ clean 8/8 (startup burst + 60 s idle ×3 + 25 s idle ×2) | | `--compilation-config='{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'` | ✅ clean 8/8 at 1M | → The corruption tracks **piecewise CUDA/HIP graph replay in the prefill path** after a cold window. With prefill graph-free (eager or `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`) the model is fully healthy: fact probes pass, tool calling OK, needle-in-haystack 3/3 at 2k/6k/12k/100k/900k tokens, and a 5-minute cold soak followed by a fresh request is correct. Other models on the same host/stack (Kimi-K3 with eager prefill + FULL decode graphs, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731) do not show this — consistent with the piecewise-prefill-graph attribution: decode-side graphs essentially never replay cold, because the preceding prefill has just warmed the GPU. This smells like a ROCm/HIP graph runtime issue (queue/doorbell state after idle → first graph replay misfires) rather than a model bug, but filing here since the practical impact is "GlmMoeDsa default config silently corrupts on gfx942" and the workaround is a vLLM flag. Related (same class — HIP graph replay silently wrong on AMD — but none match the idle-triggered gfx942 manifestation): - ROCm/hip#3887 — HIP graph replay reads stale device-pointer values (gfx1201/RDNA4, ~200+ nodes) - ROCm/aiter#3632 — W4A4 fused MoE kernel not HIP-graph-safe (gfx950) - pytorch/pytorch#155684 — HIP graph misuse yields silent wrong results where CUDA raises ## Workaround `--compilation-config='{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'` — no measurable decode-speed loss (decode keeps FULL graphs; only prefill runs graph-free). Single-stream decode on this host: 44.5 tok/s (prose) / 61.9 tok/s (code) at 1M `max_model_len`. ## Repro 1. Serve `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8` on 8×gfx942 with the default compilation config. 2. `sleep 60` 3. ```bash curl -s localhost:8000/v1/completions -H 'content-type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"glm","prompt":"The capital of France is","max_tokens":16,"temperature":0}' ``` → garbage (`!0.1...`). Repeat immediately → ` Paris.` (correct). Vary the prompt each round to rule out prefix-cache effects; alternate idle/burst to see the pattern.

signals.title: [Bug]: DeepSeek-V4 NIXL failure returns corrupted reasoning with empty content
signals.text: ### Your current environment Both roles used the same base image and source overlay. The role-specific model runner and speculative settings were: ```text Base image: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.27.0-cu129-ubuntu2404 Runtime vLLM: 0.26.1rc1.dev657+g793ca6998 Source commit: 793ca6998adfa5a3ab22d6012dee78044b8ba901 Model: DeepSeek-V4 Topology: disaggregated Prefill/Decode Tensor parallelism: TP=8 on Prefill and Decode KV connector: NixlConnector with HMA Prefill model runner: V1 Prefill speculative decoding: disabled Decode model runner: V2 Decode speculative decoding: DSpark, num_speculative_tokens=7 Reasoning parser: deepseek_v4 KV load failure policy: fail ``` ### 🐛 Describe the bug After a failed NIXL/HMA receive, DeepSeek-V4 can return HTTP 200 with corrupted tokens in `reasoning` and an empty `content` field. Clients that read only `choices[].message.content` see an apparently empty response. Disabling thinking exposes the corrupted output in `content` instead. #### Reproduction Use disaggregated serving with DSpark disabled on Prefill and enabled on Decode. Prefill arguments: ```sh --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \ --kv-transfer-config \ '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_load_failure_policy":"fail"}' ``` Decode arguments: ```sh --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \ --speculative-config \ '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"greedy"}' \ --kv-transfer-config \ '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer","kv_load_failure_policy":"fail"}' ``` Send chat-completion requests with `max_tokens=128` using: 1. the default request; 2. thinking explicitly enabled; 3. thinking explicitly disabled; and 4. reasoning parsing disabled. On [`793ca6998`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/793ca6998), the asymmetric configuration fails the NIXL compatibility handshake. No KV transfer completes successfully, but the requests resume decoding. #### Expected behavior With `kv_load_failure_policy="fail"`, a failed NIXL compatibility handshake or KV receive should terminate the request with an error. The API must not return HTTP 200 or expose generated tokens in either `content` or `reasoning`. #### Actual behavior A four-mode matrix ran eight requests per mode: | Request mode | HTTP 200 with 128 tokens | `content` | `reasoning` | |---|---:|---|---| | default | 8/8 | empty | corrupted output | | thinking enabled | 8/8 | empty | corrupted output | | thinking disabled | 8/8 | corrupted output | empty | | reasoning parsing disabled | 8/8 | corrupted output | empty | All 32 requests generated 128 tokens. The apparent empty output in the first two modes is therefore response-field routing, not an absence of generation. #### Cause The failed HMA receive is reported as receive completion without a request-level failure reaching the scheduler, so Decode resumes with missing KV data and generates corrupted tokens. When thinking is enabled, the DeepSeek-V4 responses contain corrupted tokens in `reasoning` while `content` is empty. This is consistent with response parsing treating the generated text as reasoning, but the exact parser mechanism has not been isolated. The field split changes how the KV corruption is exposed; it does not show that parsing caused the KV failure. The fix proposed in [PR #52232](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52232) is model-agnostic and is expected to prevent this DeepSeek-V4/DSpark failure by terminating the request before output parsing. #### Related work - [Issue #52234](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52234) reports the underlying NIXL/HMA receive failure returning HTTP 200 with corrupted tokens. - [PR #52232](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52232) proposes model-agnostic request-level failure propagation. Although its serving regression uses Gemma, the fix is expected to cover this DeepSeek-V4/DSpark case as well. - [PR #49230](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49230) validates NIXL speculative configuration compatibility and provides the deterministic handshake-failure trigger used by this reproduction. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Bug]: Qwen3.6-27B (dense Gated-DeltaNet) permanently hard-wedges the V1 engine — two reproducible modes (2 large images; long multi-turn text), possibly related
signals.text:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (x86_64), glibc 2.35 Python: 3.12.13 | platform Linux-6.17.0-1026-nvidia-x86_64 PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130 (CUDA build 13.0) vLLM Version: 0.23.0 CUDA available: True | CUDA runtime 13.0.88 | driver 595.71.05 GPU: 8× NVIDIA B200 [pip3] flashinfer-python==0.6.12 [pip3] transformers==5.12.0 [pip3] triton==3.6.0 env: VLLM_USAGE_SOURCE=production-docker-image, VLLM_ENABLE_CUDA_COMPATIBILITY=0, TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=7.5 8.0 8.6 8.9 9.0 10.0 12.0+PTX ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Summary vLLM **0.23.0**, **Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B** (dense FullAttn + Gated-DeltaNet), single GPU TP=1, `--attention-config TRITON_ATTN`, `--max-model-len 262144`, `--enable-prefix-caching`, `mamba_cache_mode=align`. The engine **permanently hard-wedges** (generation stops, `/health` still 200, only restart recovers) in two reproducible cases: - **Mode A** — a request with **two large images** → **fixed** by raising `--max-num-batched-tokens` 8192→32768. - **Mode B** — concurrent **long multi-turn (~180k-token) prefills** → **not** fixed by `--max-num-batched-tokens`. Reported together because both wedge the same GDN model and **we can't tell if it's one bug or two** (stacks and fix-behavior differ). Related to #40707 / #47738 (both env 0.18–0.23). ## Mode A — 2 large images (scheduler-admission wedge) Each request has **two distinct 3024×4032 images** (11,844 vision tokens each). At `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192` it wedges on the first batch: `running=1, waiting=11`, gen frozen, KV≈0.9%. py-spy MainThread is **idle in the scheduler** (`_process_engine_step`), admitting none. Single-variable bisection: **8192 → WEDGE, 32768 → CLEAN** (65 completed); `--max-num-seqs` 64/384 and `--mm-processor-cache-gb` 256/0 make no difference (still WEDGE). > **Our workaround (works for us):** setting **`--max-num-batched-tokens 32768`** eliminates Mode A entirely — the multimodal load that reliably wedged at 8192 runs clean at 32768. We are running with this as our interim fix. (It does NOT help Mode B.) Mechanism (arithmetic exact; causation inferred): `encoder_cache_size = max(max_num_batched_tokens, max_tokens_per_mm_item=16384)`. At 8192 → 16384 holds one 11,844-token image but not two (23,688); at 32768 → holds two. Matches #40707's precondition (item 1 pinned, item 2 can't load, gap < block_size 16 → `_mamba_block_aligned_split` truncates to 0 → request skipped). Consistent with #40707, though no mamba frame appears in the stack. ## Mode B — long multi-turn text ~180k-token prefill (GDN-forward wedge) Each request is one distinct ~180k-token multi-turn conversation, no images. Wedges after ~4 completions at **both** batched 8192 and 32768: `running=1–2, waiting=10–11`, gen+prompt frozen, KV≈0.1%, ≥5 requests hit the 1200 s timeout. py-spy MainThread is **active inside the model forward** — batched-32768 run unambiguously in the GDN kernel `qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py:1532 chunk_gated_delta_rule → qwen3_5.forward → cuda_graph → execute_model`; batched-8192 run in a compiled Triton launch of the same forward. Not the scheduler. Trigger: a large **one-shot prefill** hitting the GDN chunked-prefill path — in production this is the full re-prefill after the prefix cache for a long conversation is evicted; the synthetic reproduces that single long prefill directly. (Caveat: the two dumps 3 s apart hit different compiled submodules, so the forward is grinding but never returns within 1200 s — a genuine client-side wedge, but these dumps can't fully separate an infinite hang from a pathologically-slow non-returning forward.) ## Same bug? Unknown. Both involve the GDN/mamba hybrid path, so a shared cause is plausible, but the evidence differs: Mode A = idle in scheduler, fixed by `--max-num-batched-tokens`; Mode B = active in the GDN forward, not fixed. Flagging both for maintainers who know the GDN internals; not asserting either way. ## Relation - **#40707** (OPEN) — matches Mode A; here on dense 27B / TP=1. Fix **#40709 unmerged** (not in any release through v0.27.1). - **#47738** (CLOSED, Qwen3.6-27B two images) — referenced fix **#47771 closed unmerged**. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [RFC]: First-class agentic inference support in vLLM
signals.text: # RFC: First-class agentic inference support in vLLM ## Motivation The [vLLM Agentic API project](https://github.com/vllm-project/agentic-api) has completed an MVP supporting Codex and Claude Code with vLLM as the inference engine. It is a high-performance Rust runtime for the capabilities these clients need beyond token generation: stateful continuation, tool loops, web search, MCP, streaming, and Responses/Messages compatibility. Agentic workloads are increasingly important to llm-d and the broader serving community. The question is how vLLM and Agentic API should evolve together as these workloads become more stateful and operationally complex. Emerging capabilities such as [Computer History](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/customization/computer-history) show how agentic systems are beginning to use persistent activity, search, and external context to resume work and understand what happened across tools. vLLM already supports Responses and Messages APIs, an optional in-process Responses store, and MCP/tool-server integrations. Agentic API builds on that foundation with a broader runtime for stateful continuation, tool loops, web search, vendor-neutral integrations, and the operational needs of agentic inference workloads. These capabilities are complementary, but vLLM does not currently plan to pursue the full Agentic API scope in its existing serving surface. How should vLLM and Agentic API evolve together to support this next generation of agentic inference workloads? ## Proposed change We propose that vLLM make agentic inference a first-class supported capability by integrating more tightly with Agentic API. The project’s MVP provides a working starting point for stateful Responses and Messages APIs, tool orchestration, and vendor-neutral integrations. The options below describe different ways to bring those capabilities into the vLLM ecosystem; this RFC seeks agreement on the desired integration model and the boundaries that should remain stable. ### Goal Agentic API aims to provide a vendor-neutral integration layer connecting agentic clients to databases, third-party APIs, and external tools while preserving and optimizing vLLM’s inference capabilities. It should also provide llm-d with practical Responses API and Messages API solutions that externalize conversation state and orchestration without forcing hard affinity to the engine that served an earlier turn. ### Scope and boundary The boundary is intentional: vLLM Core focuses on model execution, scheduling, batching, tokenization, rendering, parsing, and structured decoding; Agentic API focuses on state, external integrations, tool orchestration, and client compatibility. The goal is to make these capabilities more tightly integrated and accessible through the vLLM ecosystem. ### Desired outcome The goal is for the vLLM ecosystem to expose a first-class agentic inference experience by building on vLLM’s existing Responses, Messages, response-store, and MCP/tool-server support and integrating the broader capabilities provided by Agentic API. This RFC seeks alignment on how Agentic API and vLLM should become more tightly integrated to reach that goal. ## Options These options are not mutually exclusive. A first-class boundary could be the near-term step before deciding whether to merge or formally package Agentic API with vLLM. | Option | Description | Proposed change | Main tradeoff | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **1. Merge** | Move Agentic API into vLLM Core. | Merge the code, consolidate APIs and tests, and document the agentic serving experience in vLLM. | One project and release process, but vLLM takes on persistence, integrations, and workflow orchestration. | | **2. Remain separate** | Continue with today’s architecture and independent evolution. | Improve documentation, publish a dedicated Agentic API website or landing page, and clearly document how it integrates with vLLM. | Clear boundaries, but leaves the broader agentic workload experience outside vLLM’s existing serving surface and risks capability gaps and compatibility drift. | | **3. Official dependency** | Keep a separate repository, but officially distribute or depend on Agentic API for Responses and agentic inference. | Add supported packaging and version compatibility, vLLM documentation and examples, and a maintained integration path. | Better integration, but tighter versioning and packaging coupling. | | **4. First-class runtime boundary** | Keep the repositories separate while defining supported interfaces, compatibility guarantees, and shared tests. | Establish shared contracts, conformance tests, release coordination, and cross-linked documentation or landing pages. | Preserves flexibility, but requires sustained coordination. | ## Key questions 1. How should vLLM extend its existing Responses, Messages, response-store, and MCP/tool-server support to provide a broader agentic inference experience? 2. What should agentic applications, including coding harnesses, be able to rely on from the vLLM ecosystem? 3. Which responsibilities should remain separate even if the projects are distributed together? 4. What interfaces and tests should vLLM, Agentic API, and llm-d share? ## Additional context - [vLLM Responses API and Tool Calling lookahead (#34857)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/34857) - [vLLM session-centric KV-cache orchestration (#48501)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48501) - [vLLM Agentic API Codex CLI integration (#54)](https://github.com/vllm-project/agentic-api/issues/54) - [vLLM Agentic API response-store semantics (#14)](https://github.com/vllm-project/agentic-api/issues/14) - [vLLM multi-turn Responses API support (#33089)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/33089) - [vLLM Rust frontend / Anthropic Messages RFC (#47753)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47753) - [llm-d-router session-centric KV lifecycle orchestration (#1979)](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-router/issues/1979) - [llm-d-router external Responses state store (#1104)](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-router/issues/1104) - [llm-d-router Session Control Protocol (#2003)](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-router/issues/2003) - [llm-d-router agentic routing profiles (#1867)](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-router/issues/1867) ## Recommended direction The long-term goal should be for vLLM to provide a first-class agentic serving experience that builds on its existing Responses, Messages, response-store, and MCP/tool-server support and adds the orchestration and integrations needed by real agentic workloads. The immediate goal is tighter integration between Agentic API and vLLM Core so that vLLM’s support for agentic workloads is visible and accessible throughout the ecosystem. The options above provide several paths to that outcome, from merging the projects to establishing an officially supported dependency or first-class integration contract. ## CC list @qandrew @vMaroon @blasrodri @BugenZhao @njhill @chaunceyjiang @mgoin @bbrowning @robertgshaw2-redhat @noobHappylife @maralbahari @tjtanaa @ashwing

signals.title: [Bug]: Marlin MoE support probe raises TypeError instead of returning a verdict for unset group_size
signals.text: ### Describe the bug `compressed-tensors` leaves `group_size` unset (`None`) for channel-strategy weights. `CompressedTensorsWNA16MoEMethod` stores it raw (`compressed_tensors_moe_wna16.py:73`), and three sites then compare it against an `int`: | site | comparison | |---|---| | `oracle/int_wna16.py:163` → `marlin_utils.py:378` | `group_size <= 0` | | `oracle/int_wna16.py:1512` (weight prep re-reads `weight_quant.group_size`) → `marlin_utils.py:344` | `group_size > 0` | | `compressed_tensors_moe_wna16.py:73` | feeds both of the above | ``` TypeError: '<=' not supported between instances of 'NoneType' and 'int' ``` The first raise is inside `_backend_incompatibility_reason`, whose contract is to **return** a reason string. Backend selection therefore aborts with a traceback instead of rejecting Marlin and trying the next candidate. Regression from #44570 (`454ea5b526`), which moved the probe into the oracle and dropped the `group_size = weight_quant.group_size or -1` that `get_moe_method` used to apply. Seven other sites in the `compressed_tensors` package normalise this field (e.g. `schemes/compressed_tensors_wNa16.py:67`). ### Affected checkpoints Configs fetched 2026-08-20, both int4 `pack-quantized`, `strategy: channel`, `group_size: null`, experts quantized: - [RedHatAI/Mixtral-8x22B-v0.1-quantized.w4a16](https://huggingface.co/RedHatAI/Mixtral-8x22B-v0.1-quantized.w4a16) — hidden 6144, intermediate 16384 - [lokeshe09/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-INT4-W4A16-channelwise](https://huggingface.co/lokeshe09/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-INT4-W4A16-channelwise) — hidden 2816, moe_intermediate 704, 128 experts Both satisfy Marlin's shape checks once `group_size` is `-1`, so this is a load failure, not a nicer error. ### Reproducer ```python from compressed_tensors.quantization import QuantizationArgs, QuantizationStrategy, QuantizationType from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.marlin_utils import check_moe_marlin_supports_config from tests.kernels.moe.utils import make_dummy_moe_config args = QuantizationArgs(num_bits=4, type=QuantizationType.INT, strategy=QuantizationStrategy.CHANNEL, symmetric=True, dynamic=False) assert args.group_size is None check_moe_marlin_supports_config( make_dummy_moe_config(num_experts=8, hidden_dim=4096, intermediate_size=1024), args.group_size, allow_tile_padding=True) ``` `hidden_dim` must be a multiple of 128 — the default `hidden_dim=1` fails the shape check before `group_size` is read. ### Platforms Reachable on CUDA through the `auto` priority list, and **on XPU** through `--moe-backend marlin`: `select_wna16_moe_backend` handles an explicit backend at `int_wna16.py:258-274` without consulting `_get_priority_backends()`, and `MoEBackend` (`config/kernel.py`) has no platform gate on `"marlin"`. So the `intel-gpu` label does fit. On ROCm `check_moe_marlin_supports_config` returns `False` at `marlin_utils.py:368` before any comparison. Fix: #53163. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] I have searched for similar issues. - [x] I have already asked the chatbot for help.

signals.title: [Bug]: CompressedTensorsWNA16MoEMethod rejects grouped int8 MoE checkpoints (regression)
signals.text:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text Collecting environment information... ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0 Clang version : Could not collect CMake version : version 4.4.2 Libc version : glibc-2.39 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.13.0+xpu Is debug build : False CUDA used to build PyTorch : None ROCM used to build PyTorch : N/A XPU used to build PyTorch : 20260000 ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.12.3 (main, Jun 19 2026, 12:46:00) [GCC 13.3.0] (64-bit runtime) Python platform : Linux-7.0.0-28-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.39 ============================== Intel XPU / GPU Info ============================== Is XPU available : True XPU runtime version : 20260000 Intel GPU models : GPU 0: Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B70 Graphics --Compile time-- oneAPI compiler version : Could not collect SYCL compiler build : Could not collect oneCCL version : 2022.0.0 --Runtime-- Intel Graphics Compiler (IGC): 2.34.4 Intel GMM (libigdgmm) : 22.10.0 ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug `CompressedTensorsWNA16MoEMethod.__init__` asserts per-channel for 8-bit weights (`vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors_moe/compressed_tensors_moe_wna16.py:85`): ```python elif self.num_bits == 8: assert self.group_size == -1 ``` This rejects grouped int8 MoE checkpoints, which is what `llm-compressor`'s `W8A16` preset emits by default: ```python >>> from compressed_tensors.quantization.quant_scheme import PRESET_SCHEMES >>> PRESET_SCHEMES["W8A16"]["weights"] QuantizationArgs(num_bits=8, type='int', symmetric=True, group_size=128, strategy='group', ...) ``` For `strategy="channel"` the field is `None`, and `None == -1` is `False`, so the assert fires for grouped **and** channel int8 alike. The assert also sits before `select_wna16_moe_backend` at `:100`, so no backend — including Marlin — is reached. **This is a regression.** [#47154](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47154) (`c8d2f3cb14`, 2026-06-30) removed exactly this assert from `CompressedTensorsWNA16MarlinMoEMethod`, titled "allow int8 grouped WNA16 MoE on Marlin". [#44570](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44570) (`454ea5b526`, 2026-07-31) then merged that class into `CompressedTensorsWNA16MoEMethod` and re-added the assert. `c8d2f3cb14` is an ancestor of `454ea5b526`, so the earlier decision was undone by consolidation rather than reversed deliberately. Affected checkpoint, config read from the Hub: [`88plug/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-W8A16`](https://huggingface.co/88plug/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-W8A16) — `num_bits=8, strategy=group, group_size=128`, `input_activations=None`, and `targets` includes `re:.*mlp\.experts\.(gate_up_proj|down_proj)$`, so the experts themselves are quantized. compressed-tensors is auto-detected, so this hits the assert on load with no opt-in flag. `MoeWNA16Method` has the same assert at `moe_wna16.py:225` and is filed separately, since it needs an additional allocation fix. I have a patch and will open it against this issue. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] I have searched for similar issues. - [x] I have already asked the chatbot for help.

signals.title: [Bug]: GPTQ MoE with `group_size: -1` crashes in `MoeWNA16Method.create_weights` (reached via the ROCm Marlin fallback)
signals.text: > Rewritten 2026-08-20. The first version of this report was wrong on every specific; see the edit history. **Found by inspection, not reproduced** — I have no ROCm hardware. ### Describe the bug Any GPTQ MoE checkpoint with `group_size: -1` crashes in `MoeWNA16Method.create_weights`, for `bits: 4` and `bits: 8` alike. The normalisation loop at `moe_wna16.py:259` is a no-op, because `x % -1 == 0` for every `x`: ```python while intermediate_size_per_partition % group_size or hidden_size % group_size: ``` `group_size` stays `-1` and reaches the scale allocations at `moe_wna16.py:304` and `:316` (`:331`, `:343` for `qzeros`): ```python >>> 4096 // -1 -4096 >>> torch.zeros(8, 512, 4096 // -1, dtype=torch.bfloat16) RuntimeError: zeros: Dimension size must be non-negative. ``` ### How it is reached — not via `--quantization moe_wna16` The explicit flag is refused: `is_moe_wna16_compatible` (`moe_wna16.py:162`) requires `quant_method == "gptq" and not desc_act`, and the `-1g` GPTQ MoE checkpoints I found all have `desc_act: true`, so `override_quantization_method` returns `None` and `vllm/config/model.py:1318` raises "does not match" first. (I checked the repos below, not the whole Hub.) The live route takes no flag, at `auto_gptq.py:246-256`: if `check_moe_marlin_supports_layer` fails, it falls back to `MoeWNA16Config.get_quant_method`. That branch checks neither `desc_act` nor `group_size`, and `check_moe_marlin_supports_config` returns `False` unconditionally on ROCm (`marlin_utils.py:368`) — so on ROCm **every** GPTQ MoE layer takes it. `MoeWNA16Method.__init__` then succeeds (`kInt4Static` is in the `SUPPORTED_W` list inside `TritonWNA16Experts._supports_quant_scheme`, `triton_moe.py:583-591`; `_supports_current_device` is `is_cuda_alike() or is_xpu()`, `:571-572`) and `create_weights` crashes. On CUDA the fallback is not taken for these shapes: 4096 % 128 == 0 and 14336/tp % 64 == 0 at every TP, so Marlin accepts. ### Affected checkpoints - [TheBloke/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-GPTQ](https://huggingface.co/TheBloke/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-GPTQ), default `main` revision: `bits: 4, group_size: -1, desc_act: true`; `hidden_size` 4096, `intermediate_size` 14336, 8 experts. Its `gptq-8bit--1g-actorder_True` branch is `bits: 8, group_size: -1`. - Eight sibling `-1g` Mixtral GPTQ repos with the same config shape. ### Not reproduced Unreachable on the hardware I have: on XPU int8 is rejected by `XPUExpertsWNA16._supports_quant_scheme` before `create_weights`, and int4 `-1g` keeps the Marlin path because `marlin_utils.py:368` is ROCm-only. Someone with an MI300-class card and any of the above checkpoints should hit it with default flags. I can prepare a patch if a ROCm maintainer confirms the route. Related but not precedent: #34118 shows ROCm GPTQ MoE reaching `moe_wna16` with default flags, but it is a closed `[Feature]` request about non-SiLU activations, with a traceback in `apply()`, not `create_weights`. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] I have searched for similar issues. - [x] I have already asked the chatbot for help.

signals.title: [Bug] DeepseekV4 cannot start on sm_121 (GB10): unguarded DeepGEMM call, and CutlassScaledMM.is_supported() ignores compute capability
signals.text: ### Your current environment - vLLM `0.26.1rc1.dev608+g99a10304d` (container image, aarch64) - 2× NVIDIA GB10 (**sm_121**, 121 GiB unified memory each), CUDA 13.0, driver 580.173.02 - Two-node TP=2 via the built-in multi-node `mp` executor (`--nnodes 2 --node-rank {0,1} --master-addr … --distributed-executor-backend mp`, rank 1 `--headless`) - Model: `MJPansa/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-NVFP4` (mixed precision: routed experts NVFP4, attention / shared experts / head not quantized) - `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0` and `VLLM_MOE_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0` are set Other models start and serve fine on the same two-node setup with the same image (Qwen3-235B-A22B-NVFP4, Mistral-Small-4-119B, Qwen3.8-27B-FP8), so the cluster wiring itself is good. ### 🐛 Describe the bug DeepseekV4 cannot start on sm_121. There are two separate architecture gates that report "supported" and then fail inside compiled kernels. **1. `mhc_pre_broadcast_tilelang` calls DeepGEMM unconditionally** `vllm/model_executor/kernels/mhc/tilelang.py` has three call sites for `tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm`. Two of them are guarded: ```python use_deep_gemm = is_deep_gemm_supported() ... if use_deep_gemm: tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm(...) else: _tilelang_hc_prenorm_gemm(...) ``` The third one, inside `mhc_pre_broadcast_tilelang` (the first-layer 2-D input path taken from `models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/model.py`), is not: ```python from vllm.utils.deep_gemm import tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm( residual_flat, fn_broadcast, gemm_out_mul, gemm_out_sqrsum, n_splits, ) ``` On sm_121 this aborts during `determine_available_memory`: ``` RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'Assertion error (/workspace/.deps/deepgemm-src/csrc/apis/hyperconnection.hpp:56): Unsupported architecture' ``` The shipped DeepGEMM extension only contains kernels for two architectures: ``` $ strings vllm/third_party/deep_gemm/_C.cpython-312-aarch64-linux-gnu.so | grep -oE 'sm[0-9]{2,3}' | sort -u sm100 sm90 ``` Note this happens **even with `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0`**. That env var does work — `is_deep_gemm_supported()` returns `False` with it set and `True` without it — but this call site never consults it. A fix that works: guard the call and fall back to `_torch_hc_prenorm_gemm`, which already exists in the same file and implements exactly this contract (`out[0] = x.float() @ fn.t()`, `sqrsum[0] = x.float().square().sum(-1)`); the broadcast shapes line up as-is. It requires a single split, so `n_splits` has to be forced to 1 on the fallback path before the output tensors are allocated. With that patch the model loads all 48 shards and gets past this point. **2. `CutlassScaledMM.is_supported()` ignores compute capability** Past the first issue, DeepseekV4's attention input projections fail: ``` File "vllm/models/deepseek_v4/attention.py", line 493, in _run_parallel_input_projections File "vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/fp8.py", line 461, in apply File "vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/scaled_mm/BlockScaledMMLinearKernel.py", line 132, in apply_weights File "vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/scaled_mm/cutlass.py", line 320, in apply_block_scaled_mm RuntimeError: dispatch_scaled_mm, /workspace/csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/w8a8/cutlass/c3x/scaled_mm_helper.hpp:17 ``` The selection gate in `kernels/linear/scaled_mm/cutlass.py` is: ```python @classmethod def is_supported(cls, compute_capability: int | None = None) -> tuple[bool, str | None]: if not current_platform.is_cuda(): return False, "requires CUDA." return True, None ``` `compute_capability` is accepted and never used, so the CUTLASS c3x kernel is selected on any CUDA device and then rejects sm_121 in the C++ dispatcher. A Triton implementation exists in the same directory, but `use_triton` on `BlockScaledMMLinearKernel` only affects the input-quantisation step, not the matmul, and there is no env var to override the backend choice. ### Suggested fix Both gates should consult compute capability rather than assuming Hopper/datacenter-Blackwell: - `CutlassScaledMM.is_supported()` should return `False` on architectures without the compiled c3x kernels so selection can fall through to the Triton kernel. - `is_deep_gemm_supported()` should reflect the architectures actually compiled into the extension (currently sm90/sm100), not just the env var — otherwise every DeepGEMM call site needs to be individually correct. - `mhc_pre_broadcast_tilelang` should be guarded like its two siblings regardless. Happy to open a PR for the `mhc_pre_broadcast_tilelang` guard if that shape of fix is acceptable.
signals.author: ivanusto

signals.title: [Bug]: GLM-5.2 MTP accepts 0% of drafts on MI355X (gfx950); disabling expert parallelism hits hipErrorIllegalAddress
signals.text: ### Your current environment `collect_env.py` output isn't available (the nodes were tied up); details taken from the container image and run logs: ``` vLLM : 0.27.1+rocm723 PyTorch : 2.11.0+gitd0c8b1f ROCm : 7.2.3 Container : vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.27.1 GPU : 8x AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950) amdgpu : 6.16.13, kernel 6.8.0-137-generic Model : amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 (quark MXFP4) MoE backend: aiter ``` ### 🐛 Describe the bug GLM-5.2 MTP starts fine on MI355X and then accepts **zero** draft tokens. Speculative decoding is pure overhead — it drafts at ~40-230 tok/s and accepts none of it. ```bash export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 vllm serve /models/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 \ --served-model-name amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 \ --trust-remote-code \ --async-scheduling \ --distributed-executor-backend mp \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --enable-expert-parallel \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.80 \ --max-model-len 262144 \ --max-num-seqs 2 \ --moe-backend aiter \ --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \ --tool-call-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \ --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' ``` Startup resolves as expected — target `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`, draft `DeepSeekMTPModel` — then: ``` SpecDecoding metrics: Mean acceptance length: 1.00, Accepted throughput: 0.00 tokens/s, Drafted throughput: 37.80 tokens/s, Accepted: 0 tokens, Drafted: 378 tokens, Per-position acceptance rate: 0.000, 0.000, 0.000, Avg Draft acceptance rate: 0.0% ``` What I tried: | # | change | result | |---|---|---| | A | as above | `acceptance length 1.00`, per-position `0.000, 0.000, 0.000` | | B | `num_speculative_tokens: 1` | `acceptance length 1.00`, per-position `0.000` | | C | `--kv-cache-dtype auto` | `acceptance length 1.05`, per-position `0.046, 0.000, 0.000` | | D | drop `--enable-expert-parallel` | crashes, see below | B rules out the startup warning's explanation: ``` WARNING [speculative.py:912] Enabling num_speculative_tokens > 1 will run multiple times on same MTP layer, which may result in lower acceptance rate ``` Position 0 is 0.000 at `num_speculative_tokens=1` too, so re-running GLM-5.2's single nextn layer isn't what's breaking this — the very first draft token is never accepted. C says fp8 KV contributes but isn't the cause: bf16 KV lifts position 0 from 0.000 to ~0.05, still far from usable. D, without expert parallelism, dies during memory profiling instead: ``` terminate called after throwing an instance of 'c10::AcceleratorError' Search for `hipErrorIllegalAddress' in https://rocm.docs.amd.com/projects/HIP/en/latest/index.html Exception raised from ~CUDAGraph at /app/pytorch/aten/src/ATen/hip/HIPGraph.cpp:302 ``` I also checked whether the unquantized nextn layer is being mis-handled by the quark loader — it isn't, as far as I can tell. Layer 78 is genuinely unquantized in this checkpoint (789 `.weight`, 0 `.weight_scale`, 781 entries in `quantization_config.exclude`), but `DeepSeekMTPModel` sets `mtp_start_layer_idx = num_hidden_layers` and names it `model.layers.78`, which is what the exclude patterns match on. So the exclusions should apply. For reference, SGLang on the same node with the same checkpoint gets a working draft: ``` Decode batch, #running-req: 1, ..., accept len: 3.00, accept rate: 0.67, cuda graph: True ``` This may be the same root cause as #48568 (MI300X / gfx942), which points at MTP's `mtp_block` reduce-scattering under `--enable-expert-parallel` with TP>1 while the predictor layer doesn't restore full tokens. Filing separately because the symptom here is different in a way that matters: on gfx950 there's no hang and no error — it silently produces a 0% acceptance rate, so a benchmark run looks healthy and just reports worse numbers. Disabling EP also fails differently (illegal address rather than working around it). Happy to run further diagnostics on gfx950 if that helps. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] I have searched for similar issues and read the [documentation](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/).
signals.author: tianxiaojiang4

signals.title: [Bug]: EngineCore fails to start with ValueError("value too large") when one processed multi-modal item exceeds mm_processor_cache_gb
signals.text: ## Your current environment <details> <summary>Environment</summary> ``` OS : Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS (x86_64) Python : 3.12.3 PyTorch : 2.13.0+cu130 CUDA runtime : 13.0.88 Nvidia driver : 580.126.20 GPU : NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (96 GB) vLLM : 0.27.2rc1.dev193+gaa9903490 (nightly image for aa9903490) ``` Code paths are unchanged on current main (verified at 7ddb50788). </details> ## 🐛 Describe the bug `cachetools.Cache.__setitem__` raises `ValueError("value too large")` when a single item is bigger than the cache's entire `maxsize`. The multi-modal processor caches (`vllm/multimodal/cache.py`) insert processed items without guarding against this, so any configuration where one processed multi-modal item exceeds `mm_processor_cache_gb` turns into a hard failure instead of an uncached item. The worst case is memory profiling: the profiling dummy is by construction the maximum-size item, so if the model's max item is larger than the cache, the engine cannot even boot. Hit in practice with the Qwen3.8 model card's "Long Video Understanding" recipe (video pixel budget 469,762,048, a processed max-size video item is several GiB) and the default `mm_processor_cache_gb=4`: ``` (EngineCore pid=520) ERROR [core.py:1346] EngineCore failed to start. ... File ".../vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py", line 1650, in _cached_apply_hf_processor File ".../vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py", line 1531, in _merge_mm_kwargs File ".../vllm/multimodal/cache.py", line 392, in get_and_update_item File ".../cachetools/__init__.py", line 299, in __setitem__ File ".../cachetools/__init__.py", line 81, in __setitem__ raise ValueError("value too large") ValueError: value too large ``` Raising `--mm-processor-cache-gb` (e.g. to 24) works around it, but the error gives no hint that the cache size is the problem, and an item bigger than the whole cache can never be a cache hit in the first place — evicting the entire cache to fail the insert is lose/lose. Expected behavior: items larger than the cache capacity are served uncached (with a warning suggesting `mm_processor_cache_gb`), and the engine boots. Reproduction sketch (any oversized item does it; no GPU needed to see the raise itself): ```python import torch from vllm.multimodal.cache import MultiModalCache cache = MultiModalCache.get_lru_cache(0.000001, object) # ~1 KiB cache["big"] = torch.zeros(4096, dtype=torch.uint8) # 4 KiB # ValueError: value too large ``` End to end: serve `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8` with the model card's long-video `video_preprocessor_config.json` (`size.longest_edge: 469762048`) and default `mm_processor_cache_gb`; boot dies with the traceback above. I have a working fix that routes the three insert sites through a size guard (deterministic by item size, so the P0 metadata shadow and P1 receiver caches stay coherent — oversized items are simply always resent with data): https://github.com/dkrisman/vllm/commits/fix/mm-cache-skip-oversized Happy to open it as a PR.
signals.author: dkrisman

signals.title: [Bug] Streaming completions end with no finish_reason / no [DONE] — xgrammar "Failed to advance FSM" is one logged trigger, but some drops are fully silent (no engine error)
signals.text: ### Summary While serving a Qwen 3.8 27B NVFP4 checkpoint with `--enable-auto-tool-choice` (xgrammar FSM backend for tool-call constrained decoding), the engine logs a `Failed to advance FSM` ERROR for some requests, and the HTTP SSE stream for those requests terminates **without a final `finish_reason` chunk and without the `data: [DONE]` sentinel**. Downstream clients (e.g. an OpenAI-compatible SDK consumer) receive only partial content and cannot distinguish a normal completion from a truncated one. Importantly, the "no `finish_reason` / no `[DONE]`" symptom is **broader than the logged FSM error**: on the same instance we also observed client-visible mid-stream drops where the engine logs **nothing** — no `Failed to advance FSM`, no ERROR, no disconnect, no abort — while the engine is healthy and actively serving. The API-server layer logs no error, warning, or client-disconnect event for the affected request in either case. So the missing terminal chunk is the real user-facing bug; the FSM failure is one observed (logged) trigger, and a clean-engine occurrence suggests the failure path can be silent. Per the FSM error message itself ("Please file an issue"), filing here. ### Environment - vLLM: `0.26.1rc1.dev298+g1ea84d74b.d20260803` (pip inside container) - Image: `eugr/spark-vllm:latest` (sha256:1d335d4fb3d1c5dce6e79f87a4019a04e98fa9ceb7b894d50d413159382ab6c6) - Hardware: NVIDIA GB10 (Grace Blackwell, sm_121a), CUDA 13.x (eugr image) - Model: Qwen 3.8 27B NVFP4, `served-model-name qwen3.8-27b` - Single node, TP=1 ### Launch command ``` vllm serve /model \ --served-model-name qwen3.8-27b \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \ --trust-remote-code \ --tensor-parallel-size 1 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.45 \ --max-model-len 262144 \ --max-num-seqs 4 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}' ``` ### Observed engine logs (timestamps UTC) ``` (EngineCore pid=304) ERROR 08-18 23:06:09 [backend_xgrammar.py:162] Failed to advance FSM for request chatcmpl-ab4973be9a4cd69e-86178720 for tokens 271. Please file an issue. (EngineCore pid=304) ERROR 08-18 23:10:38 [backend_xgrammar.py:162] Failed to advance FSM for request chatcmpl-803065810e03ac9d-8173c9f7 for tokens 271. Please file an issue. ``` Additional distinct requests with the same error signature were observed within a 48 h window on the same instance (request IDs available on request): 2 further occurrences, all at token 271 or nearby. Note: both FSM failures reported "for tokens 271" — the FSM advance failure appears reproducible at a specific token position, which may indicate a particular token id / grammar state combination. ### Symptoms 1. Client receives a partial stream of content deltas, then the connection ends cleanly (no HTTP error, no 5xx). 2. No final chunk with `finish_reason`, no `data: [DONE]`. 3. Engine continues serving subsequent requests normally (KV cache ~4–6 %, 0–2 running requests, no preemptions, no OOM, no crash). 4. **Two observed variants**, both producing the identical client symptom: - (a) Logged trigger: the single `Failed to advance FSM` ERROR above, nothing else. The API server logs no error/warning/disconnect. - (b) **Silent trigger**: no engine log line at all — no FSM error, no ERROR, no disconnect, no abort — while the engine is healthy and actively serving (e.g. 00:43 and 00:48 UTC 2026-08-19, `Running: 1 reqs`, ~15–20 tok/s generation, clean 00:40–00:50 UTC window). ### Impact Clients cannot distinguish this from a benign early stop. An agent framework treating "no finish_reason + partial text" as an error will surface it as a truncated/incomplete response, causing user-visible failures and wasted retries. Frequency observed: ~18 client-visible drops over ~2 days on a moderately loaded single-node box (plus 2 more on 2026-08-19, one of which was the silent variant), and several of the affected completions were ordinary text turns (not tool calls). Because the silent variant logs nothing, operators cannot currently correlate a client-side truncation with any server event. ### Questions / hypotheses (for maintainers) - Is there a known fix for FSM advance failure in the xgrammar backend (the line in question: `vllm/v1/.../backend_xgrammar.py:162`)? - Should a failed FSM advance degrade gracefully (e.g. fall back to unconstrained decoding for the remainder of the sequence) and still emit a terminal `finish_reason` so clients get a clean stream end? - Is the "for tokens 271" repeat a clue to a specific grammar state (e.g. a token that is valid per the tokenizer but invalid in the FSM)? - **What causes the silent variant** — a `finish_reason` / `[DONE]` terminal chunk being dropped with no server-side error at all? Is there any code path where the API server closes the SSE stream for a healthy in-flight request without logging, and could a WARN/DEBUG be added so this is diagnosable? ### Minimal repro status No minimal prompt-level repro yet; the failure correlates with specific request content during normal chat/tool-call traffic. Happy to capture the full request payload for a failing request ID if maintainers want it (data contains private content — will redact or share via a secure channel).
signals.author: Duckmanjbr

signals.title: [Bug] GDN/mamba-hybrid: profiled peak activation under-predicts prefill peak; max-num-batched-tokens also sizes the CUDA-graph pool
signals.text: ### Summary For GDN / mamba-hybrid models, the startup memory profile under-predicts the real peak activation of a large prefill chunk, so a config that vLLM accepts at startup can be unable to serve prompts a few thousand tokens long. Separately, lowering `--max-num-batched-tokens` frees memory **twice** (smaller profiled activation *and* a smaller CUDA-graph pool), which is not documented and is large enough to change the achievable context by 10%. ### Measured, RTX 5090 (31.4 GiB), 64-layer hybrid (16 full-attention + 48 GDN) All rows are `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.93`, fresh boot per row, effective args asserted from the engine's own `non-default args:` dump. "Text ladder" = 2k → 6k → 12k → 24k → 2k → 12k token prompts in one engine. | `--max-num-batched-tokens` | peak activation (profiled) | CUDA-graph pool | KV cache available | context | text ladder | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 8192 | 2.84 GiB | 0.89 GiB | 8.89 GiB | 238,400 | **dies at 6k** | | 4096 | 2.42 GiB | 0.52 GiB | 9.72 GiB | 238,400 | dies at repeat 12k | | 3072 | 2.32 GiB | 0.52 GiB | **9.82 GiB** | **262,144** | passes | | 2048 | 2.21 GiB | 0.52 GiB | 9.93 GiB | 238,400 | passes | Two independent observations: **1. The profiled peak is optimistic for the GDN prefill path.** At 8192 the engine started happily, reported `2.84 GiB for peak activation`, and then died on a 6000-token prompt with 41 MiB free, inside `flash_linear_attention/ops/chunk_o.py:168 o = torch.empty_like(v)`. `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd` allocates a chain of full-chunk intermediates (`g, o, A, w, h, v_new`); whatever the profiling run exercises, it is not the worst case of that chain. (The engine dying rather than degrading is filed separately.) **2. The chunk budget has a hidden second memory effect.** Going 8192 → 3072 reduced the CUDA-graph pool from 0.89 to 0.52 GiB on top of the activation saving. Combined, that returned **0.93 GiB to the KV cache**, which took the same card from 238,400 to the model's full native **262,144** tokens — at identical prefill throughput (6457 vs 6460 tok/s on a 2051-token benchmark). So on hybrid models the default 8192 can simultaneously be *unsafe* and *cost context*. Also logged at startup and worth surfacing more prominently: ``` CUDA graph memory profiling is enabled ... --gpu-memory-utilization=0.9300 is equivalent to --gpu-memory-utilization=0.8991 without CUDA graph profiling Add 3 padding layers, may waste at most 6.25% KV cache memory ``` That padding note is a 16/48 attention/GDN layer split being padded to a common group size — up to ~0.61 GiB (~16,000 tokens of context) at these sizes. ### Suggested direction - Include the hybrid/linear-attention prefill path in the memory profiling run at full `max_num_batched_tokens`, so the reported peak activation reflects it. - Consider a smaller default `max_num_batched_tokens` for mamba/GDN-hybrid architectures, or a startup warning when `util` is high and the model has linear-attention layers. - Document that `max_num_batched_tokens` also sizes the CUDA-graph pool. - Revisit whether the 3-padding-layer KV waste is avoidable for a 16/48 split. ### Environment note Our stack carries a third-party quantization overlay, so absolute GiB values are ours; the profiling logic, the graph-pool sizing, the KV padding, and the failing allocation are all stock vLLM / stock `third_party/flash_linear_attention` code. Happy to re-run any variant on this hardware.
signals.author: malaiwah

signals.title: Multi-node startup deadlock in in_the_same_node_as() gloo barrier at 2 nodes x TP-16 with the Ray executor (regression between 0.26.1rc1.dev78 and 0.26.1rc1.dev148)
signals.text: ## Summary Starting a 2-node, TP-16 deployment of DeepSeek-R1 (FP8) with the Ray distributed executor deadlocks during distributed initialization. All 16 ranks start, but the gloo barrier inside `in_the_same_node_as()` never completes. The process sits idle for exactly 30 minutes and then dies on the gloo TCP deadline: ``` RuntimeError: Application timeout caused pair closure [.../gloo/transport/tcp/unbound_buffer.cc:78] Timed out waiting 1800000ms for recv operation to complete ``` The traceback is identical on every reproduction: ``` parallel_state.py:1838 initialize_model_parallel -> :2009 ensure_model_parallel_initialized -> :1328 init_model_parallel_group -> :519 __init__ -> shm_broadcast.py:1022 create_from_process_group -> :2267 in_the_same_node_as -> distributed_c10d.py:5356 barrier ``` The same configuration on a **single node** works. The failure requires two nodes, and it reproduces on hosts with no NVLink fabric between them (InfiniBand only, non-MNNVL). ## Regression range This is a regression, not an unsupported configuration. Using the per-commit wheels at `https://wheels.vllm.ai/<sha>/`, with the container base image, model, flags and every non-vLLM dependency held byte-identical across arms (`torch 2.13.0+cu130`, `torchvision 0.28.0+cu130`, `flashinfer-python`/`flashinfer-cubin` `0.6.15.post1`, `flashinfer-jit-cache 0.6.15.post1+cu130`), six commits were scored: | Commit | Version | Result | | --- | --- | --- | | `35efdf6b3` | `0.26.1rc1.dev34` | pass | | `6f00a1ae3` | `0.26.1rc1.dev78` | **pass (last known good)** | | `5f8f72866` | `0.26.1rc1.dev148` | **hang (first known bad)** | | `0eec856cc` | `0.26.1rc1.dev156` | hang | | `92643d68f` | `0.26.1rc1.dev195` | hang | | `0cf49a5d1` | `0.26.1rc1.dev276` | hang | At the release level, `v0.26.0` is good and `v0.27.0` is bad, and the failure still reproduces on current `main` after `v0.27.1`. The bisect stops at `(6f00a1ae3, 5f8f72866]` because the 69 commits in between publish only `manylinux_2_28_aarch64` wheels and no `cp38-abi3` `x86_64` wheel, so they cannot be scored on this hardware. Checked at `<sha>/`, `<sha>/vllm/`, `<sha>/cu130/` and `<sha>/cu130/vllm/` for an interior commit against a control commit that does publish x86_64, to rule out a path mistake on our side. ## What the evidence rules out - **Not a change to `in_the_same_node_as` itself.** The function's source is byte-identical across the whole bracket (SHA-256 of `inspect.getsource` matches on all six arms, 92 lines). Whatever regressed alters *which ranks reach the barrier, and when* — the calling context — not this function's code. - **Not the kernel libraries.** Rebuilding a bad-side arm with the good-side `flashinfer-python 0.6.15.post1` still hangs, so the flashinfer / tvm-ffi / tilelang bundle is not the carrier. `torch`, `torchvision`, `triton`, NCCL and the CUDA toolkit are identical on both sides of the boundary. - **Not shared-memory exhaustion.** `No available shared memory broadcast block` never appears; the count is zero on every arm. - **Not infrastructure.** Both nodes are present and communicating in every failing run (two distinct worker IPs in the logs), and the identical allocation passes on good commits. - **Not custom all-reduce, and not an MNNVL-specific path** — these hosts have no NVLink fabric between nodes. - **Red herrings.** The logs lead with `ImportError: .../deep_ep_cpp...: undefined symbol: _ZN3c104impl3cow23materialize_cow_storageERNS_11StorageImplE`, plus a post-timeout `ray.exceptions.ActorHandleNotFoundError` cascade at `ray_executor_v2.py:566` and `Engine core initialization failed`. None of it is causal: **the same `deep_ep_cpp` ImportErrors appear in the runs that pass**, and the Ray errors are teardown after the deadline fires. ## Reproduction 2 nodes x 8 H100 (80 GB), InfiniBand interconnect, no inter-node NVLink, Ray executor: ``` vllm serve <deepseek-r1-fp8-checkpoint> \ --tensor-parallel-size 16 \ --pipeline-parallel-size 1 \ --data-parallel-size 1 \ --max-model-len 4096 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \ --block-size 128 \ --load-format runai_streamer \ --distributed-executor-backend ray ``` Expected: the server initializes and serves. Actual: startup hangs in `in_the_same_node_as`, then dies ~30 minutes later on the gloo deadline. ## Notes One candidate worth ruling out early: `435c4dad9` (#50311, "[ROCm][CI] Avoid Ray worker startup env race") sits in the unscorable window and its title matches the implicated area, but its diff touches only `requirements/test/rocm.in` and `requirements/test/rocm.txt` and ships no runtime code, so it is not the cause. No commit in the window is being asserted as the culprit — the remaining commits could not be scored for lack of x86_64 artifacts. Happy to run a specific candidate commit, a patch, or additional diagnostics on the 2-node setup if that would help narrow the 69-commit window. --- _This issue was drafted with assistance from the `opus` AI model._
signals.author: janbernloehr

signals.title: [Bug]: `find_mm_placeholders` may return an incorrect position for `PromptInsertion`
signals.text: ### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Description When `PromptInsertion` inserts tokens that overlap with adjacent tokens in the original prompt, `find_mm_placeholders` may locate an earlier occurrence instead of the tokens inserted by the prompt update. For example: - Original prompt contains `[32000]` at index 3. - The insertion target is `[32000]`. - The inserted placeholder tokens are `[32000, 32000]`. After applying the update, the resulting sequence around the target is: ```text [..., 32000, 32000, 32000, ...] original inserted ``` The inserted placeholder starts at index 4. However, `find_mm_placeholders` scans the resulting prompt for `[32000, 32000]` and finds the sequence starting at index 3, which includes one token from the original prompt. ## Expected behavior The placeholder position should refer to the tokens inserted by `PromptInsertion`, so `start_idx` should be 4. ## Actual behavior `find_mm_placeholders` reports `start_idx=3`. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
signals.author: Yiqin-17

signals.title: [Bug]: Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime permanent engine hang on a specific audio file via /v1/audio/transcriptions (empty multimodal embeddings)
signals.text: > **About this report**: This analysis was produced automatically by **Hermes (an autonomous AI agent)** on behalf of a user. Reproduction happened on a rented cloud GPU instance (vast.ai, RTX 3090 24 GB, CUDA 13.0.2) accessed via SSH — there is no local GPU involved. ### Your current environment ```text OS : Debian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm) (x86_64) — vast.ai cloud instance GPU : NVIDIA RTX 3090 (24 GB, sm_86) CUDA Version : 13.0.2 Python : 3.12 vLLM Version : 0.27.1 (official image vllm/vllm-openai:v0.27.1) VLLM Build Commit : 6e448d0ea9bf3d88d898b65449ca6dc2aec170ac Model : mistralai/Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime-2602 (snapshot 2769294da9567371363522aac9bbcfdd19447add) vLLM serve args : --tokenizer-mode mistral --config-format mistral --load-format mistral --trust-remote-code --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"PIECEWISE"}' --max-model-len 16000 --max-num-seqs 1 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 --served-model-name whisper-1 ``` ### 🐛 Describe the bug Serving `mistralai/Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime-2602` with vLLM v0.27.1 (V1 engine), one specific WAV file sent to `/v1/audio/transcriptions` makes the **entire engine hang permanently**: - The log floods with `Realtime model received empty multimodal embeddings for 1 input tokens. Returning zero embeddings to avoid engine crash.` (`voxtral_realtime.py:305`). - The GPU stays at **100 % utilization** and VRAM at ~21/24 GB — the engine appears to decode indefinitely (zero embeddings never produce an EOS). - `/health` stops responding, the port stays open but no request is ever answered. The only way out is killing the vLLM process. - Reproduced **twice in a row** at exactly the same audio file (the first 150 requests of the same benchmark batch all succeeded, then this file hangs the server deterministically). The audio file is **not** silent or unusual: 16 kHz, mono, 16-bit WAV, 5.4 s, RMS −24.5 dBFS, peak −3.8 dBFS, 62 % silence. Its RMS/silence statistics are almost identical to 9 sibling files of the same batch that all transcribe fine. **Failing audio file (for reproduction):** https://drop.n0ne.de/u/NZsVNE.wav ### Steps to reproduce 1. Start vLLM as above (Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime-2602, any GPU with ≥ 16 GB VRAM). 2. Wait for `/health` to return OK. 3. POST the attached WAV to `/v1/audio/transcriptions` (multipart `file`, `model=whisper-1` or any served name, `language=de`). A plain curl `-F file=@...` is enough. 4. Observe: the request never returns, `/health` stops responding, GPU stays at 100 %. Expected behavior: the request either returns a transcription (the reference text of this TTS sample is "Zug einfährt auf Gleis sieben, bitte zurücktreten von der Bahnsteigkante."), or the engine survives and continues serving. Actual behavior: permanent engine hang; the whole server becomes unresponsive and must be restarted. ### Logs Excerpt of `vllm.log` during the hang (repeated thousands of times): ```text (EngineCore pid=2044) WARNING 08-19 09:45:46 [voxtral_realtime.py:305] Realtime model received empty multimodal embeddings for 1 input tokens. Returning zero em (EngineCore pid=2044) WARNING 08-19 09:45:47 [voxtral_realtime.py:305] Realtime model received empty multimodal embeddings for 1 input tokens. Returning zero em (EngineCore pid=2044) WARNING 08-19 09:45:47 [voxtral_realtime.py:305] Realtime model received empty multimodal embeddings for 1 input tokens. Returning zero em ``` Meanwhile `nvidia-smi` reports `100 %, 21208 MiB, 24576 MiB` and `curl /health` times out / returns nothing. ### Related issues — checked, none explains this - **#38233** (closed, "Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime hangs/crashes on multiple sessions due to encoder_cache_usage saturation on 16GB GPU") — multiple `/v1/realtime` sessions and encoder-cache saturation on 16 GB. Ours: a **single** `/v1/audio/transcriptions` request, 24 GB GPU, no cache saturation, no sessions. - **#45022** (open PR, "fix boot-OOM / silent-hang / max-len crash on 16 GiB") — fixes boot-time failures on 16 GiB. Ours: boots fine on 24 GB, hangs after ~150 healthy requests at one specific file. - **#44461** (closed, "Fix token feedback timeout silent hang") — a timeout in the realtime `feed_tokens()` background task. Ours: plain transcription endpoint, no realtime session, no token feedback involved. - **#39229 / #39202** ("Fix Voxtral Realtime crash on mixed-batch transcription") — crash with mixed prefill+decode batches. Ours: `--max-num-seqs 1`, strictly one request at a time, no mixed batch. - **#50860** (open, "Resumable (realtime) sessions retain raw mm_feature.data...") — memory retention across realtime sessions. Ours: single short request, no sessions. The common denominator of the existing reports is that the *zero-embedding fallback* in `voxtral_realtime.py` is a known fragile spot; this report adds a concrete deterministic input that turns that fallback into a **permanent whole-server hang** instead of the intended "keep other requests alive".
