signals.title: [Bug] v1 detokenizer: client stop strings match inside the reasoning segment, decapitating think-in-prompt models (lm-eval sends stop on every request)
signals.text: ## Summary vLLM's v1 detokenizer evaluates client `stop` strings against the **whole output stream**. With think-in-prompt chat templates (DeepSeek-V4 family, Qwen3 family), generation begins *inside* the reasoning segment — and chain-of-thought naturally restates phrases like `Question:`. Any client that sends stop sequences silently decapitates the reasoning: the stop fires mid-`<think>`, `</think>` never arrives, and the reasoning parser returns `content: null`. This is easy to hit without knowing it: **lm-evaluation-harness sends `stop[:4]` on every `local-chat-completions` request**, so benchmark numbers on thinking models served by vLLM can be silently destroyed while the same checkpoint behind a hosted API (which scopes stops to content) scores normally. The failure masquerades as a model problem; it is a serving-layer one. ## Reproducer Any think-in-prompt model whose CoT can restate a stop string. With a DeepSeek-V4-family or Qwen3-family model served by vLLM: ```bash curl -s http://HOST:PORT/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{ "model": "MODEL", "temperature": 0.6, "seed": 7, "max_tokens": 8192, "stop": ["Question:"], "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "GSM8K-style word problem here"}]}' ``` On an affected build the response ends with `finish_reason: "stop"` after a few dozen tokens with `content: null` (the reasoning restated `Question:`); without the `stop` field the same seed answers correctly. Measured on our deployment: the reproducer goes 43 tok / `content: null` → 344 tok / correct answer with the guard; **GSM8K n=50 (t0.6/p0.95) goes 8–15 nulls, 0.66–0.84 → 1 null, 0.98.** (The residual null is an unrelated reasoning-runaway mechanism.) ## Fix (working, dogfooded, public — take it if you want it) Branch: https://github.com/Capicua25x/vllm-rocm-rdna4/tree/fix/suppress-stops-in-reasoning (one commit on `vllm/v1/engine/detokenizer.py`, port to 0.26.1) Per-request guard, no configuration: at detokenizer construction, if the request's **last prompt token is the reasoning start marker**, client stop strings stay dormant until the end marker appears in the output. Markers come from `--reasoning-config` (`reasoning_start_str`/`reasoning_end_str`) when set, falling back to `<think>`/`</think>` — not model-specific. EOS and `max_tokens` are unaffected; non-thinking requests are untouched by construction. Opt-out: `VLLM_SUPPRESS_STOPS_IN_REASONING=0` (process-wide). The subtle case (caught in third-party review of the original patch): with speculative decoding, the `update()` that carries `</think>` also carries up to k tokens of the reasoning that preceded it — on closing the guard, the stop-check offset advances past the marker so stops are evaluated only over what follows. Controls: a stop present in *content* still fires; a stop on a non-thinking request still cuts at the exact match. Provenance: the original version of this guard has run in production since 2026-08-05 on a 2-node DeepSeek-V4-Flash deployment (vLLM 0.21.1, speculative decoding k=5) under real agent traffic, with independent third-party validation on a second deployment; the branch above is the mechanical port to 0.26.1, verified by a CPU behavioral test included on the branch (`tests/v1/engine/test_suppress_stops_in_reasoning.py`, run in the 0.26.1 runtime: dormant-in-reasoning, non-thinking unaffected, one-chunk spec-decode leak, env opt-out — 4/4); the measured table is from the 0.21 deployment. ## Design question for maintainers The guard fixes the default behavior gap vs hosted deployments, but the right long-term shape may be per-request: e.g. scope `stop` to content by default for reasoning requests and add an explicit `stop_in_reasoning: true` escape hatch. I maintain the fix as a rebased branch on my fork rather than shepherding a PR (one-person operation) — anyone who wants to carry it upstream is welcome to it, and I'll re-run numbers against any candidate patch on request.
signals.author: Capicua25x

signals.title: [Bug]: PD P2P supply and demand are computed independently, and nothing checks they match
signals.text: ### Summary In the PD (prefill/decode disaggregated) flow over the P2P secondary tier, the producer's **supply** and the consumer's **demand** are computed by two independent code paths on two different engines, and **nothing anywhere verifies that they agree**. The protocol depends on them agreeing. When they diverge, the consumer's unmatched demand parks until `_LOAD_TIMEOUT_S = 30.0` (`vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/session/client.py:33`) and it recomputes the prompt. #52808 and #53062 are two instances of this. They were found separately, have different triggers, and were fixed (or are being fixed) separately. Six more divergence sites exist and are unguarded. This issue names the invariant and proposes a test mechanism that fails CI when a future change breaks it. Line numbers for source files are against `main` @ `5a4c8d9924`. Line numbers for `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py` are against #52912's branch (`657fcc1b4`), since the tests referenced below are part of that PR and are not on `main` yet. ### Why PD has no enforcement, and symmetric P2P does In **symmetric** P2P the consumer sends a `LookupMsg`, the server answers from tier lookups and pins, and only then does the consumer fetch. Supply is *derived from* demand, so they cannot disagree — a warm producer is the best case. The **PD** leg has no such round trip. `P2PSecondaryTierManager.lookup` for a PD consumer is: ```python # PD consumer (we are the decoder): all kv blocks should be on the # prefiller side. Return HIT immediately. return LookupResult.HIT ```   — `vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/manager.py:350` The decoder asserts by construction that every block it wants is on the prefiller. It never checks. Meanwhile the prefiller independently decides what to store, through a chain of filters that know nothing about what the decoder will ask for. The invariant *"producer supply ⊇ consumer demand"* is load-bearing and unenforced. ### There is no cross-check today — not even an observation I looked for any assertion, metric, counter, or log that compares the two key sets. There is none. The P2P tier emits no metrics at all. The three closest signals all fall short, and two of them are dead code in PD: 1. **`server.py:966-979`** — the only place both sides of the mismatch appear together, as a `debug` log: `remaining` (demanded, never supplied) next to `leftover_available` (supplied, never demanded). Counts only, no keys, off by default. 2. **`server.py:372`** — `if req.lookup_supplied and req.demanded:` warns and fails the fetch immediately rather than letting the peer hit the load timeout. `lookup_supplied` is only ever set by the symmetric lookup-pin path, so **this never fires in PD** — as its own comment says. 3. **`client.py:229`** — `assert all(st.probes.get(key) is True for key in keys)`, guarded by `st.probed`, which PD never sets. **Also dead in PD.** So the two guards that would catch a mismatch are both gated on symmetric-only state. In PD, a mismatch surfaces only as an eventual `TransferDoneMsg(success=False)` or a 30s timeout, in both cases without naming which keys were missing. #52808 shows the practical cost: the timeout path prints a `PYTHONHASHSEED` hint that had nothing to do with the failure, and the reporter had to verify and rule it out. ### The divergence surface Each row alone is sufficient to break a round. Producer-side rows drop keys the consumer will demand; consumer-side rows demand keys the producer will not supply. | # | Side | What drops / over-demands | Location | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | producer | `if block_id == 0: continue` — null-block sentinel | `offloading/scheduler.py:1304` | | 2 | producer | SWA chunk unreachable within its alignment segment | `scheduler.py:1312` (`is_store_reachable_swa_chunk`, `:129`) | | 3 | producer | EAGLE/MTP volatile trailing chunk while decoding | `scheduler.py:404` (in `storable_chunks`, `:382`) | | 4 | producer | `prepare_store` returns `None` (primary allocation failure) | `scheduler.py:1326` | | 5 | producer | prefix-hit key that is not `HIT` in primary at cascade time | `tiering/manager.py:615` — **#53062** | | 6 | producer | `max_offload_tokens` / `offload_prompt_only` truncation | `scheduler.py:588` | | 7 | consumer | `_sliding_window_lookup` promotes **every key it scans**, not just the final window, so out-of-window chunks enter the `FetchMsg` | `scheduler.py:633` + `tiering/manager.py:404` | | 8 | consumer | eager unconditional `HIT`, no existence check | `p2p/manager.py:350` | Plus the policy gate that caused #52808: under `BLOCK_LEVEL`, `scheduler.py:1075` sets `next_stored_chunk_idx = num_chunks`, skipping prefix-hit chunks entirely. Fixed for the producer leg by #52912. Only #5 and the policy gate are being addressed. Rows 1, 2, 3 are currently consistent with the demand side, but only because two hand-mirrored pieces of logic happen to agree — which is exactly the fragility below. ### Why this needs a mechanism rather than another point fix #51840 changed `lookup` to return `HIT_PENDING` instead of `RETRY` when a promotion is initiated. In `_sliding_window_lookup`, `HIT_PENDING` counts toward the consecutive-hit streak while `RETRY` resets it. So a change to lookup *semantics*, in a different file, silently changed **which keys the consumer demands** — widening it on `v0.27.1` to include 55 out-of-window SWA chunks a warm producer can never supply. Nothing in the test suite noticed; the divergence was found by hand-instrumenting a container and counting chunks (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52912#issuecomment-5345686593). That is the regression class to guard: the invariant spans two engines and half a dozen files, so any single-file change can break it invisibly. ### Proposed guard: exhaustiveness sentinels The suite already has the right pattern. `_SCAN_BEHAVIOR` in `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py:1252` is a table keyed by every `LookupResult`, with `test_scan_behavior_declared_for_every_lookup_result` parametrized over `list(LookupResult)` — a new enum member fails the suite until someone declares its behavior. That is what makes a guard survive future commits instead of pinning today's bugs. Three sentinels in the same style would cover the surface above: **1. `_CASCADE_SUPPLY_BEHAVIOR: dict[LookupResult, Disposition]`** — guards row 5. For each `LookupResult` the primary tier can return at cascade time, declare `SUPPLY` / `DEFER` / `DROP`. Drive a real `TieringOffloadingManager` with a stubbed primary returning the parametrized result plus a recording request-level tier, and assert the observed disposition matches the declared one. Today: `HIT → SUPPLY`, `HIT_PENDING / RETRY / MISS → DROP`. When #53062 lands, `HIT_PENDING` flips to `DEFER` and the table records that as deliberate intent rather than a coincidence. Reuses `MetricsSecondaryTierManager` (`tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tiering_offloading.py:99`) and the existing `manager_setup` fixture. **2. `_POLICY_KEEPS_PREFIX_HITS: dict[OffloadPolicy, bool]`** — guards the #52808 gate at `scheduler.py:1075`. For each `OffloadPolicy`, declare whether prefix-hit chunks stay in the store path; drive `request_runner` over a warm prefix and assert. A future policy has to declare, and if it declares `False`, assert the P2P tier does not select it for a producer leg. **3. `_GROUP_STORE_PRUNING: dict[type[KVCacheSpec], ...]`** — guards rows 1, 2, 3 and consumer over-demand 7. `get_sliding_window_size_in_chunks` (`scheduler.py:109`) already switches on spec type — `SlidingWindowSpec`, `ChunkedLocalAttentionSpec`, `MambaSpec`, `FullAttentionSpec` — and closes with `assert isinstance(kv_cache_spec, FullAttentionSpec)`. So a new attention type does fail closed, but only at runtime on a model that uses it, never in CI. The sentinel enumerates the handled spec types, requires each to declare whether the store path prunes and which demand scan the load path uses, and for every pruning type asserts the relation that `test_sliding_window_demand_is_store_reachable` (`test_scheduler.py:1517`) already checks for SWA. These are pure-CPU unit tests needing no new harness. ### What already exists, and where it stops #52912 added `test_request_level_supply_covers_consumer_demand` (`test_scheduler.py:2365`), which asserts the invariant at the scheduler level over `warmth × with_swa_group`. Two limits worth recording: - Supply is measured at `prepare_store` call args against a `MagicMock` manager, so everything downstream — the cascade's `HIT`-only filter (row 5), `submit_store`, and the session parking in `_OutboundRequestState` — is invisible to it. #53062 lives entirely in that stretch. - Demand comes from `_demanded_keys` (`test_scheduler.py:2343`), which *reimplements* the scan on a bypass scheduler. It can drift along with production rather than pinning it — the #51840 failure mode. ### Also worth doing, not proposed here Listing these so they are not lost, in rough order of value: - **Tier-level supply invariant** — the same assertion with a real `TieringOffloadingManager`, so the cascade filter is in scope. - **Demand-oracle drift guard** — pin `_demanded_keys` against a real consumer leg's actual lookups, so the oracle cannot drift silently. - **Make the runtime failure loud** — promote the `server.py:966-979` debug log and name the unmatched keys with their KV cache group indices (`get_offload_group_idx`), so a mismatch is diagnosable from a single log line instead of an instrumented rebuild, and so the misleading `PYTHONHASHSEED` hint stops being the headline. - **Demand-driven serving for the PD leg**, as symmetric P2P already has. This removes the invariant rather than guarding it, and was raised as the long-term direction in the #52912 discussion (cc @Etelis @nilig @ronensc @orozery). ### Happy to hand over I have the sentinel tests locally and am glad to open the PR, or to hand the patch to whoever is already in this code — @almogtavor and @AbarnaaSree both volunteered on #53062, and the two overlap. --- AI assistance was used to survey the code paths and draft this issue; the analysis and every cited location were reviewed and verified by hand. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the core devs or team in the [vLLM Forum](https://discuss.vllm.ai) first
signals.author: liranschour

signals.title: [Bug]: MooncakeStoreConnector stores invalid recurrent states with mamba_cache_mode=align, causing silent output corruption
signals.text: ### Your current environment The issue was reproduced on vLLM `main` at: ```text commit: 0ad04cff1b10267a2642becbf31f62c91018cad5 runtime vLLM version: 0.27.2rc1.dev142+g0ad04cff1 Python: 3.12.3 PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu129 CUDA runtime: 12.9 GPU: 8 x NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 (the reproduction uses TP=2) NVIDIA driver: 580.173.02 mooncake-transfer-engine: 0.3.12.post1 transformers: 5.15.0 triton: 3.7.1 OS: Ubuntu 24.04.2 LTS GCC: 13.3.0 ``` ### 🐛 Describe the bug ### Summary `MooncakeStoreConnector` can publish external prefix-cache keys for recurrent-state boundaries that do not contain a valid state. With `MambaSpec(mamba_cache_mode="align")`, vLLM may intentionally leave some logical state boundaries without a materialized recurrent-state block. Such entries use `NULL_BLOCK_ID = 0`. The normal Mooncake Store save path currently resolves that block ID to an address and publishes the corresponding Store key without rejecting the null block. As a result: 1. A producer publishes a key for a boundary such as token 2112 or 2960 even though no valid GDN/Mamba/ShortConv state was captured there. 2. Mooncake Store lookup sees that the key exists and reports the longer prefix as externally reusable. 3. The consumer loads the bytes successfully and skips recomputation up to that boundary. 4. Generation silently diverges from a cold baseline. There is no Put/Get error, and in some cases the generated tokens remain the same while logprobs differ significantly. Byte-level instrumentation shows that Mooncake transfers the selected bytes exactly. The invalid all-zero bytes already exist on the producer side because the selected recurrent-state block is `NULL_BLOCK_ID`. This points to invalid key publication in the producer save path, rather than data corruption in Mooncake transport. ### Why this is user-visible This can affect normal serving whenever all of the following are true: - a model has recurrent state, for example GDN, Mamba1, Mamba2, or ShortConv; - `MooncakeStoreConnector` external prefix caching is enabled; - a long producer request creates Store keys for an intermediate boundary that did not receive a valid recurrent-state snapshot under the producer's prefill/chunking history; - a later request reuses that boundary. The request succeeds with HTTP 200 and Mooncake reports successful Put/Get operations, but the model output can be wrong. ### Generic reproduction for recurrent-state models The same producer/consumer pattern was validated with GDN, Mamba1, Mamba2, and ShortConv caches, on both hybrid and pure recurrent-state models. The smallest tested profile is `state-spaces/mamba-130m-hf`. The model-specific values used in the successful reproductions are: | Profile | `MODEL` | State type | Producer repeats | Consumer repeats | Common prefix | Invalid Store hit | |---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Smallest | `state-spaces/mamba-130m-hf` | pure Mamba1 | 1000 | 1000 | 3026 | 3024 | | Pure Mamba2 | `mistralai/Mamba-Codestral-7B-v0.1` | pure Mamba2 | 1000 | 1000 | 3031 | 3024 | | ShortConv hybrid | `LiquidAI/LFM2.5-350M` | ShortConv + Full Attention | 1000 | 1000 | 3027 | 3024 | | Mamba2 hybrid | `Zyphra/Zamba2-1.2B-instruct` | Mamba2 + Full Attention | 1000 | 1000 | 3030 | 2960 | | GDN hybrid | `Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B` | GDN + Full Attention | 1250 | 700 | 2126 | 2112 | <details> <summary>Reproduction commands</summary> All tested runs used TP=2. The commands below are parameterized so any row can be selected. For example, the smallest profile is: For `mistralai/Mamba-Codestral-7B-v0.1`, also pass `--load-format safetensors`. Other model-specific loading flags can be added without changing the producer/consumer sequence. ```bash export MODEL=state-spaces/mamba-130m-hf export SERVED_MODEL=mamba-130m-hf export VERIFICATION_CODE=PURE-MAMBA-STORE export PRODUCER_REPEATS=1000 export CONSUMER_REPEATS=1000 export PYTHONHASHSEED=0 ``` #### 1. Start Mooncake Store ```bash mooncake_master \ --port 50061 \ --default_kv_lease_ttl 30m ``` Save the following configuration as `/tmp/mooncake-store.json`: ```json { "mode": "embedded", "metadata_server": "P2PHANDSHAKE", "master_server_address": "127.0.0.1:50061", "global_segment_size": "4GB", "local_buffer_size": "1GB", "protocol": "tcp", "device_name": "", "enable_offload": false } ``` ```bash export MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/mooncake-store.json ``` #### 2. Generate a shared-prefix producer/consumer request pair ```bash python3 - <<'PY' import json import os from transformers import AutoTokenizer model = os.environ["MODEL"] served_model = os.environ["SERVED_MODEL"] code = os.environ["VERIFICATION_CODE"] producer_repeats = int(os.environ["PRODUCER_REPEATS"]) consumer_repeats = int(os.environ["CONSUMER_REPEATS"]) shared = ( "Cache correctness record. The exact verification code is " f"{code}. Remember it for a later question. " ) producer_prompt = ( shared + "neutral cache context " * producer_repeats + "Producer-only task: write the cache and answer ACK:" ) consumer_prompt = ( shared + "neutral cache context " * consumer_repeats + "Consumer-only question: What is the exact verification code? " "Answer only with the code:" ) common = { "model": served_model, "max_tokens": 16, "temperature": 0, "seed": 0, "logprobs": 1, } for path, prompt in ( ("/tmp/producer-request.json", producer_prompt), ("/tmp/consumer-request.json", consumer_prompt), ): with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as output: json.dump({**common, "prompt": prompt}, output) tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model, trust_remote_code=True) producer_ids = tokenizer.encode(producer_prompt, add_special_tokens=True) consumer_ids = tokenizer.encode(consumer_prompt, add_special_tokens=True) common_prefix = 0 for producer_id, consumer_id in zip(producer_ids, consumer_ids): if producer_id != consumer_id: break common_prefix += 1 print({ "producer_tokens": len(producer_ids), "consumer_tokens": len(consumer_ids), "common_prefix_tokens": common_prefix, }) PY ``` The important shape is that the common prefix reaches an intermediate Store boundary for which the producer did not retain a recurrent-state snapshot. The exact boundary depends on the model's state-cache page size and tokenizer, so assert the actual external hit metric rather than relying only on prompt character counts. #### 3. Record a cold baseline Start vLLM without a KV connector: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2,3 vllm serve "$MODEL" \ --served-model-name "$SERVED_MODEL" \ --port 8002 \ --tensor-parallel-size 2 \ --max-model-len 4096 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \ --enforce-eager \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \ --mamba-cache-mode align ``` ```bash curl -sS -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data-binary @/tmp/consumer-request.json \ http://127.0.0.1:8002/v1/completions > /tmp/cold-response.json ``` Stop the baseline server so that the Store consumer can use the same GPUs. #### 4. Populate Mooncake Store from a producer ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 vllm serve "$MODEL" \ --served-model-name "$SERVED_MODEL" \ --port 8000 \ --tensor-parallel-size 2 \ --max-model-len 4096 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \ --enforce-eager \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \ --mamba-cache-mode align \ --kv-transfer-config '{ "kv_connector":"MooncakeStoreConnector", "kv_role":"kv_producer", "kv_connector_extra_config":{ "cache_prefix":"state-boundary-repro", "enable_lookup":false } }' ``` ```bash curl -sS -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data-binary @/tmp/producer-request.json \ http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions > /tmp/producer-response.json ``` Wait until the Put succeeds and becomes visible to Store lookup. #### 5. Restore the prefix in a separate consumer ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2,3 vllm serve "$MODEL" \ --served-model-name "$SERVED_MODEL" \ --port 8002 \ --tensor-parallel-size 2 \ --max-model-len 4096 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \ --enforce-eager \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \ --mamba-cache-mode align \ --kv-transfer-config '{ "kv_connector":"MooncakeStoreConnector", "kv_role":"kv_consumer", "kv_connector_extra_config":{ "cache_prefix":"state-boundary-repro", "enable_lookup":true, "load_async":true } }' ``` ```bash curl -sS -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data-binary @/tmp/consumer-request.json \ http://127.0.0.1:8002/v1/completions > /tmp/store-response.json ``` </details> Verify all three conditions: 1. Store metrics show a non-zero external prefix hit and successful Get operations. 2. The Store response differs from the cold response in generated token strings and/or per-token logprobs. 3. Repeating the experiment with `--max-num-batched-tokens` set to the invalid Store-hit boundary makes that boundary a real state-capture boundary; the restored output then exactly matches the cold output. This third step is a diagnostic control, not a general workaround. ### Observed result (Qwen3.5-9B example) Mooncake Store reports successful operations: ```text producer: Put 56 keys, 484442112 bytes, 0 failed keys consumer: Get 14 keys, 121110528 bytes, 0 failed keys consumer external prefix cache hit: 2112 tokens ``` However, deterministic output differs from the cold baseline: ```text cold baseline: HYBRID-528-GDN. The exact verification code is Mooncake Store consumer: HYBRID-528-GDN The exact verification code is HY maximum absolute per-token logprob difference: 1.4653081893920898 ``` The mismatch is deterministic in repeated runs. ### Expected result An external prefix-cache key should only be published when every state required to resume from that boundary is valid and recoverable. If the recurrent-state block at a candidate boundary is `NULL_BLOCK_ID`, the producer should not publish that boundary as reusable. Lookup should return the longest earlier boundary that is valid for all required cache groups, and the consumer should recompute the remaining tokens. For deterministic greedy decoding, a cold run and a correctly restored Store run should produce the same text, generated tokens, and per-token logprobs. ### Root-cause evidence Instrumentation immediately before Mooncake Put and immediately after Mooncake Get at the 2112-token boundary shows: ```text Qwen3.5 GDN recurrent states: producer states using physical block 0: 6 / 6 producer states containing only zero bytes: 6 / 6 producer -> consumer byte-exact matches: 6 / 6 SHA-256 for every zero state: 6334891ad0b99640af1d1dd5dc8863447ff79bb5b3d9936f8bcfc98a5c41922d Qwen3.5 Full Attention KV entries: producer entries containing non-zero bytes: 2 / 2 producer -> consumer byte-exact matches: 2 / 2 ``` Therefore: - the recurrent-state entries are already invalid before transport; - the Full Attention KV entries are valid; - Mooncake transfers all selected entries byte-for-byte; - the failure is caused by publishing a key whose recurrent state resolves to the null block. As a diagnostic control, adding `--max-num-batched-tokens 2112` to all three servers changes the producer's state-capture boundary: ```text GDN recurrent states at 2112: physical blocks: non-null blocks 1, 2, and 3 non-zero states: 6 / 6 producer -> consumer byte-exact matches: 6 / 6 Full Attention KV: producer -> consumer byte-exact matches: 2 / 2 output comparison: text: exact match generated tokens: exact match maximum absolute per-token logprob difference: 0.0 ``` This is a diagnostic control, not a general production workaround: arbitrary request lengths can expose other intermediate boundaries. ### Cross-model evidence The same default-vs-aligned experiment was repeated on five full models covering four recurrent-state implementations. `bad boundary` is a boundary advertised by Store lookup under the default scheduler configuration. `null state` is measured on the producer before Put. | Model | Cache architecture | Page size | Bad boundary | Producer recurrent-state evidence | Mooncake transfer | User-visible result | Aligned control | |---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|---| | Qwen3.5-9B | GDN + Full Attention | 528 | 2112 | 6/6 GDN states use null block and are all zero | 8/8 total entries byte-exact | Tokens differ; max logprob diff 1.465308 | Exact at 2112 | | Zyphra/Zamba2-1.2B-instruct | Mamba2 + Full Attention | 80 | 2960 | 14/14 Mamba2 states use null block and are all zero | 16/16 total entries byte-exact | Tokens differ; max logprob diff 2.302462 | Exact at 2960 | | LiquidAI/LFM2.5-350M | ShortConv + Full Attention | 16 | 3024 | 4/4 ShortConv states use null block and are all zero | 6/6 total entries byte-exact | Tokens happen to match; max logprob diff 0.150565 | Exact at 3024 | | state-spaces/mamba-130m-hf | Pure Mamba1 | 16 | 3024 | 2/2 Mamba1 states use null block and are all zero | 2/2 entries byte-exact | Tokens differ; max logprob diff 2.436541 | Exact at 3024 | | mistralai/Mamba-Codestral-7B-v0.1 | Pure Mamba2 | 16 | 3024 | 2/2 Mamba2 states use null block and are all zero | 2/2 entries byte-exact | Tokens differ; max logprob diff 2.756008 | Exact at 3024 | The pure Mamba results show that hybrid Full Attention groups are not required to trigger the bug. ### Suspected code path All links below point to the tested commit. 1. [`NULL_BLOCK_ID` is defined as block 0](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/0ad04cff1b10267a2642becbf31f62c91018cad5/vllm/v1/attention/backends/utils.py#L46). 2. [`MambaManager.remove_skipped_blocks()` replaces skipped state blocks with the null block](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/0ad04cff1b10267a2642becbf31f62c91018cad5/vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py#L1431-L1459). 3. [`ChunkedTokenDatabase.prepare_values()` resolves logical chunks through `block_ids` and computes transfer addresses](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/0ad04cff1b10267a2642becbf31f62c91018cad5/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/store/data.py#L211-L241), but does not reject `NULL_BLOCK_ID`. 4. The normal save path [builds keys from processed token ranges](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/0ad04cff1b10267a2642becbf31f62c91018cad5/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/store/worker.py#L838-L848), [prepares the addresses](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/0ad04cff1b10267a2642becbf31f62c91018cad5/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/store/worker.py#L918-L928), and [submits the batch Put](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/0ad04cff1b10267a2642becbf31f62c91018cad5/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/store/worker.py#L967-L975) without filtering null state blocks. 5. In contrast, the [partial-tail save path already skips `NULL_BLOCK_ID`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/0ad04cff1b10267a2642becbf31f62c91018cad5/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/store/worker.py#L675-L686). The ordinary save path appears to need equivalent validity handling while keeping token ranges, keys, group indices, addresses, and sizes aligned. ### Suggested fix direction One possible minimal fix is to reject a candidate Store boundary when any recurrent-state group resolves to NULL_BLOCK_ID. More generally, the save path should only publish a boundary after verifying that all cache groups required to resume from that boundary are recoverable. ### Related issues and PRs I searched existing vLLM issues and PRs for `MooncakeStoreConnector`, `NULL_BLOCK_ID`, recurrent/Mamba state boundaries, skipped blocks, and incorrect-output reports. I did not find an issue or PR that already contains this exact, directly reproduced normal-save-path failure. The closest existing report is #50630: - #50630 describes a broader missing-capability/boundary-invariant problem around recurrent caches. It explicitly lists write-side chunk fragmentation, where a recurrent snapshot is registered under a block hash for a different boundary, as an open class. - However, #50630 focuses primarily on EAGLE/MTP cache-peek behavior and states that it had not established whether the write-side path was reachable on `main`. - This report directly demonstrates reachability without EAGLE, MTP, speculative decoding, or P/D disaggregation. It isolates the ordinary `MooncakeStoreConnector` Put path, identifies `NULL_BLOCK_ID` before Put, proves byte-exact Put/Get, and reproduces silent output divergence on five models. <details> <summary>Other related but distinct work</summary> | Issue / PR | Relationship | Difference from this report | |---|---|---| | #49499 | Mooncake Store silent recurrent-state corruption with TP > 1 | Fixed TP-shard dedup/keying. The tested commit already contains this fix; here each transferred entry matches its producer bytes, but the producer bytes come from the null block. | | #49502 | Mooncake Store partial-tail and read-side hit-boundary handling | Addresses reliable partial-tail offload and lookup-side boundaries. This report exercises ordinary full-entry save and invalid key publication on the write side. | | #44451 / #44488 | Skipped/null Mamba blocks make KV-event token/hash mapping ambiguous | Concerns `BlockStored` event metadata. This report concerns actual Mooncake Store keys and state payloads used for inference. | | #43559 / #51113 / #51351 | Recurrent-cache poisoning and capability handling with EAGLE/MTP | #51113 fixes mid-block state published as an aligned state under EAGLE/MTP. The tested commit contains it; this reproduction enables neither EAGLE nor MTP and instead finds a null source block in the ordinary Store save path. | | #51468 | External Mamba-state/local Full Attention hit divergence | Fixes an assertion in partial-tail truncation after local eviction. This report uses ordinary prefix matching and reaches successful inference with silently incorrect state. | | #49757 | Stale block-table rows during dummy runs | Prevents dummy kernels from overwriting externally loaded recurrent state. This report captures invalid bytes before Put, rather than consumer state overwritten after Get. | | #49360 | `MooncakeStoreConnector` hang on a GDN model | A transport/liveness failure under EFA and offload pressure, rather than successful retrieval followed by silent incorrect output. | </details> ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: int4 per-token-head KV cache: triton_reshape_and_cache_flash_per_token_head_quant returns wrong values
signals.text: Observed on main @ eac636a7fa476983cdae34b45a984e9852aad375 (NVIDIA H200, driver 580.159.03, CUDA 13.0). `tests/quantization/test_per_token_kv_cache.py::test_reshape_and_cache_per_token_head` fails in the int4 branch (`kv_quant_mode=INT4_PER_TOKEN_HEAD`, `quant_min=-8.0`, `quant_max=7.0`): the dequantized round-trip (unpack nibbles → zero-point → scale → inverse RHT) lands far outside the assertion tolerance (atol=rtol=0.5) vs the bf16 reference. **Deterministic failure** — head_size=64, num_kv_heads=1, num_tokens=42 (seed 0, block_size 16), i.e. `[int4-0-16-64-1-42]`. Fails on every run with identical mismatch statistics (inputs are seed-deterministic): ``` AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not close! Mismatched elements: 35 / 64 (54.7%) Greatest absolute difference: 3.0546875 at index (0, 38) (up to 0.5 allowed) Greatest relative difference: 3651.2666015625 at index (0, 52) (up to 0.5 allowed) ``` **Flaky failures** — pass/fail flips across runs on identical code: - head_size=128, num_kv_heads=1, num_tokens=42 (`[int4-0-16-128-1-42]`): 64/128 (50.0%) mismatched, abs 4.002 @ (0, 70), rel 25.5 @ (0, 101) - head_size=64, num_kv_heads=4, num_tokens=7 (`[int4-0-16-64-4-7]`): 149/256 (58.2%) mismatched, abs 3.93 @ (2, 26), rel 256 @ (0, 37) All int8 and fp8 parametrizations, and the remaining int4 combos, pass consistently. **Minimal repro:** ```bash pytest tests/quantization/test_per_token_kv_cache.py \ -k "test_reshape_and_cache_per_token_head and int4-0-16-64-1-42" ``` **Analysis:** the kernel under test is `vllm.v1.attention.ops.triton_reshape_and_cache_flash.triton_reshape_and_cache_flash_per_token_head_quant` (assertion at `tests/quantization/test_per_token_kv_cache.py:256`). A deterministic 54.7% element mismatch at ~6x the allowed absolute tolerance rules out tolerance noise and points to a correctness defect in the int4 pack/RHT path (candidate causes: zero-point packing or nibble ordering). The two shape-dependent flaky combos additionally suggest a race or uninitialized/leftover cache state whose manifestation depends on shape/head layout. The qcfg fixture carries IDs int4/int8/fp8; the stacked parametrize resolves bottom-up, so `[int4-0-16-64-1-42]` = seed 0, block_size 16, head_size 64, num_kv_heads 1, num_tokens 42. All failing combos share seed 0 / block_size 16, but those are the only values in `SEEDS`/`BLOCK_SIZES`, so there is no signal there. Happy to collect a failing-tensor dump if that helps isolate it.

LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/ffmpeg/lib:/usr/local/openmpi/lib:/usr/local/lib64:/usr/local/lib:/usr/local/neuware/lib64::/usr/local/lib:/usr/local/neuware/lib64 TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/torchinductor_root PYTORCH_NVML_BASED_CUDA_CHECK=1 TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPILE_THREADS=1 ``` We identified a bug that triggers an assertion failure in NixlConnector caused by inconsistent block counts between the Prefill (P) side and the Decode (D) side. Root Cause When tool call functionality is enabled, the tools dictionary undergoes template serialization on both the P and D sides. However, the iteration order of dictionary keys during serialization is not deterministic across the two sides. This leads to different tokenization results — specifically, the tokenizer produces a token ID sequence whose length differs by exactly one token between the P and D sides. Trigger Condition If the number of tokens on the P side is an exact multiple of block_size, and the D side encodes exactly one additional token beyond that multiple, then the D side will require one more block than the P side. This mismatch violates the block count assertion and causes the process to abort. Expected Behavior The serialization of the tools dict should be deterministic (e.g., using sorted keys) across both sides to ensure identical tokenization results, or the block allocation logic should tolerate such differences when tool calls are enabled. ### 🐛 Describe the bug I encountered the error after 3 hours of load testing on the Swebench dataset. I printed `local_num_tokens` and `remote_num_tokens` on the decode side and found a discrepancy: `local_num_token` = `remote_num_tokens` + 1. If `remote_num_tokens % block_size == 0`, then the `num_blocks` in the decode will be 1 more than `remote_blocks`, leading to a fatal error. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Bug]: CLIP pooling model silently returns identical (empty-prompt) embeddings for all completion-style input text requests under sustained multimodal load
signals.text: ### Your current environment - vLLM v0.11.2, OpenAI-compatible server (`vllm serve`), Kubernetes deployment - Model: `DFN5B-CLIP-ViT-H-14` (CLIP dual-encoder), `--runner pooling`, dtype float16, TP=1 - Relevant flags: `--mm-processor-kwargs '{"use_fast": true}' --mm-processor-cache-gb 8 --no-enable-chunked-prefill --no-enable-prefix-caching --load-format runai_streamer` - GPU: NVIDIA L40S, driver 580.159.04 - 5 identical replicas behind a round-robin router; also reproduced hitting a single engine pod directly ### 🐛 Describe the bug Under sustained multimodal (image-embedding) traffic, **text embedding requests using the completion-style `input` field start returning the SAME vector for every input** — exactly equal to the embedding of the empty string. No errors are returned; responses are well-formed 200s. This silently breaks any retrieval system using text queries (kNN returns identical neighbors for every query). Evidence collected on the affected deployment (cosine similarities, embeddings are L2-normalized): | Test | Affected (under/after heavy image load) | Healthy baseline (idle deployment, identical config/image digest/model files) | |---|---|---| | cos(`"voiture rouge"`, `"un chat noir dans la neige"`) via `input` | **1.0000** | 0.4651 | | cos(`""`, `"voiture rouge"`) via `input` | **1.0000** | 0.4815 | | image embeddings (chat-style `image_url`) | correct, bit-identical to healthy baseline | correct | | `/tokenize` of the same text | correct tokens (identical to baseline) | correct | Isolation performed: - All 5 replicas broken identically; a **freshly restarted pod is broken as soon as it starts receiving the production traffic mix** (continuous unique-image embedding batches + occasional text `input` requests). - Not the router: reproduced calling an engine pod directly. - Not the model/tokenizer/config: files md5-identical to the healthy deployment; `/tokenize` returns correct tokens; image tower produces bit-identical embeddings to the healthy deployment. - Not hardware/driver: identical GPU and driver on both deployments. - **Load-correlated and self-healing**: when the batch image traffic was scaled down, the text `input` path returned to correct, input-dependent embeddings **without any restart** (4/5 replicas recovered exactly to baseline values; 1 replica kept returning input-dependent but wrong vectors until restarted). - Chat-style `messages` text requests are input-dependent throughout (different code path), only the raw `input` path collapses. The symptom (output == empty-prompt embedding, exactly) suggests the prompt is lost between request parsing and the model forward, while tokenization itself works. Given the load correlation, our prime suspect is the multimodal processor cache / P0-P1 shared-memory object store (`vllm/multimodal/cache.py`): the traffic that triggers it consists of ~unique images (measured MM cache hit rate 0.1–0.5%, i.e. constant churn/eviction at the 8 GB cap). This looks like the *silent* sibling of the crash-variant reports: - #33865 (Embeddings API assertion `Expected a cached item for mm_hash`) - #31404 (MM cache AssertionError aborts requests) - #26195 (missing item in MultiModalReceiverCache) - #27858 (shm inconsistencies / cross-request data mixing) — same substrate, same "silent wrong data" flavor **Attempted mitigation — NOT yet validated under the triggering load**: we deployed `--mm-processor-cache-gb 0` on a new engine dedicated to the text traffic, and isolated it from the batch image traffic (so that engine has not yet seen the faulty load pattern). The original engines still run with the cache enabled and simply recovered when the batch traffic paused — so we cannot yet confirm that disabling the cache prevents the corruption; it is our prime-suspect mitigation based on the load correlation. Cost of disabling is negligible for us either way (measured hit rate 0.1–0.5% with ~unique images). Happy to provide more details. We unfortunately cannot share the exact production traffic, but the trigger profile is: continuous unique-image embedding batches (thousands/hour) interleaved with occasional text `input` requests on the same CLIP pooling engine.

signals.title: [Bug]: bare assert in BasevLLMParameter._assert_and_load gives no diagnostics on weight shape mismatch
signals.text: ### Your current environment 0.27.1 env - doesn't matter for this ### 🐛 Describe the bug Loading a checkpoint whose scale tensor has the wrong shape fails with a bare AssertionError — no parameter name, no shapes, no hint what to fix. File "vllm/model_executor/parameter.py", line 94, in _assert_and_load assert self.data.shape == loaded_weight.shape or self._is_1d_and_scalar( AssertionError Repro: compressed-tensors FP8, strategy: channel, weight_scale written as [out] instead of [out, 1]. The checkpoint is at fault, but the error says nothing about which parameter or which shapes collide. It took a debugger to find; the message below would have made it a one-line fix. vLLM reports the analogous case well elsewhere — a missing parameter raises ValueError: There is no module or parameter named 'fc.weight_scale' in ... and lists the available names. Second concern: assert is stripped under python -O. self.data.copy_(loaded_weight) then runs unchecked, and copy_ broadcasts — a 1-element per-tensor scale would be silently spread across all channels instead of rejected. Patch (no signature change; the parameter does not carry its name, so shapes only): ``` def _assert_and_load(self, loaded_weight: torch.Tensor): - assert self.data.shape == loaded_weight.shape or self._is_1d_and_scalar( - loaded_weight - ) + if self.data.shape != loaded_weight.shape and not self._is_1d_and_scalar( + loaded_weight + ): + raise ValueError( + f"weight shape mismatch: parameter has {tuple(self.data.shape)}, " + f"checkpoint has {tuple(loaded_weight.shape)}" + ) self.data.copy_(loaded_weight) ``` ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Bug]: LinearBase.load_weights substitutes the module for a missing parameter, surfacing as a confusing AttributeError
signals.text: ### Your current environment 0.27.1 env - doesn't mater for this ### 🐛 Describe the bug In `LinearBase.load_weights` the lookup falls back to `self` when the parameter does not exist: ```python param: Parameter if "." in name: submodule, _, attr = name.rpartition(".") param = getattr(self.get_submodule(submodule), attr, self) ``` `self` is the *module*, not a `Parameter`, so the annotation one line above is violated. Loading then proceeds and fails several frames later inside the module's own `weight_loader`: ``` File "vllm/model_executor/layers/linear.py", line 732, in weight_loader param_data = param.data AttributeError: 'MergedColumnParallelLinear' object has no attribute 'data' ``` Nothing in that message names the tensor that could not be resolved. **Repro:** load a quantized DFlash2 draft model (compressed-tensors FP8, `strategy: channel`). `qwen3_dflash.py` fuses q/k/v and gate/up through explicit per-name entries (`".q_proj": (".qkv_proj", "q")`) and defines no `stacked_params_mapping`, so `...mlp.gate_proj.weight_scale` does not resolve, the module is substituted, and the error above appears instead of "no such parameter". **Patch** — keeps the fallback, refuses to load into a non-parameter: ```diff if param is None and name == "bias": continue + if not isinstance(param, torch.nn.Parameter): + raise ValueError( + f"{self.prefix}: cannot load {name!r} — no such parameter, " + f"got {type(param).__name__} instead. This usually means the " + f"checkpoint carries a tensor the layer does not declare, e.g. a " + f"quantization scale on a layer built without a quant_config." + ) param.weight_loader(param, loaded_weight, shard_id) ``` ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

``` AttributeError: 'MergedColumnParallelLinear' object has no attribute 'data' ``` **Cause.** `configure_quant_config()` is called from `initialize_model()` with `vllm_config.quant_config` — the *target* model's config. A draft model builds its own config object in `get_draft_quant_config()` (`model_executor/models/utils.py`), which never passes through there, so its `packed_modules_mapping` stays the empty dict from `base_config.py`. `find_matched_target()` can then no longer map `gate_up_proj` back to `gate_proj`/`up_proj`, those layers are built **unquantized**, and their `weight_scale` has no target at load time. Non-fused layers (`down_proj`, `o_proj`) match without the mapping, so a quant kernel *is* selected and the failure looks unrelated to quantization. **Repro** — no GPU, no weights, just the draft checkpoint's `quantization_config`: ```python c = CompressedTensorsConfig.from_config(draft_quant_cfg) print(c.packed_modules_mapping) # {} — never populated targets = list(c.target_scheme_map) find_matched_target("layers.0.mlp.gate_up_proj", None, targets, {}) # -> None find_matched_target("layers.0.mlp.gate_up_proj", None, targets, {"gate_up_proj": ["gate_proj", "up_proj"]}) # -> 're:.*mlp\.(gate|up|down)_proj$' ``` Observed with a compressed-tensors FP8 (`strategy: channel`) draft model; the draft model class already carries the correct mapping by inheritance — it just never reaches the config. Any quantized drafter with fused projections is affected. **Fix** in `get_draft_quant_config()`: ```python quant_config = VllmConfig.get_quantization_config(draft_model_config, draft_load_config) if quant_config is not None: draft_cls, _ = get_model_architecture(draft_model_config) configure_quant_config(quant_config, draft_cls) return quant_config ``` ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Bug][KVOffload] PD Multi Tier discards parked KV after a fixed 60s, so a queued consumer recomputes
signals.text: ### Your current environment vLLM `main` (nightly `5a4c8d99`), plus #52912 applied. Two instances, prefill and decode, each running `OffloadingConnector` with `TieringOffloadingSpec` (CPU primary + `p2p` secondary tier). ### Describe the bug A PD Multi Tier producer discards stored KV 60 s after `submit_store` when no `FetchMsg` has bound the `kv_request_id` yet, so a consumer whose fetch is issued later finds nothing, burns its own 30 s load deadline, and recomputes the prompt. `_UNBOUND_STORE_TIMEOUT_S = 60.0` (`vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/manager.py`) is a fixed timer counted from store time. Nothing ties it to whether the consumer's request still exists or is merely queued behind other work, so the reap can fire while the request it belongs to is perfectly alive. When the late fetch arrives, the consumer waits out `_LOAD_TIMEOUT_S = 30.0` (`.../p2p/session/client.py`) before falling back to recompute. This is separate from #52808 and is not addressed by #52912; that fix makes a warm producer cascade its blocks, this is about how long those blocks survive while the peer has not asked for them yet. Reproduced with two vLLM instances and three curls - no router, no proxy, no scheduler involved. The only difference between the two cases is how long the consumer waits before fetching: | case | consumer fetch delay | consumer leg | bytes pulled | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | control | 5 s (inside the park) | 0.30 s | 580,962,816 | | late | 65 s (past the park) | 38.31 s | 0 | Producer log for the late case: ``` P2P <producer-ip>:7777: unbound store kv_request_id=park-late-39 timed out after 60s without a fetch - failing 1 job(s) ``` ### Why this fires in practice The window is not exotic. Any deployment where the decode leg's fetch can be issued more than 60 s after the producer stored will hit it, and under saturation that is ordinary: the fetch is only issued once the decode request is admitted, so its delay tracks queueing, not the transfer itself. I see both sides of it in loaded runs - producer-side `unbound store ... timed out` warnings and consumer-side load timeouts on the same `kv_request_id`. Each occurrence costs a 30 s stall plus a full prompt recompute, which feeds back into the saturation that caused the delay in the first place. Both leg-dispatch orders lose, so this cannot be fixed by the caller: - dispatch the legs concurrently and the fetch can arrive **before** the store, so demand parks and the consumer burns its 30 s deadline. This is what llm-d/llm-d-router#2451 fixes on the routing-proxy side, by running the prefill leg to completion before dispatching decode - dispatch them sequentially, as that PR does and as the NIXL path already did, and the store lands first but the fetch can arrive **after** the 60 s reap - this issue ### Steps to reproduce Two instances, `PF` = producer, `DE` = consumer, both with the tiering spec and a `p2p` secondary tier. ```sh M=<model>; ID=park-$$ PROMPT=$(awk 'BEGIN{p="unique-'$ID' ";for(i=0;i<900;i++) p=p "alpha bravo charlie delta echo ";print p}') # producer leg: stores KV under ID, parks it (no peer has fetched yet) curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'producer http=%{http_code} t=%{time_total}\n' \ -X POST "http://$PF:8000/v1/completions" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d "{\"model\":\"$M\",\"prompt\":\"$PROMPT\",\"max_tokens\":1,\"temperature\":0,\"kv_transfer_params\":{\"remote_decoder\":{\"kv_request_id\":\"$ID\"}}}" sleep 65 # 5 reproduces the working control curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'consumer http=%{http_code} t=%{time_total}\n' \ -X POST "http://$DE:8200/v1/completions" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d "{\"model\":\"$M\",\"prompt\":\"$PROMPT\",\"max_tokens\":4,\"temperature\":0,\"kv_transfer_params\":{\"remote_prefiller\":{\"kv_request_id\":\"$ID\",\"remote_host\":\"$PF\",\"remote_port\":7777}}}" # watch vllm:kv_offload_load_bytes_total on the consumer across the pair ``` With `sleep 5` the consumer pulls the blocks in ~0.3 s. With `sleep 65` it transfers nothing and returns after ~38 s. ### The NIXL path already solves this `NixlConnector` faces the same question - how long does P hold blocks that D has not read yet - and answers it with a renewable lease rather than a fixed timer: - `_kv_lease_duration` (`nixl/base_scheduler.py`), default **30 s**, configurable via `kv_lease_duration` - `_heartbeat_interval = _kv_lease_duration // 6`, and D sends periodic lease-renewal heartbeats to P for every request it still intends to read - `decoder_kv_blocks_ttl`, default 480 s, for the client-driven turn-2 case So NIXL's nominal pin is *shorter* than the tier's 60 s, yet a queued consumer never loses its blocks: the lease is tied to consumer liveness, and only a consumer that has actually gone away lets it lapse. The p2p tier has no equivalent - no renewal, no way for the consumer to signal intent, and no config knob - so it cannot distinguish "the peer is still queued" from "the peer will never come". ### Suggested direction Tie the parked store's lifetime to the consumer's liveness instead of a fixed interval from store time. A few shapes that would work: - adopt the NIXL contract: let the consumer renew the parked store the way D renews P's lease, so a queued request keeps its KV and a dead one releases it promptly - failing that, let the consumer register intent for a `kv_request_id` before it is admitted, so the producer knows a peer is coming - at minimum make the interval configurable like `kv_lease_duration` is, since the right value depends on the deployment's admission latency Worth surfacing the reap as its own counter either way - today it is only a warning line, so operators see the consumer's recompute without the producer side that explains it. cc @liranschour

### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Environment (summary) - vLLM v0.27.1, OpenAI-compatible server (Docker), single RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell - Image: official `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.27.1` locally rebuilt with transformers pinned to 5.14.1 (workaround for #51744); vLLM/scheduler code unmodified. Full `collect_env` output in the environment section. - Model: nvidia/Gemma-4-31B-IT-NVFP4, `--max-num-seqs 256 --max-model-len 131072 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90` - MTP speculative decoding via separate BF16 drafter (`num_speculative_tokens: 4`) - `--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser gemma4 --reasoning-parser gemma4` - Clients: LiteLLM proxy → `POST /v1/chat/completions` with SSE streaming + tool calls. We do NOT use the session-based streaming-input / realtime API (no `resumable` requests; verified zero realtime/StreamingInput log lines). ## Symptom During a client traffic burst (~16 req/min sustained, many held open 600 s by the proxy and retried), the scheduler wedged permanently: | UTC | Running | Waiting | deferred | KV cache | gen tok/s | |-------|---------|---------|----------|----------|-----------| | 10:08 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0.0% | idle | | 10:45 | 29 | 92 | 92 | 90.0% | 53.3 | | 10:57 | 3 | 227 | 227 | 20.9% | 1.2 ← collapse | | 12:10 | 4 | 487 | 468 | 20.0% | 5.5 | At 12:20, over a 60 s `/metrics` window: prompt throughput 1,946 tok/s, generation 0.48 tok/s, ~0.2 engine steps/s, `request_success_total` +0 (all finish reasons), `num_preemptions_total` 0, `abort` count 0 over the container's 4-day lifetime. `num_requests_waiting_by_reason`: `deferred` 473, `capacity` 19. GPU at 100% SM / 11% memory-bus (pure prefill), prefix-cache hit rate degraded 77% → 18%. `/health` returned 200 throughout; Docker healthcheck stayed green. The state never recovered on its own (observed >1.5 h); a container restart fully cleared it. ## Analysis - The collapse point matches `len(running) + blocked == max_num_seqs (256)` exactly (227 deferred + 29 running). After that, the admission gate (`num_running = len(self.running) + self.num_waiting_for_streaming_input; if num_running >= self.max_num_running_reqs: break`) appears to break out on every step even though the KV cache is ~80% free. - `reason="deferred"` maps to `len(self.skipped_waiting)` as a whole (`WAITING_FOR_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_GRAMMAR` | `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` | `WAITING_FOR_STREAMING_REQ`), so we cannot tell from metrics which status held the 473. `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` is ruled out (no KV connector configured). We don't use the streaming-input API, which per #28973 is the only path into `WAITING_FOR_STREAMING_REQ` — yet `_try_promote_blocked_waiting_request()` returning `False` unconditionally for that status (unchanged on current `main`) is the same never-promoted pattern PR #45406 describes for `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS`. The remaining candidate is grammar-waiting requests from the tool-call-heavy traffic never being promoted/cleaned; notably, zero xgrammar/structured_output warnings or errors were logged in the incident window, and no requests finished with `finished_reason="error"`. - Whatever the sub-state: requests parked in `skipped_waiting` were never promoted, never aborted, and (apparently) counted against admission, so the engine served ~0 requests indefinitely while accepting new ones and reporting healthy. ## Related (checked, believed non-duplicate) - #45406 / #45387 / #45388: identical structural pattern (parked requests never promoted → `schedule()` empty forever, restart-only), but for the KV-connector status. Still open/unmerged. - #52693 / #52717: same streaming-input code area, but an acute EngineCore crash, not a silent wedge. - #41967: streaming+tool-call under MTP, but a content-corruption bug (closed). ## Repro Production incident; we do not have a standalone repro. Trigger conditions were: sustained concurrent streaming tool-call load (hundreds of connections held open by an upstream proxy with 600 s timeout + retries) against a single engine at `max-num-seqs 256`. Happy to provide fuller metric dumps or log excerpts on request, but our capacity for interactive debugging is limited — treating this primarily as an incident report with data. `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG` and `VLLM_TRACE_FUNCTION=1` were not enabled (production system; the trace overhead is not viable there) — for what it's worth, the standard logs contained zero WARNING/ERROR lines in the entire incident window. If the wedge recurs despite our new admission limits upstream of vLLM, we can attempt a capture with DEBUG logging enabled. We searched existing and past issues before filing; the closest matches and why we believe this is not a duplicate are listed under "Related" below. ## Suggested direction Same as #45406's premise: statuses in `skipped_waiting` need either a promotion path, a cleanup/abort path (e.g., on client disconnect), or exclusion from the admission count — no status should be able to consume scheduler capacity irrevocably. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Bug]: DC unavailable for GlmMoeDsa (GLM-5.2 FP8) on SM90 — sparse MLA backend lacks decode-LSE support
signals.text:
### Your current environment I am working on Air gapped environment, that is why I am posting it here ### 🐛 Describe the bug

Environment

  • vLLM: 0.26.0

  • Hardware: 8× NVIDIA H200 (SM90)

  • Model: GLM-5.2-FP8

  • Resolved architecture: GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM

  • Tensor parallelism: --tensor-parallel-size 8

  • Expert parallelism: --enable-expert-parallel

  • Decode context parallelism: --decode-context-parallel-size 8

  • KV cache dtype: fp8_ds_mla

  • Maximum model length: 131072

Full vllm collect_env output is attached.

Summary

DCP=8 cannot currently be enabled for GLM-5.2 (GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM) on Hopper/SM90 when using the required fp8_ds_mla KV-cache dtype.

The currently available sparse-MLA attention backends appear to have mutually incompatible capabilities:

As a result, there does not currently appear to be a selectable sparse-MLA backend satisfying all of:

SM90 + fp8_ds_mla + decode-LSE + DCP

Reproduction

Using the default sparse MLA backend:

--tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --decode-context-parallel-size 8 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla

the server fails during initialization with:

RuntimeError: DCP requires attention impls to return the softmax lse for decode, but the impl FlashMLASparseImpl does not return the softmax lse for decode.

When forcing:

--attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE

backend selection fails with:

ValueError: Selected backend AttentionBackendEnum.FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE is not valid for this configuration. Reason: [ 'kv_cache_dtype not supported', 'compute capability not supported', 'FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE SM10 does not support fp8_ds_mla kv-cache dtype' ]

Why this matters

GLM-5.2 uses sparse MLA with a single latent KV head. With TP=8, the KV cache is replicated across the tensor-parallel ranks.

For our workload, this significantly limits long-context decode concurrency.

At a 262,144-token request length, the measured maximum concurrency is approximately 1.50×, corresponding to roughly 393K KV tokens per GPU against approximately 20 GB of available KV-cache memory.

DCP would allow the decode attention workload to be distributed across the 8 GPUs, which is important for our long-context serving workload.

Question for maintainers

Is decode-LSE support planned for FLASHMLA_SPARSE on SM90?

FLASHMLA_SPARSE appears to be the only currently available backend that satisfies both:

  1. SM90 support

  2. fp8_ds_mla KV-cache support

However, DCP currently rejects it because:

can_return_lse_for_decode = False

The underlying flash_mla_sparse_fwd operation appears to expose LSE as an output already. Is the remaining blocker primarily in the vLLM integration layer, or does making FLASHMLA_SPARSE DCP-compatible also require changes to the sparse MLA/indexer path?

In particular, does DCP require the sparse MLA index/top-k selection to be coordinated across DCP ranks, rather than only exposing the decode LSE?

If so, what is the intended implementation path for making FLASHMLA_SPARSE DCP-compatible on SM90?

Related issues

This appears related to the existing GLM-5.2 / DCP work in #50095, as well as earlier sparse-MLA/DCP issues such as #45425 and #48611.

The specific capability gap I'm tracking is:

SM90 + fp8_ds_mla + decode-LSE + DCP=8

At present, no available sparse-MLA backend appears to satisfy all four requirements.

Attachments

  • Full python -m vllm.collect_env output

  • nvidia-smi output

  • Full traceback using default FLASHMLA_SPARSE

  • Full traceback when forcing FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE

  • Full vLLM serving command/configuration

signals.title: [Bug][ROCm] All-reduce dispatch has an 8–16 MiB "dead zone" on ROCm (CUSTOM's per-world-size table is CUDA-only) that forces PyNCCL/RCCL, which then crashes with `hipErrorLaunchOutOfResources`
signals.text: ### Your current environment <details> <summary>collect_env output (summary; full output attached)</summary> - vLLM: `0.23.1.dev1+g9ddef7117.d20260715` — official ROCm image `rocm/vllm:rocm7.14.0_cdna_ubuntu24.04_py3.14_pytorch_2.11.0_vllm_0.23.0` - PyTorch: 2.11.0 (ROCm 7.14.0), Python 3.14 - RCCL: 2.30.4-HEAD:2b22ab0 (from `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` output) - Hardware: 8× AMD Instinct MI300X (gfx942), single node, TP=8 - Model: an FP8-quantized MoE model, bf16 activations, `hidden_size=6144`. The mechanism below is dtype/size-driven, not model-specific — any TP=8, bf16-activation model on ROCm is exposed to it. - Launch flags relevant to repro: `--tensor-parallel-size 8 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 1 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048` (chunked prefill), `VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=FP` </details> ### 🐛 Describe the bug Serving with TP=8 and chunked prefill (`--max-num-batched-tokens 2048`), a prompt whose total token count is *not* an exact multiple of 2048 produces one final, smaller "remainder" chunk. **If that remainder chunk's all-reduce message happens to land between 8 MiB and 16 MiB, it is silently routed to PyNCCL — bypassing both of vLLM's faster ROCm all-reduce backends — where RCCL's consolidated generic collective kernel then crashes:** ``` hipModuleLaunchKernel kernel=_Z23ncclDevKernel_Generic_224ncclDevKernelArgsStorageILm4096EE grid=(56,1,1) block=(256,1,1) lds=0 -> ret=701 (too many resources requested for launch) ``` ``` RuntimeError: NCCL error: unhandled cuda error (run with NCCL_DEBUG=INFO for details) File ".../vllm/distributed/device_communicators/cuda_communicator.py", line 295, in all_reduce out = pynccl_comm.all_reduce(input_) File ".../vllm/distributed/device_communicators/pynccl.py", line 188, in all_reduce self.nccl.ncclAllReduce(...) File ".../vllm/distributed/device_communicators/pynccl_wrapper.py", line 388, in NCCL_CHECK raise RuntimeError(f"NCCL error: {error_str}") ``` All 8 TP workers fail on the identical kernel/grid/error within microseconds of each other — the synchronous-collective-failing-in-lockstep pattern, confirmed via an `LD_PRELOAD` HIP-launch shim that resolves kernel names on any non-zero return code. **Root cause traced by reading the actual dispatch source (`cuda_communicator.py`, `quick_all_reduce.py`, `custom_all_reduce.py`, `all_reduce_utils.py`) and confirming live with one temporary debug print at the `pynccl_comm.all_reduce()` call site:** 1. `CustomAllreduce.should_custom_ar` gates on `inp_size < self.max_size`, where `max_size = min(CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE_MAX_SIZES[device_capability_str][world_size], 8*1024*1024)` (`custom_all_reduce.py`). **`CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE_MAX_SIZES`'s keys (`all_reduce_utils.py`) are CUDA compute-capability strings only** (`"9.0"`, `"10.0"`, `"10.3"` — H100/B100/B200-class). A ROCm `device_capability_str` never matches any of them, so on **every** ROCm run `max_size` silently falls back to the flat **8 MiB** Python default, regardless of TP degree. (`SYMM_MEM_ALL_REDUCE_MAX_SIZES` has the identical gap, though that path is CUDA-only today so it's latent rather than active.) 2. `QuickAllReduce.should_quick_allreduce` gates on `min_size <= inp_size <= qr_max_size`. With `VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=FP` (the only setting under which QUICK_REDUCE is enabled at all — default is `NONE`), `_QR_MIN_SIZE[(bf16, world_size=8)][FP]` = **16 MiB**. 3. **Any message sized `[8 MiB, 16 MiB)` satisfies neither gate** and falls through to PyNCCL/RCCL unconditionally — not because of an unusual dtype, shape, or non-contiguous tensor, just because both size windows miss it by construction. Confirmed live: the crashing message measured exactly `shape=(1189, 6144)`, bf16 → `1189 × 6144 × 2 = 14,610,432 bytes ≈ 13.93 MiB` — squarely in the gap. Logged at the same call site: `dtype=torch.bfloat16 contig=True weak_contig=True mod16=0` — every other QUICK_REDUCE gate (dtype, 16-byte alignment, `is_weak_contiguous`) passes cleanly; size alone routes it to PyNCCL. **Verified workaround (env-var only, no code change):** setting `VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_MIN_SIZE_BYTES_MB=1` lowers QUICK_REDUCE's floor below 8 MiB and closes the gap. The identical request that crashed deterministically (twice, in 32.8s and 34.7s, byte-identical kernel/error signature both times) then completes cleanly: zero PyNCCL fallback calls at that call site, zero `ret=701` events, server stays healthy afterward. ### Two separable issues here 1. **(This repo, clear bug, small fix.)** `CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE_MAX_SIZES` / `SYMM_MEM_ALL_REDUCE_MAX_SIZES` in `all_reduce_utils.py` have no ROCm/gfx9xx entries, so `CustomAllreduce`'s per-world-size sizing silently collapses to a flat 8 MiB cap on every ROCm GPU regardless of TP degree — this looks unintentional (the CUDA table is clearly meant to scale down as world_size grows; ROCm gets no equivalent table at all) and it's what creates the size gap against QUICK_REDUCE's 16 MiB floor in the first place. Two ways to close it that don't require touching RCCL: add ROCm entries to the size table (matching CUSTOM's max up with QUICK_REDUCE's min for whatever world_size/dtype combos are supported), or lower `QuickAllReduce`'s default `_QR_MIN_SIZE` so it doesn't leave a gap above CUSTOM's ROCm default. We're not proposing a specific patch since either fix shape has tradeoffs only you can weigh (buffer sizing, perf) — happy to test whichever you'd prefer on our 8×MI300X node. 2. **(Likely ROCm/rccl, unconfirmed root cause.)** `ncclDevKernel_Generic_2` — RCCL's consolidated generic collective kernel — resource-faults (`hipErrorLaunchOutOfResources`) on what should be an unremarkable ~14 MiB AllReduce on 8×gfx942. We don't have a minimal RCCL-only (non-vLLM) repro to isolate this further yet, but it is 100% deterministic and reproduces identically across separate process launches at the same message size/channel count. If (1) above is fixed, this stops being reachable through vLLM's default dispatch — but it seems worth knowing about independently, since any other RCCL caller hitting this exact size class on MI300X would presumably hit the same fault. Happy to file this half separately on `ROCm/rccl` if that's more useful to you than folding it in here — let us know. ### Repro ```bash # image: rocm/vllm:rocm7.14.0_cdna_ubuntu24.04_py3.14_pytorch_2.11.0_vllm_0.23.0 python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model <any FP8 MoE model, hidden_size=6144, bf16 activations> \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 1 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 --trust-remote-code --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 # env: VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=FP (other env vars omitted, not load-bearing for this bug) ``` Send any prompt whose total token count `T` satisfies `T mod 2048` in roughly **[683, 1365]** (the exact bounds scale with `hidden_size`/dtype — this is `[8 MiB, 16 MiB)` in bytes for the final chunked-prefill chunk). We reproduced with `T ≈ 79,013` (`T mod 2048 = 1189`), `max_tokens=1` (prefill-dominated), deterministic, ~33s to crash. A shorter, cheaper repro at the same `T mod 2048` remainder should reproduce identically without needing a long prompt — we didn't get to minimize prompt length before filing; happy to do that if useful. Full logs available: HIP-launch-shim capture across all 8 workers (kernel name/grid/return code), the Python traceback, and the size/dtype/contiguity instrumentation referenced above. Attached / gist-linked below. **Evidence bundle (gist):** https://gist.github.com/skimanwhite/2db33bce00981e15ed853b1b21acaf72 - HIP-launch shim capture, all 8 TP workers, identical `ret=701` signature - Full Python traceback down to `pynccl_wrapper.py`'s `NCCL_CHECK`, plus the size/dtype/contiguity instrumentation line for the failing message - The ~17-line temporary debug patch to `cuda_communicator.py` used to capture the above (instrumentation only, not a proposed fix) - Before/after repro: crashes twice (byte-identical signature) without the workaround env var, succeeds cleanly with it

signals.title: [Bug]: tools/recipes/recipe_json_to_vllm_config.py silently mis-parses the -cc (compilation-config) short alias
signals.text: ### Your current environment This is a pure argument-parsing logic bug in a standalone offline script (`tools/recipes/recipe_json_to_vllm_config.py`) — it does not touch vLLM's runtime/engine, GPUs, or model loading, so `collect_env.py` output isn't applicable. Repro requires only Python + `pyyaml` + network access to `recipes.vllm.ai`. - File as of commit `9b3382685e85` (2026-08-12), latest touching this path - Python 3.14 (bug is version-independent — pure string/list parsing) - `PyYAML` (script's only dependency) ### 🐛 Describe the bug `recipe_json_to_vllm_config.py` silently produces a **wrong** `config.yml` for any recipe whose `argv` uses the `-cc` (compilation-config) short alias with dotted inline assignment, e.g. `-cc.pass_config.fuse_rope_kvcache=True`. It does not error or warn — it just corrupts the output. **Repro:** ```bash python3 tools/recipes/recipe_json_to_vllm_config.py \ --model openai/gpt-oss-120b --hardware mi300x ``` This resolves to `https://recipes.vllm.ai/openai/gpt-oss-120b/hw/mi300x.json`, whose `argv` is: ```json ["vllm", "serve", "openai/gpt-oss-120b", "--tensor-parallel-size", "1", "--attention-backend", "ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN", "-cc.pass_config.fuse_rope_kvcache=True", "-cc.use_inductor_graph_partition=True", "--gpu-memory-utilization", "0.95", "--block-size=64", "--tool-call-parser", "openai", "--enable-auto-tool-choice"] ``` **Expected:** `config.yml` contains a `compilation-config:` mapping with `pass_config.fuse_rope_kvcache: true` and `use_inductor_graph_partition: true`, and `attention-backend: ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` as a scalar. **Actual:** the generated `config.yml` is: ```yaml model: openai/gpt-oss-120b tensor-parallel-size: 1 attention-backend: - ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN - -cc.pass_config.fuse_rope_kvcache=True - -cc.use_inductor_graph_partition=True gpu-memory-utilization: 0.95 block-size: 64 tool-call-parser: openai enable-auto-tool-choice: true ``` `--attention-backend` has become a 3-element list containing two garbage strings, and the `compilation-config` settings are lost entirely. This is the Recipes-recommended AMD MI300X config for a shipping model, not a synthetic edge case. **Root cause:** After consuming `--attention-backend`, `argv_to_config()` gathers subsequent tokens as values until it sees the next option: ```python while i < len(argv) and not is_option_token(argv[i]): raw_values.append(argv[i]) i += 1 ``` `is_option_token()` is: ```python def is_option_token(token: str) -> bool: if token.startswith("--"): return True if token in SHORT_ALIASES or token == "-O": return True return token.startswith("-O") and len(token) > 2 ``` `SHORT_ALIASES` only contains `-tp`, `-pp`, `-dp`. The token `-cc.pass_config.fuse_rope_kvcache=True` doesn't start with `--`, isn't in `SHORT_ALIASES`, isn't `-O`, and doesn't start with `-O` — so `is_option_token()` returns `False`, and it gets swallowed as an extra value of the *preceding* flag instead of being recognized as the start of a new option. The script has no handling for `-cc` at all, even though `-cc.<field>=<value>` is real vLLM CLI syntax (`--compilation-config` / `-cc`) that the Recipes API actively emits. **Suggested fix:** 1. Add `-cc` to `SHORT_ALIASES`: ```python SHORT_ALIASES = { "-tp": "tensor-parallel-size", "-pp": "pipeline-parallel-size", "-dp": "data-parallel-size", "-cc": "compilation-config", } ``` 2. Make `is_option_token()` also recognize the dotted inline form as an option boundary: ```python if any(token.startswith(a + ".") for a in SHORT_ALIASES): return True ``` 3. In `argv_to_config()`, handle `-cc.<dotted.path>=<value>` by splitting off the alias, treating the remainder as a dotted path under `compilation-config`, and merging via the existing `merge_value()` / `normalize_key()` helpers — the same machinery already used for `--key.path=value`. I've implemented and verified this fix (confirmed it correctly produces a nested `compilation-config` block for the recipe above) and am happy to open a PR if that's useful. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Searched existing/past issues and PRs (`argv_to_config`, `is_option_token`, `tools/recipes`, `compilation-config`, `fuse_rope_kvcache`, `-cc.pass_config`) — no existing report. The two PRs that built this tool (#51308, #51878) never touch `SHORT_ALIASES` or `-cc` handling, so this has been present since the tool was introduced.

signals.title: [Bug]: /metrics ignores Prometheus name[] query filters
signals.text: ### Your current environment <details> <summary>Relevant environment</summary> ```text vLLM source: main at d626108 Python: 3.12.14 prometheus-client: 0.25.0 prometheus-fastapi-instrumentator: 8.0.0 FastAPI: 0.136.3 Starlette: 1.6.0 ``` This issue is isolated to the ASGI metrics endpoint and is not GPU- or model-dependent. </details> ### 🐛 Describe the bug Upper-layer schedulers and resource managers, such as llm-d and aibrix, rely on the `/metrics` endpoint to retrieve selected vLLM resource-utilization metrics for placement, routing, and scaling decisions. The default HTTP exposition implementation provided by `prometheus_client` supports repeated `name[]` parameters so these consumers can request only the samples they need. vLLM currently does not preserve this default capability. Every filtered request instead returns the full, potentially large metrics payload, forcing the server to serialize and transfer unrelated samples and the caller to receive, parse, and discard them. With frequent scheduler polling or many vLLM instances, this wastes substantial network bandwidth and CPU resources on both sides. The `/metrics` endpoint ignores the `name[]` query parameter supported by `prometheus_client` for returning selected metric samples. ### Reproduction 1. Start a vLLM server: ```bash vllm serve facebook/opt-125m ``` 2. Request one metric: ```bash curl -sG http://localhost:8000/metrics \ --data-urlencode 'name[]=vllm:num_requests_waiting' ``` ### Observed behavior The response contains the complete metrics payload, including unrelated metrics. ### Expected behavior The response should contain only the requested sample. Repeated parameters should also work: ```text /metrics?name[]=vllm:num_requests_waiting&name[]=vllm:prompt_tokens_total ``` An unknown metric name should return an empty `200 OK` response. Requests without `name[]` must continue returning all metrics. ### Root cause `attach_router()` registers the endpoint through `Instrumentator.expose()` before appending the `prometheus_client` ASGI mount. FastAPI resolves the first route, so `prometheus_client.make_asgi_app()` never receives the query parameters. Multiprocess mode also requires special handling because `MultiProcessCollector` can discover metric names after registry registration. The default restricted registry can therefore return an empty response for valid late-discovered metrics. ### Suggested fix Serve `/metrics` through the Prometheus ASGI application without adding the duplicate Instrumentator exposition route, while filtering multiprocess samples after collection. The implementation should preserve: - Existing unfiltered `/metrics` behavior. - Repeated `name[]` parameters. - Counter sample filtering such as `_total` without implicitly returning `_created`. - Late-discovered metrics in multiprocess mode. I searched existing and historical issues and open PRs for Prometheus metric filtering, `name[]`, and restricted registries and did not find a matching report. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
