signals.title: [Feature][Model Runner V2] Support extract_hidden_states speculation
signals.text: ## Purpose Fixes #49562. `extract_hidden_states` is supported by the existing model runner, but Model Runner V2 currently rejects the configuration and has no speculator for forwarding the sampled token while caching the target model's auxiliary hidden states. This PR: - allows the `extract_hidden_states` speculative method with Model Runner V2; - requests auxiliary hidden-state outputs from the target model; - adds a Model Runner V2 `ExtractHiddenStatesSpeculator` that forwards sampled tokens and caches the selected hidden states through the existing `ExtractHiddenStatesModel`; - adds focused configuration, dispatch, cache, and failure-path tests. Duplicate-work check on 2026-07-25: - #49562 was open with no assignee or comments; - searching open PR bodies for `49562` returned no results, and this fork head had no existing PR; - #46399 concerns dynamic speculative decoding for fixed-K proposers, while #46788 concerns DeepSeek auxiliary-layer indexing. Neither implements Model Runner V2 support for this method. AI assistance was used to help implement and validate this change. The submitter reviewed every changed line and understands the change end-to-end. ## Test Plan The final patch was reapplied to upstream main `33ef67e9fb5f3f9c2dfe1aa95e9880d5ecd7b38b`, then checked with: ```bash git diff --check ruff check \ tests/test_config.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_extract_hidden_states_speculator.py \ vllm/config/vllm.py \ vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py \ vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/__init__.py \ vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/extract_hidden_states.py ruff format --check \ tests/test_config.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_extract_hidden_states_speculator.py \ vllm/config/vllm.py \ vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py \ vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/__init__.py \ vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/extract_hidden_states.py mypy vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/extract_hidden_states.py python -m pytest \ tests/test_config.py::test_v2_model_runner_supports_extract_hidden_states \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_extract_hidden_states_speculator.py \ tests/v1/spec_decode/test_extract_hidden_states.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2_eplb.py -q ``` The predictable-model GPU E2E was run on one RTX 3090 with driver `580.65.06`, PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`, and the CUDA 13 toolkit: ```bash CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda-13.0 \ VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 \ VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 \ CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ python -m pytest \ tests/v1/kv_connector/extract_hidden_states_integration/test_extraction.py::test_extract_hidden_states_with_predictable_dummy_model \ -v -s ``` `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0` avoids compiling the unrelated FlashInfer sampling JIT during this feature test. A validation-only tokenizer fixture adjustment used the data-disk Hugging Face cache and `AutoTokenizer`; it was reversed immediately after the run and is not present in the commit. ## Test Result - `git diff --check`: passed. - Ruff: `All checks passed!`. - Ruff format: `6 files already formatted`. - Direct Mypy check for the new production module: `Success: no issues found in 1 source file`. - Related regression tests: `19 passed, 14 warnings in 5.52s`. - Predictable-model Model Runner V2 GPU E2E: `1 passed, 16 warnings in 64.39s`; the engine log explicitly reported `Using V2 Model Runner`. - The final commit contains exactly six files: 293 insertions and 2 deletions. The changed-file Mypy wrapper still returns nonzero because upstream `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py` has five existing errors at lines 514, 586, 1141, 1315, and 1585. These locations are outside this PR's only `model_runner.py` hunk (around line 198). The new module and both test files pass their Mypy groups. The Git pre-commit hook bootstrap could not complete because fetching the `ruff-pre-commit` environment from GitHub timed out. The scoped Ruff, format, Mypy, diff, and pytest commands above were run manually, and the commit was created with `--no-verify`. Earlier validation on the preceding main snapshot also completed a full CUDA 13 CMake/Ninja build and a custom-op numerical check with `max_abs_error=0.0`. Qwen3.5 hybrid and two-GPU tensor-parallel smoke tests each passed there. Those two model smoke tests were not rerun in this publish turn; the two intervening upstream commits do not overlap this PR's six files. No accuracy or performance benchmark was run. This change wires existing hidden-state extraction behavior into Model Runner V2; the GPU E2E validates sampled-token generation, hidden-state export, layer values, chunked prefill, and per-request output options. --- <details> <summary>Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist</summary> - [x] The purpose and resolving issue are included. - [x] The test plan includes the commands used. - [x] The test results and limitations are included. - [x] Documentation impact was considered; no user-facing configuration or model-support documentation changes are required. </details>

signals.title: [Rust Frontend] Support --allowed-media-domains
signals.text: ## Purpose `--allowed-media-domains` is declared in `UnsupportedArgs`, so passing it to the Rust frontend aborts startup with "not implemented in Rust frontend yet". At the same time `MultimodalModelInfo` always builds its `MediaConnector` with `MediaConnectorConfig::default()`, which allows any remote host. `llm-multimodal` already implements the host match, so this only wires the argument through: CLI -> `Config` -> `LoadModelBackendsOptions` -> `MediaConnectorConfig`. No engine-side change. Behavior matches `vllm/multimodal/media/connector.py`: - `--allowed-media-domains` unset: any host is allowed. - `VLLM_MEDIA_URL_ALLOW_REDIRECTS=0`: the media HTTP client is built with `Policy::none()`, so an allow-listed host cannot bounce a fetch to a disallowed target. Unset or non-zero keeps `reqwest`'s default follow behavior, mirroring `allow_redirects=envs.VLLM_MEDIA_URL_ALLOW_REDIRECTS`. ## Not duplicating an existing PR No other open PR wires media-access restrictions into the Rust frontend; `--allowed-media-domains` is still listed under `UnsupportedArgs` on `main`. ## Scope: `--allowed-local-media-path` is deliberately left out An earlier revision of this PR also wired `--allowed-local-media-path`, but it cannot work against the currently pinned `llm-multimodal` (rev `15adba5`): - `MediaContentPart` has no file variant, so a `file://` input arrives as `ImageUrl`/`AudioUrl`/`VideoUrl` carrying a string. - `AsyncMultiModalTracker::push_part` special-cases only `data:` and routes everything else, `file:` included, to `MediaSource::Url`. - `enqueue_image`/`enqueue_audio`/`enqueue_video` are private, and there is no public API that accepts a `MediaSource`, so the frontend cannot reach the guarded `MediaSource::File` path. The option would therefore be silently inert: the connector would attempt an HTTP request for a `file:` URL instead of the canonicalize-and-prefix-check path. Rather than ship a security flag that does nothing, `--allowed-local-media-path` stays in `UnsupportedArgs` (unchanged from `main`, so this is not a behavior regression) with a `TODO` in `server/src/config.rs`. It can be wired in a follow-up once the crate routes `file:` to `MediaSource::File`. Per-redirect-hop host re-validation was also raised in review. It is intentionally not added here: `connector.py` validates only the initially supplied URL and relies on `VLLM_MEDIA_URL_ALLOW_REDIRECTS` as the mitigation, which this PR now honors. Hardening past the Python path belongs in `llm-multimodal`, where the allow-list lives. ## Test Plan ``` cargo fmt --all -- --check cargo clippy -p vllm-cmd -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server --all-targets -- -D warnings cargo test -p vllm-cmd -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server ``` New tests in `rust/src/cmd/src/cli/tests.rs` cover the `vllm-rs serve` flag and the `--args-json` path used by the Python supervisor, plus the unset default. `rust/src/chat/src/multimodal.rs` adds redirect tests over a local HTTP server: an allow-listed host that 302s to a non-allow-listed host is reached under the default policy and blocked under `Policy::none()`, and a disallowed initial host is rejected outright. ## Test Result fmt and clippy clean, 706 tests pass across the three crates. Note: this change was AI-assisted; every changed line was reviewed by me and the commands above were run locally. CC: @BugenZhao

signals.title: [Model] Fix GLM-OCR MTP weight loading
signals.text: ### Summary - recognize `model.language_model.layers.*` as a valid MTP checkpoint prefix - add regression coverage for all supported MTP layer prefixes - preserve the existing behavior when the model has no MTP layers ### Why Fixes #49856. The current `zai-org/GLM-OCR` checkpoint stores its appended MTP layer under `model.language_model.layers.16.*`. `GlmOcrMTP.load_weights()` calls `get_spec_layer_idx_from_weight_name()` before `_rewrite_spec_layer_name()` removes the `language_model` wrapper. The classifier previously recognized only `model.layers.*` and `layers.*`. Consequently, every nested GLM-OCR MTP weight was classified as a non-MTP weight and skipped before its name could be rewritten, leaving eight draft parameters uninitialized. This change teaches the common classifier about the nested language-model prefix. Keeping the handling in the classifier also makes `skip_spec_layers()` apply the same classification when loading the target model. ### Validation Hardware and software: - NVIDIA RTX 4090 - Python 3.12 - PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130 - original reproduction source commit `833483f3578a2c4766977d0fe431bd32a01ce250` - repeated post-fix validation on rebased PR head `c23502a49f58533131b8baaf2a075197ba43984c` - `zai-org/GLM-OCR` revision `ca5d8b3e287e52589e37c28385d9655ee4372f9d` Before the change: ```text ValueError: Following weights were not initialized from checkpoint: model.layers.16.enorm.weight model.layers.16.hnorm.weight model.layers.16.eh_proj.weight model.layers.16.shared_head.norm.weight model.layers.16.mtp_block.input_layernorm.weight model.layers.16.mtp_block.post_attention_layernorm.weight model.layers.16.mtp_block.post_mlp_layernorm.weight model.layers.16.mtp_block.post_self_attn_layernorm.weight ``` After the change: - the MTP drafter loads successfully - `/health` becomes ready - an OpenAI-compatible multimodal request completes successfully - an image containing `vLLM MTP smoke test 49856` is transcribed exactly End-to-end server command: ```bash vllm serve zai-org/GLM-OCR \ --served-model-name glm-ocr \ --max-model-len 4096 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \ --max-num-seqs 8 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \ --enforce-eager \ --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}' curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8000/health ``` The OCR response contained: ```json { "content": "vLLM MTP smoke test 49856" } ``` Tests and checks: ```text .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/models/test_utils.py 12 passed .venv/bin/python -m ruff check \ vllm/model_executor/models/utils.py tests/models/test_utils.py All checks passed! .venv/bin/python -m ruff format --check \ vllm/model_executor/models/utils.py tests/models/test_utils.py 2 files already formatted git diff --check No errors. ``` After rebasing onto `upstream/main` at `14617c2b`, the focused tests and end-to-end GPU validation were repeated on PR head `c23502a49f58533131b8baaf2a075197ba43984c`. With the default V2 runner, the MTP drafter loaded successfully without the eight uninitialized-parameter error, and startup proceeded to the unrelated CUDA graph capture failure tracked by #51966. With `--enforce-eager` to bypass that independent graph-capture path, `/health` and `/v1/models` returned HTTP 200, and the multimodal OCR request completed with the exact output `vLLM MTP smoke test 49856`. ### Duplicate-work check Before opening this PR, searches for #49856, GLM-OCR MTP loading, and `model.language_model.layers` plus `get_spec_layer_idx_from_weight_name` found no open PR implementing this fix. Another contributor posted an intent to investigate shortly before this PR was opened, but no implementation or PR was available; this PR comes from an independently completed reproduction and validated fix. ### AI assistance disclosure AI assistance was used for issue triage, root-cause analysis, drafting the regression tests, and organizing the validation. I reviewed the changed code and validation results and am responsible for the contribution.

signals.title: SM120 NVFP4 KV cache support + MTP cudagraph fix + KV offload crash fix
signals.text: ## Summary This PR adds SM120 (RTX 5090, Blackwell consumer) NVFP4 KV cache support to vLLM, fixes MTP cudagraph routing for draft models, and fixes a crash in KV offloading when requests are aborted mid-transfer. ## Changes ### 1. SM120 NVFP4 KV Cache Support (`flashinfer.py`, `flashinfer.py` utils) SM120 does not support native TRTLLM-GEN cubins, so NVFP4 KV cache must route through the FlashInfer FA2 Tensor-Core native path. Changes include: - **`supports_kv_cache_dtype`**: Declare NVFP4 support for SM120 FA2 path - **HND layout**: Use 4-D `(B, 2*N_kv, N, F)` layout instead of 5-D for contiguous strides with `reshape_and_cache_flash` - **`use_fa2_nvfp4_kv` flag**: Routes SM120 NVFP4 through FA2 native instead of trtllm-gen - **Backend selection**: Correct backend chosen for SM120 NVFP4 prefill and decode - **`kv_data_type=torch.uint8`**: NVFP4 data stored as uint8 pairs - **`o_dtype=BF16`**: Output dtype for FA2 NVFP4 path - **Cudagraph prefill wrappers**: Support cudagraph capture for prefill wrappers on SM120 - **`_uniform_decode_query_len`**: Return correct query length for uniform decode batches - **`_prefill_wrappers_cudagraph`**: Properly handle prefill wrapper cudagraph capture - **`_prefill_qo_indptr_gpu`**: GPU-side qo_indptr for prefill - **`needs_fp8_out` guards**: Skip FP8 output checks for NVFP4 path ### 2. MTP Cudagraph Fix (`llm_base_proposer.py`, `gpu_model_runner.py`, `dflash.py`, `extract_hidden_states.py`) Fixes MTP (Multi-Token Prediction) speculative decoding performance by ensuring correct cudagraph mode routing: - **`initialize_cudagraph_keys`**: Use `cudagraph_mode` directly instead of forcing PIECEWISE for eagle draft - **`propose()` first pass**: Detect uniform decode (`max_query_len == 1`) and pass `uniform_decode` hint to dispatcher, enabling FULL cudagraph matching - **Auto-regressive loop**: Pass `uniform_decode=True` since all subsequent drafts are pure decode - **`dummy_run()`**: New `target_cudagraph_mode` parameter to pass the target model's cudagraph mode - **`gpu_model_runner.py`**: Allow FULL cudagraph for draft model; pass `target_cudagraph_mode` to drafter - **`_determine_batch_execution_and_padding`**: New `forced_cudagraph_mode` and `uniform_decode` parameters for explicit cudagraph control - **API compatibility**: `dflash.py` and `extract_hidden_states.py` accept new `target_cudagraph_mode` parameter ### 3. KV Offload Crash Fix (`offloading/scheduler.py`, `offloading_connector.py`) Fixes a crash when a request is aborted while KV blocks are mid-transfer in the offloading connector: - **`update_offload_keys()`**: New `limit_by_block_ids` parameter to scope key updates to specific blocks - **`request_finished()`**: New `block_ids` parameter to properly clean up only the blocks belonging to the finished request - **`offloading_connector.py`**: Passes `block_ids` to `request_finished()` in both single and group completion paths ### 4. JIT Warmup (`gpu_worker.py`) - Added `profile_run()` before `memory_profiling()` to trigger FlashInfer JIT compilation early, preventing OOM during cudagraph capture when kernels compile on-demand. ## Test Plan - [x] Verified on RTX 5090 (SM120) with Qwen3-Next / Gemma-4 models using NVFP4 KV cache - [x] Verified MTP speculative decoding achieves expected speedup with NVFP4 KV cache - [x] Verified KV offloading no longer crashes on aborted requests - [x] Verified BF16 and FP8 KV cache paths remain unaffected

signals.title: [Doc] Document FP8 GEMM kernel selection and Blackwell support
signals.text: ## Purpose The FP8 page was out of date and gave users nothing to debug with: - It said only Hopper and Ada Lovelace support W8A8 — Blackwell was missing. - Nothing explained which GEMM kernel vLLM picks, or what to do when the choice goes wrong. This came up in #46619, where a Blackwell user hit a silent hang with no way to tell what was happening. This PR adds Blackwell to the supported-hardware lines and a note covering: - vLLM picks the kernel at load time and logs `Selected <kernel> for <module>` at startup. - The actual CUDA candidate order — FlashInfer/DeepGEMM hybrid (Hopper only), DeepGEMM, CUTLASS, Marlin, Triton, Humming, PyTorch — per `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py:378-386`. GPUs without native FP8 land on weight-only (W8A16) Marlin. - The concrete workaround for #46619's symptom: if inference hangs with no error, `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0` or `--linear-backend cutlass`. - That `--linear-backend` covers quantized linear layers only — MoE experts use the separate `--moe-backend` (`vllm/config/kernel.py:191` vs `:216`). - That an unsupported explicit backend raises rather than silently falling back (`linear/__init__.py:590-612`). - A `vllm serve --help=KernelConfig` pointer, matching the already-merged `modelopt.md:32-34`. ### Why the CODEOWNERS hunk is bundled here No CODEOWNERS rule matched `docs/features/quantization`, so this PR was opened with **zero** auto-requested reviewers while sibling PRs of mine got 4 and 10. The added line mirrors the existing owner list for the quantization code at `/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization`, and sits above `/docs/**/*.yml` so @hmellor keeps docs-YAML precedence under last-match-wins. It is net-new coverage for 17 pages, not a duplicate of any existing rule. Per `AGENTS.md`, mechanical cleanups belong bundled with substantive work rather than opened alone — hence here rather than as its own PR. Happy to split it out if you'd rather. Not a duplicate: no PR references #46619. The open #48782 edits a different file (ModelOpt/NVFP4). ## Test Plan ```bash pre-commit run --files docs/features/quantization/llm_compressor/fp8.md .github/CODEOWNERS mkdocs build --strict ``` Claims in the note were re-derived from `main` rather than from memory: the candidate array, the SM90 gate on the FlashInfer hybrid (`vllm/utils/flashinfer.py:938-944`), the `linear_backend`/`moe_backend` split, and the raise-on-unsupported path. ## Test Result `pre-commit` — **6 passed, 0 failed**, including `markdownlint-cli2` and `typos`. `mkdocs build --strict` — **currently fails on `main`, for an unrelated reason.** The single strict-mode warning is: ``` WARNING - griffe: vllm/benchmarks/throughput.py:535: No type or annotation for parameter 'args' Aborted with 1 warnings in strict mode! ``` That file is not in this diff and is byte-identical to `origin/main` here; it was last touched by e07532b03 (#50981) earlier today. This PR's two files produce zero warnings. I have not broadened this PR to fix it — flagging it separately since it breaks the strict docs build for everyone on `main` right now. ### Model evaluation Not applicable — docs and a CODEOWNERS line, no runtime behaviour changed. --- AI assistance was used for planning and implementation, including a cross-model review pass that caught a factual error in the first version of this note (it described the fallback chain as DeepGEMM → CUTLASS → Triton, omitting Marlin between the latter two, and omitted the FlashInfer hybrid entirely). I reviewed every changed line, verified each claim against `main` myself, and ran the commands above.

signals.title: [EC Connector] EC Offloading Connector use events instead of StepTracker
signals.text: ## Purpose The CPU encoder-cache offloading connector (`ECCPUConnector`) gated cache-entry transitions on a step-count heuristic (`StepTracker`): a save was marked ready, and a load unpinned, after a fixed number of engine steps — a fragile proxy for DMA completion that can hold blocks pinned too long. This PR replaces it with a real CUDA-event completion signal: - The worker brackets each batched GPU copy with start/end events on a CUDA stream, polls `end_event.query()`, and reports completed `mm_hash`es to the scheduler via `ECCPUWorkerMetadata`. - The scheduler's `update_connector_output()` then marks completed saves ready and unpins completed loads; `has_pending_push_work()` keeps the engine stepping until every dispatched transfer is confirmed done. - Saves run on a pooled stream gated behind the compute stream (`wait_stream`) so they overlap compute; per-transfer time is logged at debug via `start_event.elapsed_time(end_event)`. - This mimics the Offloading KV connector behavior. `StepTracker` and its tests are removed. Self-contained to the CPU EC connector package; no NIXL/p2p changes. Model outputs are unchanged — this affects only *when* entries are declared ready/unpinned, strengthening the no-read-before- write guarantee. ## Test Plan ```bash source ~/Project9_vllm/vllm-venv/bin/activate python -m pytest tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/cpu/ -v pre-commit run ruff-check --files <changed files> ``` Covers: readiness held until `completed_saves` arrives; loaded entries stay pinned (survive eviction) until `completed_loads`; `has_pending_push_work` /`has_held_entries` track in-flight transfers; foreign/unknown payloads dropped; save/load byte round-trips; end-to-end scheduler↔worker save-then-load.

signals.title: [Bugfix] Bound accepted-token state lookups in GDN/KDA spec decode
signals.text: ## Summary On a hybrid GDN model (Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.6) with MTP speculative decoding and prefix caching (`--mamba-cache-mode align`), the engine dies with `CUDA error: unspecified launch failure` within 7-10 requests of agent-shaped traffic. The GPU faults, not the runtime: the signature is an SM address exception (`Xid 13`, `ESR 0x404000`) or an MMU fault (`Xid 31`), depending on whether the wild address happens to be mapped. > **Validation scope (added 2026-08-19).** Everything below was developed and validated with > `--mamba-cache-mode align` and `--enforce-eager`. That matters: `align` is the only branch in > which `gpu_model_runner` still calls `num_accepted_tokens_event.synchronize()` (the wait is > skipped when `use_async_scheduling and mamba_cache_mode != "align"`), and eager mode removes > CUDA-graph stream structure. So this PR addresses accepted-count-derived indices that are > **correctly synchronized but out of range**. It does **not** address the separate cross-stream > race reported by @noonghunna under async scheduling with the default (non-`align`) mamba cache > mode, where the accepted-count value itself arrives unsynchronized — in-kernel bounds cannot > repair a value that arrives wrong. See the discussion in this thread; that path needs stream > ordering, not bounds. Note `mamba_cache_mode` resolves per-model: with prefix caching and no > explicit flag it is `"all"` (sync skipped) when `model_config.supports_mamba_prefix_caching`, > else `"align"` (sync kept). This is the crash half of the problems reported around hybrid-Mamba + MTP. It is distinct from the prefix-cache corruption in #43559 (the coordinator-level EAGLE cache-peek gating for Mamba), which is already handled on current `main`. This PR does not touch that path and does not claim to fix #43559; it fixes a separate GPU fault in two kernels downstream. ## Root cause: unchecked accepted-count-derived indices Speculative decoding produces a per-request accepted-token count. Multiple GPU state consumers turn that count into an array index without bounding it, so a count that is stale, zero, or too large indexes outside its tensor and yields a wild address the GPU then dereferences. **Site 1** `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel` (`fused_recurrent.py`): ```python i_t = tl.load(num_accepted_tokens + i_n).to(tl.int64) - 1 # unbounded state_idx = tl.load(ssm_state_indices + i_n * stride_indices_seq + i_t) if state_idx <= 0: return # positive garbage passes p_h0 = h0 + state_idx * stride_init_state_token # dereferenced ``` `i_t` (= count - 1) is unbounded against a `stride_indices_seq`-column tensor. A zero accepted count gives `i_t == -1`, a read before this request's row (before the tensor for `i_n == 0`); a stale or too-large count reads past the row. The `state_idx <= 0` guard only rejects non-positive values, so an out-of-range read that returns a garbage positive int flows into the address math and faults the SM. **Site 2** `_copy_mamba_state_block` (`mamba_utils.py`): the block-table columns derive from the same count and index the per-request block-table row unbounded; the loaded block id becomes `state_base_addr + block_id * state_block_stride`, which is then read and written. The two sites fire under different loads. A light decode load exercises only Site 1; a heavy cache-transition load (long prefills, A->B->A prefix reuse) also drives Site 2. Both must be bounded. ## The fix Both loads are masked to the valid range, so an out-of-range index falls into the existing invalid-state path instead of producing an address. No stream-ordering change, no device sync, no measurable throughput cost. ## Test plan RTX 5090 (sm_120), Qwen3.6-27B NVFP4, TP=1, `--enforce-eager --max-model-len 16384`, MTP 3 (`qwen3_5_mtp`), prefix caching on, `align` mode. | build | crash (Xid) | corruption (A->B->A probe) | |---|---|---| | stock | dies at 7-10 requests, Xid every run | 0/N reproduced (already fixed on main) | | Site 1 fix alone | survives light load; still crashes on the first heavy probe (`Xid 31`) | 0/N reproduced | | **both fixes** | **68 heavy probes + a 39-minute soak, 0 new Xid** | **0/68 reproduced** | The A->B->A probe issues an agent-shaped sequence (long prefill, prefix reuse, 20 tool schemas) and reports whether a poisoned prefix reappears; 68/68 returned a clean verdict, which also confirms the out-of-range early-return does not drop a needed state copy. Warm throughput and MTP acceptance length (3.98-4.00 of 4) are unchanged. ## Note: a separate, still-open livelock (#49203) Independently of this crash, the same stack can occasionally hang: engine alive, `/v1/models` answering, but the in-flight request stuck at 0% GPU util with no Xid. It is rare and timing-variable (seen once, then not across the 68 probes here) and matches open issue #49203. This PR does not address it and does not claim to; the 68/68 clean-verdict result rules out this change as a cause. ## Follow-up bounds audit A follow-up audit expanded the same fail-closed rule to the remaining consumers in this path: - Both FLA wrappers now zero rejected output deterministically instead of returning with new_empty storage visible downstream. - _causal_conv1d_update_kernel now bounds the accepted-count offset before state address math; invalid active rows produce zero output and leave state unchanged. - GPU regressions cover too-small/too-large accepted counts, NULL block IDs, source/destination columns crossing the block-table row, and temporal-bias overflow. Validation after this follow-up: full pre-commit passed; on an RTX 5090, 186 FLA/causal-conv kernel tests and all 21 fused Mamba postprocess tests passed (207 total). ## Kimi K3 KDA expansion The same accepted-count-derived state selection pattern also existed in Kimi K3 KDA fused recurrent decode, in both the NVIDIA and AMD vendored kernels. This PR now masks that initial state-index load to the request row, zeroes all invalid-count output tokens, preserves state on invalid counts, and releases NVIDIA PDL dependents before the new empty/invalid early returns. Additional validation on mini-beast RTX 5090: - Patched KDA invalid-count test: 4/4 passed across NVIDIA and AMD implementations (`num_accepted` 0 and 4). - Existing KDA spec-decode correctness plus the new invalid-count target: 12/12 passed. - Negative control at previous PR head `e7f66b199` with only the new test added: 4/4 failed on old KDA for NVIDIA and AMD, proving the regression is non-vacuous. ## AI assistance disclosure OpenAI Codex assisted with the follow-up bounds audit, implementation, and regression-test generation. The submitter owns the conclusions and final review. ## Mamba2 selective-state expansion The Mamba2 selective-state-update kernel also derives its initial state-slot lookup from `num_accepted_tokens - 1`. It already clamps the lower side, but had no upper row bound. This update preserves that zero-count behavior and makes an oversized count fail closed: it writes zero output and returns before reading or writing state. RTX 5090 red/green regression: a count one past a three-column state row made the prior source select an adjacent row and emit nonzero output; the new kernel passes by emitting zero output and preserving the complete state tensor. Pre-commit passes for both changed files.

signals.title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Release a dead peer's NIXL state without waiting for TTL
signals.text: ## Purpose @chaunceyjiang's PR on the NIXL lib ([ai-dynamo/nixl#1987](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/nixl/pull/1987)) correctly fixes the crash in #49238. This PR fixes a missing cache invalidation on the vLLM side that the upstream fix doesn't touch. The D node holds the dead peer's NIXL agents until engine_ttl expires. Depending if the engine id is generated or pinned this may cause failing requetsts. With the generated UUID the replacement comes back under a new key. In this case nothing breaks, the old agents just sit there until the TTL removes them (up to an hour). But with a pinned engine id the replacement reuses the same key. In this case the D node serves stale agents and rkeys for a process that is gone and every request fails. The TTL won't ever clear them because it resets on every requests. Effectively the broken D node needs to be rebooted to fix this. This PR introduces that the cached state is invalidated as soon as the D node can tell the P node is gone: (1) either a transfer to it fails or (2) a new engine registers at a previously used network address. In this case the next request re-handshakes, resolving the issue. Note this does **not** fix the segfault itself. The segfault is fixed by @chaunceyjiang's [ai-dynamo/nixl#1987](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/nixl/pull/1987). This PR is not a duplicate. It fixes a different but related issue. ## Test Plan ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py -q ``` ## Test Result ``` 73 passed, 2 failed ``` All five new tests pass. The two failures are pre-existing (`test_abort_timeout_on_prefiller[ray]` and `[None]`), and fail identically on `main` at the same commit this branch is rebased onto. Sadly I could only unit test this.

signals.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Fix NaN handling in rejection sampler tl.argmax
signals.text: ## Summary `tl.argmax` on an all-NaN block returns an out-of-range block index (pointing into the padded region beyond `num_blocks - 1`). That index is used to load from the local-argmax tensor, producing an out-of-bounds read and an illegal memory access downstream in the rejection sampler. Two kernels in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/rejection_sampler_utils.py` are affected: - `_compute_global_target_argmax` — `tl.argmax(local_max)` at line 111, result used to index `target_local_argmax_ptr` at line 113. - `_insert_resampled_kernel` — `tl.argmax(resampled_local_max)` at line 852, result used to index `resampled_local_argmax_ptr` at line 854. When all values in the (padded) block dimension are NaN — reachable via NaN target logits — `tl.argmax` does not guarantee an in-range result. The loaded garbage index then propagates into subsequent gathers/stores, surfacing as an illegal memory access. **Fix:** in both kernels, map NaN to `-inf` via `tl.where` before `tl.argmax`, and clamp the resulting block index to `num_blocks - 1` with `tl.minimum` as a defensive bound. Two small, surgical changes; no behavior change for non-NaN inputs. ## Symptom / reproduction Observed as an illegal memory access during speculative-decoding warmup (DSpark) when serving Kimi-K3 on 8xB300 with TP=8. Confirmed the root cause with a standalone Triton repro on an RTX 4090: ```python import torch, triton, triton.language as tl @triton.jit def k(out_ptr, NUM_BLOCKS: tl.constexpr, PAD: tl.constexpr): blocks = tl.arange(0, PAD) vals = tl.full((PAD,), float("nan"), tl.float32) vals = tl.where(blocks < NUM_BLOCKS, vals, float("-inf")) idx = tl.argmax(vals, axis=0) tl.store(out_ptr, idx) out = torch.empty(1, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") k[(1,)](out, NUM_BLOCKS=4, PAD=8) print(out.item()) # unpatched: 8 (out of range); with NaN->-inf + clamp: in [0, 3] ``` On the all-NaN input, unpatched `tl.argmax` returns `idx == num_blocks` (out of range); with the NaN→-inf mapping plus clamp the index stays in range. ## Validation - Standalone Triton repro (RTX 4090): patched kernel returns an in-range index on all-NaN input; unpatched does not. - Full vLLM server on 8xB300, TP=8, Kimi-K3 with DSpark speculative decoding: server boots through warmup (previously IMA), generates coherent output, acceptance length 2.5, conc=1 throughput 110–116 tok/s (+58% vs no-spec). ## Disclosure - AI assistance (Kimi K3) was used in developing this fix. A human engineer (Gabriel Peracio, Parasail) reviewed every changed line and validated the fix on hardware as described above. - Checked for duplicates before opening: no open PR or issue covers `tl.argmax`/NaN out-of-bounds in the rejection sampler (`rejection_sampler_utils.py`).

signals.title: [Bugfix] Fix speculative decoding for short_conv (LFM2) models
signals.text: ## Purpose Supersedes #44296 (rebased onto main with the original commit and authorship preserved — thanks @Tonoken3); that PR has had failing pre-commit since opening and merge conflicts since July 6 with no author activity, so this revives it to make the merge cheap. Speculative decoding (ngram, EAGLE-3, any method) on `short_conv` (LFM2 / LFM2.5) targets silently corrupts output at the first rejected token: attention KV rolls back, but the conv sliding window retains rejected-token activations. `mamba2` / GDN already handle this via the spec-aware `causal_conv1d_update` path; `short_conv` was never wired in: 1. `MambaStateShapeCalculator.short_conv_state_shape` sizes the conv state `conv_kernel - 1` (no `num_spec`), so there is no room to roll the window back (mirror: `mamba2_state_shape` adds `num_spec`). 2. `GPUModelRunner._build_attn_group_metadata` never injects `num_accepted_tokens` for `ShortConvAttentionMetadataBuilder`, so the layer never sees the accepted-token counts. Changes vs #44296: rebased onto current main, fixed the mypy failure that blocked its pre-commit (`assert state_indices_tensor_d is not None`), added a regression test for the spec-widened conv state shape. ## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR #44296 is this fix (red CI + conflicts + stale for 8 weeks; original commit and authorship preserved here). #50146 bundles a rebase of the same target-side fix with 6 further drafter-side changes across 9 files and depends on other open PRs; this PR is the minimal, independently mergeable target-side correctness fix for released models. ## Test plan - `pre-commit run` (incl. mypy-3.10): pass. - New `tests/kernels/mamba/test_short_conv_state_shape.py`: pass. - E2E (we are the model vendor — Liquid AI serving team; LFM2.5-230M fine-tune + trained EAGLE-3 drafter with ~0.9/step acceptance, ROCm MI325X, v0.26.0 + this patch): without the fix, low-concurrency spec decode diverges after the first rejection (doubled/fused tokens, occasionally flipped outputs; under default cudagraphs it degrades to garbage from ~token 2). With it, `--enforce-eager`, `PIECEWISE`, and default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` all produce identical, correct output on fixed-seed content probes. AI assistance was used to rebase, fix, and validate this change; I reviewed every changed line and am accountable for it.

signals.title: [Test] Harden NVFP4 KV scale-layout validation
signals.text: ## Summary Harden the NVFP4 KV-cache writer test so a structurally wrong block-scale layout cannot pass behind the existing loose elementwise tolerance. - Let the test dequantizer handle linear and TRT-LLM 4x4-swizzled block scales explicitly. - Decode K as linear and V as swizzled, matching the current-main writer contract. - Add a relative-L2 bound of 0.15 for both K and V while retaining the existing elementwise check. This changes test/reference code only. It does not change a runtime kernel, backend selection, or model output. ## Why this matters `test_reshape_and_cache_flash` previously unswizzled both K and V even though the writer stores K linearly and V in the TRT-LLM layout. Its `assert_close(atol=1.5, rtol=0.5)` was loose enough to hide a structurally wrong scale ordering. Normal loss for the deterministic NVFP4 inputs is about 0.1 relative L2, while the independently measured wrong-layout regime is 0.76-0.79. In a local red/green check, deliberately interpreting the current swizzled V scales as linear failed the new guard; restoring the current writer contract passed the identical case. ## Non-duplicate rationale I checked #50084 and searched open PRs for its number, NVFP4 relative-L2/layout tests, and `dequant_nvfp4_kv_cache`; no open PR contains this hardening. #46329 changes the SM12x writer/integration contract but does not modify either test file changed here. This PR intentionally records current main's writer layout. If #46329 lands, its architecture-dependent V layout should update the explicit V flag rather than weakening the error bound. The earlier #50085 was self-closed as a duplicate runtime fix; this draft extracts only its unclaimed test-hardening portion. ## Validation On RTX 5090 (SM120), using the freshly built current-main native extension. The relevant kernel/binding files are unchanged between that build and this branch: ```text pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py \ -k "test_reshape_and_cache_flash and nvfp4" -q 24 passed, 264 skipped, 945 deselected ruff check tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py \ tests/kernels/quantization/nvfp4_utils.py All checks passed! ruff format --check tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py \ tests/kernels/quantization/nvfp4_utils.py 2 files already formatted ``` No model evaluation was run because this PR changes tests only and has no runtime behavior. ## AI assistance AI assistance was used to reconstruct the prior test diff, audit duplicate work, run the checks, and draft this description. The hardware measurements and underlying investigation were produced and verified by me. Before this draft is marked ready, I will personally review and understand every changed line as required by `AGENTS.md`.

signals.title: [Model] Add Mage-VL multimodal model support
signals.text: ## Purpose Add support for **Mage-VL** ([`microsoft/Mage-VL`](https://huggingface.co/microsoft/Mage-VL)), a 4B codec-native streaming multimodal model (Mage-ViT visual encoder trained from scratch + Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 decoder). Paper: [arXiv:2607.24904](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24904). Mage-VL shares its architecture with `LlavaOnevision2ForConditionalGeneration`, which vLLM already supports: * Qwen3 backbone with 1-D `position_ids` (no M-RoPE) * CLS-free vision tower (no `class_embedding` / `class_pos_emb`) * 3-D vision RoPE with a 4:6:6 (T:H:W) head-dim split, driven by `patch_positions` rather than `grid_thw` * interleaved `rotate_half` (`(::2, 1::2)`) * windowed vision-attention `cu_seqlens` (`frame_windows_size` on the T dim) * video frame- and codec-backends both alias to the image path inside the HF processor I diffed the two HF remote-code repos after normalising identifiers: `modeling_*`, `configuration_*`, `processing_*` and `video_processing_*` are identical modulo renames. The only deltas are outside vLLM's execution path: * Mage-VL adds an optional `streammind_gate` head shipped in a separate `streammind_gate.safetensors` (not in `model.safetensors.index.json`, not on the LM forward path). Streaming/proactive-gate inference is out of scope here. * `codec_video_processing_*` adds a DCVC-RT neural-codec engine — HF-side asset generation that runs in a subprocess. * Default `patch_size` is 16 instead of 14 (config-driven; only a fallback default needed updating). Checkpoint weight prefixes (`model.language_model.*`, `model.visual.*`, `lm_head.*`) match exactly, so the existing `WeightsMapper` applies unchanged. Per review feedback, this reuses the existing `LlavaOnevision2ForConditionalGeneration` implementation rather than adding a renamed copy. `MageVLForConditionalGeneration` is mapped onto the existing module/class in `registry.py`. The only thing the two checkpoints genuinely differ on is the *names* of the `trust_remote_code` modules they ship, so `llava_onevision2.py` now: * resolves the processor / video-processor classes from the checkpoint's `auto_map` (falling back to the OV2 names), * derives the codec module from the loaded processor's module name (`processing_mage_vl` -> `codec_video_processing_mage_vl`), * binds the frame-sampling video backend to both `LlavaOnevision2VideoProcessor` and `MageVLVideoProcessor`. Net change is +96/-28 lines. `docs/models/supported_models.md`, `tests/models/registry.py` and the existing OV2 test module are updated accordingly. ### Not a duplicate `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "Mage-VL" / "mage_vl in:body" / "microsoft/Mage"` and the equivalent issue searches return nothing — the model was released after the last vLLM release and no other PR or issue tracks it. ## Test Plan ```bash # unit tests .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/test_registry.py \ tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_llava_onevision2.py -q # lint pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/models/llava_onevision2.py \ vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py tests/models/registry.py \ tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_llava_onevision2.py \ docs/models/supported_models.md ``` E2E parity against HF `transformers` on the two example inputs shipped with the checkpoint (`examples/dog.jpg`, `examples/soccer-broadcast.mp4`), greedy decoding, 1x RTX A6000, bf16, `enforce_eager=True`. Because the shared `llava_onevision2.py` is modified, LLaVA-OneVision-2 itself is re-run on the same input before and after the change to confirm no regression. ## Test Result **Unit tests / lint** ``` tests/models/test_registry.py + test_llava_onevision2.py 391 passed, 15 skipped pre-commit (ruff, ruff-format, mypy, typos, ...) all hooks passed ``` **Image — `examples/dog.jpg`, "Describe this image in detail."** HF `transformers` (reference, matches the model card verbatim): > The image depicts a dog sitting on a patterned rug. The dog appears to be a medium-sized breed with a thick, fluffy coat. Its fur is primarily white with patches of black and brown. The dog's ears are perked up, and it has a calm and attentive expression. The background features a large, ornate rug with intricate patterns [...] vLLM free-running greedy output agrees for the first ~30 tokens and then takes a different (equally valid) continuation, which is the usual bf16 tie-break between different attention kernels. To confirm this is not a numerical bug, I teacher-forced the full HF greedy output through vLLM and compared vLLM's argmax at every position: ``` teacher-forced top-1 agreement: 122/122 = 1.0000 ``` i.e. vLLM's next-token argmax matches HF at **every** step of the reference output — the vision tower, projector and decoder are functionally equivalent. **Video (frame backend) — `examples/soccer-broadcast.mp4`, 32 frames, "Describe this video."** vLLM reproduces the model card's reference output verbatim: > The video opens with a man in a black polo shirt, sporting a short haircut, standing in a stadium. He is holding a yellow microphone with the BBC Sport logo on it. The background reveals a large crowd of spectators [...] Weight loading reports no missing or unexpected tensors. **LLaVA-OneVision-2 regression check** `lmms-lab-encoder/LLaVA-OneVision-2-8B-Instruct` on `examples/dog.jpg`, greedy, before vs after this change: ``` output is byte-identical ``` **Not covered:** the codec video backend (H.264/HEVC and DCVC-RT). It needs the external `cv-preinfer` binary or DCVC-RT checkpoints and real video bytes, so it cannot run in CI — same situation as the existing LLaVA-OneVision-2 codec path, whose marker/plumbing layer is covered by the ported unit tests. The `streammind_gate` streaming path is not implemented in vLLM. --- **AI assistance disclosure:** this change was produced with AI assistance (architecture diffing, the rename, and the test/eval scripts). I am an author of Mage-VL, have reviewed every changed line, and ran all the commands and evaluations reported above myself.

signals.title: [Model Runner V2] batch-sharded sample
signals.text: # Summary Currently before sampling, the full target logits are materialized, allocating memory of size `O(batch_size * (num_spec_tokens + 1) * vocab_size)`. This PR reduces that per-step memory allocation by a factor of `1/P` during tensor parallelism by sharding the logits and sampler inputs along the batch dimension, and sampling in parallel on a subset of the batch. Sharding the sampler inputs (`InputBatch`) was straightforward, and is handled by `BatchSharder.shard_sampler_inputs`. Requests are assigned to ranks by partitioning the request state index mapping (using `idx_mapping % tp_size`) in a deterministic way. From there, we derive the new sharded input batch CPU arrays & GPU tensors for the local rank, based on the requests that it "owns". Sharding the logits along the batch dimension is accomplished by having the model compute logits for only its slice of the vocab size by implementing the `compute_logits_local` method. After that, each rank has a `[num_tokens, vocab_size // P]` slice of the full logits. However, instead of all-gathering to get the full `[num_tokens, vocab_size]`, we instead all-to-all along the batch dimension, so that each rank ends up with `[num_tokens // P, vocab_size]`. In summary, this PR (1) reduces peak target logits memory from `O(batch_size * (num_spec_tokens + 1) * vocab_size)` => `O(batch_size * (num_spec_tokens + 1) * vocab_size / P)`, and (2) parallelizes the sampling operation, which can be particularly beneficial for TPOT whenever heavy sampling operations (e.g. top-k, top-p, block verification, etc) are performed. No changes had to be made to the `Sampler` or `RejectionSampler` because they work perfectly fine with smaller batch sizes as long as we shard the `InputBatch` properly, which we do. NOTE: A big motivation for this PR is to enable sharding of the draft logits. The cached draft logits from the speculator forward pass(es) are preallocated in memory for the worst case, with a size of `O(max_num_reqs * num_spec_tokens * vocab_size)`. We can reduce that by a factor of `1/P` as well, but sharded sampling is a prerequisite. # Speed-Bench 2K/2K, Temp=1.0, Top-p=0.95 ## DSV4 + DSpark (7 spec tokens) ### Concurrency 64 | Metric | signals.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Capture the widest uniform decode batch by default
signals.text: # [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Capture the widest uniform decode batch by default ## Purpose This PR was four fixes; at a maintainer's request it is now one. The others are #50531 (warmup lookahead reservation) and #50532 (uniform-decode dispatch). The rejection-sampler argmax fix is dropped from this stack in favour of #50183, which covers the same defect. `max_cudagraph_capture_size` defaults in units of *tokens* (`min(max_num_seqs * 2, 512)`) while the batch it has to cover is `max_num_seqs * (1 + num_speculative_tokens)` tokens. With speculation on, the widest uniform decode batch falls outside the captured range and the largest decode steps dispatch eager. On a lane at `max_num_seqs=32` and `num_speculative_tokens=16` the decode capture list collapses to a single entry while the log still reads `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, which is why the correct value had to be found by hand and passed as `--max-cudagraph-capture-size 544` during bring-up. 544 is exactly `32 * (1 + 16)`, and the rule here derives it. The fix keeps the historical ceiling for the token-strided grid and adds the decode sizes as a *request-count* grid scaled by query length, capped at 512 requests. Sizing the token grid off the speculative width instead would multiply the number of captured graphs; that was the first shape of this fix and it is not what is proposed here. Two properties the tests pin: - Without speculation the default is bit-identical to the historical `min(max_num_seqs * 2, 512)` for every `max_num_seqs` from 8 to 2048, so no non-speculative configuration changes. - Under a dynamic speculative schedule the draft width varies per batch size, so capture sizes are generated per tier rather than for the widest width alone. Covering only the widest leaves the narrower tiers dispatching eager. This is a `VllmConfig` default rather than a runner-specific path, so it affects V1 as well as V2. ## Test Plan `tests/compile/test_config.py` asserts the rule directly rather than through an engine: the non-speculative equivalence sweep above, that the widest uniform decode batch lands inside the captured range once speculation is on, that the cap is applied to requests rather than tokens, and that every tier of a dynamic schedule is covered. ## Test Result `pytest tests/compile/test_config.py` on an H100 sandbox, this branch overlaid on the pinned nightly wheel (`0.26.1rc1.dev77+g6f91edf96`): **53 passed, 9 failed**. The 9 failures are environmental and pre-existing — the same 9 fail on the unmodified tree in the same container, all with `ValueError: Free memory on device`, because the box had 75 GiB of 81 GiB of GPU memory held by another process. They are the engine-launching tests (`test_use_cudagraphs`, `test_enforce_eager`, `test_no_compilation` and similar), none of which is a capture-size test. Against that same baseline this branch takes the pass count from 33 to 53. Revert check: restoring the pre-existing formula fails exactly the `covers_widest_uniform_decode` cases — including the off-stride case, where the scalar ceiling coincidentally matches but the widest batch is still absent from `cudagraph_capture_sizes` — plus `caps_requests_not_tokens`, while leaving all 16 `unchanged_without_speculation` cases passing. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean on every touched file. ### Model evaluation `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, 400 questions, 5-shot, greedy, on `Qwen/Qwen3-4B` with the published `z-lab/Qwen3-4B-DFlash-b16` drafter at `num_speculative_tokens=16`, V2 model runner, single H100: **accuracy 0.880, 0.000 invalid, 400 questions**. This was measured on the combined set of fixes before the split, so it covers this change together with the others rather than in isolation. ## Related - #30330 — the earlier fix to the same capture-size default that this completes. - #46324 aligns spec-decode capture sizes for PIECEWISE mode specifically and does not touch the default ceiling; #49390 raises the Blackwell capture default as a platform tuning choice rather than fixing the unit mismatch. I checked for duplicate and overlapping open PRs (`gh pr list --search` on "cudagraph capture size speculative", "max_cudagraph_capture_size", "uniform decode capture"). I used AI assistance (Cursor) to draft, test, and validate this change, and I reviewed every changed line before submitting.

signals.title: [XPU][INC] Add int4 w4a8 (dynamic int8 activation) backend for INC linear layers
signals.text: INC int4 layers on XPU always dispatch to ARK when it imports, with oneDNN `int4_gemm_w4a16` only as a fallback. `int4_gemm_w4a8` was never wired in at all. This PR adds `INCXPUW4A8LinearMethod` (int4 weights + dynamic per-token int8 activations, reusing the w4a16 weight layout unchanged, falling back to w4a16 below 512 tokens) and a `VLLM_XPU_INC_WNA16_BACKEND` selector: `auto | ark | w4a16 | w4a8`. Purely additive: one new test file, no existing test modified. `auto` leaves current behaviour unchanged. ## Purpose int8 activations avoid dequantizing weights to the activation dtype, which is a win for compute-bound shapes like diffusion (FLUX at 1024×1024 is M=4608). Per-layer GEMM: 1.32× at M=4608, 1.13× at M=512, 0.84× at M=128 — hence the 512-token fallback. Kept opt-in because the best kernel is device-dependent: ARK may win on other XPUs. Note that on B70 ARK is *not* the fastest option for either workload below — both oneDNN paths beat it — which is the motivation for making it selectable. Also validates that partitioned in/out dims are multiples of 8. `XPUW4A8IntLinearKernel.can_implement()` requires this, but that check is unreachable from the INC path: INC builds its own linear method and never goes through `MPLinearKernel` selection, and the shapes only exist once `create_weights()` runs, well after backend selection. Without the check an unaligned dim is not rejected but silently truncated — the int4 packing divides both dims by 8, so `out=890` packs 111 int32s covering only 888 columns and loses 2. Tensor parallelism shards these dims, so an aligned model dimension can still yield an unaligned partition. ## Test Plan New `tests/quantization/test_inc_xpu_w4a8.py` — 32 tests. The 29 mocked ones run anywhere; the 3 real-model ones self-skip unless an XPU with `int4_gemm_w4a8` is present. ```bash pytest tests/quantization/test_inc_xpu_w4a8.py -v ``` - **backend selection** — `auto` still prefers ARK, explicit values override it, invalid/unsupported combos raise instead of falling back silently - **weight processing** — fp16 scales created, bf16 scales preserved, qweight bit-identical (no repacking) - **apply_weights** — batch gate, full 9-arg kernel convention, fp16 scales for both activation dtypes, bias, 3D shapes - **partition alignment** — unaligned input / output / sum-of-shards rejected, aligned non-power-of-two accepted, w4a16 unaffected - **end to end** — real int4 auto-round checkpoint on XPU, both GPTQ- and AWQ-packed repack branches Plus `test_auto_round.py` for regressions and ruff. Mutation-tested: flipping the env var to `w4a16` makes `test_e2e_selects_w4a8_for_every_linear` fail with `no linear layer used the w4a8 method`, so it is not vacuously green. ## Test Result **E2E FLUX.1-dev, 1024×1024, 28 steps, B70, TP=2** — the load-bearing numbers: | Model | Kernel | Time | | --- | --- | ---: | | `black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-dev` | bf16 dense | 19.46 s | | `vllm-project-org/FLUX.1-dev-AutoRound-w4a16` | ARK (current default) | 23.63 s | | `vllm-project-org/FLUX.1-dev-AutoRound-w4a16` | oneDNN w4a16 | 21.87 s | | `vllm-project-org/FLUX.1-dev-AutoRound-w4a16` | oneDNN w4a8 | **16.99 s** | 1.39× over the current ARK default, and the only quantized config that beats bf16 dense rather than losing to it. 16.99 s reproduced 4×. Numerics: cosine 0.99996 vs w4a16 with bf16 activations. **Text generation LLM smoke-test OPEA/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-int4-sym-inc** Intel Arc Pro B70, `OPEA/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-int4-sym-inc`, 32 prompts × ~710 prompt tokens + 1024 generated each, `enforce_eager`, greedy, median of 3 after warmup: | `VLLM_XPU_INC_WNA16_BACKEND` | bound kernel | wall (median) | wall (min–max) | gen tok/s | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | unset (`auto`) | ARK | 12.675 s | 12.598–12.903 s | 2,585 | | `w4a8` | w4a8 | **8.354 s** | 8.272–8.647 s | **3,922** | 1.52× over the current ARK default. 32 prompts, 22,742 prompt tokens, 32,768 generated tokens. Outputs identical between backends. Kernel binding confirmed separately — `auto` → 96 ARK, `w4a8` → 96 w4a8, `w4a16` → 96 w4a16 — so the delta is a real kernel switch, not a config no-op. ## Checklist - [x] Purpose of the PR - [x] Test plan with test command - [x] Test results (before/after, e2e) - [ ] Documentation update — N/A: `docs/configuration/env_vars.md` auto-includes from `envs.py`, and no other `VLLM_XPU_*` var is documented separately, so the `envs.py` comment is the documentation

signals.title: [Core][Distributed] Size custom all-reduce buffers at init so batch-invariant mode can use them
signals.text: ### Purpose Fixes #50136. `CustomAllreduce.should_custom_ar()` decides per call whether to use the custom all-reduce or fall through to NCCL, based on `inp_size < self.max_size`. The all-reduce tensor is `[num_tokens, hidden_size]`, so that decision tracks the token count of the forward pass — i.e. batch composition — and the same request can take different reduction orders in different batches. Under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` that is a correctness bug, which is why `ParallelConfig` currently forces `disable_custom_all_reduce = True` and every batch-invariant TP run pays the pinned-NCCL path. This removes the size dependency instead of the whole code path. **Which review this is, settled.** The open question was whether the intended guarantee is *per request* (a request is bitwise reproducible under any batching) or *per engine* (a given engine configuration is internally consistent) — a bug under the first reading, a documented limitation under the second. @tolleybot answered it on this thread: per-request is what the production case needs, since regression tests and trusted production output require a prompt to give bitwise-identical logprobs however it is batched, across runs and restarts. This PR is therefore a fix, not a feature. ### What changed **1. Decide once, at init** (`custom_all_reduce.py`). Under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`, derive the largest all-reduce the engine can ever issue from `max_num_batched_tokens × hidden_size × dtype_size` and size `max_size` — and therefore the IPC buffers — to cover it. The gate can then never flip mid-run. If the requirement exceeds the cap, or the config cannot be read, custom all-reduce declines at init and logs why, rather than disabling itself silently. **2. Fail loud, never fall back silently** (`should_custom_ar`). If an all-reduce still exceeds the buffer, raise instead of falling through to NCCL. This is the load-bearing design decision. A silent fallback is precisely the mechanism in #50136; a fix whose failure mode reproduces the bug it fixes would be worse than no fix. If the bound is ever wrong — an unmodelled path, a padded width I did not account for — the run stops with a message naming the tensor size and the buffer, instead of quietly producing non-reproducible logprobs. **3. Pin the kernel** (`csrc/custom_all_reduce.cuh`). Force `cross_device_reduce_1stage` for all sizes under batch invariance, and hard error on an explicit `VLLM_CUSTOM_ALLREDUCE_ALGO=2stage`. The 1-stage kernel sums over absolute rank indices with no address reordering (its own comment notes the result is bitwise identical across ranks); the 2-stage kernel partitions by size and rotates accumulation order per rank, so it cannot be invariance-safe. **4. Drop unaudited backends** (`cuda_communicator.py`). Under batch invariance, exclude AITER's custom all-reduce from the dispatch chain. FlashInfer is already excluded upstream by #52998, which landed the same guard while flipping the FlashInfer default on; this change builds on that guard rather than repeating it. QuickReduce is not excluded — it is constructed only on ROCm (`current_platform.is_rocm()`), so it is unreachable on the CUDA configurations validated here, but on ROCm it would be tried first. Under batch invariance on CUDA the chain is `['CUSTOM', 'PYNCCL']`. The env pin in `override_envs_for_invariance()` is retained as belt-and-braces: since #52998, the communicator itself excludes FlashInfer under batch invariance, so the pin is redundant for dispatch but guards against future refactors of that logic. **5. Stop forcing the disable** (`config/parallel.py`), now that (1) makes the decision fixed for the process lifetime. The platform-support disable (`if not current_platform.use_custom_allreduce()`) is untouched. **6. Test + docs.** A TP≥4 batch-invariance test in `tests/v1/determinism/` (the suite currently runs everything at TP=1, so the all-reduce path was untested — that gap is why #50136 was possible to write), and `docs/features/batch_invariance.md` updated to describe the new behaviour. ### Validation Bitwise comparison of output token IDs **and** per-step logprobs as raw float32 bit patterns (not `allclose`) across batch compositions: bs=1 reference, full mixed batch, shuffled batch, and tile-boundary batches of 17 and 65. | Arm | Config | Invariance | Custom AR engaged | Largest tensor | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | dense, TP=4, patched | clean | 4/4 ranks, 9918 calls each | 25,165,824 B | | 2 | dense, TP=4, `disable_custom_all_reduce` (control) | clean | none, as expected | — | | 3 | dense, long context (2048/4096) | clean | 4/4 ranks | 25,165,824 B | | 4 | MoE (Qwen3-30B-A3B), TP=4 | clean | 4/4 ranks | 33,554,432 B | | 5 | fault injection (buffer forced to 4 KiB) | raises | — | — | | 6 | throughput, patched vs control | clean both | 4/4 vs none | 25,165,824 B | Three things make those greens checkable rather than merely green. **The bound predicts the observed maximum exactly.** Dense: largest tensor through the custom kernel = 25,165,824 B = `8192 × 1536 × 2`. MoE: 33,554,432 B = `8192 × 2048 × 2`. Both are exactly `max_num_batched_tokens × hidden_size × dtype_size`, which is the formula the buffer is sized from. Resulting buffers were 30 MiB and 40 MiB per rank. Engagement counts are read from each worker with `collective_rpc`, so they are exact per-rank values (`calls=9918`, identical on ranks 0–3), not log-derived estimates. **Every patched arm crossed the old threshold.** 25,165,824 B is 3.0× the 8 MiB constructor default that applied before this change, and the MoE arm's 33,554,432 B is 4.0×. (The `CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE_MAX_SIZES` clamp is unreachable under batch invariance, since `override_envs_for_invariance()` sets `VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_SYMM_MEM=0`.) So these runs exercised tensors that previously fell through to NCCL — they sat in the regime where the gate used to flip, not one where it never would have. **Both guards fire with their intended messages.** Injecting a 4 KiB buffer so a real all-reduce exceeds it: ``` RuntimeError: custom all-reduce received a 25165824 byte tensor, above the 4096 byte batch-invariant buffer. Falling back to NCCL would break batch invariance. Re-run with VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT unset, or file a bug with the model and max_num_batched_tokens so the bound can be corrected. ``` And `VLLM_CUSTOM_ALLREDUCE_ALGO=2stage` under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`: ``` VLLM_CUSTOM_ALLREDUCE_ALGO=2stage is incompatible with VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1: cross_device_reduce_2stage partitions the message by size and accumulates in a rank-rotated order, so an element's summation order changes with message size (i.e. with batch composition) and differs across owning ranks. ``` Throughput, batch-invariant mode, same workload, identical output (14,784 tokens in both arms): ``` patched (custom AR) 8006.4 tok/s TTFT p50 53.40 ms TPOT p50 8.48 ms control (NCCL only) 3906.0 tok/s TTFT p50 67.61 ms TPOT p50 17.34 ms → 2.05x ``` See the note on this number in "Tested / not tested" below — an earlier run on a different workload measured +84%, so the direction reproduces but the magnitude does not. #### Re-validation on current main (post-#52998) Rebased onto `main` @ `6259572b2` (which includes #52998's FlashInfer default flip and its batch-invariance guard) and re-validated on the same hardware class: 4× A100-SXM4-40GB, NVSwitch NV12 all-to-all (P2P 262.0 GB/s, 24 µs/hop — matching the original run). - Dispatch under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, TP=4, with FlashInfer **installed**: resolves to `['CUSTOM', 'PYNCCL']`; FlashInfer, AITER, QuickReduce, and both symm-mem paths not constructed. - Dense arm: CLEAN across all 5 batch compositions, 4/4 ranks engaged (exact per-rank counts via `collective_rpc`), largest tensor 25,165,824 B = 8192 × 1536 × 2 — byte-identical to the original bound prediction — within the 30 MiB buffer, `largest <= max_size` on every rank, zero tracebacks. - Routing tests 5/5 green; `pre-commit --all-files` clean for this PR's files (mypy ran and passed; the one repo-wide failure, `test-nonroot-entrypoint`, also fails on unpatched main). Two recorded deviations from the original run: host driver 595.71.05 (vs 580.65.06; same nvcc 13.0.88 toolchain), and `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="8.0;9.0a"` — required because current main does not compile for SM 8.0 alone (a GDN/KDA `#ifdef` guard mismatch in `csrc/libtorch_stable`, upstream and unrelated to this PR; will be reported separately). The A100 still executes SM 8.0 code. GPU evidence above was gathered at `d3cb5924b6`; the pushed commit `edfb2f5b2d` differs from it by a one-line ruff-format wrap in a test file (no runtime code). ### Tested / not tested **Tested.** 4× A100-SXM4-40GB with NVSwitch (`NV12` all-to-all), driver 580.65.06, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130, built from source. TP=4, bf16, chunked prefill and CUDA graphs enabled, for a dense model (Qwen2.5-1.5B, `hidden_size=1536`) and an MoE model (Qwen3-30B-A3B, `hidden_size=2048`). **Not tested, and guarded rather than assumed:** - **The MXFP4-padded MoE path.** `fused_moe` pads the routed hidden dimension before the all-reduce and truncates after, so the reduced tensor is wider than `hidden_size`. That padding is gated to the TRT-LLM MXFP4 path (`hidden_dim_unpadded > 0`), which needs Blackwell-class hardware I do not have. The MoE arm exercised MoE collectives and expert-parallel shapes but not the padded width. - **Multi-node symmetric memory / MNNVL multicast.** It disables itself when the group is not single-node, so TP=4 on one node cannot reach it. - **TP sizes other than 4**, non-NVSwitch topologies, and speculative decoding. - **QuickReduce on ROCm.** It is constructed only on ROCm and would be tried first in the dispatch chain there; the CUDA validation cannot reach it. Not excluded and not validated. Every unreached path above except QuickReduce on ROCm either declines custom all-reduce at init with a logged reason or hits the fail-loud `RuntimeError` in `should_custom_ar()`; QuickReduce is unguarded and would be selected ahead of the custom path there. **The throughput result is directional, not a specification.** Two runs on this configuration measured **+84%** and **+105%** on different workloads — same direction, materially different magnitude. The control is not ordinary NCCL: `override_envs_for_invariance()` pins `NCCL_MIN/MAX_NCHANNELS=1` and `NCCL_NTHREADS=1`, so the baseline is deliberately serialised NCCL, which is the cost this change removes. Treat the direction as reproducible and the magnitude as workload-specific. ### The memory trade-off — the call I made The buffer now scales with model width. Measured and projected, per rank: | `hidden_size` | raw bound | with 1.25× margin | outcome | |---|---|---|---| | 1536 (Qwen2.5-1.5B, measured) | 24 MiB | 30 MiB | fits | | 2048 (Qwen3-30B-A3B, measured) | 32 MiB | 40 MiB | fits | | 8192 (70B class) | 128 MiB | 160 MiB | fits | | 16384 | 256 MiB | 320 MiB | exceeds cap → declines at init, uses NCCL | Only the 1536 and 2048 rows are measured; the 8192 and 16384 rows are the formula evaluated, not runs. I capped it at 256 MiB/rank — a number chosen against that arithmetic rather than against a wide-model run — so everything up to roughly `hidden_size ≈ 13k` gets the custom path and wider models fall back cleanly at startup with a logged reason. That is where I chose to stop paying, given the alternative is the serialised-NCCL path. Both the cap and the 1.25× margin (which exists because I could not bound the MoE padding exactly) are policy numbers and one-line changes if you would put them elsewhere. If you would rather not spend the memory at all, the alternative is to keep the blanket disable and document why it is load-bearing — I am happy to send that instead; it is a small docs-and-comment change. ### How the validation was checked Five defects were found during this work by cross-checks rather than by the tests passing. Each is listed with the check that now catches its class, because the checks are the part that generalises. 1. **`git apply --3way` reported per-file success, then rolled the whole patch back** when a later file failed — leaving the kernel gate, the config change and the backend filtering absent with no error printed. Caught by a semantic grep for the changed symbols, not by the tool's output. That grep now runs before every build. 2. **The hand-port to current `main` dropped `self._custom_ar_calls = 0` and `self._custom_ar_max_bytes = 0`** while keeping all six uses. `__init__` has ten early returns, so grepping the attribute name still passed; the defect surfaced as an `AttributeError` at engine init. Now covered by an AST check asserting that any attribute other methods read is assigned at the **top level** of `__init__`, so completing the constructor guarantees it exists. The check was verified to fail on the pre-fix file. 3. **The semantic grep itself produced two false alarms** — it matched lowercase `batch_invariant` where the code says `envs.VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`, and matched `disable_custom_all_reduce = True` against upstream's unrelated platform-support guard. It now asserts the batch-invariance disable is absent **and** the platform guard is present, as separate conditions. 4. **The test's engagement assertion read `capfd` before engine shutdown.** Under `capfd`, fd 1 is a regular file rather than a tty, so worker processes block-buffer their output and flush only on exit. The assertion read zero markers while 21 were present in the log — a false red that, if "fixed" by weakening the assertion, would have removed the guard. The test now reads the counters directly from each worker via `collective_rpc`, which is immune to buffering, yields exact per-rank counts, and additionally asserts `largest <= max_size`. 5. **An earlier harness summed per-rank milestone floors** and reported a call count the data did not support. It now reports rank count and per-rank floor separately, and the test reports exact counts. The test ships with a counterpart, `test_engagement_assertion_can_fail`, that runs the same engine with the custom path disabled: output stays invariant, so a test checking only reproducibility would pass, and the engagement assertion must fail. It runs by default rather than being skipped. ### The contract question — resolved Is the intended guarantee **per request** (this request is bitwise reproducible under any batching) or **per engine** (a given engine configuration is internally consistent)? The size gate is a bug under the first reading and a documented limitation under the second. I had assumed the first because it is what makes batch invariance useful for RL rollouts where trainer and sampler must agree, but flagged it as an assumption about intent. @tolleybot resolved it in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50505#issuecomment-5246281546: per-request is what the production case needs — regression tests plus trusted production output mean a prompt has to give bitwise-identical logprobs no matter what it is batched with, across runs and restarts, and per-engine consistency does not help there. He also noted that the `ParallelConfig` guard in #51292 was a placeholder rather than a vote for per-engine. This PR is scoped as a fix on that basis. --- *Disclosure: this work was done with AI assistance (Claude). I ran the experiments, reviewed the changes, and take responsibility for the content.*

signals.title: Feat/spec decode under pipeline parallel
signals.text: ## Purpose EAGLE3-style speculative decoding (`eagle3` / `dflash` / `dspark`) is rejected outright when pipeline parallelism is enabled: ``` ValueError: <method> with pipeline parallel is not supported. ``` The drafter runs on the last PP rank, but it consumes auxiliary hidden states tapped from target layers that may live on earlier stages, and those tensors were dropped at the stage boundary. This PR forwards them and lifts the guard. Lifting the guard alone is not sufficient. The code behind it had never executed, so it hid a stack of latent defects in the shared PP path — all of them reachable only once spec decode and PP run together, which means they were unobservable rather than latent-but-live: 1. **Draft tokens never reached the non-last ranks.** Only the last rank runs the drafter, so `req_states.draft_tokens` is written nowhere else — yet the *first* rank owns `embed_tokens` and builds the embeddings for the whole pipeline. It was embedding the scheduler's `PLACEHOLDER_TOKEN_ID` (`-1`) into the draft slots, so the last rank verified real proposals against logits computed from placeholders. Silent corruption. Fixed by broadcasting the proposals from the last rank on the existing deferred slot, which has identical production and consumption timing. 2. **`compute_need_sampled_mask` ended the broadcast early.** The scheduler advances `num_computed_tokens` by the full scheduled width up front and rolls the rejected part back in `update_from_output`, which under PP lands *after* the next batch is scheduled. Reading the inflated count marked requests as finishing up to `num_speculative_tokens` early, after which the last rank stopped broadcasting and the other ranks' `last_sampled_tokens` froze, repeating a stale token. 3. **The sampled-token broadcast width could mismatch.** `receive()` always allocates `max_sample_len` columns while `broadcast()` sent whatever width the sampler produced, and the non-spec path returns width 1. NCCL does not diagnose the count mismatch: the root completes and the peer hangs until the watchdog fires, so any PP + spec-decode run deadlocked on its first prefill. Fixed by padding the send side; `post_update` stops at `num_sampled`, so the pad columns are never read. ### Design Aux-state forwarding is added generically on `EagleModelMixin`. A stage packs its own taps plus those inherited from upstream into the `IntermediateTensors` payload, and sizes its recv buffers from the same rule — a tap `a` is upstream iff `a <= start_layer` — so send and recv counts agree with no negotiation. Models opt in with `supports_aux_hidden_states_over_pp`. The previous blanket error is retained for those that do not, now raised with the offending model named. Kimi-K3 opts in; no other model does, so **EAGLE3 and dflash under PP remain gated and untested.** Two smaller changes ride along, both no-ops for configurations that worked before (spec decode under PP > 1 was rejected outright): the DSpark drafter gets a real vocab embedding on the last stage, where the target's is a `PPMissingLayer`; and the draft parallel config stops inheriting the target's PP size, since the drafter is instantiated only on the last stage and is never itself pipelined. ### Scope: capped at `pipeline_parallel_size <= 2` `GPUModelRunner.load_model` raises `NotImplementedError` above 2. This reflects validation coverage, not a known defect. The forwarding rule is size-agnostic by construction and the accounting is unit-tested up to pp=8. But pp>2 is the first topology with a **middle** stage, which must both adopt upstream taps and contribute its own to the same payload, and no such run has happened on hardware. The conservative default is deliberate because this feature does not fail loudly: a drafter fed mis-ordered or missing taps still emits syntactically valid proposals that simply get rejected more often, so the only symptom is a depressed acceptance rate. Lifting the cap should require an acceptance-rate comparison at pp>2, not just a successful boot. Happy to drop the cap if maintainers would rather have the untested-but-general path available. ### Note on commit 1 The first commit is an independent bugfix — `MambaHybridModelState.postprocess_state` feeds an int32 `idx_mapping` to `index_fill_`, which accepts only int64: ``` IndexError: index_fill_(): Expected dtype int64 for index. ``` **This is reachable on main today with no speculative decoding involved.** Its only caller is the non-last-PP-rank path in `GPUModelRunner.execute_model`, so any Mamba-hybrid model (Jamba, Falcon-H1, Nemotron-H, Qwen3-Next, MiniMax, Kimi Linear) crashes under `pipeline_parallel_size >= 2` with a chunked-prefill batch. It is included here because Kimi-K3 is a hybrid model and hits it under PP. Glad to split it into its own PR if preferred. ## Test Plan **Unit.** A CPU test for the aux accounting invariant, no distributed init required: ```bash pytest tests/v1/worker/test_eagle3_aux_hidden_states_pp.py ``` 12 cases over pp ∈ {1,2,3,4,6,8}, exercising the real `EagleModelMixin` and real `get_pp_indices`. Covers tap ordering and the boundary-tap double-count hazard (a tap landing exactly on `start_layer` must be counted as upstream by exactly one stage). The parametrization intentionally runs past the pp<=2 cap, since the accounting is general and this is what a future enablement would build on. **End-to-end.** Kimi-K3 (93 layers, DSpark drafter, `num_speculative_tokens=7`) at TP8 × PP2 on 2× 8×B200 with EFA. Two checks: 1. *Correctness*: greedy decode compared token-for-token against the identical topology with speculative decoding disabled. Speculative decoding is supposed to be output-neutral, so any divergence is a bug. 2. *Acceptance rate*: the sensitive detector. Corruption of aux taps crossing the PP boundary degrades acceptance before it produces visibly wrong text. Throughput measured on 128 fixed GSM8K prompts, same seed, concurrency 1 → 32. ## Test Result Unit: 12 passed. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean. **Correctness**: greedy output is token-for-token identical to the same topology without speculative decoding. **Acceptance**: 2.32 of 7 draft tokens per step. **Throughput** (output tok/s, GSM8K, 128 prompts): | Concurrency | No spec | Spec (PP2) | Speedup | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 77.30 | 174.52 | 2.26× | | 4 | 255.77 | 461.53 | 1.80× | | 8 | 423.86 | 714.01 | 1.68× | | 32 | 1138.69 | 1584.07 | 1.39× |

signals.title: [ROCm][CI] Add missing test coverage for upstream parity
signals.text: - Enable AITER only for the DeepSeek V4 KV-offload job, whose ROCm sparse indexer has no non-AITER execution path. - Deselect only `test_every_dsv3_routed_shape_is_instantiated`, which inspects an NVIDIA CUDA source file that is not staged in the ROCm test artifact. - Raise the legacy AMD Docker test container's shared-memory limit to 32 GiB, matching the paired native CI infrastructure change. - Keep the remaining skinny-GEMM tests enabled and preserve the existing 16 GiB offload test configuration. The parity jobs added by this PR exposed two ROCm CI assumptions introduced by vLLM PRs #42810 and #50089. The failures are visible in the [KV-offload step](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/11570/list?sid=019fc12a-ba06-4b1d-bd34-32a2f7dcfbfd&tab=output) and the [kernel step](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/11570/list?sid=019fc12a-ba66-44dc-9e75-3067065271dd&tab=output). These changes keep the new coverage while applying the required backend configuration as narrowly as possible. No model execution logic is changed by this PR.
