signals.title: [Feature][Model] Support stable-window-aware KV reuse for Qwen3-ASR realtime
signals.text: ## Purpose Qwen3-ASR is a single-turn ASR model, but the previous realtime session behavior handled it like a multi-turn conversation. As described in [#49658](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49658), output tokens from one segment could be prepended to the next resumable segment: ```text audio_1 -> assistant text_1 -> audio_2 -> assistant text_2 -> ... ``` This caused the conversation to grow indefinitely and mixed historical transcription tokens with later audio. It also amplified rollback failures: changing the latest explicit text did not remove older assistant output or its KV state. Unstable text could therefore remain in context, be generated again, and accumulate across segments. Resetting only the latest output was not a complete request-state reset. Using independent prompts avoids this feedback loop but loses stateful reuse. Qwen3-ASR also has a specific KV constraint: its AuT encoder is bidirectional, so representations inside the active AuT window may change when new audio arrives, while cached LLM prefix tokens must remain immutable. Setting the AuT window to one second makes direct KV reuse possible, but reduces acoustic context and degrades WER. ### PR goal Add a Qwen3-ASR realtime execution path in vLLM that can: - retain a longer AuT context without caching mutable audio representations; - reuse LLM KV only for an immutable, committed prefix; - send transcription text explicitly instead of accumulating assistant turns; - keep an unstable text boundary revisable through rollback. The change is scoped to the Qwen3-ASR realtime path and is intended to provide request-local KV reuse with lower long-form recomputation cost while preserving release-level ASR accuracy. ## Key Idea The realtime request state is split into an immutable committed prefix and a mutable active AuT window. LLM KV is reused only for the committed prefix. The active window is recomputed for every segment because its multimodal representations may still change as new audio arrives. This preserves a longer acoustic context without caching mutable multimodal state. ## Design Rationale The AuT encoder is bidirectional, so representations within the active AuT window can change when future audio arrives. Only content that has left the active window can be treated as immutable and safely reused through LLM KV. This feature therefore changes request-state and realtime-scheduler state management. It does not modify model weights, the AuT Encoder, or the LLM Decoder. The implementation controls the lifecycle of request-local multimodal state: which audio/text state is active, which state is committed, and which KV entries may be reused. For that reason, it belongs in the realtime scheduler and request-state handling rather than in model code. ## Architecture Overview ### Previous behavior ```text audio ↓ assistant text ↓ audio ↓ assistant text ↓ ... ``` Assistant turns accumulated across segments, causing the conversation state to grow. ### Proposed behavior ```text Request-local state ├── Committed prefix │ └── Immutable; LLM KV reusable └── Active AuT window ├── Recomputed for each segment └── Committed after the window becomes stable ``` Only the committed prefix is retained as immutable KV-reusable history. The active AuT window and the unstable text suffix remain revisable. Rollback moves the text/KV boundary before the next decode. ## Changes The realtime path maintains the following request-local state: ```text committed audio/text prefix + active AuT window + explicit text prefix ``` For each new inference segment: 1. Recompute the active AuT window with the new audio. 2. Truncate LLM KV state to the last committed boundary. 3. Replace the active-window audio representations and decode again. 4. Commit a completed AuT window once it is stable; only committed content is retained as immutable KV-reusable history. The request state is explicit rather than represented as conversation history. Partial transcriptions are not accumulated as assistant turns. The confirmed transcript is maintained separately and sent as the current text prefix, while the active 8-second AuT window is recomputed as audio arrives. Token-level rollback is used as a boundary management mechanism (`rollback_tokens=5`, with the first two segments using no prefix). It moves the text prompt and KV boundary together before the active audio/text suffix is replaced. Moving only the visible text boundary would leave stale multimodal representations or stale decoder KV entries available to the next decode. Only a completed AuT window is committed to reusable history. Stable history therefore benefits from LLM KV reuse, while the mutable audio window and unstable text suffix remain recomputable. ## Concrete implementation proposal for this PR This PR is specifically for Qwen3-ASR realtime support in the [`zjyzjy361/vllm`](https://github.com/zjyzjy361/vllm) fork (validation revision `58dc03a1bb8cd119a70298704739c9ecc6c2313e`). It is not a proposal to redesign the generic vLLM realtime API or to add a model-agnostic stable-window abstraction to upstream `main`. The implementation should remain guarded by `QWEN3_ASR_REALTIME_MODE=aut_stable_window_kv` and the Qwen3-ASR architecture. The forked vLLM change should be reviewed and kept organized around these Qwen3-ASR-specific responsibilities: - `vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_asr_realtime.py`: accept the configured AuT window, build the new segment prompt, carry the confirmed text prefix, and report the number of newly introduced audio features. - `vllm/entrypoints/speech_to_text/realtime/connection.py`: keep one explicit request-local state, apply `rollback_tokens`/`unfixed_chunks`, avoid assistant turn accumulation, and expose the runtime patch identifier in the session acknowledgement. - `vllm/entrypoints/speech_to_text/realtime/serving.py`: pass the Qwen3-ASR segment metadata through the realtime request path without changing behavior for other models. - `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`: when the mode is enabled, replace the mutable active audio feature, retain only the committed feature boundary, truncate/free stale encoder/KV state, and clean up on the final segment. The implementation must preserve these invariants: only committed prefix state is reused; the active 8-second AuT window is recomputed; rollback moves text and KV boundaries together; and a request cannot leak audio features, KV entries, or text state into another request. A runtime log line containing the mode, `n_window_infer=800`, and the patch id `aut-stable-window-kv-v1` should make the selected path auditable. ## Test Plan ### Scope and test target The test target is the Qwen3-ASR support in the fork above. Generic vLLM realtime behavior and unrelated models are out of scope; they only need to keep their existing regression coverage. ### Required implementation tests Add/retain focused tests in the fork (the local prototype already contains the corresponding starting point in `tests/test_aut_stable_window_kv.py`): - buffer lifecycle: 1--8 one-second segments grow one active window, segment 8 commits it, and segment 9 starts a new window; - scheduler update: active feature replacement, committed-feature accounting, stale encoder-cache freeing, and final-segment cleanup; - text/KV boundary: assistant turns are never appended, rollback changes the explicit prefix and KV boundary together, and the first `unfixed_chunks` segments carry no prefix; - isolation: two sequential requests start with empty request-local state; - protocol: `session.update` values are acknowledged and the response includes the expected Qwen3-ASR runtime patch id. Run the focused tests with: ```bash pytest -q tests/test_aut_stable_window_kv.py tests/test_audio_history_kv.py ``` ### Existing regression coverage The existing upstream Qwen3-ASR streaming example provides a basic regression smoke test: ```bash python examples/example_qwen3_asr_vllm_streaming.py ``` The existing vLLM scheduler streaming tests should also continue to pass: ```bash pytest tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py -v ``` ## Test Results ### Accuracy This table compares pooled WER for the one-second realtime baseline, the proposed stable-window path, and the official release reference. The WER baseline is the 1-second AuT realtime path with request-local LLM KV reuse. The official release path is a separate accuracy reference, not the baseline for this comparison. | Path | AuT window | LLM KV reuse | Pooled WER | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Realtime baseline | 1 s | Yes | 4.6750% | | Proposed path | 8 s | Yes | **3.7908%** | The result is from the public SpeechIO Chinese sets `SPEECHIO_ASR_ZH00000`–`SPEECHIO_ASR_ZH00026` (43,177 utterances, 65.78 hours). The proposed path reduces WER by 0.8842 percentage points, or about 18.9% relative error reduction, compared with the 1-second KV-reuse baseline. Its accuracy is consistent with the official release result; this PR does not claim to improve the underlying ASR model over the release implementation. SpeechIO references: - [SpeechIO Leaderboard](https://github.com/SpeechColab/Leaderboard) - [Official dataset manifest](https://github.com/SpeechColab/Leaderboard/blob/master/datasets/zoo.yaml) ### Long-form Performance This table compares API RTF and completion count for the 10-minute long-form experiment. The experiment uses the same Qwen3-ASR-0.6B model, 1-second inference segments, and 16,000-byte PCM16 transport chunks. | Path | API RTF | Completion | |---|---:|---:| | Fresh cumulative recomputation | 0.4037 | 600/600 | | Proposed AuT 8s + LLM KV | **0.1521** | 600/600 | The proposed path improves throughput by approximately 2.65x over fresh cumulative recomputation. The final transcript has 2,275 characters and a sequence similarity of 0.9952 against the fresh run's 2,271-character transcript. This is a comparison against the reset/fresh workaround, not a claim that the proposed path is faster than every historical audio-history-KV configuration. ### Configuration The following configuration was used for validation. | Setting | Value | |---|---| | Model | Qwen3-ASR-0.6B | | Realtime mode | `aut_stable_window_kv` | | AuT window | 800 frames / 8 s | | Inference segment | 1.0 s | | Transport chunk | 16,000 PCM16 bytes / 0.5 s | | Prefix recovery | `unfixed_chunks=2`, `rollback_tokens=5` | | LLM KV reuse | request-local, same request/session | | Global vLLM prefix caching | disabled | Global vLLM prefix caching was disabled so that the measurement reflects same-request audio-history KV reuse rather than cross-request prefix-cache hits. This implementation represents one possible integration strategy for stable-window-aware KV reuse. We welcome suggestions on the design and are happy to adapt the implementation to better align with upstream architecture. If additional refactoring or follow-up changes are preferred for upstream integration, we are happy to prepare and submit the corresponding patches. ## vLLM PR Checklist - [x] The purpose of the PR and the problem it addresses are described. - [x] The test plan and representative test command are provided. - [x] Test results include before/after WER and long-form end-to-end evidence.

signals.title: [Model] Support Solar Open2 (SolarOpen2ForCausalLM)
signals.text: ## Purpose Add support for [upstage/Solar-Open2-250B](https://huggingface.co/upstage/Solar-Open2-250B) tech report: https://huggingface.co/papers/2607.20062 ### Highlights - **Model-owned KDA layer.** The shared `KimiGatedDeltaNetAttention` was rewritten for Kimi K3 (#50000) and can no longer express Solar checkpoints (`2 * sigmoid(b)` beta, full-rank `f_proj`/`g_proj`). The pre-K3 implementation lives in `solar_open2.py` and calls the in-tree FLA KDA kernels; no shared layer file is modified. - **`vllm::solar_open2_kda_attention` is a cudagraph splitting op.** It reads `attn_metadata` and writes the KDA caches; captured inside a cudagraph segment it replays stale state (fluent output, wrong answers). Pinned by a unit test. - **Profile-time KDA prefill warmup**, sized to the scheduler batch (cap 2048 tokens): configs autotuned on a single chunk lose ~23% on real prefills (measured on B200 at the TP8 shape). - **`solar_open2` reasoning and tool-call parsers** (streaming + non-streaming), documented in `reasoning_outputs.md` / `tool_calling.md`. ## Test Plan ```bash pytest tests/transformers_utils/test_solar_open2_config.py \ tests/reasoning/test_solar_open2_reasoning_parser.py \ tests/tool_parsers/test_solar_open2_tool_parser.py \ tests/tool_parsers/test_utils.py \ tests/models/test_solar_open2_kda.py pytest tests/models/test_registry.py -k SolarOpen2 ``` Plus a full serving run on 8xB200 (TP8 + EP, Triton MoE backend, public checkpoint, precompiled wheel for this base); its `vllm/` tree is identical to this head (the only later change is a new unit test). ## Test Result - Unit tests: **463 passed** (incl. `torch.library.opcheck` on the custom op); registry init test: 1 passed. - 8xB200 serving: KV cache 107.02 GiB/rank; KDA warmup on all 8 ranks (`warmed_signatures=1`, `failed_attempts=0`, `warmup_tokens=2048`); server log free of warmup failures and tracebacks; launching with an ngram `--speculative-config` fails fast with the intended `NotImplementedError`. - feature tests: | check | result | |---|---| | chat, reasoning on/off, streaming | correct answers, exactly one `[DONE]` | | auto tool choice + tool-result follow-up | `{"city": "Seoul", "unit": "C"}`; final answer uses the result | | tool streaming | name once, then incremental argument deltas | | Responses API, typed args, streaming | `{"count": 7, "enabled": true}` (int/bool preserved) | | structured output (`json_schema`) | `{"answer": 29}` alongside reasoning | ## AI assistance disclosure Developed with AI assistance (Upstage Solar, Claude, Codex).

signals.author: sagearc

signals.title: [ROCm][MLA] Reach FULL cudagraphs for AITER MLA speculative decoding
signals.text: ## Purpose Speculative decoding on ROCm cannot reach FULL cudagraphs, for two independent reasons. This fixes both. Measured on Kimi-K3 with a DSpark draft, TP8 on MI355X. **The reported support level.** A DSpark draft group serves its whole `1 + num_speculative_tokens` block through the decode path, but `TritonMLAMetadataBuilder` reports `UNIFORM_SINGLE_TOKEN_DECODE` from a class constant, and the engine takes the minimum over attention groups -- so that one group downgrades the *whole engine* off FULL. `forward_mqa` flattens the block with `repeat_interleave` on a Python int and performs no device->host sync, so the group does satisfy `UNIFORM_BATCH`. `triton_mla.py` now reports that where the KV cache group is marked `non_causal_multi_token_decode`. Note the predicate is group scoped, not draft scoped, so a causal target sharing a draft's group is lifted too; `__init__` two lines below already uses it to raise `reorder_batch_threshold`, and the docstring records the scope. **Syncs inside the captured region.** `AiterMLAImpl.forward_mqa`'s small-head (< 16 query heads per rank) verify path expands each request's paged-KV range into one row per verify token on every MLA layer, with four device->host syncs and an allocation sized from what it just read back, each of which aborts HIP graph capture. That expansion moves into `_build_decode`, once per step, writing into persistent buffers so `mla_gluon` sees fixed addresses across replays. One sync remains there, because Gluon derives its split count from `min_kv_seq_len` and the merged causal-mask test pins that to the shortest row submitted; the builder runs outside the captured region, as `flex_attention.py`'s `.item()` in `build_for_cudagraph_capture` does. **`gpu_worker.py`.** `cache_config.kv_cache_size_tokens` is set in the engine core and the front end but never in the worker, which forward-propagates only `num_gpu_blocks`. The builder above therefore sees `None` in any multi-process deployment and falls back to a bound derived from `max_model_len`, roughly six times the real capacity. Filling it in `Worker.initialize_from_config` takes the verify buffer reservation from 295.3 MiB per rank to 46.6 MiB. The gap pre-dates this PR but is load-bearing for that reservation, so it is fixed here. **Related.** #50578 touches the same file and is best reviewed alongside. They merge cleanly in either order and do not collide on the verify path. ## Test Plan The merged causal-mask test covers exactly the code that moves here. Then serve and bench at concurrency `C` in `1 16`: ```bash pytest -q tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_causal_verify_mask.py VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 vllm serve /model \ --served-model-name moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --trust-remote-code \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.80 --max-model-len 262144 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 8384 --max-num-seqs 32 --disable-custom-all-reduce \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"/draft","num_speculative_tokens":7,"attention_backend":"TRITON_MLA"}' \ -cc '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_capture_sizes":[8,16,32,128,256]}' vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --model moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \ --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --dataset-name random --ignore-eos \ --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 256 \ --num-prompts $((C * 8)) --max-concurrency $C --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el ``` `Capturing CUDA graphs (FULL)` should appear in the server log, and `compilation.py`'s "not supported with spec-decode" warning should not. ## Test Result | | PIECEWISE (`main`) | FULL (this PR) | | --- | --- | --- | | c1 output tok/s | 12.10 | 46.30 | | c1 mean ITL | 186.98 ms | 34.26 ms | | c16 output tok/s | 174.01 | 326.46 | | c16 mean ITL | 188.28 ms | 92.91 ms | | capture memory per rank | 0.51 GiB | 2.11 GiB | | downgrade warning | present | absent | | acceptance length | 2.55 / 2.48 | 2.51 / 2.45 | Acceptance length is unchanged, so the gain is execution speed rather than better drafting. The causal-mask test passes, and the reservation logs 46.6 MiB against `GPU KV cache size: 814,051 tokens` -- from a later run than the table, which predates the `gpu_worker.py` fix; both patched runs agree on capture memory and graph mode. Absolute throughput came from `--dataset-name random`, whose synthetic prompts the draft predicts poorly (acceptance around 21%), so the FULL:PIECEWISE ratio is the controlled quantity and the absolutes are not representative of real prompts.

signals.title: [Bugfix][MiniMax-M3] Keep FP8 query allocation stable across CUDA graph replay
signals.text: ## Purpose MiniMax-M3 allocates its FP8 query buffer outside an eager CUDA-graph break, but the current allocation condition depends on request metadata that is re-evaluated inside the eager attention segment. A graph captured without a CUTLASS MSA plan can later replay with a valid plan, causing the eager CUTLASS path to receive `query_fp8=None` and fail at `assert query_fp8 is not None`. Allocate `query_fp8` whenever the configured implementation supports CUTLASS decode, which is static across capture and replay. Keep the per-request CUTLASS-versus-Triton decision inside the eager segment. CUTLASS-capable configurations may therefore produce the FP8 query for request shapes that fall back to Triton; this keeps the graph output stable without changing dynamic backend selection. This does not duplicate an existing contribution. Before opening this PR, open vLLM issues and PRs were searched for `query_fp8 MiniMax`, `use_cutlass_decode MiniMax`, and the CUDA-graph replay failure; no matching fix was found. The search was repeated while rebasing onto current `main`, and no overlapping open PR was found. This is an AI-assisted contribution. OpenAI Codex provided non-trivial assistance with the implementation, test, and rebase. The human submitter reviewed the changed lines and validation evidence before marking the PR ready. ## Test Plan - Exercise the actual MiniMax FP8 query allocation under a real `BreakableCUDAGraphCapture` on SM100. - Capture with CUTLASS enabled but no per-request CUTLASS plan. - Add the plan before replay, then verify repeated eager replays receive a non-null FP8 query at one stable CUDA address. - Run the existing MiniMax-M3 CUTLASS sparse-decode test file on SM100: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3_msa_cutlass_sparse_decode.py`. - Run pre-commit and mypy on the changed files. ## Test Result Static validation passed again after rebasing onto current `main`: - Full pre-commit hook set on both changed files. - Python 3.10 and Python 3.12 mypy hooks on both changed files. - Python bytecode compilation and `git diff --check`. The new CUDA regression was not rerun on the non-CUDA host because it requires SM100. Separate deterministic SM100 validation of the same transition used real `torch.cuda.CUDAGraph` and `BreakableCUDAGraphCapture`: - The parent behavior reproduced `assert query_fp8 is not None` when capture used the Triton fallback and replay became CUTLASS-eligible. - The patched behavior completed 100 replays. - All 101 capture/replay pointer observations were non-null and used one stable CUDA address. - The focused deterministic harness passed all 5 checks. Model/serving evaluation: a full MiniMax-M3 concurrency-512 A/B serving run completed successfully for both control and patched configurations. Aggregate token throughput changed by -0.34%, indicating no material performance regression in that comparison. A second independent concurrency-512 control/patched pair also completed end to end; neither arm reproduced the intermittent assertion in that pair.

signals.title: Bolins/shm tensor arena
signals.text: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Purpose `MessageQueue.enqueue` (`shm_broadcast.py`) already routes CPU tensors out-of-band via `_reduce_tensor` (protocol-5 `PickleBuffer`, #48442), which removed the dominant cost of the old in-band path — copying tensor bytes into the pickle stream. Two costs remain for a large multimodal `pixel_values` tensor on a TP=N worker: 1. the out-of-band buffer is published **once per node-local reader** (N transport copies for TP=N), and 2. each reader's H2D copies from a **pageable** ZMQ frame (pageable staging + first-touch faults). This PR adds an opt-in **slotted shared-memory tensor arena** that layers *on top of* `_reduce_tensor`: the writer does **one** memcpy into a free slot, every reader takes a **zero-copy view** of the *same* slot (no per-reader transport copy), and the mapping is `cudaHostRegister`-pinned so the H2D is a true DMA. Large contiguous CPU tensors are diverted by `_ArenaPickler.reducer_override`; anything it declines (too small, non-contiguous, or arena exhausted) **falls through to `_reduce_tensor` unchanged**. Net for a ~200 MB image at TP=8: **1 memcpy + 8 pinned DMAs** instead of **8 transport copies + 8 pageable stagings**. The gain scales with TP degree and tensor size, and is zero at TP=1 (no multiproc broadcast) — both now confirmed empirically below. Design doc: `docs/design/shm_tensor_arena.md`. **Safety / scope:** controlled by the `--enable-shm-tensor-arena` / `--no-enable-shm-tensor-arena` CLI flag (`ParallelConfig.enable_shm_tensor_arena`, default on — happy to flip to default-off if preferred); activates only when all queue readers are node-local; the writer **never blocks** (no free/oversized slot → fall back to `_reduce_tensor`, deadlock structurally impossible); slot reuse is gated on an **H2D-completion CUDA event**, so the writer can't overwrite a slot whose async DMA is still in flight — correct under `--async-scheduling`. ## Test Plan A/B against **current `main`**: the baseline arm is the unmodified `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` image (`nightly-65b7662d3f…`, includes #48442); the arena arm is the same image plus this PR's four files. A third arm runs this PR's code with `--no-enable-shm-tensor-arena` as a disable-control (must be behaviorally identical to base; also bounds run-to-run noise). Two setups, so the TP axis and the model-realism axis are both covered: 1. **TP-scaling sweep** — Qwen2.5-VL-3B, TP ∈ {1, 2, 4} (ViT MLP dim caps this family at TP≤4), image sizes 512²–3072², 150 prompts @ 2 req/s. 2. **Production-scale VLM** — Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B (ModelOpt NVFP4) on 8×B300, TP ∈ {4, 8}, image sizes 1024²/2048²/3072², 120 prompts @ 1 req/s. Common method: `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random-mm` (openai-chat backend), one image per request at a fixed size per cell, poisson arrivals at a **non-saturated** rate, 20 warmups (excludes the one-time arena pinning), seed 42, **2 repeats per cell**. Built-in negative controls: TP=1 (arena structurally inactive) and 512² images (~3 MB `pixel_values`, below the 8 MB divert threshold). <details> <summary>Repro commands</summary> Server (one per arm × TP; arena arms = same image + this PR's files): vllm serve $MODEL --tensor-parallel-size $TP --max-model-len 32768 \ --mm-processor-cache-gb 0 [--enable-shm-tensor-arena | --no-enable-shm-tensor-arena] Load (per image size HW, per repeat): vllm bench serve --model $MODEL --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \ --dataset-name random-mm --random-mm-bucket-config "{($HW, $HW, 1): 1.0}" \ --random-mm-base-items-per-request 1 --random-mm-limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 1}' \ --random-input-len 128 --random-output-len 64 --ignore-eos \ --num-warmups 20 --num-prompts 150 --request-rate 2 --seed 42 \ --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,90,99 --save-result </details> Still outstanding: port the standalone correctness harness (21 checks: byte-exact round-trip incl. bf16, zero-copy sharing, slot lifecycle with per-reader release, event-gated reuse, exhaustion/oversize/non-contiguous fallbacks) into `tests/distributed/test_shm_broadcast.py` alongside the #48442 tests. ## Test Result **Qwen3-VL-235B (NVFP4) on 8×B300 — E2E p99, base → arena (mean of 2 repeats):** | image (`pixel_values` size) | TP=4 | TP=8 | |---|---:|---:| | 1024² (~23 MB) | 1021 → 995 ms (−2.6%) | 1025 → 999 ms (−2.5%) | | 2048² (~96 MB) | 1584 → 1298 ms (**−18.1%**) | 1807 → 1363 ms (**−24.6%**) | | 3072² (~213 MB) | 3340 → 2771 ms (**−17.0%**) | 4132 → 3083 ms (**−25.4%**) | TTFT p99 moves the same direction (TP=8: −21.5% at 2048², −11.9% at 3072²), and at these payload sizes TTFT p50 improves too (TP=8/3072²: 1185 → 948 ms). Request throughput is identical in every cell (rate-limited by design). **TP-scaling sweep (Qwen2.5-VL-3B — separate setup from the table above):** TP=1 and 512² images are neutral (negative controls behave as designed — the arena never activates); gains appear only at TP≥2 with ≥8 MB tensors and grow with TP and size. On this small model the relative effect is larger than the 235B numbers above — up to −34% E2E p99 at 3072²/TP=4 (3020 → 1992 ms) — because the same transport cost is a much bigger fraction of a 3B's per-request time, and at 2 req/s its large-image cells carry queueing that the stall removal also drains. The 235B table above is the more conservative, production-representative measurement. The disable-control arm on this setup bounds noise at roughly ±5% per cell. **Statistical honesty:** with n=2 repeats, individual p99 cells are noisy (the 235B control shows single-cell swings up to ~±17%). The claim rests on the pattern, not any one cell: the arena is ahead in **all 12** TTFT/E2E comparisons across both models, monotonically in TP degree and tensor size — the shape the mechanism predicts (per-reader transport + pageable staging replaced by one memcpy + pinned DMA), and the E2E-tail bias matches head-of-line blocking on co-scheduled decodes. **Summary:** neutral outside the large-image + TP≥2 regime; **~18–25% p99 reduction** inside it on a production-scale VLM. **Process note:** the disable-control caught a bug in an earlier revision of this PR — `--no-enable-shm-tensor-arena` was silently ignored (the gate read `get_current_vllm_config()` outside its context and fell back to the default). Fixed by threading the flag explicitly through the executor; the control was re-validated inert (0 arena activations) before the numbers above. <details> <summary>Historical: original measurement vs the pre-#48442 in-band baseline</summary> Same-seed interactive multimodal workload (uncapped images, TP=4 ×2 workers on one 8-GPU node, ~1.2k aligned requests): TTFT p50 93→89, p90 401→241, p99 1321→862, max 2139→1375 ms; requests >1.5 s: 9→0. These numbers predate #48442 and therefore overstate the delta vs current main; kept only as provenance for the original problem analysis. </details> --- <details> <summary>Essential Elements Checklist</summary> - [x] Purpose of the PR - [x] Test plan — executed (repro commands above); unit-test port to `tests/distributed/` still outstanding - [x] Test results — A/B vs current `main` on two models × TP 1–8, with disable-control - [x] Documentation — `docs/design/shm_tensor_arena.md` </details>
signals.author: BolinSNLHM

signals.title: [Feature] IndexCache for DeepSeek-V4 (validated on V4-Flash-0731, including DSpark on to accelerate on top of
signals.text: ## Summary: This work is built to support Dspark + IndexerCache to achieve best deepseek v4 flash serving performance. ## Purpose Adds DSA IndexCache support to DeepSeek-V4, so C4A layers marked shared reuse the top-k the previous C4A layer left in the shared `topk_indices_buffer` instead of running their own indexer. Same config surface as the DeepSeek-V3.2 feature (`use_index_cache` / `index_topk_freq` / `index_topk_pattern`, see [docs/features/index_cache.md](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/docs/features/index_cache.md)); addresses #45350. The indexer dominates decode KV traffic on this model at long context: per decode token per C4A layer it reads `(S/4) x 132 B` of its own K cache, while the main sparse MLA reads only `index_topk x 576 B`. Across DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731's 21 C4A / 20 C128A / 44 SWA caches that is ~65% of decode KV traffic at 32K and ~81% at 128K, and the indexer is TP-replicated so every rank pays it in full. ### Relationship to #49085 #49085 implements the same feature for Hopper and is the earlier work; its authors (@wangyicong52, @zzz3bbb3) got there first on the two non-obvious points — per-PP-rank handling, and keeping skipped indexers' KV-cache specs registered while parking their linear weights on the meta device. Two behavioural differences worth a maintainer decision: 1. This PR gates on `use_index_cache`, matching the documented V3.2 surface. #49085 activates on `index_topk_freq > 1` alone, which would make `--hf-overrides '{"index_topk_freq": 4}'` silently enable on V4 while silently doing nothing on V3.2. 2. This PR uses `c4a_idx % index_topk_freq`; #49085 keeps V3.2's `index_skip_topk_offset` (default 2), so its first two C4A layers always compute. Theirs is more faithful to V3.2 and I am happy to switch. ## Design notes Only C4A layers (`compress_ratio == 4`) carry an indexer in V4, so **the frequency and pattern are indexed over the C4A layers, not over all layers**. Applying the V3.2 absolute-`layer_id` formula to DeepSeek-V4-Flash marks *every* C4A layer as shared (they are all even), so nothing populates the buffer and every layer reads stale contents — silently, with no error. A regression test pins this. Three further constraints, each covered by a test: - `topk_indices_buffer` is rank-local, so the first C4A layer **of each pipeline stage** computes its own top-k (derived from the same `get_pp_indices` split `make_layers` uses). - `compress_ratios` can be longer than `num_hidden_layers` (44 entries on V4-Flash, 46 on V4-Flash-0731, for the MTP/draft slots), so selection slices to `num_hidden_layers`. - A pattern is one `F`/`S` character per C4A layer — 21 on V4-Flash-0731, not 43 — and may not start with `S`. Wrong-length patterns raise rather than silently applying a prefix. Skipped layers keep their indexer allocated and simply never run it, so the change is confined to `attention.py` and needs no KV-cache-grouping or weight-loading changes. Memory savings are left to a follow-up. ## Test Plan ```bash pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_index_cache.py -v ``` E2E hardware: single node, 8xH100 80GB, TP=8, upstream vLLM 0.26.0 with this patch, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`. ```bash # long context / frequency sweep vllm bench latency --model <0731> --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 -tp 8 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --max-model-len 33792 \ --input-len 32768 --output-len 128 --batch-size 2 \ --hf-overrides '{"use_index_cache": true, "index_topk_freq": N}' # quality: GSM8K 200q 5-shot, MMLU 500q 5-shot, greedy # throughput: short prompt + 512 output tokens at fixed concurrency ``` ## Test Result 14/14 unit tests pass. ### Frequency sensitivity 32768-token input x batch 2, and MMLU 500 questions 5-shot. All arms are the same build with only `index_topk_freq` varying, so `freq=1`/off is a true no-skip control (confirmed by the log line firing only on freq>1 arms): | freq | indexers run | 32K latency | Δ | MMLU | |---|---|---|---|---| | off / 1 | 21/21 | 3.004 s | — | 85.4% | | 2 | 11/21 | 2.890 s | -3.8% | 85.6% | | 3 | 7/21 | 2.842 s | -5.4% | 85.0% | | 4 | 6/21 | 2.831 s | -5.8% | 84.8% | | 6 | 4/21 | 2.808 s | -6.5% | 85.0% | The latency curve saturates quickly — freq=2 captures most of the win, and skipping three times as many indexers (freq=6) only reaches -6.5%. MMLU spans 84.8-85.6%, within the ~1.6pp binomial noise at n=500. vLLM 0.25.1 and the older `DeepSeek-V4-Flash` checkpoint reproduce the freq=2/3 numbers within noise. ### Quality and throughput matrix (GSM8K, 200q 5-shot, best of 3 timed passes) | cell | DSpark | IndexCache | accuracy | throughput | |---|---|---|---|---| | c4 | off | off | 96.0%, 96.5% | 4087, 4525 tok/s | | c2 | off | **on** | 96.0%, 96.0% | 4322, 4081 tok/s | | c1 | **on** | off | 96.0%, 97.0% | 3449, 3742 tok/s | | c3 | **on** | **on** | 97.0% | 3873 tok/s | IndexCache changes neither accuracy nor throughput here. Note this shape is ~91% prefill tokens (180K prefill vs 17K decode) and saturates the GPU, so it is not informative about speculative decoding; the concurrency sweep below is. ### Throughput vs concurrency (short prompt, 512 output tokens) | concurrency | c4 baseline | c1 DSpark | c3 DSpark + IndexCache | |---|---|---|---| | 4 | 560 tok/s | **1419** | 1201 | | 16 | 1670 tok/s | 3289 | **3419** | | 64 | 4910 tok/s | 6975 | **7187** | The two features are complementary and stack: at the concurrencies that matter for serving, DSpark + IndexCache is the fastest configuration. Draft acceptance is 63-69% (mean accepted length 4.2-4.5 of 5) with IndexCache both on and off, so IndexCache does not measurably degrade the draft. ### Long-context correctness A needle-in-a-haystack probe (18,930-token prompt, needle at depth 0.15 / 0.5 / 0.85, greedy) retrieves correctly with IndexCache off, at freq=2, and at freq=3. ### DSpark interaction DeepSeek-V4's DSpark draft builds its decoder layers with `topk_indices_buffer=None` and layer ids >= `num_hidden_layers`, so draft layers resolve to `compress_ratio == 1` and never construct an indexer; the two features are structurally orthogonal. Enabling both is exercised end to end at every concurrency above. ## Notes Not covered, stated rather than implied: no Blackwell run (#49085 hard-rejects non-SM90 for this feature; this PR does not gate, which may be wrong); no PP>1 e2e run (the per-stage rule is unit-tested only); Meanwhile, if B200 number testing needed, I will provide later follow up test in NVFP4. AI Assistance are used for this development. --- ## Full measurement set (AIPerf) Everything below is `aiperf profile` against `vllm serve` on the same node: single 8xH100 80GB, TP=8, upstream vLLM 0.26.0 + this patch, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`, AIPerf 0.12.0. Output length is pinned with `ignore_eos:true` + `min_tokens` (without it the model stops early and throughput deltas measure differing OSL, not speed), `--request-count` = 16x concurrency, `--warmup-request-count` = concurrency. `ISL x concurrency` is chosen to fit the ~108K-token KV pool at each point; beyond that requests queue and the run becomes a scheduling test rather than a throughput test. ### Controls Two arms exist purely to bound what a real effect must beat: - **`freq=1`** enables IndexCache but skips nothing, so it must land on top of `off`. It does, everywhere. - **`off` re-run** gives the run-to-run noise floor. | control | throughput delta vs `off` | |---|---| | `freq=1`, all five workloads | -0.1% .. +0.1% | | `off` re-run, 3 workloads | -0.1% .. +0.0% | TTFT is the exception: identical configs vary by up to 5.8% on the 4K point, so no TTFT claim below ~6% is meaningful there. ### Output token throughput, delta vs `off` | workload | ISL/OSL | conc | freq=1 | freq=2 | freq=3 | freq=4 | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | summarisation (prefill-heavy) | 32K / 16 | 3 | -0.0% | +3.3% | +5.2% | **+5.6%** | | long chat | 32K / 256 | 3 | +0.1% | +3.5% | +4.9% | **+5.2%** | | mid chat | 16K / 256 | 6 | +0.0% | +2.8% | +3.9% | **+4.2%** | | RAG | 7K / 172 | 12 | +0.1% | — | **+3.2%** | — | | short chat | 4K / 256 | 24 | -0.1% | +2.0% | +2.8% | **+3.1%** | Absolute baselines: 13.63, 146.34, 285.82, 466.5, 1057.42 out tok/s respectively. ### Latency, delta vs `off` (freq=4; freq=3 for RAG) | workload | e2e | TTFT | ITL | |---|---|---|---| | 32K / 16 | -5.3% | -5.1% | — | | 32K / 256 | -5.0% | -5.1% | -4.8% | | 16K / 256 | -4.0% | -4.6% | -3.7% | | 7K / 172 | -3.1% | -2.7% | — | | 4K / 256 | -3.0% | -1.9% | -3.2% | ### Accuracy per frequency | freq | GSM8K (200q, 5-shot) | MMLU (500q, 5-shot) | |---|---|---| | off | 96.0% | 85.4% | | 1 (control) | 96.0% | 85.0% | | 2 | 95.5% | 85.4% | | 3 | 96.0% | **86.2%** | | 4 | **96.5%** | 85.0% | No trend: the best GSM8K score is at freq=4 and the best MMLU at freq=3, and the `freq=1` control differs from `off` by 0.4pp on MMLU while being semantically identical to it. All deltas sit inside that noise. **This is a no-harm result, not proof of quality preservation.** Both benchmarks' prompts (~900 and ~500 tokens, i.e. ~225 and ~125 compressed) are below `index_topk=512`, so every layer selects the whole compressed sequence and IndexCache is mathematically a no-op. Long-context quality evidence is limited to the needle probe (retrieved at all three depths with IndexCache off, freq=2 and freq=3); a RULER/LongBench run at 32K is still owed. ### Where the time actually goes A torch-profiler run (eager, prefix caching off, conc 12 at 8K) attributes GPU kernel time as: | bucket | freq=0 | freq=6 | |---|---|---| | TP all-reduce + other | 6176 ms | 5254 ms | | MoE | 1003 ms | 980 ms | | norm/rope | 395 ms | 394 ms | | **indexer** | **91.7 ms (1.2%)** | **30.4 ms (0.4%)** | | compressor | 43 ms | 42 ms | The indexer is 1.2% of kernel time; the single largest kernel is `cross_device_reduce_1stage` (TP all-reduce) at ~69%. Removing 81% of the indexer work saves 61 ms directly, yet wall-clock improves several percent — the rest comes from ranks spending less time waiting inside the all-reduce. This configuration is communication-bound, which is also why the gain saturates between freq=3 and freq=4 (+0.3-0.4pp) and why a faster indexer kernel would not help much. ### Interaction with DSpark speculative decoding Decode-heavy (short prompt, 512 output tokens, `ignore_eos`), output tok/s: | concurrency | baseline | DSpark | DSpark + IndexCache | |---|---|---|---| | 4 | 560 | **1419** | 1201 | | 16 | 1670 | 3289 | **3419** | | 64 | 4910 | 6975 | **7187** | At serving concurrencies the two stack and DSpark + IndexCache is the fastest configuration. Draft acceptance is 63-69% (mean accepted length 4.2-4.5 of 5) with IndexCache both on and off, so IndexCache does not measurably degrade the draft. ### Honest summary of magnitude **+3% to +5.6%** depending on shape and frequency, saturating at freq=3-4, free at inference time, with no measurable accuracy cost in the regimes tested. That is smaller than the 7-8% reported for vllm-ascend in #45350. On this hardware the gap is explained by the profile above (communication-bound, indexer at 1.2%), by the KV pool capping `ISL x concurrency` so the indexer's share cannot grow, and by Hopper reading an FP8 indexer cache at 132 B/token where `use_fp4_indexer_cache` would halve it. ### Measurement caveats - The e2e numbers were produced by the 0.26.0-based build; upstream restructured `attention_impl` in #51430 after 0.26.0, so the rebased branch carries the same gates at the new call sites but has not itself been re-run on GPU. - One RAG data point initially showed +9.8%; its `freq=1` control read +6.6%, which flagged the baseline as un-warmed. A repeat with two independent baseline arms put the true figure at +3.2%. The table above uses the corrected value. - Single node only: no Blackwell run, and no PP>1 run (the per-stage rule is unit-tested only).

signals.title: [Bugfix][DeepSeek V4] Handle trailing system messages in prompt rendering
signals.text: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Purpose Co-authored-by: laolaoPlayer <2584941823@qq.com> Address the DeepSeek V4 trailing-system prompt-rendering edge case reported in [#40854](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/40854#issuecomment-4864596205) and [#46256](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/46256) and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/11951. When the final message has the `system` role, `render_message` leaves the prompt at a bare system-message boundary instead of appending the assistant transition. Generation can then stop immediately and return empty content. This change appends the existing assistant/thinking transition only when the `system` message is truly the final message. Existing `user` and `developer` behavior is unchanged, and no transition is inserted before a later `user`, `assistant`, or `latest_reminder` message. Open PR #43937 addresses the same symptom with an unconditional `system` allow-list entry. That broader condition changes existing `system -> latest_reminder` golden fixtures. This PR uses a trailing-only guard to preserve those prompts. The difference was documented in [#46256](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/46256#issuecomment-5204237778). No documentation update is needed because this fixes existing tokenizer behavior without adding an option or API. ## Test Plan - Add a regression test for `system -> user -> system`. - Add a non-regression test for `user -> assistant -> system -> user`. - Run the complete DeepSeek V4 tokenizer test file: ```bash VLLM_PLUGINS="" \ PYTHONPATH=/workspace/vllm-cpu-test-bootstrap-pr:/workspace/vllm-pr-c14a568e2 \ /workspace/vllm-pr-c14a568e2/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ -p no:cacheprovider \ --confcutdir=/workspace/vllm-pr-c14a568e2/tests/tokenizers_ \ /workspace/vllm-pr-c14a568e2/tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v4.py ``` - Run Ruff check, Ruff format check, and `git diff --check`. - Reuse the completed real-environment validation through the production router. ## Test Result - Before the fix: `1 failed, 1 passed`; the trailing-system prompt was missing `<｜Assistant｜></think>`. - Focused regression tests after the fix: `2 passed`. - Complete `tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v4.py`: `28 passed in 14.57s`. - Ruff check: `All checks passed!`. - Ruff format check: `2 files already formatted`. - `git diff --check upstream/main..HEAD`: passed. - Real environment: four scenarios were each run three times after deploying the source patch to all four nodes and restarting the cluster. All 12/12 requests passed. The target case returned `"4"` instead of an empty response, with no regression in the other scenarios. See the [full report](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51262#issuecomment-5204365444). - No additional NPU run was performed after rebasing because the source patch was unchanged. ## AI Assistance AI assistance was used to inspect the renderer control flow, implement the regression coverage and fix, compare related open work, and prepare validation. The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests listed above. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose and related issues are documented. - [x] The unit-test and static-check commands are provided. - [x] Unit-test, static-check, and real-environment results are recorded. - [x] Documentation impact was considered; no documentation change is needed. </details>

signals.title: [V1] Fix CPU sampler ignoring request seeds in mixed batches (#51226)
signals.text: Correct the logic check in TopKTopPSampler.forward_cpu to ensure we only skip to the compiled unseeded random sampler if all requests in the batch have no custom generators (seeds). If even one request in the batch has a seed, we fall back to the native path to correctly isolate and apply each request's seed generator. Also make uvloop optional in llm/v1/utils.py to allow importing and running test suites on Windows/macOS. ## Purpose Fixes issue #51226. Currently, `TopKTopPSampler.forward_cpu` selects the compiled unseeded random sampler whenever `len(generators) != batch_size`. This causes request-specific seeds to be completely ignored on CPU when running in a batch alongside unseeded requests. This PR changes the check to `len(generators) == 0` so that the compiled unseeded sampler is only used when no request in the batch is seeded. If any request is seeded, the sampler falls back to the native Gumbel sampling path which correctly applies the request generators. Additionally, this PR makes the `uvloop` import in `vllm/v1/utils.py` optional (falling back to standard library `asyncio`) so that vLLM V1 can be imported and unit-tested on Windows/macOS. ## Test Plan I added the unit test `test_cpu_sampler_mixed_seeding` in `tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py` which creates a batch of two requests (one seeded, one unseeded) and verifies that the seeded request remains fully deterministic across runs while the unseeded request remains non-deterministic. Run the test command: $env:PYTHONPATH="."; .venv\Scripts\python -m pytest tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py -v -k test_cpu_sampler_mixed_seeding ## Test Result tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py::test_cpu_sampler_mixed_seeding PASSED [100%] =================== 1 passed, 131 deselected in 3.08s =================== --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signals.title: [Core] Disable fuse_allreduce_rms under VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT (non-deterministic under TP)
signals.text: ## Purpose Fixes #51290. `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` is bit-stable on a single GPU but **non-deterministic under tensor parallelism**: repeating a byte-identical workload against the same engine returns different logprobs (and, on near-ties, different tokens) once `tensor_parallel_size > 1`. The cause is the fused all-reduce + RMSNorm pass (`fuse_allreduce_rms`, a FlashInfer kernel), which reduces in a run-to-run-varying order under TP. It is enabled by `enable_allreduce_rms_fusion()` exactly when `TP > 1` on Hopper/Blackwell with flashinfer, i.e. the regime where batch invariance is expected to hold. This disables the fusion when batch invariance is requested, mirroring the existing `disable_custom_all_reduce = True` guard in `ParallelConfig` (which handles the analogous non-batch-invariant custom all-reduce path). It is an 8-line early return; TP=1 and non-batch-invariant runs are unaffected. ### Relationship to #50505 This is the Hopper/Blackwell-side complement to #50505. On cc≥90 the `fuse_allreduce_rms` pass replaces the TP all-reduce with a FlashInfer fused kernel, bypassing the custom all-reduce that #50505 pins to its deterministic 1-stage path. Disabling the fusion here lets the all-reduce fall through to that path. The two compose: with #50505 the fallback is the fast 1-stage custom all-reduce (~97% throughput); without it, NCCL (see Performance). On A100 the fusion pass is inactive (cc<90), so #50505 alone covers that hardware; this PR is what extends the fix to Hopper/Blackwell. ## Test Plan Run the same workload 8 times against one engine and count distinct bit-exact outputs (from #51290). Requires the `if __name__ == "__main__":` guard because TP>1 uses spawn. ```python import os, itertools os.environ["VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT"] = "1" from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams def main(): llm = LLM(model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct", tensor_parallel_size=4, gpu_memory_utilization=0.9, enable_prefix_caching=True) sp = SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, max_tokens=1, logprobs=20) prompts = [f"{'the quick brown fox ' * 50} item {i}:" for i in range(2000)] runs = [] for _ in range(8): out = llm.generate(prompts, sp, use_tqdm=False) runs.append([(o.outputs[0].token_ids[0], o.outputs[0].logprobs[0][o.outputs[0].token_ids[0]].logprob) for o in out]) groups = [] for i, r in enumerate(runs): if not any(runs[g[0]] == r and g.append(i) is None for g in groups): groups.append([i]) print(f"{len(groups)} distinct bit-exact outputs over {len(runs)} identical runs") if __name__ == "__main__": main() ``` ## Test Result Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, H100, vLLM 0.25.1 (the fix function is byte-identical on `main`): | config | distinct bit-exact outputs / 8 | verdict | |---|---|---| | `tensor_parallel_size=1` | 1 | deterministic (unaffected) | | `tensor_parallel_size=4`, before | 8 | non-deterministic | | `tensor_parallel_size=4`, after this PR | 1 | deterministic | With the fix, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` at TP=4 auto-disables the fusion (the `Enabled custom fusions: allreduce_rms` / `Auto-selected flashinfer allreduce` log lines disappear) and the 8 identical runs collapse to a single bit-exact output. Also confirmed on Llama-3.1-70B (dense, TP=4), and the bug reproduces on both 0.20.2 and 0.25.1. ## Performance Disabling the fusion has a throughput cost, confined to `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` + TP>1 (non-batch-invariant runs and TP=1 are unaffected). Decode-heavy generation, TP=4, H100: | model | fusion on (baseline) | fusion off (this PR) | cost | |---|---|---|---| | Qwen2.5-7B (128 x 256 tok) | 18,355 tok/s | 7,450 tok/s | ~2.5x slower | | Llama-3.1-70B (64 x 128 tok) | 1,618 tok/s | 935 tok/s | ~1.7x slower | This cost reflects the NCCL fallback used before #50505. With #50505's deterministic 1-stage custom all-reduce enabled, the all-reduce falls through to that path instead, which runs at ~97% of fused throughput at default dispatch. So the number above is a pre-#50505 artifact, not an inherent cost of this PR. The cost is largest for decode-heavy workloads, where the all-reduce runs every layer per token; prefill-heavy workloads (long prompt, few output tokens) see considerably less. I checked whether a cheaper, performance-preserving fix inside the fused kernel exists, and none does. The fused kernel is nondeterministic by construction, and no config knob restores determinism: - **Backend:** both `mnnvl` and `trtllm` are nondeterministic on 0.25.1 (H100). `mnnvl` (multicast/Lamport) diverges with token flips. `trtllm` (fixed-order fp32 reduction, but Lamport/two-shot) is smaller-magnitude yet still not bit-exact: 8 distinct logprob groups over 8 identical runs (0 token flips that run, but the sub-bit-exact residual still tips near-ties at scale). - **`fp32_acc`:** already `True` by default, insufficient. - **Autotune:** `enable_flashinfer_autotune=False` does not help. The divergence is intra-process (repeated `generate()` against one engine diverge with the kernel selection already fixed), so it is the kernel's runtime reduction order, not autotune selection. - **One-shot:** forcing `use_oneshot=True` overflows the one-shot workspace on large tensors, and the one-shot path is itself nondeterministic on small tensors. So disabling the fusion under BI is the correct trade, consistent with the existing `disable_custom_all_reduce` guard. Performance is recovered by #50505 (the deterministic 1-stage custom all-reduce this PR falls through to). A fully-fused deterministic kernel would only claw back the last few percent over that and is not needed here.

signals.title: [LoRA] Add fixed-weight routed LoRA reference path
signals.text: ## Purpose Foundational implementation for #49705. This PR adds fixed-weight routed LoRA support for requests of the form: `base(x) + sum_i w_i * LoRA_i(x)` The goal is to make vLLM capable of carrying and applying multiple LoRA adapters per token before adding learned/router-based MoE-LoRA routing in follow-up work. This PR includes: - `LoRARoutingRequest` for grouping multiple concrete `LoRARequest`s. - `LoRARouteMapping` for per-token adapter slots and weights. - Shared route-building helpers for v1 GPU/TPU input paths. - Routed LoRA metadata conversion in the Punica wrapper. - Reference routed LoRA execution for linear layers. - Coverage for replicated, column-parallel, row-parallel, QKV, quantized base layers, and fully sharded LoRA. - Fail-closed behavior for embeddings/logits, which are not supported in this PR. This PR intentionally does not add: - learned/router-based MoE-LoRA gates, - per-layer dynamic routing, - optimized routed Punica/Triton kernels, - embedding/logits routed LoRA support. Those are planned as follow-up work under #49705. Duplicate-work check: - Checked RFC #49705 comments. - Checked open PRs referencing `49705 in:body`; none found. - Checked open PRs for routed/MoE LoRA keywords. Related PRs #46772 and #39230 are adjacent work, but neither implements routed mixtures of multiple LoRA adapters per request/token. AI assistance was used while developing this PR. I reviewed the resulting changes and tests. ## Test Plan - Unit tests for routed request validation and helper behavior. - Unit tests for v1 routed LoRA state/mapping construction. - Reference-output tests comparing routed LoRA layer outputs against explicit PyTorch oracles. - Coverage includes replicated linear, quantized base linear, QKV, fully sharded column/row/QKV paths. ## Test Result ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/lora/test_lora_routing.py tests/lora/ test_layers_utils.py -q # 18 passed .venv/bin/pre-commit run ruff-check --files <changed files> # Passed .venv/bin/pre-commit run ruff-format --files <changed files> # Passed .venv/bin/python -m py_compile vllm/lora/layers/base_linear.py vllm/lora/ layers/column_parallel_linear.py vllm/lora/layers/row_parallel_linear.py tests/lora/test_lora_routing.py vllm/lora/routing_utils.py # Passed git diff --check origin/main..HEAD # Passed No model evals were run because this PR adds infrastructure/reference execution tests and does not change default model behavior unless routed LoRA requests are explicitly used.

signals.title: [Bugfix] Fix hybrid attention cache miss due to eagle drop
signals.text: ## Purpose This PR fixes an unexpected prefix cache miss bug in hybrid sparse attention models. ## Bug Setup: - Kimi K3, TP8 B300 - Block size: 1536 - Prefix-match unit (PMU): 128 - Cache retention interval: 0 (only cache at prompt boundary) Turn 1: prompt_length=24576, cache_hit_length=0 [expected] Turn 2: prompt_length=50000, cache_hit_length=23040 [expected] Turn 1: prompt_length=24577, cache_hit_length=0 [expected] Turn 2: prompt_length=50000, cache_hit_length=0 [unexpected - full miss] The cause: Mamba caches state at two prompt-boundary positions: - the last block-aligned position for `prompt_length - 1`; and - the last PMU-aligned position, registered as a partial block entry. With `prompt_length=24576` those are 23040 and 24576. With `prompt_length=24577` both collapse to 24576. Full attention is cached up to 24576. The current prefix cache implementation requires Eagle to match one block (128 in this case) past the candidate and then dropping it. The `23040` mamba checkpoint in case 1 satisfies a cache hit where `23040 + 128` is cached in full attention. But in case 2 there is no mamba checkpoint that can satisfy it, and thus leads to a full miss. ## Fix The PR fixes by moving the mamba/SWA cache state position forward when using eagle so that it can match an extra unit/block of full attention cache to drop. ## Test Plan ## Test Result --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details> **BEFORE SUBMITTING, PLEASE READ <https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/contributing>** (anything written below this line will be removed by GitHub Actions)

signals.title: [Bugfix][Model] deepseek-vl2: restore original DeepseekV2Config defaults for omitted language_config fields
signals.text: ## Purpose Loading `deepseek-ai/deepseek-vl2-small` (and `deepseek-ai/deepseek-vl2`) currently crashes during model initialization: ``` TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'NoneType' and 'int' ``` at `DeepseekV2Attention.__init__` (`self.kv_lora_rank + self.qk_rope_head_dim`). Working around that surfaces a second failure while loading `embed_tokens`: ``` AssertionError # loaded_weight.shape[output_dim] == self.org_vocab_size ``` Both failures share one root cause. DeepSeek-VL2 checkpoints ship an incomplete `language_config` that relies on the defaults of the *original* DeepSeek-VL2 `DeepseekV2Config` (`vocab_size=102400`, `kv_lora_rank=512`, `qk_nope_head_dim=128`, `qk_rope_head_dim=64`, `v_head_dim=128`). For example, `deepseek-vl2-small`'s `language_config` contains neither `vocab_size` nor `kv_lora_rank`. vLLM does not use the model's remote config; `DeepseekVLV2Config` parses `language_config` with the built-in Transformers `DeepseekV2Config` (`DeepseekVLV2TextConfig`), whose generic defaults differ: - `DeepseekV2Config().vocab_size == 32000` (not 102400) - `DeepseekVLV2TextConfig.kv_lora_rank` is forced to `None` So omitted fields silently resolve to wrong values: 1. `kv_lora_rank=None` makes `ModelConfig.is_deepseek_mla` return `False` (`use_mla=False`); combined with the non-zero `qk_*_head_dim` defaults the decoder falls through to `DeepseekV2Attention`, which computes `kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim` → `None + int` → `TypeError`. 2. `vocab_size=32000` mismatches the checkpoint's 102400-row `embed_tokens`, tripping the assertion in `VocabParallelEmbedding.weight_loader`. This fix restores the original DeepSeek-VL2 defaults **only for fields the checkpoint does not set**, before building the text config: ``` deepseek_vl2_reference_defaults = { "vocab_size": 102400, "kv_lora_rank": 512, "qk_nope_head_dim": 128, "qk_rope_head_dim": 64, "v_head_dim": 128, } for key, value in deepseek_vl2_reference_defaults.items(): language_config.setdefault(key, value) ``` ## Test Plan Serve deepseek-ai/deepseek-vl2-small and confirm it no longer crashes ## Test Result --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signals.title: [ROCm][Perf] Skip redundant sparse index remap on non-indexer layers
signals.text: ## Summary With cross-layer index sharing, only some attention layers update the shared top-k buffer. The old path still remapped that buffer on every layer. This PR runs the remap only when the layer owns an indexer. For GLM-5.2 with `index_topk_freq = 4`, this reduces remaps from 78 to 21 per forward pass. ## Safety - Layer 0 always owns an indexer, so the shared output is initialized before reuse. - Non-indexer layers do not change the inputs to the remap. - The default `index_topk_freq = 1` path is unchanged. - Speculative decoding still remaps on every layer. ## Results MI355X, TP=4, rank 0, same serving workload: | remap kernel | before | after | change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | launches | 139,378 | 37,254 | **-73.3%** | | GPU time | 2,392.1 ms | 645.7 ms | **-73.0%** | | launches per layer | 1.000 | 0.269 | matches 21/78 | The red box below is a redundant remap on a layer with no indexer. signals.title: [ROCm][Perf] Skip cleaning sparse prefill MQA logits
signals.text: ## Summary The sparse prefill path creates the MQA-logits buffer with `torch.full(..., -inf)`. This launches an FP32 fill before every logits kernel. This PR passes `clean_logits=False` to AITER, so the buffer uses `torch.empty` and the fill is removed. ## Safety The only consumer is `top_k_per_row_prefill`. It reads each row only inside `[cu_seqlen_ks, cu_seqlen_ke)`. Its vectorized path also guards the final partial load, so padding values are never read. The top-k result is unchanged. ## Results MI355X, TP=4, rank 0, comparable before/after captures: | metric | before | after | |---|---:|---:| | FP32 fill launches | 18,162 | **0** | | FP32 fill GPU time | 1,250.2 ms | **0 ms** | | MQA-logits launches | 18,108 | 17,930 | The removed fill was **0.89% of total GPU kernel time**. signals.title: [Quantization][Humming] Support MXFP4 weight + block-FP8 activation for MoE
signals.text: ## Purpose Enable Humming MoE GEMM with **MXFP4 weights + block-FP8 (group-128) activations**. To do this we had to: ## Cap MoE tuning K-block at 128 Small-M tiles can select a K-block of 256 (`block_shape[2]`), whose TMA descriptor the driver rejects at `cuLaunchKernelEx` (`CUDA_ERROR_MISALIGNED_ADDRESS`). It fires in `profile_run`, so `--enforce-eager` does not avoid it. `_cap_tuning_config_k_block` caps `block_shape[2]` at 128 — what Humming already uses for larger M — so the W4A8 MoE runs under CUDA graphs. ### Usage On an MXFP4-weight checkpoint (e.g. `nm-testing/Qwen3-30B-A3B-MXFP4A16`): ``` VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG='{"dtype":"float8e4m3","group_size":128}' ``` The per-token variant `{"dtype":"float8e4m3"}` and BF16 dispatch for non-block schemes are unchanged. ## Test Plan - `tests/quantization/test_humming_mxfp4_block_fp8.py`: schema→`QuantKey` mapping, `(kMxfp4Static, kFp8Dynamic128Sym)` now allowed, block-FP8 config is `is_block_quantized` with a `[1, 128]` block, and default (no block shape) stays per-token/deferred. Schema-mapping cases skip when Humming isn't installed. - `tests/evals/gsm8k/configs/humming/Qwen3-30B-A3B-MXFP4A16-humming-act-fp8-block.yaml` — GSM8K config, added to `config-act-fp8.txt`. ## Test Result QuantKey-level verification passing locally: ``` grouped-128 float32 == kFp8Dynamic128Sym : True grouped-128 uint8 == kFp8Dynamic128Sym : False (old behavior) per-token float32 == kFp8DynamicTokenSym: True group-32 uint8 == kMxfp8Dynamic : True ``` ``` |Tasks|Version| Filter |n-shot| Metric | |Value | |Stderr| |-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:| |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.9447|± |0.0063| | | |strict-match | 5|exact_match|↑ |0.9454|± |0.0063| ``` Nsight compute trace of the situ mul quant kernel: [nsight-compute-situ-mul-quant-trace.ncu-rep.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31149498/nsight-compute-situ-mul-quant-trace.ncu-rep.zip) > [!NOTE] > Draft: end-to-end GSM8K accuracy on H200 still to be run. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signals.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Remove heuristic speculative method inference
signals.text: ## Summary This PR removes speculative-method guessing from model and path names. The method must now come from the user or a checkpoint schema that explicitly declares it; ambiguous configurations fail with an actionable error instead of silently falling back to `draft_model`. This matters for neutral training paths. In the original Qwen3-8B + DFlash reproduction, the misdetected `draft_model` path had acceptance length **1.02**, while explicit `method="dflash"` reached **3.88**. ## Configuration contract - `method` is the sole algorithm selector. It may come from `"method"` in `--speculative-config`, `--spec-method`, or a known schema declaration such as speculators format. - Paths, names, architectures, and structural `model_type` values never select the method. - `model` identifies an external draft source only; it does not select or validate the method. - An ordinary target with no speculative configuration remains non-speculative, even if it contains auxiliary weights. - `mtp` and `dspark` may omit `model` to reuse weights embedded in the target checkpoint. The explicit method selects the corresponding loader. - Model-free methods such as `ngram` and `suffix` reject `model`. - After method selection, checkpoint metadata fills only missing implementation settings. User values win field by field. - Proposal depth can default from speculators `speculative_tokens`, `n_predict`, or DFlash/DSpark block metadata. When block metadata is known, an explicit DFlash/DSpark value may reduce but not exceed the trained proposal depth. - A speculators-format checkpoint used as the top-level model continues to work without explicit flags because its schema declares the algorithm and proposal depth. For checkpoints such as DeepSeek-V4 that can support multiple implementations, metadata configures the method selected by the user; it does not choose among `draft_model`, `mtp`, and `dspark`. ## Behavior change and compatibility This PR does **not** introduce a new configuration interface. - **Existing interfaces, unchanged:** `--speculative-config` and the existing `--spec-method`, `--spec-model`, and `--spec-tokens` aliases all remain supported. - **Behavior before this PR:** when `method` was omitted, vLLM could guess it from model/path substrings and otherwise fall back to `draft_model`. - **Behavior after this PR:** path/name guessing is removed. `method` must be supplied through an existing interface or declared by a known checkpoint schema. Therefore, an existing JSON configuration that relied on guessing only needs an explicit `method`: ```bash vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B \ --speculative-config '{ "method": "dflash", "model": "/path/to/checkpoints/6" }' ``` When the checkpoint exposes its proposal depth, `num_speculative_tokens` can be omitted; otherwise it remains required. A generic autoregressive draft should use `method="draft_model"`. The old `"model": "ngram"` and `"model": "[ngram]"` sentinels are rejected; use `method="ngram"`. ## Validation - Model evaluation from the motivating reproduction: acceptance length **1.02** with the misdetected `draft_model` versus **3.88** with explicit `dflash`. GPU evaluation was not rerun for the configuration-only follow-up. - `tests/test_config.py`: **238 passed, 2 deselected**. - Focused method/schema/default matrix: **24 passed, 216 deselected**. - DSpark configuration tests: **11 passed**. - All configured pre-commit hooks passed on the follow-up files, including Ruff, mypy, Markdown lint, SPDX, and configuration validation. <details> <summary>Commands run</summary> ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_config.py \ -k "not test_rope_customization and not test_eagle_draft_model_config" .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_config.py \ -k "spec_model_declaration or block_drafters or explicit_method_selects_deepseek_v4_loader or dspark_reuses_embedded_target_and_defaults_tokens or speculators_format_declares or speculators_format_preserves" .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ tests/transformers_utils/test_dspark_mla_config.py .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \ docs/features/speculative_decoding/README.md \ docs/features/speculative_decoding/adaptive_verification.md \ tests/test_config.py \ tests/transformers_utils/test_dspark_mla_config.py \ vllm/config/speculative.py \ vllm/transformers_utils/configs/k3_dspark.py ``` </details> ## Contribution notes - This is not a duplicate of #47490, which preserves auto-detection and validates explicit mismatches; this PR removes auto-detection. - This is not a duplicate of #44566, which only propagates speculators token depth. - This is not a duplicate of #52165, which detects DeepSeek-V4 DSpark metadata for routing; here the explicit method remains authoritative. - AI assistance was used. I reviewed every changed line and ran the validation above.

signals.title: [Render][1/n] Paged shared memory storage for mm tensor ipc.
signals.text:
## Purpose Paged shared memory storage for mm tensor ipc. 0. This compares two approaches for IPC of mm tensors: - **Paged shared memory (pshm):** mm tensor → shm → swap_blocks_batch → GPU - **ZMQ RPC:** mm tensor → ZMQ IPC → CPU Buffer → Pin Memory → GPU 1. CPU‑to‑GPU (H2D) bandwidth saturates when transferring 1 MiB blocks, so a page size of 1 MiB is a reasonable choice for shared memory storage. 2. A typical multimodal data payload is around 10 MiB, which is larger than page size of 1 MiB. Therefore, using paged shared memory for storing and transferring mm tensors is practically meaningful. 3. For payloads smaller than one page (e.g., 0.5 MiB), shared memory space is wasted, and the performance is nearly identical to that of ZMQ RPC. Hence, such small payloads offer no practical advantage. 4. Every copy operation along the mm data path introduces overhead, with dynamic memory allocation and pin memory being particularly expensive. Thus, removing the ZMQ IPC → CPU Buffer → Pin Memory steps in the ZMQ RPC path would bring significant performance gains. Supplement↓
### 1. CPU‑to‑GPU (H2D) bandwidth saturates when transferring 1 MiB blocks PTAL: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48936 ### 2. A typical multimodal data payload is around 10 MiB Qwen2VL outputs 10,764 patches when the input is a 1920×1080 image. Stored in bf16, this takes about 24 MiB; stored in uint8 (see #50411), it uses about 12 MiB. ### 3. For payloads smaller than one page (e.g., 0.5 MiB), the performance is nearly identical to that of ZMQ RPC. Hence, such small payloads offer no practical advantage. https://github.com/noooop/snippet/tree/main/benchmarks/pshm/h2d | Scenario | Data Path | ZMQ Usage | |----------|-----------|-----------| | **zmq** | CPU Source → ZMQ Send → ZMQ IPC → ZMQ Receive → CPU Buffer → Pin Memory → GPU | **Transfers full data payload** | | **zmq+shm (copy)** | Shared Memory → CPU Read → Clone → Pin Memory → GPU | **Control only** | | **zmq+shm (no-copy)** | Shared Memory → Zero-copy CPU Read → GPU | **Control only** | ### 4. Removing the ZMQ IPC → CPU Buffer → Pin Memory steps in the ZMQ RPC path would bring significant performance gains. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5ac2684976ee22c04fe0d2f968c6cf6096b383f2/vllm/v1/serial_utils.py#L416-L425
## Test Plan tests/models/multimodal/generation_ppl_test/test_qwen.py::test_pshm ## Test Result Model: Qwen/Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct mm_device_do_normalize: True VLLM: dtype:torch.bfloat16 head_dtype:torch.bfloat16 41096328.0 Transformers: Constant 41081356.0 Difference (%): 0.03644475610785584 PASSED ---

signals.title: support rl feature : weight checker
signals.text: ## Purpose In the RL training loop: start_weight_update → update_weights* → finish_weight_update, we need to confirm that after the training side pushes/synchronizes the Actor weights to the rollout inference engine, the weights held by the engine are indeed consistent with what we intended to push. Before the training loop begins, check the correctness of the weight-update function to avoid off-policy training crashes. To confirm that this weight update actually landed and was not corrupted or partially written, a reproducible verification mechanism is needed. **weight_checker** is designed for exactly this: it computes a **SHA-256 checksum for each weight tensor of the model** and takes **snapshots (snapshot)** and **comparisons (compare)** before and after the update, so that you can verify ahead of time "whether the weights actually changed / whether they are complete." The four actions that weight_checker depends on: * **snapshot**: Compute a SHA-256 value of the current weights and store it as a baseline * **compare**: Recompute the current SHA-256 values Gang compare them with the snapshot, returning `match` + `mismatches` * **checksum**: Return the current per-tensor SHA-256 values without storing them (idempotent) * **reset**: Randomize the weights after a snapshot, to set up detection of whether a later weight update was correct RFC： #[52689](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52689) ## Test Plan A single parameterized test file drives the dev server for each TP setting and verifies: -snapshot returns a structured response with a positive tensor count, and repeated snapshots are consistent. -compare requires a prior snapshot (400 otherwise), matches when weights are unchanged, and still matches after a sleep/wake cycle and after a generate request. -checksum returns per-tensor 64-character SHA-256 digests, is stable across calls, and does not clobber an existing snapshot. -reset rewrite the model weight to check update is correct. -error handling rejects missing/unknown actions cleanly while /health stays up. -world size matches the configured tensor_parallel_size. | Test group | Functional points covered | Priority | | --- | --- | --- | | API| Snapshot creation and replacement; compare state handling; checksum stability and snapshot isolation; sleep/wake and generation consistency; invalid-action handling; server health; reset and weight-update verification | P0 | | TP | Checksum and comparison behavior with tensor parallelism enabled | P1 | | EP | Checksum coverage of locally owned expert weights with expert parallelism enabled | P1 | ## Test Result default test tp=1 and 2 and tp2ep test tp use
