signals.title: [Frontend] Add reusable TP1 initialized-engine snapshots
signals.text: ## Purpose and prior art RFC #34303 and #37921/#37925 put CUDA checkpoint primitives below CRIU disk persistence. #35934 and #46089 explore related lifecycle and provider shapes, while #52132 keeps the frontend alive during EngineCore L3 sleep. This PR targets a different event: no serving process remains, and a trusted same-host operator restores one prepared Linux x86-64 TP1 engine before HTTP bind. @simon-mo asked me to split the generic CLI refactor out of #51360. This branch is stacked on `lazy-cli-dispatch`; the [snapshot-only comparison](https://github.com/thaw-ai/vllm/compare/lazy-cli-dispatch...tp1-snapshot-product) is 16 files (`+2,904/-39`). It contains the snapshot CLI, product code, Docker runtime, documentation, 27 unit cases, and one optional GPU end-to-end job. ```bash vllm snapshot create MODEL --snapshot-dir PATH --revision MODEL_SHA [serve args] vllm snapshot inspect PATH vllm snapshot restore PATH --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 ``` ## The fix `vllm snapshot create` initializes the engine and records a deterministic one-token oracle. Compact capture is the default: the existing sleep level 2 lifecycle releases model weights and KV cache before CRIU dump. Restore reloads that state, reproduces the captured token ID, text, and sampled log probability, and only then binds HTTP. A mismatch fails closed. This revision addresses the August 19 review: - The generic lazy CLI work is a separate prerequisite. - The Dockerfile now calls one installer script that owns the CRIU 4.2.1, CUDA plugin, and checkpoint-helper pins. - The manifest is a strict frozen Pydantic model. Secure path checks, atomic publication, credential exclusion, and runtime compatibility checks remain explicit. - `controller.py` is now 121 lines of public transaction orchestration. The private host runtime owns CRIU, PID/session, TCP, `io_uring`, GPU inventory, and rollback behavior. - Restore rejects an occupied captured PID before changing artifact state or calling CRIU, then uses pidfds to pin and clean the restored tree. - The branch includes an optional full-H200 create, inspect, restore, HTTP, second-restore, and cleanup job. The runner privilege contract still needs CI owner confirmation. ## Measured The matched large-model campaign used source `5dd888926f`, Qwen3-32B BF16 TP1, and one H100 PCIe 80 GB. Model and generated-cache files were resident; compact artifact files were evicted before each restore. | Path | Median activation | Samples | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Ordinary warm process | 54.7029 s | 3 | | Compact snapshot restore | 20.3795 s | 3 | | Reduction | 34.3234 s, 62.7% | 3 per arm | The compact artifact used 5,879,914,496 allocated bytes. The 65,540,298,478-byte model tree remained external. Creation took 78.5275 seconds, n=1, so the measured saving broke even on the third activation. Every accepted trial returned token ID `12095` and text ` Paris`. ## Verified on hardware Exact source `e464e2f6ae` on main `6df7adc17f` built a Linux amd64 image in 957 seconds on an RTX 4090 Laptop GPU rig. The image carried exact source labels and vLLM version `0.1.dev20225+ge464e2f6a`; native CUDA extensions came from the published current-main ancestor `44cf3f0466`. Qwen3-0.6B compact creation took 58.961 seconds, n=1, and produced a 3,565,976,397-byte manifest-reported artifact. The same artifact restored twice in the same container across `docker stop` and `docker start`, in 3.233 and 2.931 seconds, n=1 each. Both public requests returned token ID `12095`, text ` Paris`, and sampled log probability `-0.42565488815307617`, exactly matching the manifest. A control with the expected log probability shifted by 10 failed closed in 3.514 seconds, n=1, without publishing a ready server. Final checks found no container, process, listener, GPU process, link remap, or changed `io_uring` state. ## Test plan ```text .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_launch_cli.py \ tests/cuda/test_cuda_compatibility_path.py # 69 passed, two pre-existing warnings uvx pre-commit run --files <changed files> # all applicable hooks passed, including Python 3.10 mypy, ShellCheck, # Docker version validation, and the root lazy-import check ``` The snapshot portion adds 27 collected unit cases. They retain the public CLI, strict manifest, failure-before-mutation, PID-reuse, private-path, external TCP, and `io_uring` contracts. The optional GPU script checks 18 static contracts and the same-artifact two-restore flow. No model evaluation was run because this does not change model execution or output logic. The hardware gate instead compares the captured and restored one-token output through the public API. Native Linux arm64 `vllm-runtime-base` built from exact source `e464e2f6ae` in 499 seconds on an 8.2 GB Docker VM. The image logged the arm64 skip and contained none of CRIU, `cuda-checkpoint`, or the CUDA CRIU plugin. Initialized snapshots remain Linux x86-64 only in this PR. AMD support will follow separately. ## Product envelope - One NVIDIA GPU, TP1, PP1, DP1, and prefill-context parallel size 1. - Same trusted host and GPU, with matching driver, kernel, runtime, engine arguments, selected environment, and checkpoint tools. - Root or passwordless `sudo`, plus a private local artifact that can contain process memory and secrets. - No external established TCP peer at capture, active `io_uring`, concurrent restore, cross-host migration, GPU relocation, or ordinary-start fallback. - Compact capture requires an immutable model revision. Full-state capture keeps model state for local or mutable model sources. AI assistance was used. I take responsibility for the implementation, compatibility boundary, and measurements.

signals.title: [Core][V1] Add bounded session-affinity scheduler
signals.text: ## Purpose Add an opt-in V1 `SessionAffinityScheduler` for concurrent multi-turn and agent workloads. Before delegating to `AsyncScheduler`, it promotes at most one cache-warm continuation from a recently active typed `session_id` within a bounded FCFS window. A candidate must have an actual local prefix-cache hit. Preempted requests are never bypassed, and reordering stops after the FCFS head reaches a configurable wait deadline. The scheduler validates that asynchronous scheduling is enabled so the scheduler and worker execution modes cannot diverge. This PR also adds: - a KV-cache lookup that returns the cached-prefix length without emitting KV events; - CLI and config knobs for the affinity window, minimum cached blocks, maximum head wait, and session TTL; - automatic prefix caching documentation and focused scheduler tests. Related: #42185, #48049, #51375. ### Scope and non-duplication This is narrower than #42185: it does not apply generic cache-affinity ordering to the full queue. It only considers exact cache-warm continuations from recently scheduled typed sessions inside a bounded FCFS window. It also differs from #51375: it does not globally rank requests by residual prefill cost or SJF. Cross-session ordering remains FCFS except for the bounded continuation promotion described above. ### AI assistance OpenAI Codex was used to help inspect the codebase, implement the change, and run tests and benchmarks. The human submitter reviewed the changed lines and is responsible for the contribution. ## Test Plan - `.venv/bin/pytest tests/v1/core/test_session_affinity_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -q` - `.venv/bin/pytest tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py -k session_affinity_scheduler_args -q` - `.venv/bin/pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD` - Online A/B replay on two NVIDIA A30 GPUs with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-AWQ, one engine per GPU, automatic prefix caching enabled, `max_num_seqs=8`, `max_model_len=32768`, and the same 48-incident / 378-step replay plan. The affinity run used `window=32`, `min_blocks=4`, `max_wait=30s`, and `ttl=300s`. ## Test Result - Scheduler and prefix-cache pytest suite: `238 passed`. - CLI argument test: `1 passed`. - Pre-commit: all hooks passed. - Online A/B: all `48/48` incidents and `378/378` steps succeeded on both engines. - Throughput: `9.94 -> 12.41 incidents/min` (`+24.78%`). - Wall time: `289.62s -> 232.11s` (`-19.86%`). - Token-level prefix hit rate: `71.46% -> 83.70%` (`+12.25 pp`). - Incident P95 latency: `286.93s -> 224.81s` (`-21.65%`). - Step TTFT P95: `60.32s -> 48.09s` (`-20.28%`). These A/B numbers are from the targeted high-contention multi-session replay described above; they are not intended as a claim for generic serving workloads. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [x] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signals.title: [ROCm] Enable fused QK-norm+RoPE+gate Triton kernel for Qwen3-Next/Qwen3.5
signals.text: ## Purpose `Qwen3NextAttention` fuses the gated QKV split + QK-RMSNorm + (partial) NeoX RoPE + gate copy into a single Triton kernel (`fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate`, added in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44176). The kernel is pure Triton and backend-agnostic, but it is gated behind `current_platform.is_cuda()`, so ROCm falls back to the slow multi-op eager path, even though the kernel runs correctly and fast on AMD GPUs. This PR relaxes that one-line guard to `is_cuda_alike()` so ROCm gets the same fusion. It affects the whole `Qwen3NextAttention` family: Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5, Qwen3.5-MoE Measured on MI325X (gfx942), bf16, against the model's real eager branch (`GemmaRMSNorm` + the `rotary_emb` custom op), 300 timed iters after 50 warmup: | Seq len (tokens) | Eager (µs) | Fused (µs) | Speedup | |---|---|---|---| | 1 (decode) | 279.4 | 33.0 | 8.47× | | 8 | 279.3 | 33.6 | 8.32× | | 64 | 281.7 | 33.9 | 8.32× | | 512 | 277.4 | 33.7 | 8.22× | | 4096 | 562.3 | 138.7 | 4.05× | Note: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47719 is an opt-in AITER path that additionally fuses the KV-cache write. ## Test Plan Add a test case in `tests/kernels/core/test_fused_qk_norm_rope.py` ## Test Result ### Benchmarks Measured on MI325X (gfx942), Qwen3.5-4B with `--language-model-only` (bf16). Fused path confirmed active on all 8 full-attention layers vs. off. **Isolated kernel** — `fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate` vs. eager (GemmaRMSNorm ×2 + partial NeoX RoPE + gate copy): | T (tokens) | fused µs | eager µs | speedup | |-----------:|---------:|---------:|--------:| | 1 | 34.1 | 288.3 | 8.45× | | 64 | 34.8 | 288.3 | 8.29× | | 512 | 34.5 | 285.8 | 8.28× | | 4096 | 139.3 | 560.8 | 4.03× | **End-to-end decode throughput (tok/s), fused vs. eager path:** | Batch | eager: ON | eager: OFF | Δ | graphs: ON | graphs: OFF | Δ | |------:|----------:|-----------:|---:|-----------:|------------:|---:| | 1 | 63.1 | 57.2 | +10.3% | 286.9 | 281.1 | +2.1% | | 4 | 239.6 | 219.4 | +9.2% | 956.6 | 937.2 | +2.1% | | 16 | 785.8 | 724.2 | +8.5% | 3113.7| 3060.0| +1.8% | | 64 | 2972 | 2764 | +7.5% | 8875 | 8776 | +1.1% | | prefill 4001 tok | 103.7k | 100.3k | +3.4% | 162k | 165k | ≈ parity | --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signals.title: [Engine Core] Gather engine notifications from workers to frontends
signals.text:
First split of #45411. Notification channel only; LoRA events, the Rust frontend consumer, and the scheduler hook will follow as separate stacked PRs. ```mermaid flowchart LR W0["Worker rank 0
notification buffer"] --> G["EngineCore
gather from every rank"] WN["Worker rank N
notification buffer"] --> G G --> O["EngineCoreOutputs"] O --> F0["API server 0"] O --> FN["API server N"] ``` - `vllm/v1/notifications.py`: tagged msgspec union with `CustomNotification(key, payload)`, and a process-local worker buffer. - `WorkerBase.take_notifications()`: drains that buffer. One default implementation covers every worker type. - `EngineCore.gather_worker_notifications()`: `collective_rpc("take_notifications")`, keeping every rank. - `EngineCoreOutputs.engine_notifications`: appended field, plus the matching Rust `WireEngineCoreOutputs` field and `protocol/notifications.rs`. - `EngineCoreProc` broadcasts to all API servers so their `/metrics` agree. Why gather instead of piggybacking on `ModelRunnerOutput`: the executor only reads one rank's reply, so anything the other ranks published would just get dropped, and some paths (non-last PP rank via `with_kv_conn_output_only`) return early without a full output. The gather itself fires once when the serving loop starts, then only if you opt in with `VLLM_WORKER_NOTIFICATION_POLL_INTERVAL` (off by default). This keeps the rpc off of the engine steps path. It might be worth considering replacing this with a doorbell, for rare state change notifications, but I left that out of this PR for simplicities sake. `cargo test -p vllm-engine-core-client --lib`: 101 passed. `pytest tests/v1/engine/test_notifications.py`: 13 passed. ## AI assistance disclosure Developed code and the test harness with AI assistance (Claude Code). All changes were reviewed line-by-line by myself, who ran the tests and reviewed output.

signals.title: [Model] Add tower and connector LoRA support for LFM2-VL
signals.text: ## Purpose Part of #31479. Enable tower and connector LoRA support for LFM2-VL. LFM2-VL already implements `SupportsLoRA` and exposes its multimodal module mapping, but it is missing the token-budget helpers required by the tower/connector LoRA path. Its projector also uses plain `nn.Linear` layers, which cannot be replaced by vLLM's LoRA wrappers. This change: - converts the two projector linear layers to `ReplicatedLinear` - preserves their weight names and tensor-only forward behavior - adds `get_num_mm_encoder_tokens` - adds `get_num_mm_connector_tokens` The projector packs each `downsample_factor × downsample_factor` group of vision tokens into one connector token. Therefore: ``` encoder tokens = image tokens × downsample_factor² connector tokens = encoder tokens ÷ downsample_factor² ``` Duplicate check: - searched open and closed PRs for `LFM2 get_num_mm_encoder_tokens` - searched open and closed PRs for `lfm2_vl tower connector LoRA` - found no LFM2-VL implementation covering this feature - #49525 changes text-LoRA key mapping for multimodal wrappers and is orthogonal to this change AI assistance disclosure: OpenAI Codex assisted with issue triage, implementation, and test drafting. I reviewed, understand, and verified every changed line and the reported test results. ## Test Plan ```bash ruff check \ vllm/model_executor/models/lfm2_vl.py \ tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_lfm2_vl.py ruff format --check \ vllm/model_executor/models/lfm2_vl.py \ tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_lfm2_vl.py timeout 300 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_lfm2_vl.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py::test_set_active_mm_loras_builds_tower_and_connector_mappings ``` A focused RTX 3090 probe additionally checks: - `ReplicatedLinear` output against equivalent `torch.nn.functional.linear` operations - projector output length against the token helpers - actual conversion of both projector layers to `ReplicatedLinearWithLoRA` - loading projector weights and biases through `AutoWeightsLoader` ## Test Result Lint and formatting: ``` All checks passed! 2 files already formatted ``` Pytest: ``` 7 passed, 14 warnings in 4.78s ``` The warnings are existing `torch.jit.script_method` deprecation warnings. RTX 3090 projector probe: ``` downsample_factor: 2 encoder_tokens: 32 projector_output_tokens: 8 helper_connector_tokens: 8 helper_roundtrip_encoder_tokens: 32 output_shape: (8, 1024) numeric_parity: true lora_wrappers: ReplicatedLinearWithLoRA ReplicatedLinearWithLoRA ``` Weight-loading probe: ``` loaded_parameters: linear_1.bias linear_1.weight linear_2.bias linear_2.weight weight_loading: true ``` A full generation test with a trained LFM2-VL tower/connector LoRA adapter was not run because no suitable public adapter was used for this change.

signals.title: fix(anthropic): preserve requested model alias in messages response
signals.text: Co-authored-by: @lazypool ## Purpose Fixes #51266. ### Problem When vLLM is launched with multiple model aliases (--served-model-name alias-a alias-b), the requests to the Anthropic Messages API (POST /v1/messages) specifying a secondary alias (alias-b) received responses where the model field was canonicalized to the primary alias (alias-a). ### Impact on Anthropic Clients Anthropic clients and agentic tools like Claude Code record the returned model name in the assistant message and perform turn-by-turn model equality checks (request.model == previous_assistant_message.model). Because "alias-a != alias-b", Claude Code concluded that a model switch occurred across turns and stripped thinking blocks from the conversation history, breaking multi turn agentic tool use loops. ### Solution - Updated "AnthropicServingMessages.create_messages" to pass "request.model" into "messages_full_converter" and "message_stream_converter" - messages_full_converter: sets model = requested_model or generator.model - message_stream_converter: sets "model = requested_model or origin_chunk.model" on the "message_start" event - This preserves the requested model identity for Anthropic clients without altering the shared OpenAI serving path or its test contracts (PR #24663) ## Test Plan Added unit tests in "tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py": 1. test_requested_model_alias_preserved: verifies non-streaming responses return the requested alias (alias-b) instead of the canonical "generator.model" (alias-a). 2. test_default_model_when_requested_model_is_none: verifies safe fallback to generator.model when requested_model is not supplied. 3. test_stream_converter_preserves_requested_model_alias: verifies streaming converter's message_start event emits the requested alias (alias-b). Run commands: ```bash # Run targeted alias preservation tests PYTHONPATH=. pytest tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py -k "test_requested_model_alias_preserved or test_stream_converter_preserves_requested_model_alias or test_default_model_when_requested_model_is_none" # Run full Anthropic conversion test suite PYTHONPATH=. pytest tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py - AI usage disclosure: YES - I have used AI for understanding the code and also the flow of data from initial stage to last stage. Then I have also understood the syntax like how things are actually working. Rest I write the logic myself and fully understand all code submitted and can explain this all without any help of AI.

signals.title: [Rust][Benchmark] Load HF datasets from parquet shards via hf-hub, fixing truncated-cache sampling
signals.text: ## Purpose Fix a silent under-sampling bug in the Rust bench's `hf` dataset loader and rework the download path. **The bug:** HF datasets were cached as JSON snapshots truncated to the row count of whatever run happened first, keyed only by `dataset-config-split`. A later run requesting more prompts silently reused the truncated file — e.g. requesting the full 1319-prompt GSM8k test split yielded `samples=100 requested=1319` + `skipping dataset oversampling`, so the benchmark ran on 100 prompts while claiming to be a GSM8k run. **The rework:** - Rows now come from the dataset-viewer's auto-converted parquet shards (`refs/convert/parquet`), downloaded via hf-hub into the **standard HF hub cache** (`$HF_HOME/hub`) — shared bidirectionally with `hf download` and Python `huggingface_hub`. The cache unit is the immutable shard, so cache contents can never depend on a previous run's request size; a physically truncated shard fails loudly (missing parquet footer) instead of silently under-sampling. - The `/rows` pagination fallback is removed: per the [dataset-viewer docs](https://huggingface.co/docs/dataset-viewer/rows), `/rows` itself only works for datasets with parquet exports, so it could never succeed where the parquet path fails (verified empirically on script-based/gated datasets — both endpoints return identical errors). - New fallback for **private datasets** (which the dataset viewer does not process): discover native `*.parquet` files on the main branch via hf-hub repo listing, following the datasets library's layout conventions (config dirs, split-named files). - Sampling semantics aligned with Python `vllm bench serve`: shard order is shuffled with `--seed` (mirrors the datasets library's streaming shard shuffle instead of always sampling the split prefix), and up to 2x the requested rows are read so validity filtering backfills from real rows instead of duplicating samples. - datasets-server discovery calls now use the same auth chain as hf-hub shard downloads: `HF_TOKEN` env var, then the `hf auth login` token file (previously only the env var, so gated datasets failed at discovery for logged-in users without the env var). - `parquet` crate added with `default-features = false` + `json` — **no arrow dependency**; `Row::to_json_value()` feeds the existing `serde_json`-based column-detection pipeline unchanged. New deps in the graph: `thrift`, `snap`, `lz4_flex` (no rustls/ring; `cargo metadata` clean against `deny.toml` bans). Also fixes the stale `--random-range-ratio` README row, which still documented the removed `[len*r, len]` / default-1.0 semantics (the flag defaults to `0.0` and samples `[len*(1-r), len*(1+r)]`), and stale `AGENTS.md` module descriptions. ## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR Checked open PRs touching this area: - #50277 (draft) makes the datasets-server *endpoint* configurable for mirror routing — different problem; this PR incidentally helps that use case since shard downloads (the bulk of traffic) now honor `HF_ENDPOINT` via hf-hub, with only the two discovery calls remaining on `datasets-server.huggingface.co`. Will conflict textually in `hf_dataset.rs`; happy to coordinate. - #49641 fixes the *Python* loader when `--hf-split` is omitted — different codebase path. - #51104 is Rust multi-turn ShareGPT — no overlap in `hf_dataset.rs`. ## Test commands and results ``` cargo test -p vllm-bench # 148 passed, 0 failed cargo clippy -p vllm-bench --all-targets # 0 warnings cargo test -p vllm-bench -- --ignored test_download_gsm8k test_native_parquet # 2 passed (network: full-split regression guard + main-branch discovery) ``` Live-endpoint verification (Kimi-K3 @ 1M ctx, tiktoken tokenizer): - GSM8k `--num-prompts 1319`: **1319/1319 successful** (bug scenario previously produced 100); cold-cache dataset load 1.2s (one 419KB shard vs 14 paginated JSON calls before), warm 0.4s. - Cache interop: pre-populating with `hf download openai/gsm8k --repo-type dataset --revision refs/convert/parquet`, then running the bench → blob mtimes byte-identical before/after (zero re-download). Cross-implementation comparison vs Python `vllm bench serve` (same endpoint/tokenizer/seed, `--skip-chat-template` on Python): | test | Python | Rust | |---|---|---| | GSM8k full split input tokens | 77527 | **77527** (identical) | | MT-Bench 80-prompt input tokens | 5218 | **5218** (identical) | | result JSON schema | 34 keys | same 34 + 11 additive | Known intentional divergence (pre-existing, documented in README): the Rust loader sends prompts raw and derives per-row output lengths from the answer column, while Python's per-dataset classes may apply chat templates and fixed default output lengths (GSM8k: 193599 input tokens with template vs 77527 raw). ## Model evaluation N/A — benchmark client change; no model/serving code touched. Note the sampling-semantics alignment (shard shuffle + 2x read) changes *which rows* are benchmarked for `num_prompts < split size`; full-split runs are unaffected. ## AI assistance This PR was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). The submitter has reviewed the changes and run the tests above. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signals.title: [Rust][Benchmark] Align speed-bench CLI flags with Python and add flag parity test
signals.text: ## Purpose `VLLM_USE_RUST_BENCH=1` delegation (#50081) execs `vllm-bench` with the raw argv, so Python-documented flags must parse in the Rust CLI. The speed-bench flags had drifted: - `--speed-bench-output-len` did not exist in Rust — it failed with `unexpected argument`, and without it the output length silently fell back to `--sharegpt-output-len` → `--random-output-len` (default **128** vs Python's **4096**), making delegated speed-bench results non-comparable. This was also reported by a user on Slack (`vllm bench serve` rejecting `--speed-bench-output-len` while `--help=all` lists it, on a build from the pre-#50081 default-delegation window). - The subset flag is spelled `--speed-bench-dataset-subset` in Python but `--speed-bench-config` in Rust. A follow-up review of the spec-decode bench path against Python also found the Rust `/metrics` parser predates the Python fix in #41916, so the same latent bug was still present here. ## Changes - Add `--speed-bench-output-len` (default 4096, matching Python) and use it for the speed-bench dataset instead of the sharegpt/random fallback. - Accept `--speed-bench-dataset-subset` as a visible alias of `--speed-bench-config`. - Add `rust/src/bench/tests/cli_parity.rs`: every Python `vllm bench serve` flag must be a known vllm-bench flag/alias or an explicit `PYTHON_ONLY` allowlist entry (24 deliberate gaps: asr/bfcl/blazedit/spec-bench/timed-trace groups, plotting, etc.), plus stale-allowlist checks in both directions. The snapshot of Python flags (`python_serve_flags.txt`) is kept current by `tests/benchmarks/test_rust_bench_cli_parity.py`, so drift is caught by whichever CI (cargo or pytest) sees the change first. - Port the #41916 spec-decode `/metrics` parsing fix: match on the metric name (before labels) and only read `_total` counter samples, so `_created` timestamp series and label values containing e.g. `num_drafts` can no longer corrupt the counts. The parser is extracted as `parse_spec_decode_metrics()` with unit tests. - Warn that `--tokenizer-mode` is ignored: the flag was accepted for CLI compatibility but silently unused. Non-`auto` values now log a warning describing the actual resolution chain (HF `tokenizer.json` → tiktoken → server-side `/tokenize`; `mistral_common` tokenizers fall back to server-side tokenization), and the README documents it. ## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR Searched open PRs/issues for `speed-bench`, `speed_bench_output_len`, `bench cli parity`, `rust bench delegation`, `spec decode benchmark metrics` — no open PR touches the Rust bench speed-bench flags, CLI parity testing, or the Rust `/metrics` parser. ## Test plan - `cargo test -p vllm-bench`: 152 unit tests (incl. new alias/default test and 3 spec-decode parser tests) + 3 parity tests pass; `cargo clippy --all-targets` clean; `cargo fmt` clean. - `pytest tests/benchmarks/test_rust_bench_cli_parity.py`: 1 passed; ruff check/format clean. - Live-endpoint validation against a Kimi-K3 deployment (`--backend vllm`, 32 prompts, `--speed-bench-output-len 64`, `--disable-shuffle`, same tokenizer, Python run with `--skip-chat-template`): request data is token-identical between Python and Rust (total_input_tokens 5620 == 5620, per-request `input_lens` arrays element-wise equal, all output_lens 64); warm-vs-warm metrics agree within single-burst noise (throughput −4%, median ITL ±1%). Rust JSON schema remains a strict superset of Python's. - Spec-decode stats re-verified live after the parser fix (MTP deployment): acceptance rate 42.5%, drafts 525, draft tokens 3675 (= drafts × 7 spec tokens), per-position acceptance monotonically decreasing — consistent with pre-change runs on the same server, which does not expose `_created` series (the fix targets servers that do). - `--tokenizer-mode mistral` smoke-tested against the live endpoint: the warning fires once at config time and the run completes normally. ## Model evaluation N/A — benchmark client CLI change; no model output or serving path is affected. ## AI assistance disclosure This PR was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). The submitter has reviewed every changed line and run the tests above. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signals.title: [XPU][MoE] Resize batched Triton MoE tiles and change grid order
signals.text: # Purpose Two changes to the expert-batched Triton MoE (`BatchedTritonExperts`): - Grid order. `batched_triton_kernel` is launched with the expert id as the fastest-varying grid axis, so consecutive programs walk different experts' weights. `batched_triton_kernel_swapped` puts the tile index on axis 0 instead, so consecutive programs share an expert's weight tile. Same tiles computed, only the program-to-tile assignment changes. It is selected on XPU only, because the reorder costs up to 5.5% decode throughput on H200, so CUDA and ROCm keep the original kernel and the original grid. - Tile sizes. `try_get_optimal_moe_config` gains an optional `default_config_func`, consulted after the config override and the tuned-JSON lookup, so tuned configs still win wherever they exist. `BatchedTritonExperts` passes `get_default_batched_config`, which narrows `BLOCK_SIZE_N`/`BLOCK_SIZE_K` to 32 on XPU. The shared heuristic sizes tiles for one large `[M, K] x [K, N]` GEMM, but the batched layout runs `E` small GEMMs of at most `max_num_tokens` rows, where wide N/K tiles are mostly masked-off work. Blockwise-quantized shapes keep the shared config's K because `moe_mmk` derives scale-group offsets from it, and configs without `num_warps` (batch-invariant, wna16) pin their own tiles. `batched_triton_kernel` keeps its source and its position in the file, so its Triton cache key is unchanged and CUDA compiles the same kernel it does today. `batched_triton_kernel_swapped` differs from it by exactly the two `tl.program_id` assignments. `default_config_func` has exactly one caller, so no other config path changes. ## Testing XPU: 2× Intel Arc Pro B70, TP=2, DeepSeek-V2-Lite bf16, `moe_backend=batched_triton`, base = merge-base `bca7bea24`. | metric | base | this PR | |---|---|---| | serving throughput, `--dataset random` (output tok/s) | 110.98 | 184.61 | | offline throughput (tok/s) | 128.81 | 170.29 | | latency, batch size 32 (s) | 105.48 | 79.62 | | GSM8K, 400 questions, 5-shot | 0.3500 | 0.3450 | The GSM8K delta is −0.0050 against a one-sigma band of 0.0238, i.e. no measurable accuracy change, with identical total generated tokens. H200: 2× H200, dp2 with `--enable-expert-parallel --all2all-backend deepep_low_latency`, which is the CUDA configuration that routes through `BatchedTritonExperts`. Decode is ISL 128 / OSL 512 at concurrency 32, base = vLLM main. | model | base | this PR | reorder ungated | |---|---|---|---| | Qwen3-30B-A3B, eager | 321.2 | 320.0 | 304.0 | | Qwen3-30B-A3B, cudagraphs | 320.7 | 319.8 | 303.2 | | Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, eager | 275.4 | 275.1 | 269.5 | | Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B, eager | 227.0 | 230.0 | 226.2 | Output tok/s. The third column is the first revision of this PR, which applied the reorder on every platform: it costs 5.4% and 5.5% on the two Qwen3-30B configs and 2.1% on Qwen3.5-35B, which is what the XPU gate is there to avoid. With the gate, CUDA decode is within 0.4% of main on every config, prefill is flat, and GSM8K returns the same answers in all three arms. <details> <summary>Full perf detail, kernel-level isolation and test commands</summary> Latency at batch size 1 is flat (50.18s → 49.63s), as expected, since one token per expert leaves the kernel launch-bound either way. `bench serve` on sharegpt improves 90.12 → 159.67 output tok/s, but that workload measured ±15% run-to-run on this node (same build twice: 159.67 → 138.38), so the random-dataset and offline numbers above are the ones I would rely on. Isolating the grid order alone on XPU, with the same tensors, the same tiles and the same warp count, changing only the program-to-tile assignment: | shape | expert-first | tile-first | speedup | |---|---|---|---| | E=32, M=256, N=1408, K=2048 | 1359.8 µs | 676.9 µs | 2.01x | | E=64, M=256, N=1408, K=2048 | 3633.9 µs | 1024.0 µs | 3.55x | | E=64, M=256, wide 128/64 tiles | 6436.4 µs | 1181.4 µs | 5.45x | | E=64, M=3072, N=1408, K=2048 | 30476.8 µs | 5951.2 µs | 5.12x | Output was bitwise identical in every case. `batched_triton_kernel.cache_key` is the same on this branch as on `main`, so an existing Triton cache still hits on CUDA. H200 decode cells are means over repeated runs: 5 reps for base and the ungated reorder on Qwen3-30B eager, cudagraphs and Qwen3.5-35B; 3 reps for this PR on Qwen3-30B eager and Qwen3.5-35B; single runs for Qwen3-Next-80B and for this PR under cudagraphs. Spread across the 5-rep cells is about 1.5%, so the 5% gap the ungated reorder shows is well outside it. Running the arms in the opposite order reproduces it (302.3 output tok/s over 3 reps, against 304.0 in the original order), so it is not a warmup or thermal artifact. H200 prefill, ISL 2048 / OSL 8 at concurrency 64, total tok/s: | model | base | this PR | |---|---|---| | Qwen3-30B-A3B, eager | 15127 | 15122 | | Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, eager | 17684 | 17704 | | Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B, eager | 8227 | 8249 | | Qwen3-30B-A3B, cudagraphs | 14885 | 14916 | The Qwen3.5-35B row drops the first rep in both arms: for that model the first prefill run is compile-dominated (13856 base, 13877 this PR) and every later rep sits at 17.7k in both arms. H200 GSM8K, 200 questions, 8-shot, correct answers out of 200: | model | base | this PR | reorder ungated | |---|---|---|---| | Qwen3-30B-A3B, eager | 184 | 184 | 184 | | Qwen3-30B-A3B, cudagraphs | 188 | 188 | 188 | | Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, eager | 23 | 23 | 23 | | Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B, eager | 85 | 85 | 85 | Identical counts, which is what should happen on CUDA given that this PR runs main's kernel with main's grid there. The low absolute score on Qwen3.5-35B is a prompt-template mismatch in my eval harness rather than a model or PR problem, and it is the same in all three arms. ``` pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_batched_moe.py \ -k "swapped or blockwise_quant_k_tile or td_matches_plain or td_zero_expert \ or backend_mapping or supports_current_device or batched_experts_end_to_end" ``` → 13 passed, 768 deselected. ``` pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_batched_moe.py -k test_batched_mm ``` → 103 passed, 96 skipped on XPU, which covers the swapped kernel through `invoke_moe_batched_triton_kernel` on the fp8 and blockwise paths as well as bf16. ``` pre-commit run --files <changed files> pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --files <changed files> --hook-stage manual ``` → ruff-check, ruff-format, typos, mypy-3.10, mypy-3.12 all Passed. `test_batched_mm_swapped_grid` runs the swapped kernel on whatever device is present and compares it against `native_batched_masked_quant_matmul`, which pins the tile→(expert, m, n) mapping to an independent reference and checks no row past an expert's token count is written. It targets the swapped kernel specifically because `test_batched_mm` goes through `invoke_moe_batched_triton_kernel` and so only covers the kernel the running platform selects. I confirmed it is not vacuous by transposing the in-kernel `pid_m`/`pid_n` decode, which fails 2 of its 3 shapes; the third is `max_tokens_per_expert=1`, where `randint(low=0, high=1)` gives every expert zero tokens and the kernel early-exits. A mutation that merely permutes the tile order does not fail, which is expected since a permutation is what this PR does. `test_swapped_kernel_matches_original_source` compares the two kernels line by line, ignoring the `def` line and the `tl.program_id` assignments, so a change that lands in only one copy fails on CUDA too, where the swapped kernel is never launched. Adding `+ 0` to one copy's `num_pid_n` fails it. </details> ## AI assistance AI assistance (Claude) was used here: for the benchmark and A/B harnesses, the accuracy and perf runs, and for drafting the test and comments. I reviewed everything.

signals.title: Fix weight tying
signals.text: Fixes #51063. vLLM decides whether to tie `lm_head` purely from `tie_word_embeddings` and never looks at the checkpoint, so a config claiming tied weights against a checkpoint with a real `lm_head` silently discards it and generates gibberish. `ModelConfig.maybe_untie_word_embeddings` now checks the safetensors metadata and builds the model untied so the head loads; after loading, `torch.equal` re-ties it if it was just a redundant copy (as in `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`) or warns and keeps it if it genuinely differs. This matches `PreTrainedModel.tie_weights`. The reverse case, untied config with no head in the checkpoint, now ties and warns instead of leaving the head uninitialised. That makes the per-model workarounds redundant. `AutoWeightsLoader` now skips weights whose target parameter aliases one already loaded, which removes ~50 hand-rolled `lm_head` skips and also covers the ~20 models that tie with no skip at all. Five models hardcoded tying with `assert config.tie_word_embeddings` (`gemma`, `gemma2`, `commandr`, `cohere2_moe`, `mpt`). Untying at config time would trip these, so the asserts are dropped and an untied config keeps using the embeddings exactly as it does today. Those five still have no real `lm_head`, so they cannot honour one in a checkpoint; left for a follow-up. So `AutoWeightsLoader` now skips weights whose target parameter aliases one already loaded. That removes ~50 hand-rolled `lm_head` skips and also covers the ~20 models that tie with no skip at all.

signals.title: fix: handle quantized qkv_proj in DFlash fused-KV buffers
signals.text: ## Summary Fixes #51581 — DFlash-family speculative decoding crashes at engine init when the drafter is quantized. The DFlash fused-KV path sliced the raw `.weight` of the KV projections and fed it to a single fused GEMM, bypassing the quant method. This reworks the fused context-KV precompute into a tiered strategy: - `FUSED` — unquantized drafters: fuse qkv weights as before (fastest path, unchanged). - `SCALED_MM` — simple per-tensor FP8 with cutlass fp8 support: keep weights quantized, fuse per-output-row scales, run `cutlass_scaled_mm`. - `FUSED_DEQUANT` — simple per-tensor FP8 without cutlass fp8: dequant once into a fused bf16 weight at build time. - `PER_LAYER` — anything else (marlin / block-quant / mixed): project per layer and concat, always correct. The fused buffers are now built lazily at the first precompute (after `process_weights_after_loading`), so quantized layers are fully materialized; compute dtype follows the model config. The same strategy applies to `laguna_dflash` (stacked bmm) and `gemma4_dspark` (K-only) via a FUSED/PER_LAYER split. ## Validation - Standalone validator: **27/27 PASS** — strategy selection (incl. SCALED_MM / FUSED_DEQUANT gates), fused == per-layer bit-exact on CPU (qwen3 / laguna / gemma4), quantized projection never sliced, real FP8 precompute vs per-layer truth on GPU, fp16 path. - Real engine on Qwen2.5-7B + 4-layer synthetic draft (A100): dflash real **534.9 tok/s**, syn-accept-len **1167.5 tok/s (1.80x vs baseline 649.4)** — no regression after rework. - Bug→fix A/B: old eager build crashes (`AttributeError: workspace` on marlin path); lazy build runs clean (eager + cudagraph). - Note: A100 has no cutlass FP8 (`cutlass_fp8_supported()==False`), so `SCALED_MM` is gated there and falls to `PER_LAYER`; `SCALED_MM` is covered by CPU strategy tests.

signals.title: [Bugfix][KV Cache] Fix incremental multimodal block hashing
signals.text: ## Purpose `Request.append_output_token_ids()` computes block hashes incrementally when a new full block is completed. If that block overlaps multiple multimodal features, the existing incremental path starts from only the final feature and can omit an earlier feature in the same block. The resulting hash then differs from a freshly constructed request with identical tokens and multimodal input. This change starts multimodal hashing from the first feature overlapping the new block, using the existing `get_mm_features_in_window()` helper. It adds a regression test for both supported hash functions and checks that incremental and fresh construction produce identical block hashes. Addresses the multimodal hashing subproblem identified in #49377 and #49448. The prior investigation and patch direction in #49448 are credited to @edwardlong-ctrl, who is also attributed in the commit trailer. This does not duplicate an open PR: - #49448 was closed unmerged by its author. - #49619 rehashes after streaming-session token replacement; it does not change the ordinary `append_output_token_ids()` path fixed here. - #50114 skips no-op hasher calls before a full-block boundary; it retains the last-feature assumption addressed here. - Searches for `49377 in:body` and multimodal block-hash keywords found no open PR implementing this fix. AI assistance was used in developing this PR. ## Test Plan The repository uv environment is denoted by `<venv>` below. ```bash <venv>/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py \ -k 'incremental_append_with_multiple_mm_features' <venv>/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py \ -k 'request_block_hasher or hash_tokens_different_mm_input' <venv>/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py ruff check vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py \ tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py ruff format --check vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py \ tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py git diff --check origin/main...HEAD ``` An additional seeded local differential test compares incremental hashing with fresh hashing across randomized multimodal layouts and block boundaries. ## Test Result - New regression: 2 passed, 77 deselected. - Neighboring request block-hasher tests: 8 passed, 71 deselected. - Randomized differential check: 500 layouts and 1,147 completed block boundaries; every incremental hash list matched fresh construction. - Ruff checks, formatting checks, and `git diff --check`: passed. - Complete test file: 61 passed, 18 failed. All 18 failures occur while `ModelConfig` attempts to access Hugging Face in the network-restricted test environment; they do not reach the modified block-hashing path. - Model evaluation: not applicable; this changes cache-key construction and does not change model execution or generated outputs.

signals.title: [Bugfix] Record non-ImportError attention backend probe failures instead of crashing engine init
signals.text: ## Purpose Fixes #51658. The backend probe in `CudaPlatform.get_valid_backends` catches only ImportError. The loop exists to mark unavailable backends and keep going, but anything else raised while importing or validating a backend, say a PermissionError from a read-only flashinfer cache dir or an OSError from a broken driver install, escapes and takes down engine init even when a usable backend is next in the priority list. The recorded reason is also the bare string "ImportError", so the paths it does catch lose the actual failure detail. Changes, both in `vllm/platforms/cuda.py`: - the enumeration path catches Exception, records the reason as "ExceptionType: message" (the format suggested in the issue), and logs the traceback at debug level. KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit still propagate. - the selected-backend path raises the existing ValueError with `from e` so the root cause stays in the chain. `rocm.py` and `get_vit_attn_backend` have the same pattern. The ViT one has a safe TORCH_SDPA fallback so the stakes are lower, and I kept this PR to the two sites named in the issue. Happy to do rocm.py here or as a follow-up if preferred. Duplicate check (2026-08-10): #51658 has no linked PR, and open-PR searches for "51658 in:body", "backend probe" and "get_valid_backends" come back empty. ## Test Plan New `tests/v1/attention/test_cuda_backend_probe_errors.py`, mock-based and CUDA-gated. The nearby selection test file covers mamba backends and the ROCm probe has its own file, so this follows that per-platform pattern rather than extending an unrelated suite. ``` pytest tests/v1/attention/test_cuda_backend_probe_errors.py -v ``` - ImportError / PermissionError / RuntimeError / OSError / AttributeError raised by the probe are recorded as invalid reasons instead of crashing - one failing backend does not stop later backends from being probed - selected-backend probe failure raises ValueError with `__cause__` preserved - KeyboardInterrupt is not swallowed ## Test Result Probe raising each exception type, before vs after: | Exception raised in probe | main | this PR | |---|---|---| | ImportError | recorded as bare "ImportError" | recorded with message | | PermissionError | propagates, engine init dies | recorded, probing continues | | RuntimeError | propagates, engine init dies | recorded, probing continues | | OSError | propagates, engine init dies | recorded, probing continues | | AttributeError | propagates, engine init dies | recorded, probing continues | | KeyboardInterrupt | propagates | propagates (unchanged) | Test suite: 7 failed, 1 passed on main; 8 passed with the fix. Run on an A100 machine. `ruff check` and `ruff format` clean on both changed files. No model evaluation: nothing numeric changes. Behaviour differs only in cases that previously crashed engine init. AI assistance was used on this change (Claude Fable 5); I reviewed every line and ran the validation myself.

signals.title: [6/N][KV-Cache Layout Refactor] Standardize KV cache layout
signals.text: ## Purpose The core of the KV-cache layout standardization series (RFC #42082). **Stacked on #51704 → #51612** — the diff shown includes them until they land and this retargets. Standardizes every KV cache allocation on the logical `[L, B, H, N, C]` vocabulary: - `KVCacheLayout` enumerates the physical stride permutations (`LBHNC`, `LBNHC`, `LHBNC`, `BLHNC`, `BLNHC`, `BHLNC`); `reshape_kv_cache` views each flat allocation as dense `[num_blocks, block_bytes]` tiles; per-layer caches are always logical `[B, H, N, C]` views with the physical layout expressed via strides (MLA binds the squeezed `[B, N, C]`). - Layout resolution has a single writer: attention-backend selection publishes the layout into `CacheConfig` (test override > backend-required > `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT` > connector preference > `LBNHC`); every consumer reads it from there. - The AITER backends opt into separate K/V head groups (`[B, 2, N, H*hs]`, `LBHNC` required) through `customize_spec`, keeping the fused QK-norm+RoPE+cache kernel dispatched with the exact block-interior contract aiter v0.1.19 asserts — fusion never regresses at any commit in the series. - The KV block zeroer matches main's per-segment form (block dim is always 0 in standardized views); block copies are a plain `unflatten` + index copy; connectors (NIXL, mooncake, moriio, hf3fs, offloading, example) and the attention benchmark runner consume the standardized views and published layout. - `indexes_kv_by_block_stride` and per-backend cache-shape/stride-order hooks are removed — the standardized views make them constant. Replaces #44458 (same content, restacked). ## Test Plan / Result Validated on B200 (full history in #44458): backend-correctness suites (FlashAttention/FlashInfer/Triton/Flex 127P), full MLA suite and `test_prefix_prefill` at exact main failure-set parity, connector unit battery at parity, zeroer/attn-utils/model-runner suites green, e2e smokes across FLASH_ATTN / TRITON(+int8 per-token-head) / FLASHINFER / FLEX / fp8 / CUTLASS_MLA (DeepSeek-V2-Lite). ROCm/AITER validation in progress on AMD. --- AI-assisted (Claude); under review by submitter ## Validation CPU suites (kv-cache-utils, packing, zeroer, attn-utils, gpu-model-runner, nixl / mooncake / moriio / offloading / simple-offload): green. The only failures on this host are environmental and reproduce identically on the base branch (same 5 test ids): GPU 0 is held by another process, and NIXL is not installed. `tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py`: 1729 passed. 20 more OOM'd against a GPU another process had filled; rerun on a reserved GPU they pass (290 passed, 0 failed). E2E on this branch, all deterministic on re-run: | model | exercises | result | |---|---|---| | `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` | dense attention | pass | | `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat` | MLA specs, compressed KV | pass under LBNHC, LBHNC and BLHNC | | `ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny` | hybrid attention + Mamba | pass | Not run here (needs a bigger box): DeepSeek-V4 and MiniMax-M3 themselves, so the DSV4 multi-group overlay, the `fp8_ds_mla` 584/656-byte paths, the compact MXFP4 indexer and M3's sparse/indexer backends have unit coverage but no e2e. Those paths are covered by `tests/v1/core/test_contiguous_kv_packing.py` and `tests/v1/worker/test_dsv4_packed_zeroer_geometry.py` using the real DSV4 page sizes. To reproduce e2e: ```bash vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3 # and repeat each with VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLHNC ``` --- AI-assisted (Claude); every changed line reviewed and tests run by the submitter.

signals.title: [MoE][NVIDIA] Add shared expert fusion for TRTLLM FP8
signals.text: ## Summary - Extend the FusedMoE abstraction so shared experts can be represented as always-on routed expert slots on NVIDIA GPUs. - Enable the path for the NVIDIA DeepSeek-V3.2/GLM-5.2 model when routed and shared expert storage formats match. - Run fused FP8 shared experts through the modular FlashInfer TRTLLM backend, including expert-row padding required by the kernel. - Append and pack constant shared-expert routes in one Triton kernel, avoiding the extra top-k concatenation that regressed single-token decode. - Preserve ROCm AITER's native fused-shared-expert routing behavior. ## Motivation Shared-expert fusion was effectively limited to ROCm/AITER. NVIDIA models therefore launched the routed MoE and shared MLP separately even when both used compatible FP8 storage. FlashInfer's native shared-expert entry point is not usable for this FP8 configuration, but its externally routed TRTLLM FP8 kernel handles the shared expert correctly when the shared rows and always-on route are included in the routed problem. This change adds that representation to FusedMoE and keeps the single-token path efficient by synthesizing the shared route while packing top-k IDs and weights. ## Duplicate-work check I searched open PRs for `shared expert fusion`, `FusedMoE shared experts NVIDIA`, and `FlashInfer shared expert`, and inspected the related issue and PRs. - #51695 standardizes model-level FSE enablement/quantization compatibility; it does not add NVIDIA routing, weight preparation, or FlashInfer execution. This PR may need a small rebase if that selection refactor lands first. - #50963 tracks FlashInfer's native FP4 shared-expert API. This PR implements the externally routed TRTLLM **FP8** path and does not close that FP4 issue. - #51632 fixes ROCm Triton expert-count alignment and does not implement the NVIDIA path. No open PR found in those searches implements this change. ## Correctness Real-weight model evaluation: - Model: GLM-5.2-FP8 under `models/deepseek_v32/` - Hardware: TP8 across two NVIDIA GB200 nodes - Model override: `vllm.models.deepseek_v32.nvidia.model:DeepseekV32ForCausalLM`, forcing the NVIDIA implementation and avoiding the HF torch-compile path - GSM8K exact match: **0.9325246** Local tests on NVIDIA GB200: ```text .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_routing.py -q 507 passed .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/deepseek_v32/test_sequence_parallel.py tests/kernels/moe/test_routing.py tests/quantization/test_fp8.py -k 'shared_expert_fusion or standard_router or trtllm_fp8_moe_validates_kernel_expert_count or flashinfer_trtllm_pads_fused_shared_expert_rows or trtllm_fp8_modular_uses_padded_fused_expert_count or trtllm_pack_appends_fused_shared_experts or monolithic_kernel_must_handle_fused_shared_experts_natively or fp8_moe_modular_apply_includes_fused_shared_experts' -q 14 passed, 524 deselected .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_unquantized_backend_selection.py -q 26 passed, 1 skipped .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_layer.py -k fused_shared_experts_cuda -q 1 passed, 510 deselected .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/deepseek_v32/test_sequence_parallel.py -q 4 passed pre-commit run --files <all 28 changed files> Passed, including ruff, mypy, typos, SPDX, and repository checks ``` ## Performance Dummy-weight GLM-5.2-FP8, TP8 across two 4xGB200 nodes, 16 input and 16 output tokens per request. The benchmark used the NVIDIA model override, `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1`, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, the default 83 regular capture sizes, prefix caching disabled, five warmup waves, and nine measured closed-loop burst waves per concurrency. Breakable graphs set compilation mode to `NONE`, so these results do not use torch/Inductor compilation. | Concurrency | TTFT unfused | TTFT fused | Change | TPOT unfused | TPOT fused | Change | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 29.738 ms | 28.739 ms | -3.36% | 8.215 ms | 8.274 ms | +0.72% | | 8 | 30.477 ms | 29.515 ms | -3.16% | 9.160 ms | 8.828 ms | -3.63% | | 32 | 67.968 ms | 66.573 ms | -2.05% | 10.826 ms | 10.549 ms | -2.55% | | 128 | 261.856 ms | 255.693 ms | -2.35% | 15.830 ms | 15.946 ms | +0.74% | | 512 | 284.948 ms | 282.755 ms | -0.77% | 27.052 ms | 26.588 ms | -1.71% | | Concurrency | Output throughput unfused | Output throughput fused | Change | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 103.85 tok/s | 103.90 tok/s | +0.06% | | 8 | 757.21 tok/s | 781.11 tok/s | +3.16% | | 32 | 1,956.06 tok/s | 1,997.35 tok/s | +2.11% | | 128 | 3,829.45 tok/s | 3,873.43 tok/s | +1.15% | | 512 | 11,139.04 tok/s | 11,072.50 tok/s | -0.60% | TTFT is queued-to-first-token time; median queue time remained below 0.6 ms. Fusion is neutral at concurrency 1 and improves median throughput by 1.1-3.2% at concurrency 8-128. The fused concurrency-512 run was bimodal: five waves completed in 0.71-0.74 seconds and four in 0.90-0.92 seconds. Its p99 TTFT was 485.07 ms versus 306.78 ms unfused, and p99 TPOT was 39.48 ms versus 27.07 ms unfused. The median throughput result therefore does not show a benefit at concurrency 512, and the tail behavior needs further investigation. ### Kernel profile I also captured matched PyTorch/CUPTI traces for fixed decode batches. These runs used the same dummy model, TP8 topology, `max_num_seqs=1024`, `max_num_batched_tokens=32768`, breakable `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` CUDA graphs, and all 83 regular capture sizes as the end-to-end benchmark. The table reports the median steady-state GPU annotation on rank 0; profiler wall time is not used. | Decode batch | Unfused main stream | Unfused shared stream | Fused main stream | Main-stream change | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 8.147 ms | 7.640 ms | 8.287 ms | +0.140 ms (+1.72%) | | 8 | 9.145 ms | 8.622 ms | 8.811 ms | -0.334 ms (-3.65%) | | 128 | 15.662 ms | 14.876 ms | 15.835 ms | +0.173 ms (+1.11%) | The unfused shared-expert stream completes before the main stream at all three sizes, so its work is already hidden rather than added to the critical path. Fusion removes that competing stream and helps batch 8, but its modular routing overhead slightly exceeds the overlap benefit at batches 1 and 128. This matches the end-to-end TPOT trend. The combined append-and-pack kernel costs 0.104-0.118 ms per decode step across 75 MoE layers (1.39-1.58 microseconds per layer). It has already removed the prior materialize-plus-concatenate path. Eliminating the remaining kernel would require a FlashInfer interface that can consume an implicit always-on shared route; no further safe vLLM-only optimization was identified from these traces. ### MoE operator microbenchmark I separately measured one GLM-5.2-FP8 MoE layer from precomputed router logits through routing, expert execution, runtime activation quantization, and combine. The gate projection, TP communication/final all-reduce, attention, scheduler, and frontend are excluded. Dummy BF16 weights were converted to block FP8 before timing, so offline weight quantization is also excluded. The benchmark uses the TP8 **per-rank** matrix shape on one GB200: hidden size 6144, intermediate size 256 (= 2048 / TP8), 256 routed experts, one shared expert, top-k 8, BF16 activations, block-FP8 [128, 128] weights, and GLM-5.2 sigmoid/noaux routing with routed scale 2.5. It configures `tp_size=1` with pre-sharded weights, so it is a kernel microbenchmark rather than an actual distributed TP8 run. Every token count has its own manually captured exact-shape `torch.cuda.CUDAGraph`; vLLM model-runner CUDA graph dispatch is disabled. The main baseline uses the monolithic FlashInfer TRTLLM routed MoE plus a separate block-FP8 DeepGEMM shared MLP. To give the baseline its strongest overlap behavior, `VLLM_SHARED_EXPERTS_STREAM_TOKEN_THRESHOLD=32768` forces the shared MLP onto its auxiliary stream at every measured size; instrumentation confirmed `MULTI_STREAM_OVERLAPPED` at both 1 and 8192 tokens. The fused path uses the modular FlashInfer TRTLLM kernel with 257 logical experts padded to 260. Results are the median of three process-level medians on the same GB200. | Tokens | Fused latency | Main always-overlap latency | Fused change | Fused throughput | Main throughput | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 0.0369 ms | 0.0370 ms | -0.4% | 0.027M tok/s | 0.027M tok/s | | 2 | 0.0419 ms | 0.0423 ms | -1.1% | 0.048M tok/s | 0.047M tok/s | | 4 | 0.0531 ms | 0.0535 ms | -0.7% | 0.075M tok/s | 0.075M tok/s | | 8 | 0.0757 ms | 0.0782 ms | -3.3% | 0.106M tok/s | 0.102M tok/s | | 16 | 0.1024 ms | 0.1070 ms | -4.3% | 0.156M tok/s | 0.149M tok/s | | 32 | 0.1481 ms | 0.1497 ms | -1.0% | 0.216M tok/s | 0.214M tok/s | | 64 | 0.1979 ms | 0.1936 ms | +2.2% | 0.323M tok/s | 0.331M tok/s | | 128 | 0.2227 ms | 0.2113 ms | +5.4% | 0.575M tok/s | 0.606M tok/s | | 256 | 0.2512 ms | 0.2393 ms | +5.0% | 1.019M tok/s | 1.070M tok/s | | 512 | 0.2712 ms | 0.3488 ms | -22.3% | 1.888M tok/s | 1.468M tok/s | | 1024 | 0.3055 ms | 0.3863 ms | -20.9% | 3.351M tok/s | 2.651M tok/s | | 2048 | 0.4039 ms | 0.4704 ms | -14.1% | 5.071M tok/s | 4.353M tok/s | | 4096 | 0.6699 ms | 0.6859 ms | -2.3% | 6.114M tok/s | 5.972M tok/s | | 8192 | 1.2046 ms | 1.2348 ms | -2.4% | 6.801M tok/s | 6.634M tok/s | Fusion is neutral at the smallest shapes, loses 2-5% at 64-256 tokens where the dense shared MLP overlaps effectively, wins 14-22% at 512-2048 tokens, and remains 2-3% faster once both paths approach GEMM throughput limits. Forcing overlap above the default 256-token threshold improves the main baseline by only 0.8-4.0% at 512-8192 tokens because the FlashInfer routed MoE and DeepGEMM shared MLP compete for the same GPU resources. ## AI assistance disclosure AI assistance from OpenAI Codex was used to implement, debug, test, benchmark, profile, clean up, and prepare this draft PR. The human submitter is responsible for understanding and defending the change and must review every changed line and confirm the reported tests before marking the PR ready for review.

signals.title: [Bugfix][Core] Align hybrid block sizes across PP stages
signals.text: ## Purpose Fixes #51752. Hybrid block-size alignment currently discovers a non-SSM attention backend only from the local pipeline stage. A PP rank that owns only SSM/KDA layers therefore returns early, while an attention-owning rank aligns `block_size`, `mamba_block_size`, and related page sizes. The resulting per-rank KV specs can disagree before the frontend synchronization path is reached. This PR: - gathers non-SSM backend presence across the PP CPU group; - selects the first backend-owning rank in PP/layer order, preserving the existing first-attention-backend behavior; - performs backend-dependent alignment only on that source rank, then broadcasts the aligned block and padded-page configuration to every PP rank; - uses the shared synchronization in both the generic platform path and the CPU override; - adds regression coverage where the source uses a runtime-generated backend that cannot be imported on another rank. Broadcasting the aligned configuration avoids reconstructing backend classes on ranks that do not instantiate them. This is required for dynamic static-sink and chunked-local attention backends created with `type()`. This is not a duplicate of #49845. That PR reconciles multiple attention backend classes visible within one rank; this PR handles a pipeline stage that has no local attention backend at all and must obtain the aligned configuration from another PP stage. I directed the work, reviewed the complete set of changes, and independently verified the final implementation and validation results. OpenAI Codex was used only as a limited implementation aid under my direction. I have reviewed and confirmed the final diff in full and remain responsible for the correctness, quality, and overall contribution.

signals.title: [Docker] Update to nixl-1.3.2
signals.text: ## Purpose The KV-connectors layer installs `nixl` from requirements/kv_connectors.txt, then force-reinstalls the CUDA-matched backend wheel so the correct nixl_ep_cpp.so is present. That second install passes `--no-deps` and no version, which bypasses the `nixl` meta package's `nixl-cu*==<version>` constraint and resolves whatever nixl-cu${CUDA_MAJOR} is newest on PyPI. The image therefore silently ships a different NIXL than it pins: with `nixl == 1.3.1` in kv_connectors.txt, the CUDA 13 image ends up with `nixl 1.3.1` / `nixl-cu12 1.3.1` / `nixl-cu13 1.3.2`. Because the `nixl` meta package dispatches on torch.version.cuda and re-exports nixl_cu13's bindings, 1.3.2 is what actually loads while the pin reads 1.3.1. 1.3.2 fixes a telemetry-gating bug in 1.3.1 where an agent created with telemetry disabled leaves getXferTelemetry returning NIXL_ERR_NO_TELEMETRY, which breaks callers that request transfer telemetry. [Documented in this Dynamo issue](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/issues/12952) This PR attempts to fix the silently drifting nixl backend package version, and capture fix for above issue by moving to latest nixl version. ## Fix - ~~Pin the version in the command to update nixl-cu${CUDA_MAJOR}~~ (changed to below after discussion with stakeholders) - Remove the redundant nixl-cu reinstallation. - Bump the pin to nixl 1.3.2, the version CUDA 13 images have been shipping in practice. - Bump the nixl version used by XPU build as well to fix the test that showed this issue. ## Test Plan - Run the test in https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/issues/12952 ## Test Result Image built with this PR: ``` ============ Serving Benchmark Result ============ Successful requests: 100 Failed requests: 0 Maximum request concurrency: 8 Benchmark duration (s): 55.70 Total input tokens: 102399 Total generated tokens: 25600 Request throughput (req/s): 1.80 Output token throughput (tok/s): 459.61 Peak output token throughput (tok/s): 594.00 Peak concurrent requests: 16.00 Total token throughput (tok/s): 2298.01 ``` Image built without this PR: ``` ### Benchmark result: Traceback (most recent call last): File "/usr/local/bin/vllm", line 10, in <module> sys.exit(main()) ^^^^^^ File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/entrypoints/cli/main.py", line 95, in main args.dispatch_function(args) ...... signals.title: [MoE][Humming] Enable Chord W4A16 MoE as a humming backend drop-in
signals.text: ## What [Chord](https://github.com/novitalabs/chord) is Novita's W4A16 MoE CUDA operator for the Kimi INT4 family — same kernel family and layer contract as humming. This PR drops it in through the existing humming surface: swap the `humming` package and vLLM stays oblivious. No new interfaces. The glue on the framework side — three small gates: 1. `quant_utils`: enumerate the compressed-tensors group-32 W4A16 scheme keys (fp16/bf16/fp32 scale variants) next to the existing per-channel int4 key. 2. `int_wna16` oracle: map CT `QuantizationArgs` through a K-major packed-transpose bridge instead of raising. 3. `compressed_tensors_moe_wna16`: pass `backend`/`layer` to `make_wna16_moe_kernel` when HUMMING wins the vote. Related: shares the destination with #48918 (@yiliu30) — that one takes a wider uint2–8 acceptance rule plus layout selection at `create_weights`; this PR is scoped keys + conversion in the shared `convert_to_humming_moe_kernel_format` funnel, on current main (`beca88e59e`). First-mover credit goes to them. ## How to enable Install [chord](https://github.com/novitalabs/chord) (`pip install git+https://github.com/novitalabs/chord` — the distribution ships a top-level `humming` import root; don't co-install upstream `inclusionAI/humming`, the name collision is intentional), then run exactly the humming serve command — no chord-specific flag anywhere: ```bash vllm serve /models/moonshotai/Kimi-K2.6 --quantization humming ... ``` vLLM resolves the provider through `find_spec("humming")`; whichever package sits at that name — upstream humming or chord — is what executes. ## What actually ran torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13, 8×H200, Kimi-K2.6 (CT INT4 group-32, 384 experts). `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_humming_w4a16.py -q` → 6/6 (humming-native checkpoint, CT K-major, and `--quantization humming` routes on Kimi EP8 shapes). Same serve command for both providers (TP8 + DCP8, fp8 KV, `--quantization humming`), ShareGPT clients: Prefill (osl=1, prefix cache off): | | humming | chord | chord/baseline | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | TTFT mean (ms) | 2022 | 1849 | **0.91x** | | in+out tok/s | 20716 | 22712 | **1.10x** | Decode (second run over same prompts, prefix fully hot; out tok/s): | bs | humming | chord | ratio | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 8 | 483 | 503 | **1.04x** | | 64 | 1650 | 1740 | **1.06x** | | 128 | 2514 | 2715 | **1.08x** | Accuracy at parity: | benchmark | humming | chord | | --- | --- | --- | | OCRBench FINAL (1000, official config) | 941 | 947 | | GSM8K 5-shot flex / strict (lm-eval, n=500) | 0.312 / 0.238 | 0.332 / 0.254 | Scope note: the serving results above are TP8 end-to-end only. The PD-disaggregated EP8 profiles — the deployment shape this operator targets hardest — lead at kernel level too (H200 EP8 prefill 1.09–1.22x, decode 1.12–1.31x stage-level vs humming; B300 EP8 decode ~1.8–2.2x ( we have not present results for EP8 E2E here, but validated in our production to be effective.). Operator-level tables and methodology: [chord/docs/performance.md](https://github.com/novitalabs/chord/blob/main/docs/performance.md). ## AI Assistance Prepared with AI assistance; the submitting human reviewed every changed line and executed all of the above. Co-authored-by: Kimi K3 <noreply@moonshot.cn> Signed-off-by: Kevin-XiongC <kevin_xiong1997@outlook.com>

signals.title: [Bugfix] vLLM crashes at startup when DeepEP v2 is used with `--enforce-eager` wiht TRTLLM Bf16
signals.text: ## Purpose When running the following command: ``` vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite \ --data-parallel-size 2 \ --enable-expert-parallel \ --all2all-backend deepep_v2 \ --enforce-eager ``` vLLM will crash at startup with the following error ``` expert_indices.size(1) == args->top_k (1 vs. 6) : expert_indices dim1 must match top_k. ``` This error is caused by `TrtLlmBf16ExpertsModular` not properly extracting the `top_k` value when DeepEP V2 returns the topk_ids in it's "expanded" layout. This PR updates the logic to use the correct value for `top_k` in this backend and improves the DeepEP V2 + MoE unit test to cover the expanded and non expanded layouts for the `flashinfer_trtllm`, `flashinfer_cutlass`, and `trtllm_fp8` backends. ## Test Plan I expanded the existing unit test to cover more cases and ran lm_eval on ``` vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite \ --data-parallel-size 2 \ --enable-expert-parallel \ --all2all-backend deepep_v2 \ --enforce-eager ``` ## Test Result lm_eval results ``` |Tasks|Version| Filter |n-shot| Metric | |Value | |Stderr| |-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:| |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.3821|± |0.0134| | | |strict-match | 5|exact_match|↑ |0.3783|± |0.0134| ```

signals.title: [3/N] Harden Transformers modelling backend multi-modal path
signals.text: Continues from #51408 and #51657 Supersedes #50107 and #50899 --- ## Added - Multi-modal processor caching, for `transformers>=5.15.0`. `OffsetsMultiModalProcessor` states each expansion as a `PromptReplacement` built from `text_replacement_offsets`, so the base class's cached path applies instead of `apply()` being overridden. A repeated image now hits the cache rather than being reprocessed and re-shipped over IPC: 2 requests, 1 hit - `_unpad_images`/`_unpad_audios`. Processors pad to a batch-common shape, which makes an item's data depend on what it was processed beside and so uncacheable. Emu3 pads every image to the largest in the batch; audio processors pad every audio to the longest in the call - Adjacent audio placeholders split per item on the offsets path, removing the 1/N stopgap raise for every model that reports offsets ## Fixed - Image fields with a leading batch dimension were sliced on the wrong axis. Idefics3 returns `pixel_values` as `[1, total_patches, C, H, W]`, so `flat_from_sizes` on dim 0 gave the first image every row and the second an empty tensor. Latent on main, where re-batching reassembled the rows and hid it; caching items individually is what stops that cancelling out - `Idefics3Processor` rejects a prompt holding `<image>` when no images are passed, which is exactly how the unexpanded prompt has to be tokenized. Falls back to the tokenizer, as `idefics3.py` already does for the same reason - `num_image_patches` on the offsets path was guessed as one row per image; it now comes from the processor's `_get_num_multimodal_tokens`. Idefics3 produces 13 ## Changed - `MultiModalProcessor` is selected by transformers version: `LegacyMultiModalProcessor` below 5.15.0, `OffsetsMultiModalProcessor` from 5.15.0 on. Processing common to both moved to `_MultiModalProcessorBase` - **Behaviour change**: from 5.15.0, a processor reporting no replacement offsets is refused rather than served by searching the expanded prompt. The error names the processor and the `replace_<modality>_token` hook it needs, and points at reporting it upstream or pinning `transformers<5.15.0`. Measured against 5.16.0.dev0, 87 of 145 `ProcessorMixin` subclasses implement no hook, though most are not generative multi-modal processors and most of the rest have native vLLM implementations ## Notes - Emu3 loses its BOS token on this path: `Emu3Processor` prepends it only when images are passed, and the unexpanded prompt is tokenized without them. Fixed by huggingface/transformers#47924, merged but not yet released; `xfail` until it is - The cached path processes cache misses in one call, so `image_processor([img_1])` must equal `image_processor([img_0, img_1])[1]`. The unpadding above covers processors that pad; `test_processing_correctness_transformers` catches the rest per model ## Tests - Both processors are exercised whichever version is installed. `create_processor` builds the class directly, because the registry only ever builds the one the version gate selects, which would otherwise leave the legacy path with no coverage while `requirements/common.txt` still allows `transformers>=5.5.3` - Added `test_repeated_image_hits_the_processor_cache`. `_test_processing_correctness` builds a cache but only compares cached against uncached output, so a silent bypass passes it; this asserts `make_stats().hits`. Legacy reports 0 hits of 0, offsets 1 of 2 - Added `test_spliced_prompt_matches_hf_expansion`, comparing both processors' token ids. The legacy path returns HF's own expansion, so it is the reference for the splice. This is what found the Emu3 BOS loss - Added `test_nested_image_fields_split_per_image` and `test_tokens_structuring_an_image_are_masked_not_dropped`, both on SmolVLM

signals.title: [qwen3] correct linear_attn norm and a_log parameter dtype to F32 for qwen 3.5 series
signals.text: ## Purpose For Qwen 3.5 series (Gated Delta Net) models, the parameter `language_model.model.layers.{i}.linear_attn.norm.weight` is stored in **fp32** in the [HF checkpoint](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-27B/tree/main?show_file_info=model.safetensors.index.json), but vLLM currently allocates it in **bf16** (for bf16 models) and silently casts the loaded values into it. If this is used with offline sharded state, the pre-sharded chedckpoints norm layer will use bf16, so the sharded checkpoint deviates from the original fp32 weight. However, Qwen 3.6 series, the linear_attn.norm weight is stored in `bf16`. We need to differentiates the two series and use the correct dtype. The same for linear attn a log parameter, for Qwen 3.5 series, the a log parameter dtype is `F32`, as well for Qwen 3.6 series, the a log parameter dtype is `BF16`. This PR adds a new text config attribute `real_model_type` demonstrating the real model type is qwen3_5 or qwen3_6. For now, the official qwen 3.5 and qwen 3.6 repo config.json does not contains `real_model_type` in `text_config`, the behavior after this pr is the same with before. But if `text_config` has the `real_model_type` field specified, and its value is, for now, `qwen3_5` or `qwen3_6`, the linear attention a_log and norm parameter will be correctly set with the weight. ## Test Plan Tested manually with offline pre shard command: ``` python examples/features/sharded_state/save_sharded_state_offline.py --model ~/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--Qwen--Qwen3.x-27B/snapshots/6a9e13bd6fc8f0983b9b99948120bc37f49c13e9 --output /home/sharded_weigts --max-num-seqs 512 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-file-size 1073741824 ``` for Qwen 3.5 series: 1. the sharded output norm layer parameter is F32 2. the sharded output a log layer parameter is BF16 For Qwen 3.6 series: 1. the sharded output norm layer parameter is BF16 2. the sharded output a log layer parameter is BF16 ## Test Result --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signals.title: [Profiler] Fix start_profile permanently no-op after max_iterations auto-stop
signals.text: ## Summary `WorkerProfiler.step()`'s max_iterations auto-stop calls `_call_stop()` directly instead of the public `stop()`, so `_active` never resets. Any later `start_profile` then silently no-ops forever, since `start()` bails out early whenever `_active` is still True -- only `stop()` resets it. This breaks the `max_iterations` "fire and forget" use case: profiling only ever runs once per worker process, with no error to explain why a second `/start_profile` did nothing. Fix: call `self.stop()` instead of `self._call_stop()` on auto-stop, so `_active`/`_active_iteration_count`/`_profiling_for_iters` reset like a normal stop. ## Test plan - [x] `test_max_iterations` now also asserts `_active`/counters reset after auto-stop - [x] New `test_restart_after_max_iterations`: start -> auto-stop via max_iterations -> start again -> verifies it actually restarts

signals.title: Fix seed loss when batch contains unseeded requests
signals.text: Fix seed loss when batch has unseeded requests. ## Purpose Fixes #51226. On CPU, `TopKTopPSampler.forward_cpu` decided whether to take the unseeded fast path by checking `len(generators) != logits.shape[0]`. Since `generators` only holds an entry per *seeded* request, this check evaluates true (mismatch) whenever even one request in the batch is unseeded — so the whole batch fell through to the fast path and every per-request `torch.Generator` was discarded, including generators for requests that *did* specify a seed. A seeded request's determinism therefore depended on whether everything else sharing its batch also happened to be seeded. This PR changes the condition to `not generators`, so the fast path is only taken when the batch has zero seeded requests. Seeded requests now keep their own generator regardless of what else is batched with them. ## Test Plan ## Test Result --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [X] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signals.text: ## Purpose Add retention interval support to `OffloadingConnector`. The Mooncake KV connector supports retention interval support via the `envs.VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL` env variable. It is used to avoid storing/loading blocks that are outside of the sliding window of the attention mechanism. This is implemented via block masks.
