signals.title: [Rust Frontend] Add MiniMax M2 append-think reasoning parser
signals.text: ## Summary - add the explicit `minimax_m2_append_think` Rust reasoning parser - prepend `<think>` once while preserving all generated output as visible content - preserve special tokens and keep automatic MiniMax model routing on the normal parser - cover parser lifecycle, empty deltas, factory registration, and parser-name diagnostics ## Duplicate-work check This does not duplicate an existing PR. Before implementation I checked: - roadmap issue #44280 and its comments - open PRs referencing `44280` - open PR searches for `minimax_m2_append_think` and MiniMax M2 append-think parser terms No overlapping Rust implementation or claim was found. The item was claimed in #44280 before implementation. ## Tests - `cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-parser --lib` — 420 passed - `cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-chat --lib` — 266 passed - `cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-parser -p vllm-chat --all-targets -- -D warnings` — passed - `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` — passed ## Full-model serving regression A CPU-only end-to-end serving regression was run with the locally built PR Rust binary and the full `allenai/Olmo-3-7B-Instruct` weights (13.59 GiB), using `--reasoning-parser minimax_m2_append_think`. A different model was intentionally used because the parser is selected explicitly and MiniMax M2.5 itself is approximately 434 GiB across 125 weight shards. - Rust frontend, Python engine, tokenizer/template loading, and OpenAI HTTP serving all started successfully. - Non-streaming output preserved generated text as content and prepended exactly one marker: `content = "<think>hello world"`, `reasoning = null`. - Streaming reconstruction produced `content = "<think>hello world"`, empty reasoning, one `<think>` prefix, and `finish_reason = "stop"`. A model-quality evaluation is not applicable because this change does not affect model execution, logits, or sampling; the full-model run validates parser integration and HTTP behavior. ## AI assistance AI assistance was used to analyze the parser architecture, implement the change, and run validation. This PR is intentionally opened as a draft and must be reviewed line by line by the human submitter before being marked ready.

signals.title: [Bugfix] Fix K-tile handling in the Triton MoE and block-FP8 GEMMs
signals.text: ## Purpose Fixes #52576. Two Triton GEMMs on the quantized-MoE path get the K tile wrong, and in both cases a sibling code path already handles it correctly: - `fused_moe_kernel_gptq_awq` applies `k_mask` to the scale and both zero-point loads but leaves the weight load unmasked, so the final K iteration reads past the end of the packed weight tensor; the sibling `fused_moe_kernel` masks the identical load, and a masked-to-zero scale multiplies the values read, so this is a memory-safety fix, not a numerical one. - `w8a8_triton_block_scaled_mm` reads one scale pair per K tile, indexed `(k * BLOCK_SIZE_K) // group_k`, which is correct only when `BLOCK_SIZE_K` divides `group_k`; nothing enforced that, the comment above the default config stated the requirement inverted, and `invoke_fused_moe_kernel` already clamps this while this launcher did not. Neither change affects the paths that are correct today: `k_mask` is `None` when `block_k_diviable` is true, so the generated code for the divisible case is unchanged, and the block-FP8 default config already sets `BLOCK_SIZE_K = block_k`, so only a tuned config asking for a larger tile behaves differently. **Not a duplicate.** `gh pr list --state open` was checked for `fused_moe_kernel_gptq_awq`, `moe wna16 out of bounds`, `w8a8_triton_block_scaled_mm`, and `BLOCK_SIZE_K block_shape`. The nearby open PRs are all in different code: #44563 clamps `BLOCK_SIZE_K` inside `get_moe_wna16_block_config` for the **CUDA** `moe_wna16_gemm` instantiation set, #45539 and #46209 fix bounds and index widths in `csrc/.../moe_wna16.cu`. None touches the Triton `fused_moe_kernel_gptq_awq` weight load or `fp8_utils.py`. Re-checked 2026-08-17: the two newer open PRs in this file, #51515 (ROCm WNA16 block assignment) and #42193 (WNA16 warmup), leave the `b_ptrs` load alone, and none of the four open PRs touching `w8a8_triton_block_scaled_mm` (#40925, #47988, #48588, #41834) changes the config lookup or the per-tile scale index. **AI assistance was used** to find and diagnose both defects and to draft this change. ## Test Plan - `compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck` over an int4 `w4a16` MoE matmul driven through `invoke_fused_moe_kernel`, with `K` divisible and not divisible by `BLOCK_SIZE_K`. The weight tensor is allocated last so the overrun reaches unallocated memory rather than a neighbouring tensor. - `w8a8_triton_block_scaled_mm` against a dequantize-and-matmul reference at `block_shape = [128, 128]`, with the config lookup standing in for a tuned `configs/*.json` at `BLOCK_SIZE_K` of 64, 128, 256 and 512. Both scripts are in the linked issue. They drive this repo's own code (`VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 pip install -e .`), so the line numbers below are this file's. ## Test Result Out-of-bounds read, before: ``` K= 128 BLOCK_SIZE_K= 64: qweight holds 64 bytes per row, the loop covers 64 -> exact fit ERROR SUMMARY: 0 errors K= 128 BLOCK_SIZE_K= 32: qweight holds 64 bytes per row, the loop covers 64 -> exact fit ERROR SUMMARY: 0 errors K= 96 BLOCK_SIZE_K= 64: qweight holds 48 bytes per row, the loop covers 64 -> 16 bytes past the end reported at vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/fused_moe.py:236 ERROR SUMMARY: 8 errors K= 48 BLOCK_SIZE_K= 32: qweight holds 24 bytes per row, the loop covers 32 -> 8 bytes past the end reported at vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/fused_moe.py:236 ERROR SUMMARY: 8 errors ``` Each reported access lands past the end of `qweight` (e.g. `16 bytes after the nearest allocation ... of size 12288 bytes`), and the launch then dies with `CUDA error: unspecified launch failure`. After: `ERROR SUMMARY: 0 errors` for all four, and the two non-divisible cases run to completion. The error count is not a stable property of the defect — how many accesses the driver reports before it kills the context varies — so treat the fault site, not the number, as the signal. Block-FP8 scales, max relative error against the reference: | BLOCK_SIZE_K | group_k | before | after | |---|---|---|---| | 64 | 128 | 2.226e-07 | 2.226e-07 | | 128 | 128 | 2.082e-07 | 2.082e-07 | | 256 | 128 | 2.284e-01 | 2.082e-07 | | 512 | 128 | 2.633e-01 | 2.082e-07 | **No new tests.** The existing suites cannot reach either path. `test_fused_moe_wn16` parametrizes `k` over 128 and 1024 and requires `k` to be a multiple of `group_size` (64 or 128), while the untuned path caps `BLOCK_SIZE_K` at 64 — so `K % BLOCK_SIZE_K` is always 0 there. For the block-FP8 GEMM, no shipped `N=…,K=…` config carries a `BLOCK_SIZE_K` larger than `block_k`, so the path is only reachable by adding one. Covering either would mean a kernel-level test that pins the config explicitly; happy to add one if you would like it in this PR. **No model evals.** Neither change alters output on any path that is correct today: the mask is a no-op when `block_k_diviable` is true, and the clamp is a no-op unless a tuned config asks for `BLOCK_SIZE_K > block_k`. I do not have a vLLM serving setup on this machine to run `tests/evals/` against. ## Environment - `vllm-project/vllm` at `6664d397bf091cb9371cba481d4efb8233436fe6`, installed with `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 pip install -e .` - NVIDIA B200 (sm_100), driver 595.71.05 - torch 2.13.0+cu130, triton 3.7.1, Python 3.12

signals.title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Unlink /dev/shm region after all workers map it (barrier variant of #51317)
signals.text: Fixes #51579. `SharedOffloadRegion` backs the CPU offload tier with `/dev/shm/vllm_offload_{engine_id}.mmap`, removed only by `cleanup()`, which never runs on SIGKILL/OOM/crash — every hard exit leaks a `cpu_bytes_to_use`-sized file, and a stale file with a pinned `engine_id` prevents any rank from winning creator election on the next start. Fix: after every worker `mmap()`s the file, barrier over the worker group (gloo cpu group; `_INNER_DP_WORLD` when initialized, else `_WORLD`), then the creator unlinks the path. Mappings stay valid and the kernel reclaims the memory when the last worker exits, however it exits. The barrier runs before `MADV_POPULATE_WRITE`, so the long populate phase is already covered; if the barrier fails, the creator unlinks before re-raising. Builds on #51317 by @NickLucche (same create→map→unlink idiom), replacing its `.openers` counter file with a barrier per review feedback there: a barrier only needs a superset of the node-local openers, so the under/over-count failure modes of a config-derived `expected_openers` are not representable and no config plumbing is needed. #51730 takes a different (reaper) approach. ## Test Plan ``` pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_shared_offload_region.py ``` ## Test Result 37/37 pass (3 new: unlink-after-barrier, barrier-failure cleanup, cross-process barrier + SIGKILL + restart). E2E on a 2-GPU node (TP=2 and DP=2, OffloadingConnector, pinned `engine_id`): file created then unlinked during startup, both workers map the same deleted inode, offload stores flow through the unlinked region, SIGKILL leaves `/dev/shm` empty, restart with the same `engine_id` starts clean.

signals.title: [Bugfix] Fix incorrect --kv-cache-memory flag name in optimization docs
signals.text: The actual CLI flag is --kv-cache-memory-bytes (defined in vllm/engine/arg_utils.py). Passing --kv-cache-memory errors out as an unknown argument, so fix the docs and the related error message/comments. Assisted-by: CodeBuddy <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Purpose `docs/configuration/optimization.md` and the startup error message in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py` reference a CLI flag `--kv-cache-memory` that does not exist. The actual flag is `--kv-cache-memory-bytes`. Users who follow the docs (or the runtime hint) pass an unknown argument and hit an `unrecognized arguments` error. The `--kv-cache-memory-bytes` flag was introduced by #21489 and has never had another name. There is no legacy `--kv-cache-memory` flag and no backward compatibility concern; the shorter name is simply incorrect from the start. ## Changes - `docs/configuration/optimization.md`: fix the flag name. - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py`: fix the user-visible startup error message. - `vllm/v1/worker/startup_plan.py`: fix docstrings. - `vllm/envs.py`: fix the flag reference in a comment, plus a pre-existing typo (`elpased` -> `elapsed`) that would otherwise fail the `typos` check. ## Test Plan - `ruff check` on all changed files. - `ruff format --check` on all changed files. - `typos` on all changed files. - `markdownlint-cli2` on the changed markdown file. - Related unit tests: `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py -v` ## Test Result - `ruff check`: passed. - `ruff format --check`: passed. - `typos`: passed. - `markdownlint-cli2`: passed. - Changes are text-only; no behavior change, so the related unit tests are unaffected and verified via CI. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [x] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details> **BEFORE SUBMITTING, PLEASE READ <https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/contributing>** (anything written below this line will be removed by GitHub Actions)

signals.title: [ROCm][Perf] Kimi-K3 Fused kernels for KDA prefill
signals.text: ## Purpose On ROCm, Kimi-K3's KDA prefill chunk path currently runs a pipeline of nine Triton kernels. This PR adds a fusion path for ROCm that fuses these operations based on the characteristics of their workloads: **Prologue**: The kernel that prepares the chunks leading up to the recurrent state update. It normalizes `q` and `k`, cumsum gate into `g` and `beta`, builds `Aqk` in each chunk, inverts the transition `Akk`, and produces w and u. Each 64-token chunk can be processed in parallel, so it is dispatched in `(chunk, head)` grids for parallelism. **Chunk recurrence**: This does the remaining recurrence state update. For each sequence, the state update is sequential, and dispatching workgroups on the number of sequences can lead to low CU occupancy. This path breaks a sequence down into groups of chunks where the number of groups is determined by device capability, and takes a two-pass approach to increase parallelism within sequences: - Pass 1: Each group walks a recurrence from a zero state and records how it transforms an incoming state - Perform a scan across groups from a sequence to recover each group's true initial state - Pass 2: Re-walks each group from the correct start to produce outputs The fusion chain is ~2x faster than the Triton chain, especially in the chunk recurrance stage. E2E tests shows this reduces TTFT by ~4%. | tokens / seqs | Triton chunk stage | fused chunk stage | speedup | Triton chain | fused chain | speedup | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1024 / 1 | 117.4 µs | 60.7 µs | 1.93× | 139.2 µs | 79.1 µs | 1.76× | | 4096 / 1 | 301.1 µs | 113.7 µs | 2.65× | 330.5 µs | 143.0 µs | 2.31× | | 4096 / 2 | 232.7 µs | 110.0 µs | 2.12× | 278.0 µs | 154.7 µs | 1.80× | | 4096 / 8 | 192.5 µs | 84.5 µs | 2.28× | 256.6 µs | 145.2 µs | 1.77× | | 16384 / 1 | 1174.2 µs | 335.9 µs | 3.50× | 1232.4 µs | 393.5 µs | 3.13× | The fusion path is packed into two pytorch interfaces that serve as a replacement for the original Triton chain. An additional engine argument option `--kda-prefill-backend=fused` is added to enable this fused path, and it's set as the default when it is supported. The kernels have only been tested on gfx950 at the moment, so its build and dispatch is guarded on gfx950 for now. ## Test Plan Unit tests for the fused kernels lm_eval with gsm8k on MI355X Server command ``` VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \ VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2_A8W4=1 \ AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 \ VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 \ vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \ --trust-remote-code \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \ --load-format auto \ --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \ --max-num-seqs 128 \ --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \ --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","custom_ops":["+fused_rms_norm_gated"]}' \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --kda-prefill-backend ["fused" | "triton"] ``` Benchmark ``` vllm bench serve --model moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --backend vllm --trust-remote-code --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 --max-concurrency "$CONC" --num-prompts $((CONC * 4)) --temperature 0 --ignore-eos ``` lm_eval ``` lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --model_args "model=moonshotai/Kimi-K3,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=64,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False,max_gen_toks=8192,timeout=3600" --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 20 --apply_chat_template --fewshot_as_multiturn --seed 1234 ``` ## signals.title: [CPU] [1/n] Start migrating the CPU extension to the libtorch stable ABI
signals.text:
## Purpose This PR continues the libtorch stable ABI migration (see https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/26946) for vLLM, and is the first PR dedicated completely to the stable CPU build. First CPU libtorch stable-ABI PR. Migrates `silu_and_mul`, `gelu_\*`, `rms_norm`, `fused_add_rms_norm`, and `rotary_embedding` into new corresponding `_C*_stable_libtorch` libraries. Leftover CPU kernels stay on `_C` / `_C_AVX*` until later PRs. cc @janeyx99, @Harry-Chen ### New file: `csrc/libtorch_stable/cpu/cpu_types_arm_vec.hpp` `cpu_types_arm.hpp` used to get its `Vectorized` primitives from `at::vec` (unstable ABI), so this header is a small header-only replacement using only `` and stable `torch/headeronly` types. It specializes `Vectorized` for `float/c10::Half/c10::BFloat16` and implements only the ops/conversions the migrated kernels actually call (no full `at::vec` API surface). `BF16` load/store/convert use hardware NEON instructions when `ARM_BF16_SUPPORT` is set, falling back to bit-manipulation on [uint16x8_t](url) otherwise (see truncation note below). **NOTE:** `csrc/libtorch_stable/cpu/cpu_types_arm_vec.hpp`'s `f32_to_bf16x4()` only uses the hardware `vcvt_bf16_f32` conversion when `ARM_BF16_SUPPORT` is defined (i.e. the build detected `FEAT_BF16`). On ARM hosts without that extension, it falls back to a plain bit-shift truncation. This is in contrast to ATen which does round-to-nearest-even with an explicit NaN check. Practical impact: at most a 1-ULP difference in bf16 outputs on non-FEAT_BF16 ARM hardware only. ## Test Plan - [x] CPU build produces leftover `_C` / `_C_AVX*` **and** the matching `*_stable_libtorch` modules. - [x] `torch-abi-audit` reports the three `*_stable_libtorch` libraries as **STABLE** (`unstable=0`) and leftover `_C` / `_C_AVX*` as **UNSTABLE**. **unit test** VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest -x --disable-warnings tests/kernels/core/test_cpu_activation.py VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest -x --disable-warnings tests/kernels/attention/test_cpu_attn.py VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest -x --disable-warnings tests/kernels/moe/test_cpu_fused_moe.py VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest -x --disable-warnings tests/kernels/test_onednn.py Local testing was only done on the x86_64 architecture. The ARM CPU should be tested in the CI through `.buildkite/scripts/hardware_ci/run-cpu-test-arm.sh`. ## Test Results ---
Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.
Migration progress using the Audit Python extension [torch-abi-audit](https://pypi.org/project/torch-abi-audit/): ``` -- extensions -- [UNSTABLE] [abi3-ok ] _C.abi3.so (stable_shim=0, unstable=119) [UNSTABLE] [abi3-ok ] _C_AVX2.abi3.so (stable_shim=0, unstable=94) [STABLE ] [abi3-ok ] _C_AVX2_stable_libtorch.abi3.so (stable_shim=36, unstable=0) [UNSTABLE] [abi3-ok ] _C_AVX512.abi3.so (stable_shim=0, unstable=97) [STABLE ] [abi3-ok ] _C_AVX512_stable_libtorch.abi3.so (stable_shim=36, unstable=0) [STABLE ] [abi3-ok ] _C_stable_libtorch.abi3.so (stable_shim=36, unstable=0) [NO-TORCH] [abi3-ok ] fs_io_C.abi3.so [NO-TORCH] [abi3-ok ] spinloop.abi3.so ``` Performance: Microbench of the migrated `torch.ops._C` kernels on the same machine (`OMP_NUM_THREADS=8`, bfloat16). These are the median runtimes after 10 warm up calls, then each kernel is called 1000 times for the Kernel-bound (`2048x4096`) and 10,000 times for the Dispatch-bound (`1x64`). ``` Kernel-bound op signals.title: [Bugfix] Encode special tokens found in text for MistralCommonBackend in multimodal processors
signals.text: ## Purpose Fixes #50706 vLLM crashes at engine startup for Mistral3/Pixtral models whose tokenizer resolves to transformers' `MistralCommonBackend`. Per transformers' `AutoTokenizer` resolution, this happens whenever `mistral-common` is installed (`is_mistral_common_available()`) and the model's `model_type` (`mistral`/`ministral`/`mistral3`/etc) is mapped to `MistralCommonBackend` in `TOKENIZER_MAPPING_NAMES` — whether or not the checkpoint ships more than one tokenizer format plays no part (h/t @hmellor for the correction). Affected checkpoints include e.g. `nvidia/Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B-NVFP4`, `mistralai/Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B`. `MistralCommonBackend` never encodes special tokens (e.g. `"[IMG]"`) found in plain text. During dummy multimodal input profiling (run at engine startup to size the encoder budget), `PixtralProcessor` counts a mismatch between the placeholder in the templated text and the encoded ids and raises: ``` ValueError: Mismatch in `image` token count between text and `input_ids`. Got ids=[0] and text=[1]. ValueError: Failed to apply PixtralProcessor on data={'text': '[IMG]'} with kwargs={'truncation': False, 'return_tensors': 'pt'} ``` `InputProcessingContext.get_hf_processor` now swaps in a `MistralCommonBackend` subclass (`with_placeholder_token_support`) that resolves known special-token strings found in text back to their ids, scoped only to the tokenizer instance handed to HF processors — never used for general/user-prompt tokenization. Conceptually related to but independently derived from: - #50752 — fixes the same root cause on the default tokenizer-mode path (currently blocked on the contributor-gate CI check, not real test failures) - #45525 — fixes the sibling issue (#45289) for `--tokenizer-mode mistral` ## Test Plan - Unit tests: `pytest tests/tokenizers_/test_mistral.py -q` — 8 new tests against a real `mistralai/Pixtral-12B-2409` tokenizer, covering: bug repro (stock backend doesn't encode `[IMG]`), fix correctness, memoization/idempotency, plain-text passthrough (unaffected by the change), placeholder-prefix disambiguation (`[IMG]` vs `[IMG_BREAK]`/`[IMG_END]`), and `add_special_tokens` behavior. - Manual end-to-end repro against a real affected checkpoint, exercising the same code path as engine-startup profiling: ```python from vllm.config import ModelConfig from vllm.multimodal import MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY model_config = ModelConfig( "unsloth/Mistral-Small-3.2-24B-Instruct-2506", tokenizer="unsloth/Mistral-Small-3.2-24B-Instruct-2506", revision="3ed8d341b53ea3d0e4194689905477688a6cf733", tokenizer_revision="3ed8d341b53ea3d0e4194689905477688a6cf733", max_model_len=8192, ) processor = MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY.create_processor(model_config) mm_inputs = MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY.get_dummy_mm_inputs( model_config, mm_counts={"image": 1}, processor=processor, ) ``` - `pre-commit run --files vllm/tokenizers/mistral.py vllm/utils/mistral.py vllm/multimodal/processing/context.py tests/tokenizers_/test_mistral.py` ## Test Result - `tests/tokenizers_/test_mistral.py`: **69 passed, 2 skipped** (pre-existing, unrelated skips) - Manual end-to-end repro against `unsloth/Mistral-Small-3.2-24B-Instruct-2506`: dummy multimodal input generation **crashes** with the exact `ValueError: Mismatch in image token count...` shown above **before** this fix (verified via `git stash`), and **succeeds** after. - `pre-commit run` on all changed files: **clean** (ruff check/format, mypy, forbidden-imports check, SPDX headers, typos, etc.)

signals.title: [Bugfix][Quantization][XPU] Fix GPTQ MoE loading under moe_wna16
signals.text: > **Blocks #52652** on XPU (only the `xpu.py` allowlist line is required there; `CudaPlatform` defines no allowlist, so #52652's CUDA rows are independent). ## Bug `Qwen/Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat-GPTQ-Int4` on XPU at **TP=2, no quantization flag**, fails to load. `moe_intermediate_size` is 1408, so each shard is 704 and `704 % 128 != 0` (`group_size` 128); `check_moe_marlin_supports_layer` rejects the layer and `auto_gptq.py:246-256` falls back to `MoeWNA16Config`. That fallback then has nowhere to go on XPU: `TRITON` was not an `auto` candidate there. At TP=1 the same checkpoint loads fine (`1408 % 128 == 0`, Marlin accepts, native XPU kernel runs) — thanks @yma11 for that, it narrowed the repro to TP>1. ## Changes **Fix 3 — `int_wna16.py`, the zero-flag path.** Reject the MoeWNA16 layout on XPU's native kernel explicitly (`_process_weights_xpu` contracts on the AutoGPTQ int32 K-first layout and unconditionally transposes dims 1/2, while MoeWNA16 registers uint8 N-first weights, so it would mis-shape rather than reject; it also has no zero-point input), and add `TRITON` after `XPU` in the XPU priority list so `--moe-backend auto` resolves. **Fixes 1 and 2 — only with an explicit `--quantization moe_wna16`.** | # | Fix | Without it | |---|---|---| | 1 | `moe_wna16` → `XPUPlatform.supported_quantization` | `ValueError: moe_wna16 quantization is currently not supported in xpu.` (`platforms/interface.py:966`) | | 2 | `packed_modules_mapping` forwarded to the linear delegate in `moe_wna16.py` | fused layers built unquantized; `qweight`/`qzeros`/`scales` have nowhere to load | #35865 proposes the same hooks including the identical assignment; it no longer applies as written, so this is an independent implementation rather than a fresh idea — happy to defer if it is revived. Also in the diff: `select_wna16_moe_backend`'s terminal `raise` now carries the last candidate's reason (`_make_log_unsupported_all`). That is a message change on a path every CUDA and ROCm user sees, and it belongs in its own PR — I will split it out. ## Test `pytest tests/quantization/test_moe_wna16.py -v` — the branch adds 4 test functions (8 → 12 functions, ~15 → ~20 collected). ## Gaps — this is not ready for review yet - **Test counts in the previous revision of this body were wrong** and are withdrawn; the suite has not been re-run against this tree. - **No accuracy evidence.** Fix 3 swaps the executing MoE kernel on XPU from native SYCL to Triton, so `AGENTS.md` wants a gsm8k run. Owed: gsm8k on the TP=2 zero-flag path, plus a throughput pair (native SYCL vs Triton) on the same cards. - **Counter-evidence I have not resolved.** On one of two 8-card B70 hosts, the newly routed `TritonWNA16Experts` did not survive weight loading — `UR_RESULT_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST` with an `xe` compute-engine reset at TP=2 on two different card pairs, and SIGSEGV at TP=1 with `--moe-backend triton`. The same path with the same image and checkpoint completed normally on a different B70 host, and unquantized dense and unquantized MoE both passed TP=2 on the failing host. Host-versus-image is not yet isolated. - The `(use --moe-backend triton for MoeWNA16 on XPU)` hint added by fix 3 is unreachable in any raised error — `map_wna16_backend` has no `"xpu"` key, so `backend == XPU` is only evaluated inside the `auto` loop where the reason goes to `debug_once`. To be fixed or dropped. - No sm90 run of the current fix set; fix 2 is platform-agnostic and untested on CUDA. AI assistance was used (Claude Code); every changed line reviewed.

signals.title: [Kernel][Quantization][XPU] Tensor-descriptor path for fused_moe_kernel_gptq_awq (int4)
signals.text: > **Numbers below are from a 2026-08-17 campaign on this branch's original base.** Three upstream commits have since landed on the files this PR touches (#41100, #52603, #51695). A rebase and a re-run are owed before this is reviewable; I am not asking for review yet. ## What it does Adds a tensor-descriptor (TD) load path to `fused_moe_kernel_gptq_awq`, gated on `VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD` (auto-on for XPU, opt-in on CUDA sm100+). **int4 only** — the gate is `and use_int4_w4a16`; an int8 TD implementation exists on a branch and is out of scope here. The novel part is int4: `B` is packed 2 nibbles/byte along K, so a dense descriptor cannot express the pointer path's "read the same byte twice, shift differently". The path builds the descriptor at half-K width, loads `[N, K//2]`, unpacks low/high nibbles and `tl.interleave`s them back to `[N, K]` before the transpose. ## Reaching the kernel Needs `--moe-backend triton` plus a WNA16 method that reports `may_have_bias=False`. Two get there: `MoeWNA16Method` (also needs `--quantization moe_wna16`, which on XPU needs #52651) and `CompressedTensorsWNA16MoEMethod` (`compressed_tensors_moe_wna16.py:114`, grouped int4, no extra flag on XPU). **The compressed-tensors route is not covered by any measurement below** — that is a gap, not a claim of safety. ## Guards | guard | why | |---|---| | `BLOCK_SIZE_K >= 32` (int4) | the packed-byte descriptor's last dim needs ≥16 bytes | | `BLOCK_SIZE_M >= TD_MIN_GATHER_ROWS` | descriptor gather is not amortised at tiny M; currently silent, should warn | | `K % BLOCK_SIZE_K` off-XPU | **diverges** from `invoke_fused_moe_triton_kernel`'s unconditional bail-out (`fused_moe.py:847`) by exempting XPU, where the K-tail test covers it | | hardware | `moe_use_td_hw_supported()` — XPU or CUDA sm100+ | ROCm is unreachable by construction: `moe_use_td_hw_supported()` is XPU-or-sm100 (`utils.py:678-682`) and `moe_wna16` is not in `rocm.py`'s allowlist. ## Evidence, 2026-08-17, base `3ee2df303` (XPU) / `10f9b5d74` (CUDA) Unit: B70 19/19 passed · H200 **19 skipped** (TD is off by hardware on sm90, so sm90 has zero executed coverage) · B200 11 passed, 8 skipped. E2E `vllm bench sweep serve`, medians of 3, seed 42, prefix caching off, `enforce_eager=True`: B70 output tok/s 388.62 → 436.95 (+12.4%), B200 378.24 → 596.66 (+57.8%). ## Gaps - Nothing measured under the default serving path — every run used `enforce_eager=True`, so compile + cudagraphs are untested. - The H200 leg is a null control on byte-identical code (0/3360 TD launches) and it still moved several percent, so the noise floor is not established and deltas of that size are not attributable. - The two XPU accuracy arms ran on different machines; they need one card in one session. - sm90 has no executed unit case at all, including the pointer path. - `BLOCK_SIZE_M` fallback is silent; `invoke_fused_moe_wna16_triton_kernel` emits no `warn_if_moe_use_td_ineffective`, contrary to a docstring in this diff. ## Duplicate work Open #52577 (truong-v) changes `b = tl.load(b_ptrs)` — `fused_moe.py:236`, the exact line this PR wraps in `if not USE_TD:` — to a masked load, and treats the unmasked tail as a memory-safety bug. We will conflict textually; whoever lands second preserves that mask in the `else` branch. #43389 touches the same K-loop for int4 repacking. #44563 clamps `moe_wna16`'s `BLOCK_SIZE_K`. No open PR adds a TD path to this kernel. AI assistance was used (Claude Code); every changed line reviewed. All numbers above were produced on Intel B70, NVIDIA H200 and NVIDIA B200 on 2026-08-17, not on the current head.

signals.title: [ROCm][Perf] Add a bf16x3 router GEMM for fp32 gate weights
signals.text: ## Motivation Models like MiniMax-M3, MiniMax-M2 and HunYuan-V3 store their router gate weights in fp32. On ROCm, none of the specialized GateLinear tiers can handle an fp32 weight, so the gate falls back to `F.linear`. That fallback casts the bf16 activations to fp32 in a separate kernel, then runs the GEMM on the fp32 MFMA pipe, which is ~16x slower than bf16 on gfx950. ## Proposed Fix Split the fp32 router weight into three bf16 terms at startup. At runtime, the router GEMM runs three bf16 matrix multiplies and sums them into one fp32 accumulator. This keeps the activations in bf16 (no copy to fp32) and uses the bf16 MFMA pipe instead of the ~16x slower fp32 one. The output is still fp32. Expert selection, sigmoid, bias-add and top-k are all unchanged. Measured against an fp64 reference at (M=8192, K=6144, E=128) on gfx950, the split is more accurate than the fp32 GEMM it replaces (relative L2 error 8.6e-7 vs 1.4e-6). The kernel only fires when there are at least 8192 tokens in the batch, where it is 1.55-2.99x faster. Below that the existing path wins and the kernel declines. An `OutOfResources` guard disables it gracefully rather than crashing a forward pass. ## Tests Tested on 4x MI350X (gfx950) with `amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4`. **Image:** `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-311b3513af33bc29b4acb2fde2e9313e5e9966a0` **Additional fix applied:** [#51585](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51585) (required to serve with `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN`) ### Performance | ISL/OSL | Conc | TTFT before (ms) | TTFT after (ms) | TPOT before (ms) | TPOT after (ms) | TPOT delta | |---------|------|-------------------|------------------|-------------------|------------------|------------| | 60k/600 | 8 | 11,884 | 11,733 | 18.50 | 17.87 | -3.4% | | 60k/600 | 16 | 10,064 | 9,639 | 32.72 | 30.63 | **-6.4%** | | 8k/1k | 8 | 980 | 951 | 10.43 | 10.40 | -- | | 8k/1k | 16 | 1,720 | 1,553 | 12.44 | 12.57 | -- | | 8k/1k | 64 | 3,366 | 3,336 | 24.39 | 23.96 | -1.8% | Gains concentrate at higher concurrency where prefill batches exceed the 8192-token threshold. ### GSM8K (1,319 examples, 8-shot, chat template, multiturn) | Filter | Before | After | |--------|--------|-------| | Flexible extract | 93.63% | **93.93%** | | Strict match | 93.63% | **93.93%** | No accuracy regression. Slightly better, consistent with the lower L2 error of the three-term split. <details> <summary>Serving command</summary> ```bash export VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTENTION=1 export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 export VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn export SAFETENSORS_FAST_GPU=1 vllm serve amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --distributed-executor-backend mp \ --trust-remote-code \ --block-size 128 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --language-model-only \ --max-model-len 133120 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 \ --max-num-seqs 128 \ --enable-chunked-prefill \ --async-scheduling \ --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN \ --moe-backend aiter \ --tool-call-parser minimax_m3 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 \ --no-enable-log-requests ``` </details>

signals.title: [Performance][MLA] Use FP16 logits for sparse indexer
signals.text: ## Summary - make the sparse-attention indexer request FP16 logits by default on CUDA, with an explicit `float16`/`float32` engine override - keep DeepGEMM output, local DCP top-k, and every vLLM selector on native FP16 without widening the materialized logits tensor - convert two packed FP16 score encodings to ordered keys at once, use exact native FP16 refinement, and retune persistent/decode crossover tiers - remove the experimental BF16 indexer/top-k surface and add rejection, correctness, engine-policy, DeepGEMM, DCP, and odd-length coverage - resolve the configured logits dtype during module construction so worker warm-up and inference do not depend on a thread-local config context - cover DeepSeek-V4 Flash's 64-head MXFP4 indexer in FP16 for both prefill and paged MTP decode with exact packed-cache-layout correctness tests ## Why GLM-5.2's sparse indexer materializes a large logits tensor before selecting top-k indices. Keeping the tensor and selection native FP16 reduces memory traffic. `--attention-config.indexer_logits_dtype` accepts `auto`, `float16`, or `float32`; `auto` chooses FP16 on CUDA and FP32 elsewhere. The final kernel transforms both packed halves with one 32-bit operation and reuses the exact keys in histogram and scatter. This reduced the unified FP16 kernel from 57 to 32 registers/thread at 1,024 rows and raised measured occupancy from 49.7% to 94.9%. The dtype is passed as a constant custom-op argument. Resolving it in the operator body originally failed during real-model warm-up because the worker callback does not run inside `set_current_vllm_config`; resolving it when the `SparseAttnIndexer` module is constructed fixes eager warm-up and graph replay. DeepSeek-V4 Flash's optional MXFP4 indexer cache uses the same FP16 logits path. The model-specific tests exercise 64 indexer heads, the packed 68-byte cache layout, and `next_n=3` (MTP=2), comparing both prefill and paged decode against dequantized MXFP4 references. ## Performance All selector measurements use captured real-model GLM logits, top-k 2,048, warmed CUDA graphs, and the repository `.venv`. CUDA events bracket graph replays and are not captured in the graph. Both the custom top-k and reference `torch.topk` run on CUDA; CPU transfers occur only in separate pytest failure diagnostics. Every result was checked against `torch.topk` before timing. ### Production-style fixed 256K decode graph The logits row stride and captured `max_seq_len` remain 256K while only the live KV length changes, matching reuse of a maximum-length graph. Entries are `FP16 us / FP32 us (FP32 / FP16 speedup)`: | Rows | 10K KV | 50K KV | 100K KV | 200K KV | 256K KV | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | 4.242 / 4.609 (1.087x) | 7.527 / 9.742 (1.294x) | 8.144 / 10.485 (1.287x) | 9.383 / 12.028 (1.282x) | 9.820 / 12.383 (1.261x) | | 8 | 4.732 / 5.069 (1.071x) | 7.628 / 10.008 (1.312x) | 8.941 / 11.507 (1.287x) | 11.562 / 14.032 (1.214x) | 12.573 / 15.349 (1.221x) | | 32 | 4.838 / 5.242 (1.084x) | 9.639 / 12.419 (1.288x) | 13.138 / 16.068 (1.223x) | 18.901 / 22.429 (1.187x) | 21.295 / 25.228 (1.185x) | | 128 | 5.323 / 5.549 (1.042x) | 17.500 / 19.292 (1.102x) | 27.604 / 29.836 (1.081x) | 47.513 / 66.983 (1.410x) | 56.910 / 85.397 (1.501x) | | 1,024 | 23.967 / 33.269 (1.388x) | 94.387 / 139.846 (1.482x) | 153.163 / 221.120 (1.444x) | 271.360 / 470.133 (1.733x) | 334.933 / 574.720 (1.716x) | FP16 is faster in all 25 production-style shapes: 1.042x-1.733x. ### Exact-stride matrix FP16 speedup over FP32 after retuning the selector: | Rows | 10K KV | 50K KV | 100K KV | 200K KV | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | 1.087x | 1.276x | 1.271x | 1.270x | | 8 | 1.062x | 1.300x | 1.290x | 1.214x | | 32 | 1.088x | 1.294x | 1.240x | 1.191x | | 128 | 1.051x | 1.084x | 1.048x | 1.387x | | 1,024 | 1.389x | 1.472x | 1.492x | 1.763x | | 8,192 | 1.528x | 1.627x | 1.628x | 1.839x | | 16,384 | 1.542x | 1.638x | 1.635x | 1.832x | FP16 is faster in all 28 exact-stride shapes: 1.048x-1.839x. The packed-key change invalidated the old decode crossover: persistent now wins through 32K, and measured row thresholds are 768 for 32K-64K, 512 for 64K-100K, and 1,024 for 100K-131K. ## Accuracy ### End-to-end long-context recall The final PR code was evaluated with the real `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4` checkpoint and the standard Paul Graham NIAH corpus. The paired runs used TP4, greedy decoding, FP8 E4M3 KV cache, 2,048-token chunked prefill, one sequence at a time, eager execution, disabled prefix caching, disabled FlashInfer autotuning, and no GVR. The only changed engine setting was `--attention-config.indexer_logits_dtype=float32` versus `float16`. Each context used needle depths 10%, 50%, and 90%, with two independently generated seven-digit keys per cell: | Context | FP32 exact | FP16 exact | Paired identical responses | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 50K | 6/6 | 6/6 | 6/6 | | 100K | 6/6 | 6/6 | 6/6 | | 200K | 6/6 | 6/6 | 6/6 | | 250K | 6/6 | 6/6 | 6/6 | | **Total** | **24/24** | **24/24** | **24/24** | Server-reported prompt lengths were 50,000-50,002, 100,001-100,002, 200,002, and 250,001-250,002 tokens. This is deterministic single-needle retrieval coverage, not a claim that every downstream task is unchanged. ### DeepSeek-V4 Flash FP4 indexer-cache NIAH The real `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` checkpoint was evaluated with TP4, MTP=2, FP8 main KV cache, FP16 indexer logits, eager execution, disabled prefix caching, and disabled FlashInfer autotuning. Both arms used the same ordinary fused-MoE backend because the local mega-MoE extension has a stale ABI. The only paired change was an FP8 indexer cache versus `use_fp4_indexer_cache=true`, which startup resolved to `mxfp4` and confirmed with `Using MXFP4 indexer cache for Lightning Indexer`. The standard Paul Graham NIAH corpus used one deterministic seven-digit key per cell and greedy decoding: | Context | FP8 indexer exact | FP4 indexer exact | Paired identical responses | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 50K | 3/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 | | 100K | 3/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 | | 200K | 3/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 | | 250K | 3/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 | | **Total** | **12/12** | **12/12** | **12/12** | Needle depths were 10%, 50%, and 90%. Server prompt-token counts matched between paired arms for all 12 cells and ranged from 49,983 to 249,984, so no prompt was truncated. This is deterministic single-needle retrieval coverage, not a claim that every downstream task is unchanged. Request latency is not reported because the control arm absorbed first-use JIT compilation. ### Real-input top-k set recall To isolate selector-set changes, FP32 logits captured from real GLM decode for BEAM documents were rounded to FP16 and exact top-2,048 was recomputed. Recall is `|topk(FP16) intersect topk(FP32)| / 2048`. Two layer-74 snapshots with 1,024 real rows each and 199,401-199,481 live KV tokens produced: | Rows | Mean recall | Median | 1st percentile | Worst row | Mean / max changed indices | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 2,048 | **99.9313%** | 99.9512% | 99.8047% | 99.7070% | 1.41 / 6 | A separate context sweep used two selector positions and 64 real rows per length: | Live KV | Mean recall | Worst row | Mean changed indices | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 10K | 100.0000% | 100.0000% | 0.00 | | 50K | 99.9496% | 99.9023% | 1.03 | | 100K | 99.9733% | 99.9023% | 0.55 | | 200K | 99.9428% | 99.8535% | 1.17 | | **Overall** | **99.9664%** | **99.8535%** | **0.69** | This recall measurement isolates FP16 score rounding on real distributions; the end-to-end NIAH table above measures the actual native FP16 DeepGEMM and top-k execution path. ## Validation - `cmake --build build/gvr_native_fp16 --target _C_stable_libtorch -j16` - 65 workspace/backend correctness cases passed, including FP16 odd lengths - 20 indexer dtype and retuned-selector policy cases passed - real TP4 GLM launch and warm-up passed for explicit FP32 and FP16 engine settings after moving dtype resolution to module construction - full 1,024-row FP16 equality with CUDA `torch.topk` at 10K, 50K, 100K, 200K, and 256K with a fixed 256K stride - all 56 exact-stride and all 50 fixed-stride dtype/shape cells passed correctness before CUDA-graph timing - packed transform exhaustively matched the scalar ordered-key transform for all 65,536 FP16 encodings - real DSV4 TP4 NIAH passed 12/12 with the FP8 indexer cache and 12/12 with `use_fp4_indexer_cache=true`; all 12 paired responses were identical - all 12 DeepGEMM attention cases passed on GB200, including 64-head DSV4 MXFP4-to-FP16 prefill and paged `next_n=3` decode against dequantized references; 2 full DCP FP16/FP32 decode-parity cases passed earlier - `SWEEP_MAX_CONCURRENCY=1,8,32,256 SWEEP_NUM_PROMPTS_FACTOR=3 bash ../glm_bench.sh` and a matched concurrency-1,024 factor-1 run completed 1,915 requests per dtype with no failures - all applicable pre-commit hooks on the PR changes passed `uv pip install -e . --torch-backend=auto` was attempted. The full editable build is currently blocked on unmodified current-main QUTLASS code including ATen extension headers while `TORCH_TARGET_VERSION` is defined; both changed CUDA targets build successfully. ## Duplicate-work check This does not duplicate #52149, which fixes persistent top-k candidate overflow, or #48726, which adds an opt-in fused DSA indexer/top-k path. This PR changes dtype production and native selection for the existing materialized- logits path, including DeepGEMM and DCP. ## AI assistance AI assistance was used to implement and benchmark this change. Before this draft is marked ready, the submitting human must review every changed line, reproduce the relevant validation, and be prepared to explain and defend the change end-to-end.

signals.title: [Model] Add GraniteSWA and GraniteMoeSWA via existing Granite
signals.text: ## Purpose Supersedes and closes #48270 Add vLLM support for GraniteSWA and GraniteMoeSWA models, folded into the existing Granite and GraniteMoeShared implementation, as opposed to separate models as in #48270. - GraniteSWA: Granite with per-layer sliding-window attention and a learnable per-head attention sink. The sink is passed to Attention via the native vllm attention harness, the per-layer windowing via config.layer_types and config.sliding_window, and per-layer RoPE/NoPE via config.layer_rope_theta (0 for NoPE). - GraniteMoeSWA: GraniteMoeShared-style MoE combined with the SWA/sink attention above (reuses GraniteSWAAttention). Optional shared experts via shared_intermediate_size (disabled by default); routed experts load through the standard FusedMoE param mapping. Additional features (sinks, sliding window, varying RoPE) are off by default, leaving existing Granite checkpoints unaffected. Also add checkpoint remapping for handling both old- and new-style HF MoE layers. Register both [***]ForCausalLM classes in the model registry, since HF publishes these Granite variants as distinct models. NB: transformers backend does NOT handle these models correctly. Sink tokens get dropped silently and so the model gives wrong output (see #52156). Claude was used to assist in implementing these changes. I have reviewed, corrected, and contributed the code myself, and tested the output for correctness. ## Test Plan Tests include offline parity checks against the adapted HF implementations, addition of SWA/MoeSWA checkpoints to the Granite tests, additional unit tests for case handling of added features and HF naming schemes, and GSM8K verification. Testing env uses CUDA 13.0, Torch 2.13.0, and Transformers 5.16.0. I have not included the parity check script(s) in this PR. ## Test Result All unit tests pass. I have confirmed that this code produces identical output to the HF implementation at fp32 precision, and that the transformers modeling backend does not. Bfloat 16 is near-identical (one missed token prediction in a teacher-forced setting on a randomly initialized model). Parity checks include sinks on/off, RoPE varying/global, and TP on/off. GSM8K score for the 2B SWA model is within 2 points of the published HF model card (40.3 vs 42.2 for 5-shot).

signals.title: feat(mooncake): Mooncake DCP: Chunk-Derived Namespace for KV Cache Store
signals.text: ### Motivation Under DCP > 1, the Mooncake connector on `main` forces `_spec_tp_replication_factor` to return 1 (`if self.dcp_size > 1: return 1`), disabling TP replication awareness. Every TP rank saves every chunk to its own `(tp_rank, tp_rank % dcp_size)` namespace — `tp_size`× write amplification (e.g., 8× under TP8+DCP4). Lookup fans out `tp_size` keys per chunk and requires `all()` to pass, which works but wastes store bandwidth and capacity. ### Why #51388 is superseded PR #51388 attempted to reduce write amplification by restoring the true TP replication factor (removing the `if dcp_size > 1: return 1` early return) and adding `put_step = factor // dcp_size`. However, it kept **rank-derived** namespace assignment (`dcp_rank = rank % dcp_size`), which created a structural mismatch: - **Save path** stripes chunks across ranks by `put_step = factor`. With `factor = 8` (MLA) and `dcp_size = 4`, each rank saves 1/8 of chunks. A rank with `dcp_rank = 0` saves chunks 0, 4, 8, ... — but only in namespace `@dcp0@`. - **Load path** queries all `tp_size` namespaces per chunk via `all()`. For chunk 1 (owned by `dcp_rank = 1`), it queries `@dcp0@`, `@dcp1@`, `@dcp2@`, `@dcp3@`. But `@dcp0@` only contains chunks 0, 4, 8, ... — chunk 1 was never saved there. - Result: `all()` fails because each namespace only holds 1/4 of chunks → **0% hit rate**. Five follow-up patches in #51388 tried to fix this (adjusting `put_step`, adding per-namespace DBs, etc.) but couldn't resolve the fundamental issue: **chunk → namespace was mapped indirectly via rank identity**, causing save and lookup to diverge on which namespace owns which chunk. ### This PR's approach Eliminate the indirection by making namespace a **pure function of chunk position**: `dcp_rank = chunk_id % dcp_size`. Combined with restoring the true TP replication factor: - **Save**: `put_step = factor` distributes chunks across ranks *within* a namespace. `dcp_rank = chunk_id % dcp_size` distributes chunks *across* namespaces. The two dimensions are orthogonal. - **Load**: For each chunk, derives `dcp_rank = chunk_id % dcp_size` and queries only that namespace. Save and load agree by construction. - **Lookup**: Queries `max(1, tp_size // factor)` keys per chunk (one per TP shard in the chunk's DCP namespace). For MLA: 1 key/chunk, no `all()`. For GQA: `num_kv_head` keys/chunk, `all()` across KV-head shards. For Mamba: `tp_size` keys/chunk, `all()` across TP shards. ### Performance impact (MLA, TP8, DCP4) | Metric | Before (main) | After (this PR) | |--------|--------------|-----------------| | Write amplification | 8× per chunk | 1× per chunk | | Lookup keys per chunk | 8 | 1 | | `all()` aggregation | Required | Eliminated | ### Breaking changes Both `dcp_rank` (rank-derived → chunk-derived) and `tp_rank` (self.tp_rank → self.tp_rank // factor) fields in store keys change. Existing cache entries are unreachable after upgrade. Requires one-time `reset_prefix_cache` call. Rolling update is safe — old/new keys coexist without interference, stale keys occupy capacity until reset. ### Additional safety guards - **NULL_BLOCK_ID guard**: Save and load skip chunks whose block slot is `NULL_BLOCK_ID` or out-of-range (protects against abort races). - **Token length clamp**: Save clamps `token_len` to `len(block_hashes) * hash_block_size` (prevents `AssertionError` after external cache hit). - **Empty key list early return**: Load exits cleanly when all chunks are filtered (prevents `ZeroDivisionError` in tp-rank rotation). ### Test coverage - 7 existing tests updated for new `_lookup_key_prefixes` tuple format - 15 new tests: chunk-derived save/load agreement, MLA/GQA/Mamba lookup key counts, factor restoration, write amplification, GQA tp_rank disambiguation, NULL_BLOCK guards, token_len clamp, empty key list, SWA+DCP, MTP+DCP, rolling update coexistence - All 124 unit tests pass ### Test commands ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py -v ``` ### AI assistance disclosure This PR was developed with AI assistance (Sisyphus/OhMyOpenCode). The submitting human has reviewed every changed line and run the full unit test suite. No model evaluation is needed as this change affects KV cache transfer infrastructure, not model output.

signals.title: [Kernel][XPU] Enable int8_w8a8 per-token MoE on the Triton backend for XPU
signals.text: Reopening. Withdrawn on 2026-08-18 to finish an independent review pass; that pass is done. Rebased onto current `main` (`4b7cb949a9`), one signed commit, +59/−8 across 2 files. ## Bug `int8_w8a8` MoE is unsupported on XPU by omission. `TritonExperts._supports_quant_scheme` (`experts/triton_moe.py:132-135`) gates every int8 scheme on ```python device_supports_int8 = ( current_platform.is_cuda() and current_platform.has_device_capability((7, 5)) ) or current_platform.is_rocm() ``` and there is no XPU int8 experts class either (`XPUExpertsWNA16` accepts int4 keys only), so `select_int8_moe_backend` raises. `oracle/int8.py` has no platform branch at all — the priority list is `[TRITON, HUMMING, CPU]` on every device — and `TritonExperts._supports_current_device()` already returns true for XPU. ## Reproduce ``` vllm serve soyrsoyr/deepseek-moe-16b-chat-W8A8-GPTQ \ --quantization compressed-tensors --moe-backend triton \ --enforce-eager --trust-remote-code ``` On `main`, Intel Arc Pro B70, the engine does not start: ``` ValueError: Int8 MoE backend TRITON does not support the deployment configuration since kernel does not support quantization scheme QuantKey(i8, scale(f32, static, per_channel), ...) ``` The checkpoint's experts genuinely carry this scheme: `quant_method: compressed-tensors`, `format: int-quantized`, weights `{num_bits: 8, type: int, strategy: channel, group_size: null, symmetric: true, dynamic: false}`, activations `{num_bits: 8, type: int, strategy: token, dynamic: true, symmetric: true}`, `n_routed_experts: 64`, `ignore: ["lm_head"]` only — no experts excluded. Most published W8A8 MoE checkpoints put every expert in `ignore` and would give a green run that never touches this kernel. `--trust-remote-code` is needed because the repo carries an `auto_map`. Its `configuration_deepseek.py` and `modeling_deepseek.py` are byte-identical (SHA-256) to the ones in `deepseek-ai/deepseek-moe-16b-chat`, so this executes DeepSeek's own published code. ## Change Enable only `(kInt8StaticChannelSym, kInt8DynamicTokenSym)` on XPU. Per-tensor stays refused: its activation step calls `ops.scaled_int8_quant`, which has no XPU implementation, whereas per-token uses the Triton `per_token_quant_int8` (`int8_utils.py:95-113`). A test pins that the per-tensor pair keeps being rejected. The CUDA/ROCm gate is untouched — `device_supports_int8` still keys the per-tensor entry, and the new `device_supports_per_token_int8` only widens the per-token entry by `or current_platform.is_xpu()`. ## Result With this PR, same command: engine starts, `Using TRITON Int8 MoE backend out of potential backends: ['TRITON', 'HUMMING', 'CPU']`, and `"What is 15 plus 27?"` → `"15 plus 27 is 42."`. A spy on `triton_moe.invoke_fused_moe_triton_kernel` counts **918 of 918** launches with `use_int8_w8a8=True`, so nothing silently falls back. Accuracy, `lm_eval==0.4.12`, `gsm8k`, 5-shot, full 1319 questions, `seed=42`, `batch_size auto`, identical `--model_args` on both sides: | | vLLM | `flexible-extract` | `strict-match` | |---|---|---|---| | Intel Arc Pro B70, **this PR** | `0.27.2rc1.dev154+g5fd7a8883` | **0.2085** ± 0.0112 | 0.0000 | | NVIDIA L40S, **stock `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.27.0`, unpatched** | `0.27.0` | **0.2123** ± 0.0113 | 0.0000 | Δ `flexible-extract` = **−0.0038**, inside the standard error of either run. The CUDA row is a genuine reference rather than a self-comparison: on CUDA this scheme is already supported on `main`, so the stock image runs the same Triton kernel with the same quant scheme and no patch at all. `strict-match` is 0.0000 on **both** platforms. That is this checkpoint's tokenizer emitting raw BPE markers (`Ġ`, `Ċ`) into decoded text, which breaks the `#### <number>` format `strict-match` requires — not an XPU numerical problem. It is why `flexible-extract` is the row to read. Tests: `tests/quantization/test_int8_moe_oracle.py` extended, no new file — B70 **2 passed, 4 skipped** (the skips are the CUDA/ROCm-gated cases). `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean on both changed files with ruff 0.14.0. ## Duplicate check Independent of #52652 (tensor-descriptor path for `fused_moe_kernel_gptq_awq`): different kernel, different scheme, no shared lines. #51515 also touches `experts/triton_moe.py` but rewrites the expert-assignment call inside `TritonExperts.apply`; no overlap with `_supports_quant_scheme`, and its diff applies cleanly over this branch. No open PR touches `_supports_quant_scheme`. --- AI assistance was used (Claude Code) for implementation and testing. Every changed line was reviewed, and all numbers above were produced on Intel Arc Pro B70 and NVIDIA L40S hardware on 2026-08-20.
signals.author: afierka-intel

signals.title: [Bugfix] Tolerate an unset group_size in the Marlin MoE support probe
signals.text: ## Summary `check_moe_marlin_supports_config` compared `group_size` against integers: ```python group_size <= 0 intermediate_size_per_partition % max(64, group_size) ``` compressed-tensors leaves `group_size` unset for per-channel strategies, so it arrives as `None` and both raise: ``` TypeError: '<=' not supported between instances of 'NoneType' and 'int' ``` The raise happens **inside `_backend_incompatibility_reason`**, whose contract is to return a reason string for an unsupported config. So instead of falling back to another backend, backend selection aborts and the user gets a traceback. In practice this hits compressed-tensors int4 MoE checkpoints with `strategy: "channel"`. ## Fix Normalise `None` to the `-1` this function already accepts, and widen the annotation to `int | None` to match what callers pass. `_check_marlin_supported` in the same module already declares `group_size: int | None` and tests for `None` explicitly, so this follows the existing convention rather than inventing one. ## Test plan Three cases in `tests/quantization/test_moe_wna16.py`, one per independent read of the same field. Extended that file rather than adding a new one, per `AGENTS.md`. | test | site it covers | unpatched | |---|---|---| | `test_wna16_oracle_handles_unset_group_size` | the probe, `oracle/int_wna16.py` | `TypeError` for `MARLIN` | | `test_ct_wna16_moe_method_normalises_unset_group_size` | the loading path, `CompressedTensorsWNA16MoEMethod.__init__` | `TypeError` | | `test_marlin_weight_prep_accepts_unset_group_size` | weight prep, `convert_to_wna16_moe_kernel_format` | `TypeError` | The second one matters most: it is the path a user actually walks when serving a per-channel compressed-tensors MoE checkpoint, not a synthetic call into a helper. | platform | unpatched | with fix | |---|---|---| | B200 (sm100) | **3 failed**, 1 passed | **4 passed** | | H200 (sm90) | **3 failed**, 1 passed | **4 passed** | | Intel B70 (XPU) | **1 failed**, 1 passed, 2 skipped | **2 passed**, 2 skipped | **Why two cases skip on XPU, and why that is not a coverage hole.** `select_wna16_moe_backend` consults a per-platform priority list, which on XPU is `[XPU]`. So `__init__` takes the non-Marlin branch and asserts `strategy == "group"` — a deliberate, pre-existing rejection of channelwise that this PR does not touch — and the Marlin probe is never reached. The weight-prep case needs `gptq_marlin_repack`, which has no CPU or XPU kernel. Both skip explicitly with a reason rather than passing vacuously. The probe case still discriminates on XPU because it calls `_backend_incompatibility_reason` with `backend=MARLIN` directly, bypassing the priority list — which is why the XPU column still shows a real fail-to-pass transition. An earlier revision of these tests passed without the fix on every platform. Root cause: `make_dummy_moe_config()` with no arguments yields `hidden_dim=1`, and `1 % 128 != 0` rejects Marlin *before* `group_size` is ever compared, so the probe returned a reason without touching the `None` path. The shapes are now explicit (`hidden_dim=4096`, `intermediate_size=1024`) and each test asserts its own premise. No perf or accuracy impact: this is a support-probe predicate evaluated once per layer at construction, not on any forward path. `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean, local `pre-commit run` green. ## Relationship to other work Found while investigating grouped int8 WNA16 MoE handling. **This fix is independent of that question** and correct either way — an incompatibility probe should not raise. The two mutually-exclusive alternatives for the int8 semantics are separate draft PRs, linked from the issue. --- AI assistance was used (Claude Code); every changed line was reviewed and all tests above were run personally on NVIDIA B200, H200 and Intel B70 hardware. Fixes #52713.

signals.title: [Bugfix] Keep pipelined streaming continuations off the waiting queue (#52693)
signals.text: ## Purpose Fixes #52693. A resumable streaming session could sit in both `self.running` and a waiting queue during pipelined loads. Incoming chunks were applied and enqueued while the previous chunk was still `RUNNING`, so the waiting loop raised `Invalid request status: RUNNING` and killed EngineCore. Continuations now stay in `streaming_queue` from `add_request` while the session is `RUNNING`. On stop, the request pauses to `WAITING_FOR_STREAMING_REQ` without merging; the queued chunk is applied later in promotion, after it has left the running list. Dual waiting-queue membership is refused, and a stale waiting entry is dropped instead of raising if the request is already `RUNNING`. This is not a duplicate: no open PR cites #52693. ## Test Plan ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/streaming_input/ -v .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_worker_slot_overflow.py -v ``` Test Result tests/v1/streaming_input/: 17 passed tests/v1/core/test_worker_slot_overflow.py: 3 passed The new tests failed on unfixed main with RuntimeError: Invalid request status: RUNNING, then passed after the fix. Model evaluation: N/A. This only changes scheduler queue membership for resumable sessions; generated tokens are unchanged. **AI assistance:** Cursor Grok 4.6 helped implement the scheduler change and tests. I reviewed every changed line, ran the tests listed above, and I am responsible for the change.
signals.author: AnubhabBanerjee

signals.title: [Bugfix] Support MistralCommonBackend tokenizers in structured output
signals.text: ## Purpose Structured output fails for Mistral models whose tokenizer transformers loads as a `MistralCommonBackend`. Transformers picks that class when `mistral-common` is installed and `TOKENIZER_MAPPING_NAMES` maps the model's `model_type` to it — `mistral`, `ministral`, `ministral3`, `mistral3`, `mixtral`, `pixtral`, `voxtral`, `voxtral_realtime`. vLLM reaches it whenever `resolve_tokenizer_args` does not select `tokenizer_mode="mistral"`. That class subclasses `PreTrainedTokenizerBase` rather than `PreTrainedTokenizerFast`, and the two grammar backends fail on it differently: **xgrammar — HTTP 500.** `is_mistral_tokenizer()` is `False`, so the working Mistral path is skipped and `xgr.TokenizerInfo.from_huggingface()` raises `ValueError: Unsupported tokenizer type`. The backend is built lazily on the first structured-output request, so the server starts fine and plain completions keep working. **outlines — silently wrong.** No crash: `get_cached_tokenizer` returns a `CachedTokenizer` subclass whose `convert_tokens_to_string` falls back to `"".join(tokens)`. The vocabulary it builds is wrong instead. On `mistralai/Mistral-Nemo-Instruct-2407` via `get_tokenizer(tokenizer_mode="hf")`, 409 of 129044 reduced-vocabulary entries map to the wrong token ids, collapsing onto 3 shared ids, so the grammar is compiled over a corrupted vocabulary. ## Fix `MistralCommonBackend` already carries what the Mistral path needs, and vLLM already has a wrapper that consumes it (`MistralTokenizer.__init__(tokenizer: MistralCommonBackend)`). The wrap happens once in `StructuredOutputManager`, where the tokenizer is acquired, so it covers every backend and keeps a single `MistralTokenizer` instance — the vocabulary caches keyed on the tokenizer object (outlines' `_outlines_vocabulary`, lm-format-enforcer's `lru_cache`) are not discarded. `backend_xgrammar.py` and `backend_outlines.py` are untouched. ## Test `tests/v1/structured_output/test_mistral_common_tokenizer.py`, built through `get_tokenizer`: - the reduced vocabulary is correct after wrapping and mismapped before it - both backends accept a valid document token by token, and reject an invalid token - the xgrammar bitmask width matches the vocabulary - xgrammar still raises `ValueError` without the wrapper - a non-Mistral tokenizer passes through untouched 9 tests, ~15s. ## Notes `guidance` already handled `MistralCommonBackend` and is unaffected. It rejects SentencePiece-backed instances with `TypeError: Guidance only supports Tekken tokenizers`, raised by mistral_common's own `from_mistral_tokenizer`; that is unchanged by this PR and reproduces identically without it.

signals.title: feat(rust): decode routed expert EngineCore output
signals.text: ## Summary Decode Python EngineCore routed-expert ndarray output into a typed Rust representation and provide native NumPy serialization for downstream compatibility layers. ## Why Python already emits `EngineCoreOutput.routed_experts` as a rank-three NumPy array. The Rust EngineCore client currently leaves that field opaque, preventing downstream Rust consumers from validating, aggregating, or returning the native routing trace. ## Changes - decode inline and multipart ndarray payloads - accept `uint8` and native little-endian `uint16` payloads - validate rank, dtype, frame index, overflow, and exact byte length - serialize the validated tensor as NumPy v1.0 bytes matching `np.save(..., allow_pickle=False)` - keep gRPC and public API behavior unchanged in this leaf The semantic tensor is `[tokens, layers, top_k]`. It contains no Prime-RL-specific prompt offset or envelope fields. ## Checks - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` - focused routed-output suite: 4 passed - byte-for-byte golden NumPy fixtures cover `uint8` and `uint16` - DCO-restacked review head `5a3165c32db57e7103888a462408bfaf5805b84c` has the same Git tree as the GPU-tested head - integrated small Qwen3-MoE validation returned native routed arrays before and after a live policy update ## Review note This change was prepared with AI assistance and reviewed line by line before submission.
signals.author: biswapanda

signals.title: feat(rust): expose routed expert traces over gRPC
signals.text: ## Summary Expose routed-expert capture through the Rust gRPC request and terminal response path. ## Why The Rust frontend needs a northbound API that can request routed-expert capture and return the decoded native EngineCore trace to non-Python clients without adopting a client-specific response envelope. ## Changes - use the merged `routed_experts_prompt_start` request control in gRPC response options - validate and lower the request-side prompt offset - accumulate routed-expert chunks while enforcing a stable dtype and trailing shape - return a typed terminal tensor containing only bytes, shape, and dtype - keep the prompt start out of the tensor because it is request context, not native routed-output data - keep OpenAI route behavior unchanged; constructor updates only initialize the new internal field - add gRPC round-trip, aggregation, and invalid-offset coverage Python vLLM's public format remains Base64 `.npy`. The typed tensor is an internal gRPC representation; downstream public compatibility layers serialize it to native `.npy` rather than a framework-specific object. ## Stack dependencies 1. #52721 supplies typed EngineCore routed-output decoding and native NumPy serialization. 2. #52703 supplied the Python-compatible sampling field and is already merged. This branch contains #52721 so the end-to-end path can be reviewed and tested. After #52721 merges, the final diff contains only terminal aggregation and the gRPC surface. It is independent of #52722. ## Checks - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` - focused gRPC conversion and round-trip tests passed on the rebuilt branch - DCO-restacked review head `76fe721765561483a366747344df2a6c5cd1d56d` has the same Git tree as the GPU-tested head - integrated small Qwen3-MoE validation completed pre-training capture, three training steps, policy version 1 transfer, and post-update routed capture ## Review note This change was prepared with AI assistance and reviewed line by line before submission.
signals.author: biswapanda

signals.title: [MooncakeStore] Report KV load tier in cache events
signals.text: ## Purpose Report the actual MooncakeStore replica tier in KV cache events. Mooncake already exposes whether a loaded replica is memory-backed or disk-backed, but this information was not propagated to `BlockStored` events. This change maps: * memory-backed replica → `CPU` * disk-backed replica → `STORAGE` * unknown tier → `None` Successful events are emitted only for blocks that actually load successfully. Scheduler lookup and connector protocol behavior are unchanged. ## Test Plan Run the focused MooncakeStore worker tests: ```bash PYTHONPATH="$HOME/vllm/.testdeps:$HOME/vllm" \ python -m pytest \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py \ -v \ --confcutdir=tests/v1/kv_connector/unit \ -k "test_recv_thread_emits_tiered_events_after_rotation_and_split or test_recv_thread_emits_unknown_tier_with_no_medium or test_recv_thread_does_not_emit_event_for_failed_load or test_recv_thread_skips_tier_lookup_when_events_and_logging_disabled" ``` An end-to-end MooncakeStore smoke test is also planned to validate real memory-backed and disk-backed loads on the A100 setup. ## Test Result Focused tier-related tests on the DGX/A100 environment: ```text 4 passed, 74 deselected ``` Validated: * tiered event emission for memory/disk replicas * unknown tier leaves `medium` unset * failed loads do not emit successful `BlockStored` events * replica-tier lookup is skipped when both KV events and tier logging are disabled End-to-end validation with real MooncakeStore memory/disk loads is still pending due to runtime environment setup and will be added once completed.
signals.author: g310v

signals.title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Enable Qwen3.8-27B LM-only mode without vision tower
signals.text: ## Purpose Qwen3.8-27B is served through vLLM's Qwen3.5-compatible hybrid model path. When `--language-model-only` is enabled, image and video limits are zero. The existing `_mark_tower_model` handling already prevents the vision parameters from being loaded, but the runtime can still create and profile encoder CUDA graphs because embedding-only mode keeps multimodal input support enabled. That encoder-graph setup is invalid for a missing vision tower and can prevent the text-only engine from starting. This change: - Adds `MultiModalRegistry.supports_multimodal_encoder()` to distinguish embedding-only inputs from inputs that execute the multimodal encoder. - Skips encoder CUDA-graph manager creation when all configured modalities have zero limits. - Applies the check in both the GPU model runner and GPU model-state path. - Adds registry and model-state regression coverage for embedding-only mode. The Qwen3.5 vision-tower placeholder was removed after the controlled GPU comparison below showed no measurable difference from the existing `_mark_tower_model` path. The functional fix is the encoder CUDA-graph guard. ## Test Plan CPU unit tests: ```bash VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/multimodal/test_registry.py \ tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py -q ``` Runtime matrix on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090: - Model: `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B`, the smallest checkpoint exercising the same Qwen3.5-compatible hybrid path. - `language_model_only=True`, `enable_mm_embeds=True`. - `cudagraph_mm_encoder=True`, `encoder_cudagraph_token_budgets=[64]`. - `max_model_len=512`, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.90`. - Four isolated variants: old/new tower handling crossed with encoder graph enabled/skipped. ## Test Result Unit tests: ```text 45 passed, 16 skipped, 14 warnings in 22.56s ``` Controlled runtime comparison: | Variant | Vision tower | Encoder CUDA graph | Result | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Baseline | Old `_mark_tower_model` | Enabled | Fails during capture: `StageMissingLayer('vision_tower')` | | A | Old `_mark_tower_model` | Skipped | Starts; 1.53 GiB model memory, 40.88 GiB KV, 480,182 tokens | | B | New placeholder | Enabled | Fails during capture: `NoneType` has no `patch_embed` | | C | New placeholder | Skipped | Starts; 1.53 GiB model memory, 40.88 GiB KV, 480,182 tokens | A and C both generated the expected short text response. Baseline and B fail before KV-cache initialization, so A versus Baseline does not yield a valid numeric KV-cache delta. It does establish that the encoder CUDA-graph guard is required for this embedding-only configuration. C versus A is identical at the measured resolution: no model-memory or KV-cache improvement from the placeholder. Therefore the patch keeps the capability check and removes the placeholder implementation. No throughput claim is made; the measured benefit is avoiding an invalid encoder-graph initialization path. No model-accuracy evaluation was added because the language-model weights and text generation path are unchanged. A real-weight generation smoke test was run for the two configurations that successfully initialized. ## Duplicate-work Check No issue was assigned to this PR. Searches of open vLLM pull requests and issues for Qwen3.8-27B, Qwen3.5, `language_model_only`, vision tower, and multimodal encoder found no existing PR covering this fix. signals.title: fix(build): correct preprocessor guard for GDN decode to fix Ampere c…
signals.text: fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp was mistakenly placed inside the VLLM_ENABLE_FUSED_KDA_DECODE block in ops.h. Since KDA is restricted to SM90+, this caused compilation to fail on pre-Hopper architectures (like Ampere SM 8.6) which support GDN but not KDA. This commit moves the declaration to the correct VLLM_ENABLE_FUSED_GDN_DECODE guard. ## Purpose Building vLLM from source fails on Ampere (SM 8.6) and other pre-Hopper architectures with the following error: `error: ‘fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp’ was not declared in this scope` This occurs because `fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp` in `csrc/libtorch_stable/ops.h` was mistakenly placed inside the `#ifdef VLLM_ENABLE_FUSED_KDA_DECODE` preprocessor block. Because KDA requires SM90+ (Hopper) or newer, the `VLLM_ENABLE_FUSED_KDA_DECODE` flag is not defined on Ampere systems. However, GDN is supported on Ampere (`VLLM_ENABLE_FUSED_GDN_DECODE=1`), so `torch_bindings.cpp` attempts to bind the GDN function, resulting in a compilation failure since the declaration is missing. ## Solution Separated the declarations. Moved `fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp` out of the KDA block and placed it under its correct `#ifdef VLLM_ENABLE_FUSED_GDN_DECODE` preprocessor guard. ## Test - Verified that `pip install -e .` successfully compiles and installs on an Ampere (SM 8.6) system without build errors. --- <summary> Simple fix to ensure the fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp compiles under all archs and not just post ampere archs by placing the function under VLLM_ENABLE_FUSED_GDN_DECODE preprocessor guard</summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details> **BEFORE SUBMITTING, PLEASE READ <https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/contributing>** (anything written below this line will be removed by GitHub Actions) co author: Gemini

signals.title: Fix Transformers modelling backend `RMSNormFuser.fuse` performance
signals.text: #50128 identified that `RMSNormFuser` was taking an excessively long time at startup tracing every norm module in `fuse` bypassing the caching efficiency in `match`. This PR determines and caches the attribute to read the `eps` from at in `match` so we no longer need to trace in `fuse`. Measured on the Transformers-backend fuser path: `Fusers(model, vllm_config)` (per-class matching, cold cache) plus `fuse()` on every matched instance, which is the work `recursive_replace` does. | Model | Norms | Before | After | Speedup | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` | 113 | 998 ms | 50 ms | 20.1x | | `google/gemma-3-4b-it` | 206 | 6050 ms | 105 ms | 57.8x | | `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B` | 33 | 261 ms | 45 ms | 5.8x | | `allenai/OLMoE-1B-7B-0924` | 65 | 548 ms | 83 ms | 6.6x | | `mistralai/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1` | 65 | 679 ms | 84 ms | 8.1x | Split by phase, since the two changes pull in opposite directions: | Model | match (per class) | | RMSNorm `fuse` (per instance) | | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | | before | after | before | after | | `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` | 43 ms | 37 ms | 944 ms | 2.0 ms | | `google/gemma-3-4b-it` | 112 ms | 95 ms | 5931 ms | 2.4 ms | | `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B` | 27 ms | 35 ms | 224 ms | 0.6 ms | | `allenai/OLMoE-1B-7B-0924` | 88 ms | 80 ms | 458 ms | 1.3 ms | | `mistralai/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1` | 72 ms | 81 ms | 605 ms | 1.2 ms | `fuse` no longer traces at all, so per-instance cost collapses (350x-2500x).
