signal.title: [Kimi K3][Pref] Export prefill checkpoints in a single FlashKDA pass
signal.text: ## Purpose This PR adds an optional Kimi-K3 prefill checkpoint mode for fine-grained prefix caching. When enabled, FlashKDA exports an intermediate recurrent-state checkpoint during the prefill. The checkpoint is stored in an internal request-owned Mamba block, allowing prefix cache entries smaller than the Mamba block size to be reused without an additional FlashKDA forward. Main changes: - Export recurrent-state checkpoints from the existing packed FlashKDA prefill. - Export the matching causal-conv state. - Support partial prefix caching and spec decoding. - Add internal checkpoint block allocation, lifecycle management, and scheduler metadata. - Allow the scheduler to skip the additional checkpoint-boundary forward. - Add unit tests for checkpoint metadata, block lifecycle, and prefix caching. [#52789](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52789) introduced the prefill-checkpoint infrastructure. This PR adds efficient support for fine-grained partial prefix caching and exports the checkpoint directly from the existing FlashKDA kernel, avoiding an additional or split FlashKDA forward. ## Usage ```bash VLLM_KIMI_K3_KDA_CHECKPOINT_MODE=1 \ vllm serve <model> \ --kda-prefill-backend flashkda \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --mamba-cache-mode align \ --prefix-match-unit 128 ``` This PR depends on [vllm-project/FlashKDA#7](https://github.com/vllm-project/FlashKDA/pull/7). The FlashKDA commit is temporarily pinned and should be updated after that PR is merged. ## Test Plan Setup: - TP8 on 2 × 4 GB300 - Growing prefix from 120K to 164K tokens - +2K tokens per round - 8 concurrent streams - Three runs per variant ## Test Result | Variant | P50 TTFT | **Improvement** | | --- | ---: | ---: | | #52789, non-partial | 2,151.53 ms | Baseline | | #52789, partial128 | 2,375.23 ms | **-10.40%** | | This PR, non-partial | 2,141.67 ms | Baseline | | **This PR, partial128** | **1,398.49 ms** | **34.70%** | ## Correctness Three consecutive full OCRBench runs with checkpoint mode and partial128 produced: 89.4% 89.6% 89.3% mean: 89.43% --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signal.title: [Kernel][Kimi] Fuse MoonViT Q/K complex RoPE
signal.text: ## Purpose MoonViT currently materializes the real and imaginary RoPE components in every encoder layer and invokes `ApplyRotaryEmb` separately for the strided Q and K views of its packed QKV projection. This PR adds an SM90+ Triton path that: - reads the packed-QKV Q/K views directly; - rotates Q and K in one kernel and produces the same contiguous output layout; - keeps the token count as a runtime argument to avoid recompilation for random image sizes; and - falls back to the existing implementation for unsupported devices, dtypes, shapes, and empty inputs. The kernel is adapted from SGLang's fused vision RoPE implementation, while its arithmetic order follows vLLM's current interleaved RoPE path. This is not a duplicate of an existing open PR. Searches for `MoonViT RoPE`, `Kimi vision RoPE`, `fused QK complex RoPE`, and `kimi_k25_vit` found no PR implementing this kernel. #53011 addresses eager `torch.compile` cache behavior, and #40600 targets full ViT CUDA graphs; neither fuses Q/K complex RoPE. AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used for implementation and testing. The human submitter must review every changed line and be able to defend the change before this draft is marked ready for review. ## Test Plan 1. Run pre-commit hooks on all changed files. 2. Compare BF16/FP16 fused results against FP32 complex-multiply references for Kimi K3's packed-QKV layout and dynamic token counts. 3. Capture and replay the fused path with a CUDA graph after changing inputs. 4. Benchmark the exact current MoonViT boundary (`ApplyRotaryEmb` twice, including real/imag materialization) against the fused path on B200. 5. Before marking ready, run a trained Kimi K3 multimodal end-to-end comparison. ## Test Result Local hooks: ```text .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \ vllm/model_executor/layers/rotary_embedding/vision.py \ vllm/model_executor/models/kimi_k25_vit.py \ tests/kernels/core/test_vision_rope.py \ benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_vision_rope.py All hooks passed, including ruff, formatting, mypy, SPDX, and forbidden-import checks. ``` B200 kernel tests in the vLLM nightly container: ```text /workspace/.venv/bin/python -m pytest /workspace/test_vision_rope.py -q 8 passed, 14 warnings in 17.87s ``` The tests cover BF16 and FP16, 1/257/4096 tokens, packed QKV strides, contiguous outputs, unsupported-input rejection, and CUDA graph replay. In a direct BF16 comparison with the existing vLLM path, the maximum difference was one BF16 ULP (`0.0078125`), affecting `0.00152%` of elements. B200 BF16 microbenchmark, 12 heads and head dimension 128: | Tokens | Existing Q/K RoPE | Fused Q/K RoPE | Speedup | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 256 | 150.02 us | 11.81 us | 12.7x | | 1,024 | 150.75 us | 12.06 us | 12.5x | | 4,096 | 151.15 us | 20.48 us | 7.4x | | 16,384 | 302.11 us | 57.31 us | 5.3x | A 27-layer random-weight MoonViT run using Kimi K3's vision geometry produced finite outputs with cosine similarity `0.999912` between the existing and fused paths. This is a numerical stress test, not a trained-model evaluation. Trained Kimi K3 multimodal end-to-end serving/evaluation has **not** been run yet. This PR remains a draft until that result and human line-by-line review are complete. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR. - [x] The test plan. - [x] The available test and benchmark results. - [x] No documentation update is required for this internal kernel optimization. </details>

signal.title: [CI] Fail pre-commit outright when pre-run-check doesn't pass, instead of skipping it
signal.text: ## What `pre-run-check` gates whether the `pre-commit` job is allowed to run (requires the `ready`/`verified` label, or the author having 4+ merged PRs). When it fails, `pre-commit` currently just doesn't run at all — its conclusion is `SKIPPED`, not `FAILURE`. That's a real gap: both GitHub's own required-status-check evaluation and `ci-infra`'s Buildkite `github-github-pre-commit-check` poller treat a `skipped` conclusion as non-blocking. So a PR that never satisfies `pre-run-check` can merge with a diff that was never linted at all. Concrete case: [#49688](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49688) merged this way and introduced real `ruff` `E501` violations in `vllm/platforms/cpu.py` that sat on `main` until a same-day follow-up ([#52981](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52981)) fixed them. It also caused an unrelated PR of mine to inherit a red `pre-commit` check, since the job runs `--all-files` against the whole tree — that's what led me to trace this down. ## Fix Keep the trust boundary exactly as-is (untrusted `.pre-commit-config.yaml` still never executes without a maintainer signal) — just make an unmet gate produce a real `failure` conclusion instead of `skipped`, by adding one guard step that runs only when `pre-run-check` failed and exits non-zero. Every other step keeps its default `if: success()`, so they're automatically skipped without needing to touch them individually. No changes needed downstream — both the GitHub required-check gate and the Buildkite poller already correctly block on `failure`, they just never saw one. ## Test plan - Validated the workflow YAML parses correctly and ran `pre-commit run --all-files --hook-stage manual` locally against this diff (includes the `actionlint`-backed "Lint GitHub Actions workflow files" hook) — passed. - Traced the `if:`/`needs.<job>.result` semantics against GitHub Actions' documented defaults to confirm the skip-on-prior-failure behavior for the untouched steps. - Have not been able to exercise the actual `pre-run-check`-fails branch against live GitHub Actions, since that requires a PR from a low-history author without the `ready`/`verified` label — happy to have a maintainer confirm on a test PR, or reason through it further if useful. AI-assisted change (Claude Code) — I reviewed and understand every line of the diff and traced the root cause end-to-end via the GitHub API before proposing this.

signal.title: [Frontend] Add reusable TP1 initialized-engine snapshots
signal.text: ## Purpose and prior art RFC #34303 and #37921/#37925 put CUDA checkpoint primitives below CRIU disk persistence. #35934 and #46089 explore related lifecycle and provider shapes, while #52132 keeps the frontend alive during EngineCore L3 sleep. This PR targets a different event: no serving process remains, and a trusted same-host operator restores one prepared Linux x86-64 TP1 engine before HTTP bind. @simon-mo asked me to split the generic CLI refactor out of #51360. This branch is stacked on `lazy-cli-dispatch`; the [snapshot-only comparison](https://github.com/thaw-ai/vllm/compare/lazy-cli-dispatch...tp1-snapshot-product) is 16 files (`+2,904/-39`). It contains the snapshot CLI, product code, Docker runtime, documentation, 27 unit cases, and one optional GPU end-to-end job. ```bash vllm snapshot create MODEL --snapshot-dir PATH --revision MODEL_SHA [serve args] vllm snapshot inspect PATH vllm snapshot restore PATH --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 ``` ## The fix `vllm snapshot create` initializes the engine and records a deterministic one-token oracle. Compact capture is the default: the existing sleep level 2 lifecycle releases model weights and KV cache before CRIU dump. Restore reloads that state, reproduces the captured token ID, text, and sampled log probability, and only then binds HTTP. A mismatch fails closed. This revision addresses the August 19 review: - The generic lazy CLI work is a separate prerequisite. - The Dockerfile now calls one installer script that owns the CRIU 4.2.1, CUDA plugin, and checkpoint-helper pins. - The manifest is a strict frozen Pydantic model. Secure path checks, atomic publication, credential exclusion, and runtime compatibility checks remain explicit. - `controller.py` is now 121 lines of public transaction orchestration. The private host runtime owns CRIU, PID/session, TCP, `io_uring`, GPU inventory, and rollback behavior. - Restore rejects an occupied captured PID before changing artifact state or calling CRIU, then uses pidfds to pin and clean the restored tree. - The branch includes an optional full-H200 create, inspect, restore, HTTP, second-restore, and cleanup job. The runner privilege contract still needs CI owner confirmation. ## Measured The matched large-model campaign used source `5dd888926f`, Qwen3-32B BF16 TP1, and one H100 PCIe 80 GB. Model and generated-cache files were resident; compact artifact files were evicted before each restore. | Path | Median activation | Samples | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Ordinary warm process | 54.7029 s | 3 | | Compact snapshot restore | 20.3795 s | 3 | | Reduction | 34.3234 s, 62.7% | 3 per arm | The compact artifact used 5,879,914,496 allocated bytes. The 65,540,298,478-byte model tree remained external. Creation took 78.5275 seconds, n=1, so the measured saving broke even on the third activation. Every accepted trial returned token ID `12095` and text ` Paris`. ## Verified on hardware Exact source `e464e2f6ae` on main `6df7adc17f` built a Linux amd64 image in 957 seconds on an RTX 4090 Laptop GPU rig. The image carried exact source labels and vLLM version `0.1.dev20225+ge464e2f6a`; native CUDA extensions came from the published current-main ancestor `44cf3f0466`. Qwen3-0.6B compact creation took 58.961 seconds, n=1, and produced a 3,565,976,397-byte manifest-reported artifact. The same artifact restored twice in the same container across `docker stop` and `docker start`, in 3.233 and 2.931 seconds, n=1 each. Both public requests returned token ID `12095`, text ` Paris`, and sampled log probability `-0.42565488815307617`, exactly matching the manifest. A control with the expected log probability shifted by 10 failed closed in 3.514 seconds, n=1, without publishing a ready server. Final checks found no container, process, listener, GPU process, link remap, or changed `io_uring` state. ## Test plan ```text .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_launch_cli.py \ tests/cuda/test_cuda_compatibility_path.py # 69 passed, two pre-existing warnings uvx pre-commit run --files <changed files> # all applicable hooks passed, including Python 3.10 mypy, ShellCheck, # Docker version validation, and the root lazy-import check ``` The snapshot portion adds 27 collected unit cases. They retain the public CLI, strict manifest, failure-before-mutation, PID-reuse, private-path, external TCP, and `io_uring` contracts. The optional GPU script checks 18 static contracts and the same-artifact two-restore flow. No model evaluation was run because this does not change model execution or output logic. The hardware gate instead compares the captured and restored one-token output through the public API. Native Linux arm64 `vllm-runtime-base` built from exact source `e464e2f6ae` in 499 seconds on an 8.2 GB Docker VM. The image logged the arm64 skip and contained none of CRIU, `cuda-checkpoint`, or the CUDA CRIU plugin. Initialized snapshots remain Linux x86-64 only in this PR. AMD support will follow separately. ## Product envelope - One NVIDIA GPU, TP1, PP1, DP1, and prefill-context parallel size 1. - Same trusted host and GPU, with matching driver, kernel, runtime, engine arguments, selected environment, and checkpoint tools. - Root or passwordless `sudo`, plus a private local artifact that can contain process memory and secrets. - No external established TCP peer at capture, active `io_uring`, concurrent restore, cross-host migration, GPU relocation, or ordinary-start fallback. - Compact capture requires an immutable model revision. Full-state capture keeps model state for local or mutable model sources. AI assistance was used. I take responsibility for the implementation, compatibility boundary, and measurements.

signal.title: [Feature][DSpark]: Logprobs adaptive verification
signal.text: Solves #51873 ## Purpose Lifts the restriction blocking logprobs with enable_adaptive_verification, implementing the TODO from #47808. Adaptive verification assigns per-request draft counts on device; the CPU-side `cu_num_logits_np` only holds an evenly-distributed stand-in. Using it as `cu_num_generated_tokens` would misassign logprob rows across requests. Instead, the rejection sampler now attaches the device `cu_num_logits`. The tensor rides along on the existing async D2H copy in AsyncOutput and is materialized as a list in tolists() after the copy event. ## Test Plan - `pytest tests/v1/test_outputs.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py -v`(new unit test covers the tensor-boundary hand-off through to_cpu_nonblocking().tolists()) - E2E on H100: Qwen/Qwen3-4B-FP8 + deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_4b_block7, FA3, full cudagraphs, 32 mixed prompts, greedy, logprobs=5, max_tokens=64, adaptive verification on vs. off. ## Test Result - Unit: 17/17 passed. - E2E self-consistency (adaptive on): 2048/2048 generated tokens present in their own logprobs dict. - E2E adaptive vs. non-adaptive: 0/32 requests with token drift. cc @benchislett --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signal.title: [Bugfix][Core] Align hybrid block sizes across PP stages
signal.text: ## Purpose Fixes #51752. Hybrid block-size alignment currently discovers a non-SSM attention backend only from the local pipeline stage. A PP rank that owns only SSM/KDA layers therefore returns early, while an attention-owning rank aligns `block_size`, `mamba_block_size`, and related page sizes. The resulting per-rank KV specs can disagree before the frontend synchronization path is reached. This PR: - gathers non-SSM backend presence across the PP CPU group; - selects the first backend-owning rank in PP/layer order, preserving the existing first-attention-backend behavior; - performs backend-dependent alignment only on that source rank, then broadcasts the aligned block and padded-page configuration to every PP rank; - uses the shared synchronization in both the generic platform path and the CPU override; - adds regression coverage where the source uses a runtime-generated backend that cannot be imported on another rank. Broadcasting the aligned configuration avoids reconstructing backend classes on ranks that do not instantiate them. This is required for dynamic static-sink and chunked-local attention backends created with `type()`. This is not a duplicate of #49845. That PR reconciles multiple attention backend classes visible within one rank; this PR handles a pipeline stage that has no local attention backend at all and must obtain the aligned configuration from another PP stage. I directed the work, reviewed the complete set of changes, and independently verified the final implementation and validation results. OpenAI Codex was used only as a limited implementation aid under my direction. I have reviewed and confirmed the final diff in full and remain responsible for the correctness, quality, and overall contribution.

When `return_token_ids=true`, both the Python and Rust frontends now return: - the final `prompt_token_ids` after multimodal placeholder expansion; - ordered `mm_placeholders` ranges, without pixel values or processed tensors. signal.title: [Bugfix][V1] Restore hybrid GDN prefix-cache hits under MTP spec decoding
signal.text: ## Purpose On **Qwen3.5-122B-A10B** with MTP speculative decoding, a replay of a cached prompt never reaches the depth the prefix cache could give it, and prompts whose length is a multiple of the hash unit get **no hit at all**. Measured live before this change, with a 1072-token GDN page and `--prefix-match-unit 67`: | prompt | cached tokens on replay | ceiling | |---|---|---| | 1072 | **0** | 938 | | 2000 | **0** | 1876 | | 2144 | **0** | 2010 | | 3000 | 1072 | 2881 | | 3500 | 2144 | 3417 | ### Root cause Three rules compose badly. A lookup caps at `prompt_len - 1`, because the last token must be recomputed for logits. The MTP/EAGLE drafter then rewinds the hit one hash unit (67) further. But the producer publishes the GDN state at the prompt's own tail boundary, `prompt_len // 67 * 67`, which is at or above the cap — so the recurrent group cannot resume where the rewind lands, and the coordinator intersects the two groups down to the previous full page (or to zero). The same cap breaks the full-attention side whenever `prompt_len` is a multiple of 67 — and every page multiple is, since `1072 = 16 × 67`. Its partial-tail entry is registered at `prompt_len // 67 * 67 == prompt_len`, which the `- 1` cap excludes, so full attention itself matches nothing below the page boundary and the hybrid hit collapses to 0. That is the `1072 → 0`, `2144 → 0` row above. ### Fix Write-side only, all of it gated on MTP/EAGLE plus fine-grained hashing being active: - `mamba_state_cache_position(num_tokens, block_size, hash_block_size)` in `kv_cache_utils.py`: `unit = min(hash_block_size, block_size)`, returns `(num_tokens - 1 - unit) // unit * unit` — the position a replay actually lands on. - `Scheduler._mamba_block_aligned_split` stops a prefill chunk there, so that state exists to be published. It is an **extra** stop; the existing block-aligned stops stay. Replacing them lets intermediate chunks end off-grid and re-triggers the state poisoning of #43559 (14 tests in `test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py` fail that way). - `MambaManager._cache_partial_tail_block` publishes the GDN state there instead of at the prompt tail. - `FullAttentionManager._cache_partial_tail_block` additionally publishes `(prompt_len - 1) // 67 * 67`, the deepest tail a replay can reach. The unshifted tail is kept, because requests that *extend* this prompt have a higher cap and can still match it. - `MambaManager` reports a block-aligned prompt end as unreachable through a new `reachable_block_mask()` argument, so that state is not cached in any retention mode: no lookup can land at or past a prompt's own end, and the rewound state below it is where consumers land. Guarded on the latter being cached. The rewound position is read from one `MambaManager` helper rather than recomputed per caller, and keys off whether the engine runs a drafter rather than the per-group `use_eagle` bit, which is only set on groups that take the drop. Without the last item the page multiples stay at 0 no matter where the GDN state sits: the producer had the state at 938 / 2010 / 3082, but full attention offered nothing below 1072 / 2144 / 3216 for the intersection to meet. ## Test Plan ```bash # unit pytest tests/v1/core -q # e2e: Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, 4x B200, MTP 3 tokens, sub-page hashing vllm serve $QWEN35_122B --tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-chunked-prefill \ --spec-method mtp --spec-tokens 3 --prefix-match-unit 67 --port 8110 ``` Hit depth is read from the `vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total` delta of a replay: a token-id prompt of an exact length is sent three times and the second and third deltas are the cached length. 132 lengths from 1 to 15k were swept — every page multiple with its `+1`, `+unit-1`, `+unit`, `+unit+1` neighbours, plus scattered lengths. Two further passes cover the configurations where the patch must do nothing, and quality was checked on top of real hits. ## Test Result (1) Hit Length Boundary All 132 lengths land exactly on the replay ceiling `(P - 1 - 67) // 67 * 67`. Page-boundary neighbourhoods, where the old code either missed entirely or fell back a full page: | prompt | position | before | after | replay ceiling | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1072 | k*1072 | 0 | 938 | 938 | | 1073 | k*1072 + 1 | 0 | 1005 | 1005 | | 1138 | k*1072 + unit - 1 | 0 | 1005 | 1005 | | 1139 | k*1072 + unit | 0 | 1005 | 1005 | | 1140 | k*1072 + unit + 1 | 0 | 1072 | 1072 | | 2144 | k*1072 | 0 | 2010 | 2010 | | 2145 | k*1072 + 1 | 1072 | 2077 | 2077 | | 2210 | k*1072 + unit - 1 | 1072 | 2077 | 2077 | | 2211 | k*1072 + unit | 1072 | 2077 | 2077 | | 2212 | k*1072 + unit + 1 | 1072 | 2144 | 2144 | | 3216 | k*1072 | 0 | 3082 | 3082 | | 3217 | k*1072 + 1 | 2144 | 3149 | 3149 | | 3282 | k*1072 + unit - 1 | 2144 | 3149 | 3149 | | 3283 | k*1072 + unit | 2144 | 3149 | 3149 | | 3284 | k*1072 + unit + 1 | 2144 | 3216 | 3216 | | 5360 | k*1072 | 0 | 5226 | 5226 | | 5361 | k*1072 + 1 | 4288 | 5293 | 5293 | | 5426 | k*1072 + unit - 1 | 4288 | 5293 | 5293 | | 5427 | k*1072 + unit | 4288 | 5293 | 5293 | | 5428 | k*1072 + unit + 1 | 4288 | 5360 | 5360 | | 10720 | k*1072 | 7504 | 10586 | 10586 | | 10721 | k*1072 + 1 | 9648 | 10653 | 10653 | | 10786 | k*1072 + unit - 1 | 9648 | 10653 | 10653 | | 10787 | k*1072 + unit | 9648 | 10653 | 10653 | | 10788 | k*1072 + unit + 1 | 9648 | 10720 | 10720 | Other lengths: | prompt | before | after | ceiling | |---|---|---|---| | 500 | 0 | 402 | 402 | | 999 | 0 | 871 | 871 | | 2000 | 0 | 1876 | 1876 | | 3000 | 1072 | 2881 | 2881 | | 3500 | 2144 | 3417 | 3417 | | 5000 | 3216 | 4891 | 4891 | | 7777 | 6432 | 7705 | 7705 | | 12345 | 10720 | 12261 | 12261 | | 14999 | 12864 | 14874 | 14874 | `before` comes from a CPU replica driving the real splitter and the real managers on the base commit; on the patched build that replica reproduces the end-to-end numbers length by length, so the two columns are comparable. Configurations where the patch must be inert: re-running the same 132 lengths without `--prefix-match-unit` (both groups sit at 1072, so `hash_block_size == block_size` and sub-page hashing is off) gives `((P - 1) // 1072) * 1072 - 1072` on every length, and the CPU replica shows this build and the base commit agreeing on all 132. `mamba_cache_mode=all` cannot be exercised on this model — it is not in `SupportsMambaPrefixCaching`, so vLLM falls back to `align`. Unit tests: `tests/v1/core` 492 passed. The one failure and two errors are GPU-exclusive e2e cases (`Free memory on device cuda:0 ... less than desired`) blocked by the serving process on the same box, and reproduce without this change. `tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py` is updated so the replay landing position counts as a legal intermediate chunk end alongside the partial-tail boundary. (2) Model Quality Test GPQA Diamond Score for Qwen/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B : 85.9% (match official score 86.6%) GSM8K 5-shot, 300 questions: 0.890 / 0.853 with 0.0% / 1.3% invalid on this build, against 0.847 / 0.830 with 1.7% / 2.7% invalid on the base commit. Run-to-run spread is larger than the gap, so this is "no regression", not an accuracy claim. Output quality on top of a real hit: an English passage of 700 / 1500 / 2400 / 3500 words, sent cold and then replayed (hits of 670 / 1608 / 2613 / 3819 tokens), returns byte-identical text at `temperature=0` in all four, twice over — no truncation, no repetition, no garbling. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details> ## Reproduce Low KVCache Hit Length with Qwen3.5 (1) Launch ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 \ PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True \ vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B \ --served-model-name Qwen3.5-122B-A10B \ --trust-remote-code \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \ --max-model-len 262144 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \ --max-num-seqs 64 \ --enable-chunked-prefill \ --spec-method mtp \ --spec-tokens 3 \ --prefix-match-unit 67 \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8110 ``` (2) Send the same prompt twice ```bash python3 - <<'EOF' import json, random, re, urllib.request N = 2144 BASE = "http://localhost:8110" def hits_total(): metrics = urllib.request.urlopen(f"{BASE}/metrics").read().decode() return float( re.search(r"^vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total\{[^}]*\} (\S+)", metrics, re.M).group(1) ) random.seed(N) body = json.dumps({ "model": "Qwen3.5-122B-A10B", "prompt": [random.randint(1000, 100000) for _ in range(N)], "max_tokens": 1, "temperature": 0, }).encode() for attempt in (1, 2): before = hits_total() urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request( f"{BASE}/v1/completions", body, {"Content-Type": "application/json"})) print(attempt, int(hits_total() - before)) EOF ``` (3) Check the second request's cache length Before the fix it is 0, after the fix it is 2010.

signal.title: Add routed expert loading for gpt-oss

signal.title: [Rust Frontend] Support --allowed-media-domains
signal.text: ## Purpose `--allowed-media-domains` is declared in `UnsupportedArgs`, so passing it to the Rust frontend aborts startup with "not implemented in Rust frontend yet". At the same time `MultimodalModelInfo` always builds its `MediaConnector` with `MediaConnectorConfig::default()`, which allows any remote host. `llm-multimodal` already implements the host match, so this only wires the argument through: CLI -> `Config` -> `LoadModelBackendsOptions` -> `MediaConnectorConfig`. No engine-side change. Behavior matches `vllm/multimodal/media/connector.py`: - `--allowed-media-domains` unset: any host is allowed. - `VLLM_MEDIA_URL_ALLOW_REDIRECTS=0`: the media HTTP client is built with `Policy::none()`, so an allow-listed host cannot bounce a fetch to a disallowed target. Unset or non-zero keeps `reqwest`'s default follow behavior, mirroring `allow_redirects=envs.VLLM_MEDIA_URL_ALLOW_REDIRECTS`. ## Not duplicating an existing PR No other open PR wires media-access restrictions into the Rust frontend; `--allowed-media-domains` is still listed under `UnsupportedArgs` on `main`. ## Scope: `--allowed-local-media-path` is deliberately left out An earlier revision of this PR also wired `--allowed-local-media-path`, but it cannot work against the currently pinned `llm-multimodal` (rev `15adba5`): - `MediaContentPart` has no file variant, so a `file://` input arrives as `ImageUrl`/`AudioUrl`/`VideoUrl` carrying a string. - `AsyncMultiModalTracker::push_part` special-cases only `data:` and routes everything else, `file:` included, to `MediaSource::Url`. - `enqueue_image`/`enqueue_audio`/`enqueue_video` are private, and there is no public API that accepts a `MediaSource`, so the frontend cannot reach the guarded `MediaSource::File` path. The option would therefore be silently inert: the connector would attempt an HTTP request for a `file:` URL instead of the canonicalize-and-prefix-check path. Rather than ship a security flag that does nothing, `--allowed-local-media-path` stays in `UnsupportedArgs` (unchanged from `main`, so this is not a behavior regression) with a `TODO` in `server/src/config.rs`. It can be wired in a follow-up once the crate routes `file:` to `MediaSource::File`. Per-redirect-hop host re-validation was also raised in review. It is intentionally not added here: `connector.py` validates only the initially supplied URL and relies on `VLLM_MEDIA_URL_ALLOW_REDIRECTS` as the mitigation, which this PR now honors. Hardening past the Python path belongs in `llm-multimodal`, where the allow-list lives. ## Test Plan ``` cargo fmt --all -- --check cargo clippy -p vllm-cmd -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server --all-targets -- -D warnings cargo test -p vllm-cmd -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server ``` New tests in `rust/src/cmd/src/cli/tests.rs` cover the `vllm-rs serve` flag and the `--args-json` path used by the Python supervisor, plus the unset default. `rust/src/chat/src/multimodal.rs` adds redirect tests over a local HTTP server: an allow-listed host that 302s to a non-allow-listed host is reached under the default policy and blocked under `Policy::none()`, and a disallowed initial host is rejected outright. ## Test Result fmt and clippy clean, 706 tests pass across the three crates. Note: this change was AI-assisted; every changed line was reviewed by me and the commands above were run locally. CC: @BugenZhao

signal.title: [Rust Frontend] Support stop strings in the token generate route
signal.text: This PR adds stop-string support to `/inference/v1/generate` in the Rust frontend. Python accepts `stop` there (its `sampling_params` is the full `SamplingParams`, and it builds a detokenizer unless `--tokens-only` is set, which the Rust frontend lists as unsupported), and the Rust gRPC token route already goes through the decoded stream, but the HTTP route submitted via `generate_raw()`, which drops `decode_options` entirely. So `stop` was silently swallowed by the request type's catch-all and the response came back 200 with the stop string never applied. Roadmap item is under #44280, "Audit request parameter coverage and validation". Adjacent Python-side work on the same route is #47313. The route now accepts `stop`, `include_stop_str_in_output`, `skip_special_tokens`, and `detokenize` inside `sampling_params` and lowers them into `TextDecodeOptions`, so the matching itself stays where it already lives in `vllm-text` and no route-level matching code was added. Requests without stop strings still take `generate_raw()`: stop strings are the only decode-side option observable on a token-out route, and this route exists to skip tokenizer work, so paying for detokenization unconditionally would have regressed its main use case (`detokenize: false`) for nothing. Validation mirrors `SamplingParams._verify_args` in Python's order, empty stop string first and then the `stop` with `detokenize=false` rejection, and lives in the route because `detokenize` has no representation in the shared layer. `render.rs` carries the decode options through the render round-trip, which was dropping them the same way. Two behaviors worth knowing. When a stop string matches, `vllm-text` truncates the token IDs and the output token count at the match, while Python leaves the tail in and counts it; that is shared behavior which `/v1/completions` and `/v1/chat/completions` have too, so I pinned it with a route test rather than changing the shared stream here. And continuous-usage chunks report no cached tokens until the terminal event, matching the chat route, because the decoded stream only carries usage at the end.
signal.author: ricky-chaoju

signal.title: [Bugfix][DP] Synchronize the device on pause completion
signal.text:
Addresses the third problem in #51476: `pause_generation()` resolves before the device is idle — and in DP, the pause path is itself what makes the device busy. Companion PR #52957 (independent, no shared commits) removes the DP dummy-batch burst; this PR makes the pause completion contract correct regardless of how much work is in flight. ## Purpose **1. Pause completion is a CPU-side predicate.** The pause future resolves off `has_work()` and the DP consensus is a gloo CPU all-reduce; nothing on the pause path touches a CUDA stream. `sleep()` is safe only because `GPUWorker.sleep` synchronizes before unmapping — bare pause is sleep minus the synchronizing half. RL callers pause, run their own weight-sync kernels/NCCL, then sleep; that work races whatever the engine launched last. Reported from production, surviving today only on the incidental ~0.5s between pause and sleep. **2. The pause path launches unwaited GPU work.** `DPEngineCoreProc._pause_complete` kick-starts `engines_running = True` so every rank reaches the consensus all-reduce in `_has_global_unfinished_reqs` — and the fixed every-32-step cadence then forces **32 dummy forwards per rank per pause call** on an idle engine. The final dummy batch is launched in the consensus iteration itself, is not in `batch_queue`, and is invisible to `has_work()`; one iteration later the future resolves while it can still be executing. `wait_for_requests_to_drain()` cannot compensate: the coordinator only tracks request-driven waves, so during the burst it publishes "not running" and drain returns instantly. Measured (DP=2 + EP, PowerMoE-3b, dummy batch inflated to ~110ms to model a large-MoE step): `pause_generation()` on an **idle** engine takes **3.40s** and returns with the device still busy. ## Change A device barrier at pause completion. `WorkerBase.synchronize_device()` synchronizes through the device-generic `torch.accelerator` API whenever an accelerator is registered — the same barrier `sleep()` relies on — so CUDA, XPU and any other `torch.accelerator` backend get it without an override, and it stays a no-op only where there is genuinely no accelerator (CPU); backends outside `torch.accelerator` must override with their own wait. `EngineCore._finish_pause()`: `collective_rpc("synchronize_device")`, *then* cache reset — synchronizing first also stops `clear_cache=True` from resetting state the last launched batch may still be using. Called from all three completion paths (in-proc, fast path, deferred idle callback). `collective_rpc` waits for **all** workers, which also closes `execute_dummy_batch` waiting only for the output rank. The barrier does not shrink the burst itself: an idle-engine DP pause still runs 32 dummy forwards, it just waits for them honestly. #52957 cuts the burst to a single step with a one-condition cadence change; the two PRs compose but neither depends on the other. The same contract is applied to the mirror transition: `GPUWorker.wake_up` now ends with `torch.accelerator.synchronize()`. `sleep` synchronizes on both sides of the memory transition, `wake_up` on neither — its tail work (buffer restores after level-2 sleep, `post_kv_cache_wake_up`'s re-init kernels) was unwaited, so a caller could start same-device work (e.g. RLHF weight sync right after wake) racing it. Covered by the existing sleep/wake e2e cases in the regression suite below. ## Reproduction (scripts included) Requires 2 GPUs and `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly`. Save the three files below into a directory `$W`, then: ```bash # baseline: the bug docker run --rm --gpus '"device=0,1"' --ipc=host --shm-size=16g \ -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface -v $W:/patch \ --entrypoint bash vllm/vllm-openai:nightly /patch/gpurepro.sh instr # with this PR: check out the branch, then git diff main...HEAD -- vllm/ > $W/fix.patch docker run --rm --gpus '"device=0,1"' --ipc=host --shm-size=16g \ -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface -v $W:/patch \ --entrypoint bash vllm/vllm-openai:nightly /patch/gpurepro.sh fixed ``` (If NCCL fails at init on a CUDA-13.1 driver, add `-e NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=0`.)
gpupatch.py — instrumentation only: inflates the dummy batch to ~110ms to model a large-MoE step, and adds a device_idle() probe RPC ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """Usage: gpupatch.py — instruments a vLLM install.""" import sys site = sys.argv[1] def sub(path, old, new): with open(path) as f: src = f.read() if new in src: return assert old in src and src.count(old) == 1, f"pattern not found/unique in {path}" with open(path, "w") as f: f.write(src.replace(old, new)) OLD = """\ def execute_dummy_batch(self) -> None: num_tokens = getattr(self.model_runner, "uniform_decode_query_len", 1) self.model_runner._dummy_run(num_tokens, uniform_decode=True) """ NEW = """\ def execute_dummy_batch(self) -> None: num_tokens = getattr(self.model_runner, "uniform_decode_query_len", 1) self.model_runner._dummy_run(num_tokens, uniform_decode=True) import os as _os _cycles = int(_os.environ.get("REPRO_SLEEP_CYCLES", "0")) if _cycles: # Simulate a large-MoE forward: keep the stream busy after launch. torch.cuda._sleep(_cycles) def device_idle(self) -> bool: return bool(torch.cuda.current_stream().query()) """ sub(f"{site}/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", OLD, NEW) print("instrumented") ```
repro_gpu.py — the scenario: pause / drain / probe ```python import asyncio import time from vllm import SamplingParams from vllm.engine.arg_utils import AsyncEngineArgs from vllm.v1.engine.async_llm import AsyncLLM async def main(): engine = AsyncLLM.from_engine_args( AsyncEngineArgs( model="ibm-research/PowerMoE-3b", data_parallel_size=2, enable_expert_parallel=True, gpu_memory_utilization=0.5, max_model_len=512, enforce_eager=True, ) ) async def gen(rid): async for _ in engine.generate( "The capital of France is", SamplingParams(max_tokens=8), rid ): pass async def probe(tag): idle = await engine.collective_rpc("device_idle") print(f"PROBE {tag}: device_idle={idle}", flush=True) return all(idle) await gen("warmup") await asyncio.sleep(6) await probe("settled") # sanity: True when quiet # scenario 1: pause on a quiet engine t0 = time.perf_counter() await engine.pause_generation(mode="abort") t1 = time.perf_counter() await probe("after_pause1_returned") print(f"S1 pause took {t1 - t0:.2f}s on an idle engine", flush=True) await engine.wait_for_requests_to_drain(60) await probe("after_drain1_returned") # scenario 2: second pause+drain right before sleep (the production recipe) t0 = time.perf_counter() await engine.pause_generation(mode="abort") t1 = time.perf_counter() await probe("after_pause2_returned") await engine.wait_for_requests_to_drain(60) await probe("after_drain2_returned") print(f"S2 second pause took {t1 - t0:.2f}s", flush=True) # scenario 3: drain called while the pause burst is mid-flight await engine.resume_generation() await gen("rearm") await asyncio.sleep(6) task = asyncio.create_task(engine.pause_generation(mode="abort")) await asyncio.sleep(0.8) await engine.wait_for_requests_to_drain(60) idle = await probe("drain_during_pause_burst") print(f"S3 drain returned while pause_done={task.done()}, idle={idle}", flush=True) await task engine.shutdown() asyncio.run(main()) ```
gpurepro.sh — container entrypoint ```bash #!/bin/bash # usage: gpurepro.sh instr|fixed set -x SITE=/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages if [ "$1" = "fixed" ]; then (cd "$SITE" && patch -p1 --forward) < /patch/fix.patch || exit 89 fi python3 /patch/gpupatch.py "$SITE" || exit 90 export REPRO_SLEEP_CYCLES=200000000 # ~110ms on H200 export VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=WARNING python3 /patch/repro_gpu.py ```
Output on `0.26.1rc1.dev942` (H200): | probe | baseline | this PR | |---|---|---| | device idle when engine settled | True | True | | device idle when `pause_generation()` returns | **False** | **True** | | `pause_generation()` wall time on an *idle* engine | 3.40s | 3.40s (burst kept; #52957 cuts it to 0.17s) | | device idle when drain returns | **False** | **True** | | second pause+drain before sleep | 3.40s, busy | 3.40s, idle | | drain mid-pause | "Engines are idle" while `pause_done=False`, device busy | pause already complete, device idle | ## Test Plan Three unit tests in `tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core.py` (no GPU): the pause-ordering contracts — fast path and deferred path run synchronize → cache reset → future resolution, and overlapping pause calls each complete behind their own barrier. Two adversarial DP tests for edges the pause path crosses that had no coverage: `mode="wait"` draining through the DP consensus path, and pausing a *sleeping* engine — whose ranks skip dummy batches yet must still reach consensus, with the barrier running against unmapped memory. Regression: `tests/v1/distributed/test_async_llm_dp.py -k "dp_pause or dp_sleep or prefill_schedule"` — includes the anti-#38009 staggered-race and barrier-deadlock guards and the #51481 late-request pair. ```bash python -m pytest tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core.py -k "pause_" -v python -m pytest tests/v1/distributed/test_async_llm_dp.py -k "dp_pause or dp_sleep or prefill_schedule" -v ``` ## Test Result `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` (`0.26.1rc1.dev942`), A/B on H200s, `before` = unpatched image: | suite | before | after | |---|---|---| | test_engine_core.py unit tests (new) | **3 failed** | **3 passed** | | test_async_llm_dp.py (14 cases incl. the 2 new adversarial) | 14 passed | 14 passed | | GPU probe repro | table above | table above | | offline `LLM` sleep/wake smoke, MPClient and in-proc | — | both pass | ## Essential Elements - Not a duplicate: no open PR gives pause a device barrier (#31741 adds a different, step-bounded pause endpoint and does not synchronize the device). Filed under #51476; #52957 is the independent cadence companion. - Control-plane only; no effect on model output, so no eval run is included. - AI assistance was used (the design was adversarially reviewed with a second model, which also surfaced the non-`torch.accelerator` backend hole fixed in the base implementation). The submitter has reviewed each changed line and the runs above.

signal.title: support rl feature : weight checker
signal.text: ## Purpose In the RL training loop: start_weight_update → update_weights* → finish_weight_update, we need to confirm that after the training side pushes/synchronizes the Actor weights to the rollout inference engine, the weights held by the engine are indeed consistent with what we intended to push. Before the training loop begins, check the correctness of the weight-update function to avoid off-policy training crashes. To confirm that this weight update actually landed and was not corrupted or partially written, a reproducible verification mechanism is needed. **weight_checker** is designed for exactly this: it computes a **SHA-256 checksum for each weight tensor of the model** and takes **snapshots (snapshot)** and **comparisons (compare)** before and after the update, so that you can verify ahead of time "whether the weights actually changed / whether they are complete." The four actions that weight_checker depends on: * **snapshot**: Compute a SHA-256 value of the current weights and store it as a baseline * **compare**: Recompute the current SHA-256 values Gang compare them with the snapshot, returning `match` + `mismatches` * **checksum**: Return the current per-tensor SHA-256 values without storing them (idempotent) * **reset**: Randomize the weights after a snapshot, to set up detection of whether a later weight update was correct RFC： #[52689](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52689) ## Test Plan A single parameterized test file drives the dev server for each TP setting and verifies: -snapshot returns a structured response with a positive tensor count, and repeated snapshots are consistent. -compare requires a prior snapshot (400 otherwise), matches when weights are unchanged, and still matches after a sleep/wake cycle and after a generate request. -checksum returns per-tensor 64-character SHA-256 digests, is stable across calls, and does not clobber an existing snapshot. -reset rewrite the model weight to check update is correct. -error handling rejects missing/unknown actions cleanly while /health stays up. -world size matches the configured tensor_parallel_size. | Test group | Functional points covered | Priority | | --- | --- | --- | | API| Snapshot creation and replacement; compare state handling; checksum stability and snapshot isolation; sleep/wake and generation consistency; invalid-action handling; server health; reset and weight-update verification | P0 | | TP | Checksum and comparison behavior with tensor parallelism enabled | P1 | | EP | Checksum coverage of locally owned expert weights with expert parallelism enabled | P1 | ## Test Result default test tp=1 and 2 and tp2ep test tp use signal.title: [Model] Enable LoRA support for tower and connector in GLM-ASR
signal.text: ## Purpose Part of #31479 (LoRA for the tower and connector of more multimodal models). Enable tower/connector LoRA for GLM-ASR (`GlmAsrForConditionalGeneration`). The audio tower (`GlmAsrEncoder`) and projector (`GlmAsrMultiModalProjector`) are already vLLM-native linear layers and `get_mm_mapping` already maps them, so this PR adds the token-count helpers that the LoRA mapping needs: - `get_num_mm_encoder_tokens` / `get_num_mm_connector_tokens`: every 30s chunk is padded to 3000 mel frames, which the conv stack downsamples to `audio_config.max_position_embeddings` (1500) tower rows; the projector runs on the 4x frame-merged output *before* the padded frames are trimmed, so it sees 375 rows per chunk (also the number of LM tokens a full chunk yields). Only the last chunk of an audio can yield fewer LM tokens, so `num_chunks = ceil(num_audio_tokens / 375)`. - `get_mm_lora_token_counts` override: derives the exact per-item counts from `mm_kwargs["input_features"]` (chunks x padded length). `num_mm_embeds` alone is not invertible when the tail chunk is nearly empty (e.g. a 30.02s audio yields 375 LM tokens but 2 chunks / 3000 tower rows). Before this change, starting GLM-ASR with `--enable-tower-connector-lora` fails at engine init (`TypeError: empty(): argument 'size' ... NoneType` from `get_punica_wrapper`, because the stub helper returns `None`). signal.title: [Rust Frontend] Add HY3 unified parser and local XGrammar structural-tag builder
signal.text: ## Purpose Add complete HY3 output parsing and XGrammar guided-decoding support to the Rust frontend. - Add a unified parser that applies one tokenizer-derived marker suffix to both reasoning and tool-call parsing. - Move HY3's model-specific structural-tag builder into vLLM and build its grammar from the same detected markers used by the parser. - Express the HY3 tool protocol with `xgrammar-structural-tag` primitives, including required/optional arguments and marker-bounded `any_text_excluding` values. - Expose added vocabulary from the Hugging Face and Fastokens backends, then validate the expected HY3 grammar markers during parser creation. - Add a real `tencent/Hy3` tokenizer/template roundtrip covering reasoning and tool-call history. - Accept vLLM-compatible `top_k` values from `generation_config.json`: `-1` and `0` disable top-k sampling, while positive values are preserved. Relationship to #48800: that PR adds a reasoning-only alias for unsuffixed delimiters. This PR covers the current public HY3 tokenizer and template end to end by sharing suffix discovery across reasoning, tool parsing, and structural-tag generation, then exercising combined tool-call and guided-decoding paths. AI assistance was used for implementation and validation. ## Design ### Unified parsing HY3 uses a tokenizer-specific suffix shared by every reasoning and tool-call marker. Detecting it requires tokenizer access, while the split tool-parser factory is constructed from tools alone. The unified factory owns both the tokenizer and tools, so `HyV3UnifiedParser` detects the suffix once and passes the same value into dedicated reasoning and tool constructors. The model-specific wrapper only owns suffix discovery and construction. Its runtime remains the shared `CombinedParser`: reasoning delegates to `DelimitedReasoningParser`, and tool calls delegate to the existing winnow-based HY3 tool parser. This keeps the state machines reusable and the HY3-specific layer small. ### vLLM-owned structural-tag builder The HY3 parser now owns a local `HyV3StructuralTagBuilder` and directly constructs the model-specific protocol grammar. `xgrammar-structural-tag` remains the generic format DSL, and Python EngineCore remains responsible for compiling the serialized structural tag with XGrammar and applying its token masks. The builder shares the parser's `Arc<HyV3ToolMarkers>`, so tokenizer-detected suffixes such as `:opensource` are used consistently in parsing and generation constraints. It lowers the protocol with `ConstString`, `Sequence`, `Star`, `Or`, `Tag`, `TagsWithSeparator`, and `TriggeredTags`: - `required`, named, and `auto` tool choices preserve their existing outer grammar shapes. - Required argument keys are emitted in schema declaration order. - Optional keys are represented as repeatable declared-key alternatives. - Argument values use `any_text_excluding` over every detected HY3 structural marker, preventing a value from consuming its closing marker, another argument, or an outer tool boundary. This keeps HY3 dialect policy in vLLM beside its parser. Future HY protocol revisions can evolve in vLLM while the generic structural-tag crate stays protocol-agnostic. ## Test Plan ```bash cd rust cargo fmt --all --check cargo nextest run -p vllm-parser -p vllm-tokenizer -p vllm-text cargo nextest run -p vllm-chat hy_v3 cargo nextest run -p vllm-chat structural_tag cargo clippy -p vllm-parser -p vllm-tokenizer -p vllm-text -p vllm-chat --all-targets -- -D warnings cargo build --release -p vllm-cmd --bin vllm-rs ``` Compile emitted HY3 structural tags with XGrammar and verify matcher acceptance for a valid call plus rejection for an undeclared following argument. Serve `tencent/Hy3-FP8` through the Rust frontend with a two-node TP8 engine and exercise: - Direct answers and tool calls with reasoning disabled/enabled, including streaming tool calls. - Strict `tool_choice=required` requests with structural tags, covering immediate guided decoding and reasoning-gated guided decoding. ## Test Result - Parser, tokenizer, and text crates: 559 passed, 1 skipped. - Current parser regression suite: 422 passed. - Focused HY3 parser/structural-tag suite: 24 passed. - Chat structural-tag suite: 10 passed. - Real-tokenizer HY3 roundtrip: 1 passed. - XGrammar compile/matcher check: valid HY3 call accepted; undeclared following argument rejected. - Formatting, release build, and clippy: passed. - Baseline real-model serving smoke: 5/5 passed. - Structural-tag guided-decoding smoke: 2/2 passed. | Case | Result | Finish reason | | --- | --- | --- | | Direct, `no_think` | Passed | `stop` | | Direct, `high` reasoning | Passed | `stop` | | Tool call, `no_think` | Passed | `tool_calls` | | Tool call, `high` reasoning | Passed | `tool_calls` | | Streaming tool call, `high` reasoning | Passed | `tool_calls` | | Guided strict/required tool call, `no_think` | Passed | `tool_calls` | | Guided strict/required streaming tool call, `high` reasoning | Passed | `tool_calls` | The guided smoke used Hy3-FP8 on a two-node TP8 engine with `--reasoning-parser hy_v3`. The non-streaming request produced exactly one `get_weather({"city":"Shanghai"})` call. The streaming request emitted reasoning first, then the same complete tool call, and terminated with `[DONE]`. Both responses were marker-free, and the EngineCore logs contained zero grammar-compilation or FSM-advance errors.

signal.title: Fix MNNVL Lamport mailbox publication and cleanup
signal.text: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Purpose Fix silent output corruption in vLLM's MNNVL Lamport all-gather and reduce-scatter. CUDA multicast addresses may only be written with `multimem.*`, so mailbox payloads use a relaxed, system-scope multicast store ([PTX ISA](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/parallel-thread-execution/#data-movement-and-conversion-instructions-multimem-ld-reduce-multimem-st-multimem-red)). The payload words are also the readiness signal: volatile readers reject stale or partially visible values containing the Lamport sentinel and retry, so release/acquire ordering and `fence.proxy.alias` are unnecessary. Also fix triple-buffer cleanup. The current `(epoch + 1) % 3` rule can erase epoch N+1 after a faster peer publishes it while another rank is still finishing epoch N; cleaning `(epoch + 2) % 3` targets the previously consumed stage instead. DeepSeek-V4 with MegaMoE, expert parallelism, and TP8 across two four-GPU GB300 hosts reaches these kernels through sequence-parallel all-gather and reduce-scatter. Current K3 and DeepSeek-V4 with expert parallelism disabled do not enter this path. Open-PR searches for MNNVL Lamport, multicast publication, and mailbox-stage cleanup found no duplicate fix. ## Test Plan Run the new test in the two-GPU B200 Distributed job, which provides the required CUDA multicast mapping: ```bash pytest -v -s \ tests/distributed/test_custom_all_gather_reduce_scatter.py ``` The test asserts a real CUDA multicast mapping and constructs a reachable one-epoch skew using the existing per-rank epoch metadata and mailbox stages. It invokes the shipping all-gather and reduce-scatter kernels, verifies the fast rank's N+1 publication arrived, then asserts that the slow rank's epoch-N cleanup preserves it. ## Test Result - Two-GPU GB300 production-kernel test: old `+1` cleanup erased both all-gather and reduce-scatter N+1 publications in 20/20 cycles; fixed `+2` retained both in 20/20. The final pytest covers all three stage rotations, fails on old code, and passes on fixed code. - Two-node GB300 TP8 DeepSeek-V4 with expert parallelism, MegaMoE, CUDA graphs, CUMEM/MNNVL, and custom collectives: sky-color 10/10 and bat-and-ball 10/10 before load, 128/128 correct concurrent requests, then both probes 10/10 again. - CUDA 13.2 codegen is identical on SM100 and SM103: plain CUDA C++ emits weak `STG.E.128`, while `multimem.st.relaxed.sys` emits `STG.E.128.STRONG.SYS`. Release plus proxy-fence added three memory barriers and was therefore removed. - A final two-host, eight-rank stress completed 2,000 epochs with zero mismatches for both weak and multicast stores on current GB300 hardware. The multicast spelling is retained because ordinary access to a multicast mapping remains undefined by PTX; the deterministic red/green regression is the independently reproducible stage-lifecycle bug. AI assistance was used during investigation and implementation; the human submitter reviewed the change and owns the design and validation. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose and root cause are described. - [x] The test plan provides the exact real-GPU test command. - [x] The test results include deterministic regression and end-to-end validation. - [x] Documentation impact was considered; the code and test describe this kernel-only change. </details> **BEFORE SUBMITTING, PLEASE READ <https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/contributing>** (anything written below this line will be removed by GitHub Actions)

signal.title: [XPU][INC] Add int4 w4a8 (dynamic int8 activation) backend for INC linear layers
signal.text: INC int4 layers on XPU always dispatch to ARK when it imports, with oneDNN `int4_gemm_w4a16` only as a fallback. `int4_gemm_w4a8` was never wired in at all. This PR adds `INCXPUW4A8LinearMethod` (int4 weights + dynamic per-token int8 activations, reusing the w4a16 weight layout unchanged, falling back to w4a16 below 512 tokens) and a `VLLM_XPU_INC_WNA16_BACKEND` selector: `auto | ark | w4a16 | w4a8`. Purely additive: one new test file, no existing test modified. `auto` leaves current behaviour unchanged. ## Purpose int8 activations avoid dequantizing weights to the activation dtype, which is a win for compute-bound shapes like diffusion (FLUX at 1024×1024 is M=4608). Per-layer GEMM: 1.32× at M=4608, 1.13× at M=512, 0.84× at M=128 — hence the 512-token fallback. Kept opt-in because the best kernel is device-dependent: ARK may win on other XPUs. Note that on B70 ARK is *not* the fastest option for either workload below — both oneDNN paths beat it — which is the motivation for making it selectable. Also validates that partitioned in/out dims are multiples of 8. `XPUW4A8IntLinearKernel.can_implement()` requires this, but that check is unreachable from the INC path: INC builds its own linear method and never goes through `MPLinearKernel` selection, and the shapes only exist once `create_weights()` runs, well after backend selection. Without the check an unaligned dim is not rejected but silently truncated — the int4 packing divides both dims by 8, so `out=890` packs 111 int32s covering only 888 columns and loses 2. Tensor parallelism shards these dims, so an aligned model dimension can still yield an unaligned partition. ## Test Plan New `tests/quantization/test_inc_xpu_w4a8.py` — 32 tests. The 29 mocked ones run anywhere; the 3 real-model ones self-skip unless an XPU with `int4_gemm_w4a8` is present. ```bash pytest tests/quantization/test_inc_xpu_w4a8.py -v ``` - **backend selection** — `auto` still prefers ARK, explicit values override it, invalid/unsupported combos raise instead of falling back silently - **weight processing** — fp16 scales created, bf16 scales preserved, qweight bit-identical (no repacking) - **apply_weights** — batch gate, full 9-arg kernel convention, fp16 scales for both activation dtypes, bias, 3D shapes - **partition alignment** — unaligned input / output / sum-of-shards rejected, aligned non-power-of-two accepted, w4a16 unaffected - **end to end** — real int4 auto-round checkpoint on XPU, both GPTQ- and AWQ-packed repack branches Plus `test_auto_round.py` for regressions and ruff. Mutation-tested: flipping the env var to `w4a16` makes `test_e2e_selects_w4a8_for_every_linear` fail with `no linear layer used the w4a8 method`, so it is not vacuously green. ## Test Result **E2E FLUX.1-dev, 1024×1024, 28 steps, B70, TP=2** — the load-bearing numbers: | Model | Kernel | Time | | --- | --- | ---: | | `black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-dev` | bf16 dense | 19.46 s | | `vllm-project-org/FLUX.1-dev-AutoRound-w4a16` | ARK (current default) | 23.63 s | | `vllm-project-org/FLUX.1-dev-AutoRound-w4a16` | oneDNN w4a16 | 21.87 s | | `vllm-project-org/FLUX.1-dev-AutoRound-w4a16` | oneDNN w4a8 | **16.99 s** | 1.39× over the current ARK default, and the only quantized config that beats bf16 dense rather than losing to it. 16.99 s reproduced 4×. Numerics: cosine 0.99996 vs w4a16 with bf16 activations. **Text generation LLM smoke-test OPEA/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-int4-sym-inc** Intel Arc Pro B70, `OPEA/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-int4-sym-inc`, 32 prompts × ~710 prompt tokens + 1024 generated each, `enforce_eager`, greedy, median of 3 after warmup: | `VLLM_XPU_INC_WNA16_BACKEND` | bound kernel | wall (median) | wall (min–max) | gen tok/s | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | unset (`auto`) | ARK | 12.675 s | 12.598–12.903 s | 2,585 | | `w4a8` | w4a8 | **8.354 s** | 8.272–8.647 s | **3,922** | 1.52× over the current ARK default. 32 prompts, 22,742 prompt tokens, 32,768 generated tokens. Outputs identical between backends. Kernel binding confirmed separately — `auto` → 96 ARK, `w4a8` → 96 w4a8, `w4a16` → 96 w4a16 — so the delta is a real kernel switch, not a config no-op. ## Checklist - [x] Purpose of the PR - [x] Test plan with test command - [x] Test results (before/after, e2e) - [ ] Documentation update — N/A: `docs/configuration/env_vars.md` auto-includes from `envs.py`, and no other `VLLM_XPU_*` var is documented separately, so the `envs.py` comment is the documentation

signal.title: [Bugfix][Structured Output][Spec Decode] Validate accepted blocks before commit
signal.text: ## Purpose Fixes #43338. Structured-output requests using speculative decoding must satisfy this commit invariant: > Request history and grammar state advance through the same longest > grammar-valid token prefix. Any rejected suffix remains schedulable for > resampling. At `main@4666a8ba9ed5d271bf751cf1384cab2d2dcc0cfa`, the scheduler appends the verifier's accepted token block to request history before `StructuredOutputGrammar.accept_tokens()` checks the block. Prospective grammar masks reduce the chance of an invalid token, but they cannot establish the commit invariant when one accepted block crosses either of these state transitions: 1. deferred grammar activation at the end of model reasoning; 2. grammar termination before the final accepted token in the block. The invalid suffix is therefore already visible in request state when `accept_tokens()` rejects it. Depending on the serving path, that produces an invalid structured response or terminates the request with `FINISHED_ERROR`. This PR validates accepted multi-token structured-output blocks before `Scheduler._update_request_with_output()` mutates request history. It uses the non-advancing `StructuredOutputGrammar.validate_tokens()` interface, commits only the valid prefix, and leaves the existing post-commit path as the sole grammar-state advancement operation. ### Resulting behavior - Reasoning content through a deferred end marker remains unconstrained. - Tokens after the marker must form a valid grammar prefix. - Blocks sampled after reasoning has ended are validated in full, including suffixes that follow grammar termination. - Rejected suffix tokens decrement `num_computed_tokens` and asynchronous output placeholders so they can be sampled again. - Speculative metrics count only committed draft tokens. Rejecting only the target-sampled tail does not reduce the accepted-draft count. - Unstructured requests, stale outputs, non-speculative output, and single-token output blocks retain their existing fast paths. Reasoning-boundary detection exposes prior request tokens through a read-only concatenated `Sequence`; it does not copy the committed history. A block that does not contain a boundary requires one parser call. A block that contains a boundary is scanned through cumulative delta prefixes, which supports single-token markers, multi-token markers, and markers split across scheduler steps. Each detection call uses an isolated copy of the request-scoped parser, so a stateful parser cannot consume its transition before the standard post-commit path observes it. ## Provenance and related work The state boundary is produced by the composition of two supported features, not by a single isolated regression: - #14702, merge commit `34120f5acd693924cc783dfaa33733afbe9ae8b0`, enabled structured output with speculative decoding and introduced per-position grammar-mask simulation. - #16577, merge commit `2fc9075b82e05007f460992b3f9d42d2746c41cb`, deferred structured-output grammar activation while a request is reasoning. Several changes cover narrower parts of the lifecycle: - #36138, head commit `94f4dc2e98d63dc1a3ff7cca2b35a9235df667e1`, detects reasoning activation inside a speculative window but does not establish pre-commit validation. - #44297, merge commit `e7c9df944969c251bdceed7b9d7bbcc7fec3639b`, constrains scheduled rows after a reasoning boundary, including the bonus row. It operates prospectively on scheduled draft candidates, not on the authoritative verifier result. - #44993, merge commit `0416dab275d51327b331a1c6baaec754a68d7764`, advances grammar state across an accepted reasoning boundary. The accepted block is still appended before grammar acceptance. - #45560, merge commit `dc818c198d3ff50a16f38eba567da006478239c8`, constrains GPT-OSS through a Harmony structural-tag grammar active from token zero. It is specific to the GPT-OSS path and does not cover deferred reasoning parsers or grammar termination for other models. - #43424, commit `4e96809853442f1cf9dacf83f166fc32482b6632`, supplies the pre-commit design used for the reasoning-boundary case. This PR credits its author and extends the contract to every accepted structured speculative block, avoids copying committed history, isolates stateful reasoning probes, updates speculative metrics, and covers grammar termination. A boundary-only build still fails the qualified runtime test. - #51870, commit `c3573d92f69cda2d42d3e74f80f00d0e932e5010`, replaces a mutating operation during draft-window mask simulation. It intentionally does not alter accepted output or scheduler accounting. - #48200, commit `21265a9a4841812b5088cb062fc5356abcb979d9`, refactors structured-output management. Its scheduler still appends `new_token_ids` before accepting them into the grammar, so the commit invariant remains separate from that refactor. The scope difference from #43424 is also recorded in #43338: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/43338#issuecomment-5302532715 ## Compatibility and limitations - The patch changes Python scheduler and grammar-management code only. It does not change model kernels, sampling distributions, API schemas, or compiled components. - XGrammar and Guidance have direct backend tests. Outlines and LM Format Enforcer implement the same non-advancing, longest-prefix `validate_tokens()` interface but do not have model-serving qualification in this PR. - Runtime qualification uses XGrammar 0.2.5 with DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 and DSpark K5. Other speculative methods exercise the same scheduler interface, but their model-serving behavior was not separately benchmarked. - The additional work is bounded by the accepted speculative block length. The reasoning-only path performs one parser check, and request history is not copied by the manager. - A direct Step3.5 parser test verifies that pre-commit boundary detection does not consume the parser's pending-transition state. ## Test Plan ```bash uvx --from pre-commit pre-commit run --files \ vllm/v1/structured_output/__init__.py \ vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py \ tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_structured_output.py \ tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \ tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py \ tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_structured_output.py \ tests/v1/structured_output/test_reasoning_structured_output.py ``` The tests cover: - XGrammar and Guidance rejection at a reasoning boundary; - rejection after grammar completion; - multi-token markers within a block and across committed/new token storage; - constant-history sequence access and one-check reasoning-only behavior; - preservation of request-local state in a Step3.5 reasoning parser; - synchronous and asynchronous rollback for bonus-only, partial-draft, and complete-block rejection; - speculative acceptance totals and per-position metrics; - scheduler commit, emitted output, and grammar advancement through one identical filtered prefix; - bypass behavior for unstructured requests. ## Test Result ### Source qualification - Repository pre-commit hooks: passed, including Ruff, formatting, typos, mypy, SPDX, forbidden imports, and configuration checks. - Four relevant pytest modules: `211 passed` in 170.56 seconds. - `git diff --check`: passed. Negative control at `main@ac2ae8798c7ef59c1924d5c0447a4279fa645770`: - four XGrammar/Guidance boundary and termination tests fail because accepted blocks have no pre-commit validation; - the scheduler behavior test commits `[10, 11, 12]` instead of the valid prefix `[10, 11]`. The same five discriminator cases pass with commit `fa0777ff775a870a5d6a6ff187f769e50b38c4ad`. ### Model-serving qualification Runtime conditions: ```text model: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 topology: TP2 / DCP1 target backend: B12X W4A8 speculative decoding: fixed probabilistic DSpark K5 structured-output backend: XGrammar 0.2.5 scheduler: asynchronous CUDA graph row cap: 48 concurrency: 8 ``` The runtime branch contains #44297 and #44993. The accepted-block validation is the source change in local-inference-lab/vllm#320. - Unfiltered source fails the deterministic growing strict-tool test by round 11. - A boundary-only filter fails at round 29 when a speculative suffix follows grammar termination. - Complete-block validation finishes 32 rounds and 256 HTTP requests at up to 225,634 prompt tokens per request. Of those responses, 255 contain one schema-valid tool call. One response reaches its configured 768-token output limit while still reasoning and reproduces that output-limit result on retry. - The committed source composition passes 24/24 deterministic strict-tool requests: eight buffered or streaming requests at C1 and 16 requests at C8. - An independently supplied 282,817-byte request payload returns one valid JSON tool call in each of eight concurrent replays. - Ordinary no-tool C1 decode measures 194.3 tok/s. Same-host controls with the same launch profile measure 194.02-194.81 tok/s, so no throughput regression is measurable at the precision of those runs. Reproducible image: ```text tag: voipmonitor/vllm:infernal-invocation-vllm91e2adf-b12xec2f97d-fi1ac6942-cu133-torch213-20260815-r14 digest: sha256:9fe1d1b0e8370df578f92c6431af41a9fc36076ccbebac18c77a8ae99a3454e3 ``` Detailed serving evidence: - https://github.com/local-inference-lab/vllm/pull/320 - https://github.com/local-inference-lab/rtx6kpro/blob/master/models/ds4dspark-infernal-invocation-r14.md - https://github.com/local-inference-lab/rtx6kpro/issues/67 ## AI assistance disclosure OpenAI Codex assisted with source analysis, implementation, tests, negative controls, and PR drafting. The submitted patch is supported by the source and model-serving qualification documented above. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] Purpose and affected invariant are specified. - [x] Test commands and results are included. - [x] Model-serving evaluation is included because output correctness changes. - [x] Related and partially overlapping PRs are distinguished. - [x] No user documentation change is required; the patch preserves the public API and corrects an internal commit invariant. </details>

signal.title: [Kimi-K3] Extend GEMM-RS to GEMM-AR
signal.text: ## Purpose Replaces #52687 Extends GEMM-RS, introduced by #52079, to GEMM-AR by replacing unicast store with `multimem.st`. Compared to #52687, this is better in the following way: - Any value of M is supported -> no padding/input copy is required - Flag signalling/synchronization is fully done inside the kernel -> no flag reset + entry barrier is needed However, there is still a limitation. - Currently `multimem.st` places the output in an internal multicast workspace, instead of a freshly allocated buffer, hence it is not safe to invoke this GEMM-AR kernel again without ensuring the consumer has finished using the output buffer. - This output clone can be eliminated by fusing it with the GEMM-AR kernel (e.g. extra output clone warp, or extra work for the comm warp) -> left for future work ## Microbenchmarks GB300 TP8, `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_kimi_k3_gemm_rs_ar.py`. Baseline is `torch.mm` + NCCL LDMC all-reduce M | Baseline AR | GEMM-AR | Speedup -- | -- | -- | -- 16 | 37.54 µs | 45.87 µs | 0.82× 32 | 43.26 µs | 46.56 µs | 0.93× 48 | 50.58 µs | 48.27 µs | 1.05× 64 | 44.42 µs | 47.92 µs | 0.93× 80 | 42.13 µs | 41.79 µs | 1.01× 96 | 44.18 µs | 40.80 µs | 1.08× 112 | 48.77 µs | 48.08 µs | 1.01× 128 | 50.35 µs | 48.91 µs | 1.03× 256 | 48.35 µs | 44.50 µs | 1.09× 512 | 63.74 µs | 61.18 µs | 1.04× 1,024 | 87.36 µs | 79.76 µs | 1.10× 2,048 | 126.80 µs | 112.80 µs | 1.12× 4,096 | 211.14 µs | 180.08 µs | 1.17× 8,192 | 384.66 µs | 324.22 µs | 1.19× 16,384 | 729.10 µs | 615.18 µs | 1.19× 32,768 | 1,411.73 µs | 1,165.52 µs | 1.21× Currently the dispatch is only enabled for M>=128, which has a safe margin. ## E2E perf Concurrency | Output throughput | Mean TTFT | Mean TPOT -- | -- | -- | -- 1 | 109.15 → 109.79 tok/s (+0.58%) | 363.24 → 350.55 ms (-3.50%) | 8.815 → 8.775 ms (-0.46%) 4 | 314.45 → 316.11 tok/s (+0.53%) | 845.96 → 816.42 ms (-3.49%) | 11.902 → 11.864 ms (-0.32%) 8 | 487.06 → 492.98 tok/s (+1.22%) | 1266.42 → 1193.67 ms (-5.74%) | 15.195 → 15.067 ms (-0.84%) 16 | 723.60 → 724.36 tok/s (+0.11%) | 2003.34 → 1897.72 ms (-5.27%) | 20.163 → 20.242 ms (+0.40%) 32 | 975.71 → 982.31 tok/s (+0.68%) | 2789.03 → 2709.69 ms (-2.84%) | 30.072 → 29.930 ms (-0.47%) ## Test Plan Updated unit test `tests/kernels/test_kimi_k3_gemm_rs_ar.py` E2E accuracy Benchmark | Result | Errors -- | -- | -- GSM8K, 5-shot | 96.21% exact match | 0 / 1319 OCRBench | 889 / 1000 (88.90%) | 0 / 1000 ## Test Result --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - signal.title: [ROCm][CI] Make image selection content-addressed
signal.text: <!-- Title: [ROCm][CI] Make image selection content-addressed Branch: akaratza_rocm_content_addressed_promotion Base: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48646 Companion ci-infra branch: akaratza_rocm_image_promotion_infra --> ROCm image builds can finish out of order. The base and `ci_base` jobs currently write the mutable `:base` and `:ci_base` tags themselves, so an older post-merge build can overwrite a newer result. Base refresh is also based on a Git diff, which can rebuild an image that is already available in Docker Hub. This changes selection to use the actual image inputs. The base key includes the Dockerfile, effective build arguments, metadata version, and resolved parent digest. `ci_base` is keyed the same way and includes the selected base digest. An exact registry hit skips the build, a confirmed miss rebuilds, and registry or metadata errors are retried and then fail instead of being treated as misses. PR images and caches remain isolated from trusted main. PRs may read a validated main image and reuse their own images, while main never consumes PR-scoped output. The selected base and `ci_base` are passed between jobs by digest. The long builds stop writing stable tags. The base build publishes an input-addressed tag, and `ci_base` publishes content-, commit-, and build-scoped tags. AMD jobs use `ci_base-build-$BUILDKITE_BUILD_ID`, so overlapping evaluations do not share a mutable handoff. A serialized promotion job becomes the only writer of `:base` and `:ci_base` in this flow. Before updating either tag it requires a successful commit-image smoke test, fetches main again, verifies that the build is still the latest main commit, rechecks the parent digest, and validates both candidates and their relationship. It no-ops when the stable tags are already current and restores previous values after an ordinary partial failure. Artifact-only mode is still optional. It is used only outside trusted main when `ROCM_CI_ARTIFACT_ONLY=1` and both build-required values are explicitly `0`. Missing metadata falls back to a full image. Main always builds and smoke-tests the commit image. Promotion is smoke-gated; it does not wait for the complete AMD test suite.
