signal.title: [Bug]: Whisper transcription silently drops audio when the decoder stops early inside a chunk
signal.text: ### Your current environment - vLLM `v0.27.1` (official image `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.27.1-cu129-ubuntu2404`, plus `vllm[audio]`) - Model: `openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo` - Endpoint: `POST /v1/audio/transcriptions`, `response_format=verbose_json` - Also verified by reading `main` — the code path is unchanged there. ### 🐛 Describe the bug **Audio is silently dropped from the transcript when the decoder emits end-of-transcript before the chunk it was given is exhausted.** Each audio chunk is decoded exactly once, and whatever the model did not read is transcribed by nobody. The response is `HTTP 200`, `duration` covers the whole file, and `text` reads like a finished sentence — there is no error, no warning and no field that says anything is missing. The only trace is arithmetic: the last segment's `end` against the length of the audio. This is not the chunking. **It reproduces on a file shorter than 30 s, where no splitting happens at all.** #### Measurements A 29.42 s recording of continuous speech (single chunk, no splitting): ``` duration : 29.42 segments : 2, last one ends at 21.56 => 7.9 s of speech absent from `text` ``` Deterministic — three identical runs. The missing tail is real speech; re-submitting just that region returns it verbatim. A 58.85 s recording (two chunks) loses the tail of **each** window: | window | decoded | lost | |---|---|---| | 0–30 s | 0 → 21.54 | 21.54 → 30.00 | | 30–60 s | 30.00 → 51.48 | 51.48 → 58.85 | **A third of the speech**, silently. Ruled out by measurement, not by reasoning: a token limit (`max_completion_tokens=2000` — identical output), the container (remux, and 16 kHz WAV — identical output), and an abrupt cut mid-word (padding the tail with silence — identical output). Cutting the *same* file to 29.02 s makes it transcribe completely, so the outcome depends on the content of the window, which is consistent with Whisper's known early-EOT behaviour. #### Where it comes from `vllm/entrypoints/speech_to_text/base/serving.py` submits one generation per chunk and merges the outputs. Whisper's own timestamp tokens say how far the decoder got inside a chunk, and nothing compares that to the chunk's length. The reference long-form algorithm advances its cursor to the END OF THE LAST SEGMENT for exactly this reason; here the cursor moves by the whole chunk. #### Reproduction 1. Take any recording with speech running to the very end (≈30 s is enough). 2. `POST /v1/audio/transcriptions` with `response_format=verbose_json`. 3. Compare `segments[-1].end` with `duration`. A gap of seconds is dropped speech. It reproduces more readily on conversational speech than on clean read-aloud audio. #### Why it is worth fixing in the server Every consumer has to discover this independently, and the only way to notice is to compute segment coverage — which a client that asked for `response_format=json` cannot even do, because that format carries no segments. We hit it in production as "the transcript under this video stops mid-sentence", from a user, not from a monitor. A patch is ready and is being opened as a PR referencing this issue: after the merge it compares each chunk's decoded coverage against its length and re-submits the abandoned region as its own request. On the recordings above it returns 176 → 246 and 353 → 516 characters, with the coverage gap dropping to ~0.6 s (trailing silence). One thing that fix must not do, and which cost us a review round: an abandoned region is usually **silence**, and Whisper does not stay quiet over silence. Measured here — 13.8 s of near-silence came back as `" Let's go."` with `avg_logprob -0.46`. A blocklist of known phantom phrases cannot be the defence, since that is an ordinary sentence; speech density (words per second) separates them cleanly (2.3 w/s for speech vs 0.15–0.22 for the phantoms). ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] I searched the existing issues and did not find this one reported.

signal.title: [Misc][Spec Decode] Detect DeepSeek-V4 DSpark checkpoints from config
signal.text: ## Purpose To close https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52111. `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` and `DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813` do not have MTP heads — their `mtp.*` tensors are DSpark drafters. vLLM routes them to `DeepSeekV4MTPModel` anyway and dies deep in the weight loader: ``` KeyError: 'model.layers.43.mtp_block.main_norm.weight' # Flash-0731 KeyError: 'model.layers.61.mtp_block.main_norm.weight' # Pro-0813 ``` This PR resolves the drafter from `config.json` instead of the repo name, and turns `method="mtp"` on a DSpark checkpoint into an actionable startup error. It is platform-independent: reproduced on MI325X, and on stock `vllm/vllm-openai` v0.23.0 and v0.27.1 on H100. ## Test Plan ```bash pytest tests/config/test_deepseek_v4_dspark_config.py pytest tests/config/ tests/transformers_utils/test_dspark_mla_config.py ruff check vllm/config/speculative.py tests/config/test_deepseek_v4_dspark_config.py ``` Routing is decided from `config.json` alone, so the decision is asserted end to end through a real `ModelConfig` + `SpeculativeConfig` over a synthetic checkpoint directory holding nothing but a `config.json`. Covered: explicit `mtp` rejected on the self-speculation path for both DSpark checkpoint shapes and, for Flash-0731, on the named-draft-model path; plain `DeepSeek-V4-Flash` still resolving to `DeepSeekV4MTPModel`; an omitted method auto-detecting `dspark`; and the pre-existing block-size minimum. The predicate and the variant mapping are pinned separately as unit tests. ## Test Result ``` tests/config/test_deepseek_v4_dspark_config.py 21 passed tests/config/ + tests/transformers_utils/test_dspark_mla_config.py 156 passed, 5 failed ruff check All checks passed! ``` TODO: 5 failures ## Hardware validation **Hardware validation from the contributors in the thread below:** - **8×MI325X (gfx942, ROCm 7.14)** — @zzw09773 reproduced the `KeyError` on both Flash-0731 (layer 43) and Pro-0813 (layer 61); with this change `method="mtp"` fails at config validation instead, and the suggested `method="dspark"`, `num_speculative_tokens=5` serves Pro-0813 at 50 tok/s prose / 91 tok/s code single-stream, 2.1×/3.8× over no spec decode. Pro-0813's differing `dspark_target_layer_ids` is why detection keys on presence, not contents. - **8×H100 SXM (SM90)** — @kfastino reproduced it on stock `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.27.1` (and v0.23.0) at DP4 + EP, fp8 KV cache, where config validation accepts `method="mtp"` and every DP engine core then dies on the same `KeyError`. The patch applies to v0.27.1 in 3 hunks with zero rejects and aborts in ~15 s, before any engine process spawns. - **4×H200 (SM90)** — @kfastino, TP4 + EP on v0.26.0, `method="dspark"` at k=5 and k=7: 0.89–0.93 acceptance, 2–3× speedup over the base model. This is the path the new error message points users at, on the drafter this PR routes to. No model-eval results from me: this is config validation only. It converts a crash into a startup error and does not alter any decoding path, nor the weights loaded on paths that already worked. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signal.title: [Bugfix][MiniMax-M3] Keep FP8 query allocation stable across CUDA graph replay
signal.text: ## Purpose MiniMax-M3 allocates its FP8 query buffer outside an eager CUDA-graph break, but the current allocation condition depends on request metadata that is re-evaluated inside the eager attention segment. A graph captured without a CUTLASS MSA plan can later replay with a valid plan, causing the eager CUTLASS path to receive `query_fp8=None` and fail at `assert query_fp8 is not None`. Allocate `query_fp8` whenever the configured implementation supports CUTLASS decode, which is static across capture and replay. Keep the per-request CUTLASS-versus-Triton decision inside the eager segment. CUTLASS-capable configurations may therefore produce the FP8 query for request shapes that fall back to Triton; this keeps the graph output stable without changing dynamic backend selection. This does not duplicate an existing contribution. Before opening this PR, open vLLM issues and PRs were searched for `query_fp8 MiniMax`, `use_cutlass_decode MiniMax`, and the CUDA-graph replay failure; no matching fix was found. The search was repeated while rebasing onto current `main`, and no overlapping open PR was found. This is an AI-assisted contribution. OpenAI Codex provided non-trivial assistance with the implementation, test, and rebase. The human submitter reviewed the changed lines and validation evidence before marking the PR ready. ## Test Plan - Exercise the actual MiniMax FP8 query allocation under a real `BreakableCUDAGraphCapture` on SM100. - Capture with CUTLASS enabled but no per-request CUTLASS plan. - Add the plan before replay, then verify repeated eager replays receive a non-null FP8 query at one stable CUDA address. - Run the existing MiniMax-M3 CUTLASS sparse-decode test file on SM100: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3_msa_cutlass_sparse_decode.py`. - Run pre-commit and mypy on the changed files. ## Test Result Static validation passed again after rebasing onto current `main`: - Full pre-commit hook set on both changed files. - Python 3.10 and Python 3.12 mypy hooks on both changed files. - Python bytecode compilation and `git diff --check`. The new CUDA regression was not rerun on the non-CUDA host because it requires SM100. Separate deterministic SM100 validation of the same transition used real `torch.cuda.CUDAGraph` and `BreakableCUDAGraphCapture`: - The parent behavior reproduced `assert query_fp8 is not None` when capture used the Triton fallback and replay became CUTLASS-eligible. - The patched behavior completed 100 replays. - All 101 capture/replay pointer observations were non-null and used one stable CUDA address. - The focused deterministic harness passed all 5 checks. Model/serving evaluation: a full MiniMax-M3 concurrency-512 A/B serving run completed successfully for both control and patched configurations. Aggregate token throughput changed by -0.34%, indicating no material performance regression in that comparison. A second independent concurrency-512 control/patched pair also completed end to end; neither arm reproduced the intermittent assertion in that pair.

signal.title: buffer size insuffient Dspark sd for FlashInfer MNNVL allreduce
signal.text: fixes [#50877](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/50877) ## Purpose FlashInferAllReduce.should_use_fi_ar gates on: self.max_num_tokens = max_workspace_size // (hidden_dim * element_size) max_workspace_size is the size of the whole MNNVL allocation (2 MB for TP8). But the MNNVL backend is Lamport-based and rotates through NUM_LAMPORT_BUFFERS=3 buffers, so only ~1/3 of the budget backs any single all-reduce: budget 2,097,152 bytes → gate says 146 tokens per-buffer 698,368 bytes → real capacity is 48 tokens Any tensor between 49–146 tokens passes the gate and then aborts inside the kernel. The drafter produces B × (1 + num_speculative_tokens) tokens per step — e.g. 14 requests × 4 = 56 tokens — landing exactly in this window. Without a drafter, decode batches produce B tokens and stay below 48. The same defect exists in fused_allreduce_gemma_rms_norm._can_use_flashinfer, which its docstring notes "mirrors FlashInferAllReduce". ## Fix After the existing budget bound (kept as a cheap pre-filter), call the workspace's own is_buffer_size_sufficient(tp_size, num_tokens, hidden_dim, dtype) method rather than reimplementing the Lamport arithmetic. This is on the abstract base class (flashinfer-python==0.6.15.post1, the pinned version), correct for both mnnvl and trtllm, and version-proof. ## What this does NOT fix AllReduceFusionPass has the same too-permissive bound but self.max_token_num there also drives the workspace allocation request — fixing it requires separating those two concerns and verifying the one-shot/two-shot split, which needs GB200 hardware. Leaving that for a follow-up. ## Workaround (no code change needed) VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER=0 Disables the eager FlashInferAllReduce path; the compiled fusion pass is unaffected. ## Test Plan I have added test file and you can see output below, every assertion in the capacity-accounting logic changed ran and succeeded. pytest tests/compile/passes/distributed/test_fusion_all_reduce.py -v , already existing test. On GB200 python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model <deepseek-v4> --speculative-config '{"model": "<dspark-draft>"}' --tensor-parallel-size 8 if reporter can test on GB200 that would be perfect. ## Test Result Cannot test as I do not have GB200, if @ilmarkov can test it, that would be best. ## AI assistance This fix was developed with Claude (claude-opus-4-6) assistance. I have reviewed every changed line and understand the root cause and the design. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details> **BEFORE SUBMITTING, PLEASE READ <https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/contributing>** (anything written below this line will be removed by GitHub Actions)

signal.title: fix(anthropic): preserve requested model alias in messages response
signal.text: Co-authored-by: @lazypool ## Purpose Fixes #51266. ### Problem When vLLM is launched with multiple model aliases (--served-model-name alias-a alias-b), the requests to the Anthropic Messages API (POST /v1/messages) specifying a secondary alias (alias-b) received responses where the model field was canonicalized to the primary alias (alias-a). ### Impact on Anthropic Clients Anthropic clients and agentic tools like Claude Code record the returned model name in the assistant message and perform turn-by-turn model equality checks (request.model == previous_assistant_message.model). Because "alias-a != alias-b", Claude Code concluded that a model switch occurred across turns and stripped thinking blocks from the conversation history, breaking multi turn agentic tool use loops. ### Solution - Updated "AnthropicServingMessages.create_messages" to pass "request.model" into "messages_full_converter" and "message_stream_converter" - messages_full_converter: sets model = requested_model or generator.model - message_stream_converter: sets "model = requested_model or origin_chunk.model" on the "message_start" event - This preserves the requested model identity for Anthropic clients without altering the shared OpenAI serving path or its test contracts (PR #24663) ## Test Plan Added unit tests in "tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py": 1. test_requested_model_alias_preserved: verifies non-streaming responses return the requested alias (alias-b) instead of the canonical "generator.model" (alias-a). 2. test_default_model_when_requested_model_is_none: verifies safe fallback to generator.model when requested_model is not supplied. 3. test_stream_converter_preserves_requested_model_alias: verifies streaming converter's message_start event emits the requested alias (alias-b). Run commands: ```bash # Run targeted alias preservation tests PYTHONPATH=. pytest tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py -k "test_requested_model_alias_preserved or test_stream_converter_preserves_requested_model_alias or test_default_model_when_requested_model_is_none" # Run full Anthropic conversion test suite PYTHONPATH=. pytest tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py - AI usage disclosure: YES - I have used AI for understanding the code and also the flow of data from initial stage to last stage. Then I have also understood the syntax like how things are actually working. Rest I write the logic myself and fully understand all code submitted and can explain this all without any help of AI.

signal.title: [Spec Decode] Add unit tests for metrics and custom proposer loader
signal.text: ## Purpose Two modules in `vllm/v1/spec_decode/` had no unit tests. This adds focused, CPU-only coverage (20 tests). **`metrics.py`** (13 tests): - **SpecDecodingStats** — per-position accept/draft accounting, accumulation across drafts, the `num_accepted <= num_spec_tokens` invariant, and independent per-instance state. - **SpecDecodingLogging** — no-op when empty, the mean-acceptance-length bonus-token convention, reset-after-log, and the diffusion logging path. - **SpecDecodingProm** — disabled (no speculative config) no-op, plus counter increments (incl. per-position) for both the spec-decode and diffusion paths, using an injected registry. **`custom_class_proposer.py`** (7 tests): - `create_custom_proposer` validation/error paths: module path without a dot, unimportable module, missing class, constructor failure, missing and non-callable `propose` method, and successful instantiation. Tests only; no behavior change. ## Test Plan ``` pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_metrics.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_custom_class_proposer.py -v ``` ## Test Result 20 passed.

signal.title: [Bugfix][Whisper] Recover audio abandoned inside a chunk
signal.text: ## Purpose Fixes #53144 — Whisper transcription silently drops audio when the decoder stops early inside a chunk. Each audio chunk is decoded exactly once. When the model emits end-of-transcript before the chunk it was given is exhausted, everything after its last timestamp is transcribed by nobody: `HTTP 200`, a `duration` covering the whole file, `text` that reads like a finished sentence, and no field anywhere saying something is missing. It is not the chunking — it reproduces on a file **shorter than 30 s**, where no splitting happens at all. ## Measurements Taken on `v0.27.1`, `openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo`, real recordings (details and the ruled-out hypotheses are in the issue): | recording | before | after | |---|---|---| | 29.42 s, single chunk | text ends at **21.56 s** — 7.9 s of speech absent | ends at 28.80 s, 176 → **246** characters | | 58.85 s, two chunks | tail of **both** windows lost — a third of the speech | 353 → **516** characters, 4 → 8 segments | | speech + 12 s silence + speech | — | both halves present, **nothing invented** | Coverage gap after the fix is ~0.6 s on all three — trailing silence, not speech. ## What the change does After the per-chunk outputs are merged, each chunk's decoded coverage (from its own timestamp tokens) is compared against its length. A stretch the decoder walked away from is re-submitted as its own request and appended to the chunk it came from — so ordering needs no sorting: the abandoned stretch belongs at the end of its own chunk and before the next one, which is exactly where appending puts it. Two details that are deliberate: - **Coverage is read from token ids, not logprobs.** `logprobs` are requested only for `verbose_json`, so reading them would leave `json` and `text` clients unfixed — and those are precisely the clients that cannot notice the loss themselves, having no segments to measure. - **The phantom guard is speech density, not a phrase list.** An abandoned stretch is usually silence, and Whisper does not stay quiet over silence: measured here, 13.8 s of near-silence returned `" Let's go."` with `avg_logprob -0.46`. No blocklist would carry that sentence. Density separates them cleanly — 2.3 words/s for speech against 0.15–0.22 for the phantoms — and it is applied **only** to recovered regions, where the fallback is no text at all, i.e. exactly what the transcript had before this change. A false positive there costs nothing that was not already lost; a false negative writes a sentence the speaker never said into the middle of their transcript. Everything is bounded: a minimum gap worth asking about, a pre-roll so the slice does not start mid-word (with the resulting repetition removed at the seam), a ceiling on recovery requests, and a log line whenever a stretch is left unrecovered — a silent stop would reintroduce the same defect one level deeper. Beam search is skipped rather than half-supported. ## Test plan - Unit tests for the three pure helpers, using the measured values (`tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text/test_recover_abandoned_audio.py`). Happy to move them if there is a better home — I could not find an existing test module for this entrypoint. - Verified end to end against a live deployment on the recordings above, including that a consumer-side workaround for this same defect becomes a byte-for-byte no-op once the server does the work. I have not run the full CI locally; guidance on anything else you would like covered is welcome. ## Note This is my first contribution here — please tell me if the layout or the approach should be different. The change is currently running in production on our side, patched into the image, which is why the measurements are from real recordings rather than synthetic ones.
signal.author: Perlover

signal.title: [Bug] v1 detokenizer: client stop strings match inside the reasoning segment, decapitating think-in-prompt models (lm-eval sends stop on every request)
signal.text: ## Summary vLLM's v1 detokenizer evaluates client `stop` strings against the **whole output stream**. With think-in-prompt chat templates (DeepSeek-V4 family, Qwen3 family), generation begins *inside* the reasoning segment — and chain-of-thought naturally restates phrases like `Question:`. Any client that sends stop sequences silently decapitates the reasoning: the stop fires mid-`<think>`, `</think>` never arrives, and the reasoning parser returns `content: null`. This is easy to hit without knowing it: **lm-evaluation-harness sends `stop[:4]` on every `local-chat-completions` request**, so benchmark numbers on thinking models served by vLLM can be silently destroyed while the same checkpoint behind a hosted API (which scopes stops to content) scores normally. The failure masquerades as a model problem; it is a serving-layer one. ## Reproducer Any think-in-prompt model whose CoT can restate a stop string. With a DeepSeek-V4-family or Qwen3-family model served by vLLM: ```bash curl -s http://HOST:PORT/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{ "model": "MODEL", "temperature": 0.6, "seed": 7, "max_tokens": 8192, "stop": ["Question:"], "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "GSM8K-style word problem here"}]}' ``` On an affected build the response ends with `finish_reason: "stop"` after a few dozen tokens with `content: null` (the reasoning restated `Question:`); without the `stop` field the same seed answers correctly. Measured on our deployment: the reproducer goes 43 tok / `content: null` → 344 tok / correct answer with the guard; **GSM8K n=50 (t0.6/p0.95) goes 8–15 nulls, 0.66–0.84 → 1 null, 0.98.** (The residual null is an unrelated reasoning-runaway mechanism.) ## Fix (working, dogfooded, public — take it if you want it) Branch: https://github.com/Capicua25x/vllm-rocm-rdna4/tree/fix/suppress-stops-in-reasoning (one commit on `vllm/v1/engine/detokenizer.py`, port to 0.26.1) Per-request guard, no configuration: at detokenizer construction, if the request's **last prompt token is the reasoning start marker**, client stop strings stay dormant until the end marker appears in the output. Markers come from `--reasoning-config` (`reasoning_start_str`/`reasoning_end_str`) when set, falling back to `<think>`/`</think>` — not model-specific. EOS and `max_tokens` are unaffected; non-thinking requests are untouched by construction. Opt-out: `VLLM_SUPPRESS_STOPS_IN_REASONING=0` (process-wide). The subtle case (caught in third-party review of the original patch): with speculative decoding, the `update()` that carries `</think>` also carries up to k tokens of the reasoning that preceded it — on closing the guard, the stop-check offset advances past the marker so stops are evaluated only over what follows. Controls: a stop present in *content* still fires; a stop on a non-thinking request still cuts at the exact match. Provenance: the original version of this guard has run in production since 2026-08-05 on a 2-node DeepSeek-V4-Flash deployment (vLLM 0.21.1, speculative decoding k=5) under real agent traffic, with independent third-party validation on a second deployment; the branch above is the mechanical port to 0.26.1, verified by a CPU behavioral test included on the branch (`tests/v1/engine/test_suppress_stops_in_reasoning.py`, run in the 0.26.1 runtime: dormant-in-reasoning, non-thinking unaffected, one-chunk spec-decode leak, env opt-out — 4/4); the measured table is from the 0.21 deployment. ## Design question for maintainers The guard fixes the default behavior gap vs hosted deployments, but the right long-term shape may be per-request: e.g. scope `stop` to content by default for reasoning requests and add an explicit `stop_in_reasoning: true` escape hatch. I maintain the fix as a rebased branch on my fork rather than shepherding a PR (one-person operation) — anyone who wants to carry it upstream is welcome to it, and I'll re-run numbers against any candidate patch on request.

signal.title: fix: handle quantized qkv_proj in DFlash fused-KV buffers
signal.text: ## Summary Fixes #51581 — DFlash-family speculative decoding crashes at engine init when the drafter is quantized. The DFlash fused-KV path sliced the raw `.weight` of the KV projections and fed it to a single fused GEMM, bypassing the quant method. This reworks the fused context-KV precompute into a tiered strategy: - `FUSED` — unquantized drafters: fuse qkv weights as before (fastest path, unchanged). - `SCALED_MM` — simple per-tensor FP8 with cutlass fp8 support: keep weights quantized, fuse per-output-row scales, run `cutlass_scaled_mm`. - `FUSED_DEQUANT` — simple per-tensor FP8 without cutlass fp8: dequant once into a fused bf16 weight at build time. - `PER_LAYER` — anything else (marlin / block-quant / mixed): project per layer and concat, always correct. The fused buffers are now built lazily at the first precompute (after `process_weights_after_loading`), so quantized layers are fully materialized; compute dtype follows the model config. The same strategy applies to `laguna_dflash` (stacked bmm) and `gemma4_dspark` (K-only) via a FUSED/PER_LAYER split. ## Validation - Standalone validator: **27/27 PASS** — strategy selection (incl. SCALED_MM / FUSED_DEQUANT gates), fused == per-layer bit-exact on CPU (qwen3 / laguna / gemma4), quantized projection never sliced, real FP8 precompute vs per-layer truth on GPU, fp16 path. - Real engine on Qwen2.5-7B + 4-layer synthetic draft (A100): dflash real **534.9 tok/s**, syn-accept-len **1167.5 tok/s (1.80x vs baseline 649.4)** — no regression after rework. - Bug→fix A/B: old eager build crashes (`AttributeError: workspace` on marlin path); lazy build runs clean (eager + cudagraph). - Note: A100 has no cutlass FP8 (`cutlass_fp8_supported()==False`), so `SCALED_MM` is gated there and falls to `PER_LAYER`; `SCALED_MM` is covered by CPU strategy tests.

num_speculative_tokens=2 ### Benchmark Results **Baseline (no MTP, no prefix caching):** ```bash vllm bench latency --model Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8 \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 signal.title: [Bug]: tools/recipes/recipe_json_to_vllm_config.py silently mis-parses the -cc (compilation-config) short alias
signal.text: ### Your current environment This is a pure argument-parsing logic bug in a standalone offline script (`tools/recipes/recipe_json_to_vllm_config.py`) — it does not touch vLLM's runtime/engine, GPUs, or model loading, so `collect_env.py` output isn't applicable. Repro requires only Python + `pyyaml` + network access to `recipes.vllm.ai`. - File as of commit `9b3382685e85` (2026-08-12), latest touching this path - Python 3.14 (bug is version-independent — pure string/list parsing) - `PyYAML` (script's only dependency) ### 🐛 Describe the bug `recipe_json_to_vllm_config.py` silently produces a **wrong** `config.yml` for any recipe whose `argv` uses the `-cc` (compilation-config) short alias with dotted inline assignment, e.g. `-cc.pass_config.fuse_rope_kvcache=True`. It does not error or warn — it just corrupts the output. **Repro:** ```bash python3 tools/recipes/recipe_json_to_vllm_config.py \ --model openai/gpt-oss-120b --hardware mi300x ``` This resolves to `https://recipes.vllm.ai/openai/gpt-oss-120b/hw/mi300x.json`, whose `argv` is: ```json ["vllm", "serve", "openai/gpt-oss-120b", "--tensor-parallel-size", "1", "--attention-backend", "ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN", "-cc.pass_config.fuse_rope_kvcache=True", "-cc.use_inductor_graph_partition=True", "--gpu-memory-utilization", "0.95", "--block-size=64", "--tool-call-parser", "openai", "--enable-auto-tool-choice"] ``` **Expected:** `config.yml` contains a `compilation-config:` mapping with `pass_config.fuse_rope_kvcache: true` and `use_inductor_graph_partition: true`, and `attention-backend: ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` as a scalar. **Actual:** the generated `config.yml` is: ```yaml model: openai/gpt-oss-120b tensor-parallel-size: 1 attention-backend: - ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN - -cc.pass_config.fuse_rope_kvcache=True - -cc.use_inductor_graph_partition=True gpu-memory-utilization: 0.95 block-size: 64 tool-call-parser: openai enable-auto-tool-choice: true ``` `--attention-backend` has become a 3-element list containing two garbage strings, and the `compilation-config` settings are lost entirely. This is the Recipes-recommended AMD MI300X config for a shipping model, not a synthetic edge case. **Root cause:** After consuming `--attention-backend`, `argv_to_config()` gathers subsequent tokens as values until it sees the next option: ```python while i < len(argv) and not is_option_token(argv[i]): raw_values.append(argv[i]) i += 1 ``` `is_option_token()` is: ```python def is_option_token(token: str) -> bool: if token.startswith("--"): return True if token in SHORT_ALIASES or token == "-O": return True return token.startswith("-O") and len(token) > 2 ``` `SHORT_ALIASES` only contains `-tp`, `-pp`, `-dp`. The token `-cc.pass_config.fuse_rope_kvcache=True` doesn't start with `--`, isn't in `SHORT_ALIASES`, isn't `-O`, and doesn't start with `-O` — so `is_option_token()` returns `False`, and it gets swallowed as an extra value of the *preceding* flag instead of being recognized as the start of a new option. The script has no handling for `-cc` at all, even though `-cc.<field>=<value>` is real vLLM CLI syntax (`--compilation-config` / `-cc`) that the Recipes API actively emits. **Suggested fix:** 1. Add `-cc` to `SHORT_ALIASES`: ```python SHORT_ALIASES = { "-tp": "tensor-parallel-size", "-pp": "pipeline-parallel-size", "-dp": "data-parallel-size", "-cc": "compilation-config", } ``` 2. Make `is_option_token()` also recognize the dotted inline form as an option boundary: ```python if any(token.startswith(a + ".") for a in SHORT_ALIASES): return True ``` 3. In `argv_to_config()`, handle `-cc.<dotted.path>=<value>` by splitting off the alias, treating the remainder as a dotted path under `compilation-config`, and merging via the existing `merge_value()` / `normalize_key()` helpers — the same machinery already used for `--key.path=value`. I've implemented and verified this fix (confirmed it correctly produces a nested `compilation-config` block for the recipe above) and am happy to open a PR if that's useful. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Searched existing/past issues and PRs (`argv_to_config`, `is_option_token`, `tools/recipes`, `compilation-config`, `fuse_rope_kvcache`, `-cc.pass_config`) — no existing report. The two PRs that built this tool (#51308, #51878) never touch `SHORT_ALIASES` or `-cc` handling, so this has been present since the tool was introduced.

Updates `tokenizers` from 0.22.2 to 0.23.1
Release notes

Sourced from tokenizers's releases.

Release v0.23.1

TL;DR

tokenizers 0.23.1 is the first proper stable release in the 0.23 line — 0.23.0 only ever shipped as rc0 because the release pipeline itself was broken (Node side hadn't shipped multi-platform binaries since 2023, Python side was on pyo3 0.27 without free-threaded support). 0.23.1 is the version where everything actually goes out the door together: full Node multi-platform wheels for the first time in years, Python 3.14 (regular and free-threaded 3.14t), full type hints for every Python class, and a stack of measurable perf wins on the BPE / added-vocab hot paths.

There is no functional 0.23.0 published — we tag 0.23.1 directly so users don't accidentally pull a never-shipped version.

🚨 Breaking changes

  • Drop Python 3.9 (#1952) — requires-python = ">=3.10"; 3.9 users stay on 0.22.x.
  • add_tokens normalizes content at insertion (#1995) — re-saved tokenizer.json may differ in the added_tokens block. Existing files load unchanged.
  • Type stubs are precise (#1928, #1997) — methods that returned Any now return real types; mypy --strict may surface previously-hidden errors. Stub layout also moved from tokenizers/<sub>/__init__.pyi to tokenizers/<sub>.pyi. This breaks the surface of some of the processors like RobertaProcessign's __init__ .
  • 3.14t-only: setters/getters return PyResult<T> because of Arc<RwLock<Tokenizer>>; a poisoned lock surfaces as PyException instead of a panic.

⚡ Performance — measured locally on this Mac, not lifted from PRs

Run with cargo bench --bench <name> -- --save-baseline v0_22_2 on v0.22.2, then --baseline v0_22_2 on v0.23.1. Numbers are point-in-time wall clock on a single laptop; relative deltas are what matters, absolute numbers will differ on CI hardware.

Added-vocabulary deserialize — the headline win (#1995, #1999)

bench: improve added_vocab_deserialize to reflect real-world workloads (#2000) is now representative of how transformers actually loads tokenizer.json files. The combined effect of daachorse for the matching automaton plus the normalize-on-insert refactor is enormous on this workload:

benchmark v0.22.2 v0.23.1 change
100k tokens, special, no norm ~410 ms 248 ms −40%
100k tokens, non-special, no norm ~7.1 s 273 ms −96%
100k tokens, special, NFKC ~395 ms 235 ms −40%
100k tokens, non-special, NFKC ~7.4 s 290 ms −96%
400k tokens, special, no norm ~15 s 980 ms −94%

Real-world impact: loading a Llama-3-style tokenizer with a large set of added tokens dropped from "noticeable pause" to "instant".

BPE encode

benchmark v0.22.2 v0.23.1 change
BPE GPT2 encode batch, no cache 530 ms 446 ms −16%
BPE GPT2 encode batch (cached) 690 ms 685 ms noise
BPE GPT2 encode (single) 1.95 s 1.94 s noise
BPE Train (small) 32.6 ms 31.5 ms −3%
BPE Train (big) 1.01 s 988 ms −2%

The BPE per-thread cache PR (#2028) shows much larger wins on highly-parallel workloads (+47–62% at 88+ threads on a server box, per the PR's own measurements on Vera). Single-thread batch numbers above are flat or slightly improved because cache-hit overhead was already low without contention.

signal.title: [Bugfix][Worker] Respect gpu_memory_utilization on integrated (unified-memory) GPUs; fail clean instead of wedging the host
signal.text: ## Purpose Fixes #46307. On integrated / unified-memory GPUs (GB10 / DGX Spark, GH200, Jetson) the CPU/OS and the GPU share **one physical memory pool**, so `gpu_memory_utilization` does not reserve any memory for the OS. During startup `profile_run`, the profiling transient can drive total *system* memory to OS-critical levels and **hard-wedge the entire host** (SSH dies; the machine needs a physical power-cycle). It reproduces on fully upstream paths (`TRITON_ATTN` + bf16 KV — no quantization, no custom kernels), and only on unified memory: on a discrete GPU the same over-allocation hits a separate VRAM pool and fails cleanly. Two root causes, both addressed here, both gated on `current_platform.is_integrated_gpu(...)` so **discrete GPUs are unaffected**: 1. **Dishonest budget.** `request_memory()` computes `util * total`, where `total` is the full unified pool (`mem_get_info` returns 119.6 GiB on a GB10). On these devices that budget can exceed the memory actually available to the process. We cap it by `available_system_memory - host_reserve` so the OS keeps a headroom floor. 2. **Unbounded profiling transient.** The util budget is only consulted *after* profiling (to size KV); it never bounds the profiling allocation itself. We cap the torch caching allocator (`set_per_process_memory_fraction`) **before** `profile_run` to a **host-safety ceiling** of `total - max(host_reserve, (1-util)*total)`, so an over-large transient raises a clean, actionable `torch.OutOfMemoryError` instead of physically exhausting the shared pool and taking down the host. The ceiling sits *above* the KV budget from (1) (which is bounded by *available* memory), so it never clips a legitimate KV allocation — only a catastrophic over-allocation. The host reserve is `max(VLLM_UNIFIED_MEMORY_HOST_RESERVE_GB (default 8), 5% of the pool)` — an absolute floor that also scales with pool size. New env var `VLLM_UNIFIED_MEMORY_HOST_RESERVE_GB` lets operators tune the split. ## Why this is not a duplicate - **#48322** (`[Doc] Clarify that max_num_batched_tokens also shrinks the KV cache pool`) is a **documentation** note about the same mechanism. It explains that a larger profiling batch shrinks KV; it does **not** change any code and does not prevent the host wedge. This PR is the **code fix**. - **#35929** (`fix(memory): resolve UMA concurrent profiling race condition and page cache leak`) targets a different failure: mis-attributed `non_torch` overhead when **multiple** engines profile concurrently, plus page-cache eviction of weights. It does not cap the budget by available host memory and does not bound the single-engine profiling transient that wedges the host in #46307. The two are complementary. - Current upstream `main` already made `MemorySnapshot.free_memory` honest on integrated GPUs (`psutil.available`). That fixes the **busy-box** case (`request_memory` now raises early when `available < util*total`). It does **not** fix the **idle-box** case that is #46307: on an idle 119 GiB Spark, `available > util*total`, so the check passes and the **profiling transient** overshoots and wedges. This PR adds the missing bound. Duplicate-work checks run: `gh issue view 46307 --comments` (no comments / no fix), `gh pr list --search "46307 in:body"` (only #48322, the doc PR), `gh pr list --search "unified memory profiling"` (only #35929, different). ## Changes - `vllm/utils/mem_utils.py`: `unified_memory_host_reserve_bytes`, `unified_memory_allocator_ceiling_bytes`, `cap_unified_memory_budget`, `limit_torch_allocator_to_budget` (all no-ops on discrete GPUs). - `vllm/v1/worker/utils.py`: `request_memory` caps the budget via `cap_unified_memory_budget`. - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py`: `determine_available_memory` caps the torch allocator to the host-safety ceiling before profiling and runs profiling via `_profile_run_guarded`, which converts an integrated-GPU OOM into an actionable error. - `vllm/envs.py`: `VLLM_UNIFIED_MEMORY_HOST_RESERVE_GB` (default 8.0). - `tests/utils_/test_mem_utils.py`: unit tests for the new helpers. ## Test commands and results All three checks were run in a fresh clone of upstream main @ `41798069` with this change applied, installed via `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install -e . --torch-backend=auto` (Python 3.12). Lint (ruff 0.14.0, matches `.pre-commit-config.yaml`): ``` ruff check <5 changed files> -> All checks passed! ruff format --check <5 changed files> -> 5 files already formatted ``` Types (`pre-commit`'s mypy-3.12: mypy 1.20.2 + types-torch etc.): ``` mypy --python-version 3.12 vllm/utils/mem_utils.py vllm/v1/worker/utils.py vllm/envs.py -> Success: no issues found in 3 source files ``` (The `--torch-backend=auto` env surfaces 5 pre-existing mypy errors in `gpu_worker.py`; they are identical on the unmodified base — this change introduces none.) Unit tests (mock `is_integrated_gpu`/`psutil`/`set_per_process_memory_fraction`, so they run without a GB10): ``` pytest tests/utils_/test_mem_utils.py -v \ -k "unified or cap or limit_torch or ceiling or discrete_gpu or integrated_gpu" -> 12 passed, 1 deselected, in 6.25s ``` On-silicon e2e (DGX Spark / GB10, sm121, torch 2.11.0+cu130), real engine under a `/proc/meminfo:MemAvailable` watchdog (floor never approached). Model `google/gemma-3-1b-it` bf16 (a pure upstream text path), `util=0.70`, idle box: ``` STOCK: request_memory = 83.74 GiB (= 0.70 x 119.63 full unified pool) > psutil.available 63.29 GiB -> ValueError, refuses to start (the bug). FIX: budget capped 83.7 -> 43.4 GiB; weights load; profile_run COMPLETES; "Available KV cache memory: 42.12 GiB" (within budget); KV tensors allocated (1.57M tokens); MemAvailable stays 62.6 GiB (host intact). ``` The `set_per_process_memory_fraction` ceiling was independently shown to turn an over-ceiling allocation into a clean `torch.OutOfMemoryError` on the GB10 (no wedge). The exact `gemma-4-26B-A4B` bf16 case is not reproduced verbatim: gemma-4 does not load in that env (`Gemma4Processor` import, transformers 5.12.1, upstream of `profile_run`), and a deliberate host wedge is intentionally avoided. ## Model evaluation No effect on model outputs or accuracy: the change only adjusts the startup memory budget and adds an integrated-GPU allocator ceiling. Discrete-GPU code paths are unchanged (every new branch is gated on `is_integrated_gpu`). ## AI assistance This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude). A human author reviewed every line and ran the tests above.

signal.title: [Bugfix] Fall back to native rotary when flash-attn is installed but fails to load
signal.text: ## Purpose `ApplyRotaryEmb.__init__` guards the optional flash-attn rotary import with `suppress(ModuleNotFoundError)`. That covers a *missing* module, but not an *installed but unloadable* one: when the `flash_attn` C extension cannot be loaded, Python raises `ImportError` — the parent class — which escapes the narrower guard and aborts engine startup during model loading. `ApplyRotaryEmb` is constructed by `RotaryEmbedding.__init__` (`rotary_embedding/base.py`), so this guard runs when loading essentially any model that uses RoPE — not just the VL models that call it directly. A broken optional dependency therefore takes down startup for everything. The common trigger is mundane: rebuild or upgrade PyTorch without rebuilding flash-attn. `flash_attn.ops.triton.rotary` resolves fine, then loading `flash_attn_2_cuda` fails on a moved/removed `c10` symbol: ``` ImportError: .../flash_attn_2_cuda.cpython-312-x86_64-linux-gnu.so: undefined symbol: _ZN3c104impl3cow23materialize_cow_storageERNS_11StorageImplE ``` This PR distinguishes the two cases rather than widening the guard blindly: - `ModuleNotFoundError` — flash-attn simply is not installed. Stay silent; this is the normal, expected path and its behaviour is unchanged. - any other `ImportError` — flash-attn is installed but broken. Fall back to native **and** emit `logger.warning_once`, so the user learns their flash-attn is unusable instead of silently running the slow path. A plain `suppress(ImportError)` would fix the crash but hide a genuinely broken install, which I believe is why the narrow exception type was requested in #42679. ## Why this is not a duplicate - **#42679** (merged) introduced the current `suppress(ModuleNotFoundError)`. It fixed FA4 environments where `flash_attn.ops.triton.rotary` is *absent*. It does not cover an import that fails during extension loading. - **#36900** (open since March) targets the same lines, but the failure it describes — `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'flash_attn.ops'` with `flash-attn-4` installed — is already handled by #42679's `suppress(ModuleNotFoundError)`. Its diff is also based on the older `find_spec` code that #42679 replaced, so it no longer applies. I believe #36900 can be closed as obsolete; the `ImportError` case is the only part still unaddressed. - **#43684** (merged) added a separate native fallback in this same method for a ROCm grid-limit issue, so falling back to native here is established precedent rather than new policy. I searched open/closed/merged PRs for `rotary_embedding common.py`, `flash_attn.ops.triton.rotary`, `ApplyRotaryEmb`, `suppress(ModuleNotFoundError)` and `undefined symbol` before opening this. ## Test plan and results Hardware: RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell (sm_120), CUDA 13.2, hand-built PyTorch 2.13.0, vLLM built from source. **1. Branch behaviour** — all three paths verified by patching `import_module` in the module under test (needs `set_current_vllm_config`, or the `default_vllm_config` fixture in `tests/conftest.py`): | case | expected | result | |---|---|---| | flash-attn working | fast path selected | `apply_rotary` | | `ImportError` (ABI mismatch) | warn once + fall back | fell back to `None`, one warning | | `ModuleNotFoundError` (absent) | **silent** + fall back | fell back to `None`, no warning | | repeated construction | no log spam | deduplicated by `warning_once` | The third row is the behaviour #42679 deliberately preserved; it is unchanged here. **2. Original failure** — reproduced on this machine with a genuinely ABI-mismatched flash-attn build (2.8.3.post1 compiled against an earlier torch). On unpatched code `vllm serve` aborts during model loading with the `undefined symbol` traceback above and never becomes ready. With the guard widened, the engine starts and serves normally through the native rotary path — verified with a real workload (Qwen3.6-27B-FP8 + DFlash speculative decoding, `--max-num-seqs 3`, `--max-model-len 112000`): 122.7 tok/s and 7.91 ms TPOT single stream, 230.5 tok/s aggregate at concurrency 3. **3. End-to-end with this exact commit** — after rebuilding flash-attn against the current torch, `vllm serve` starts cleanly, `/health` returns 200, no warning is emitted (fast path taken, as expected), and generation is correct with speculative decoding active (accept rate 18.2% at `num_speculative_tokens=16`). No numerical change: this only selects which rotary implementation is used when flash-attn cannot load, and the fallback is the same native path used on every machine without flash-attn. **4. Lint** ```bash pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/layers/rotary_embedding/common.py ``` All hooks pass (ruff check, ruff format, typos, mypy 3.10, SPDX, forbidden imports). ## AI assistance disclosure AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to diagnose the failure, confirm the exception hierarchy and the `nm`-level symbol analysis, run the verification above, and draft this description. I reviewed every changed line, reproduced both the failure and the fix on my own hardware, and can defend the change end to end.

signal.title: [CI] Fix MultiConnector accuracy test lifecycle
signal.text: AMD CI build [#12250](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/12250#01a01b85-79bd-4cb8-9287-e5af327ff2ca) exposed a latent lifecycle race between the sequential normal and cross-layer test layouts. The first layout left its proxy on port 8192 while the API servers were still shutting down, so the next layout reused stale processes and the replacement proxy failed to bind. Readiness also used `curl -s` against a POST-only endpoint, allowing an HTTP 405 response to count as success. - Launch and track each API server and proxy in a harness-owned process group. - Require the launched process to remain alive and probe real `/health` and `/healthcheck` endpoints with HTTP failure handling. - Gracefully terminate and reap only owned process leaders and groups, with a 30-second timeout before forced cleanup. - Wait for ROCm GPU memory to settle before starting the next layout.

signal.title: [Model] Default quantized GLM KV cache to FP8 on NVIDIA
signal.text: ## Summary - Default the KV cache to FP8 for `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` checkpoints using `fp8` or `modelopt_fp4` quantization on NVIDIA GPUs. - Apply the default only when `--kv-cache-dtype` remains `auto`; explicit cache dtype choices are preserved. - Keep non-NVIDIA platforms and unquantized GLM checkpoints unchanged. This lets both GLM-5.2-FP8 and GLM-5.2-NVFP4 use the intended FP8 KV cache without requiring an extra launch flag. ## Duplicate-work check I searched open PRs for `GLM 5.2 FP8 KV cache` and `GLM KV cache default`. No open PR implements this default. In particular, #51915 targets ROCm GLM-5.2 MXFP4 model enablement/correctness, while #51724 targets W4A16 DSA; neither changes the NVIDIA KV-cache default. ## Tests - `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_config.py -k glm52_defaults_to_fp8_kv_cache_on_nvidia -q` - `5 passed, 201 deselected` - `.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/models/config.py vllm/config/cache.py tests/test_config.py` - all applicable hooks passed - `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_config.py -q` - `204 passed`; one unrelated existing failure in `test_draft_model_enables_async_scheduling_by_default` because MRV2 rejects the `draft_model` speculative method ## Model evaluations Both evaluations omitted `--kv-cache-dtype`; startup resolved `kv_cache_dtype=fp8` from the new default. The completion requests included the required `model` field via an evaluation-only compatibility adjustment that is not part of this PR. ### GLM-5.2-NVFP4 Server: ```bash vllm serve nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 \ --enforce-eager \ --max-model-len 4096 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 \ --safetensors-load-strategy prefetch \ --moe-backend flashinfer_cutlass \ --prefill-context-parallel-size 4 \ --enable-expert-parallel \ --trust-remote-code \ --disable-uvicorn-access-log \ --port 39985 \ --seed 0 ``` GSM8K 5-shot, 1,319 questions: accuracy `0.9371`, invalid rate `0.0010`, latency `318.6s`, throughput `4.1 questions/s`. ### GLM-5.2-FP8 Ran through Slurm on two GB200 nodes with TP8 and expert parallelism. Node 0 served the API and node 1 used `--headless`; both used the same distributed arguments below with their respective `--node-rank`: ```bash vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8 \ --enforce-eager \ --max-model-len 4096 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 \ --moe-backend deep_gemm \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --enable-expert-parallel \ --distributed-executor-backend mp \ --nnodes 2 \ --node-rank "$SLURM_PROCID" \ --master-addr "$MASTER_ADDR" \ --master-port 29652 \ --trust-remote-code \ --disable-uvicorn-access-log \ --port 8100 ``` Startup allocated 69.67 GiB of FP8 KV cache per GPU (1,568,256 tokens). GSM8K 5-shot, 1,319 questions: accuracy `0.93935`, invalid rate `0.0`, latency `423.4s`, throughput `3.12 questions/s`. ## AI assistance OpenAI Codex was used to implement and test this change. This draft remains pending the submitter's line-by-line review before it is marked ready.

signal.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] DFlash2: accept unquantized linear LM heads in the candidate selector
signal.text: ## Purpose Stacked on **#52816** — this branch is `19c93519` plus one commit, so the diff above includes that PR's changes. Retarget to `main` once #52816 merges; the diff then collapses to the single fix commit. `DFlash2Qwen3ForCausalLM.compute_candidates` guards the LM head with `isinstance(self.lm_head.quant_method, UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod)`, but that class only appears when the model has no quant config at all. A quantization config that leaves the head unquantized — INC, ModelOpt, fp8 with excluded layers, ... — returns `UnquantizedLinearMethod` for a `ParallelLMHead` (the same class it returns for any unquantized linear). A quantized-body target with an unquantized head therefore fails to start: ``` ValueError: DFlash2 requires an unquantized target LM head for candidate TopK. ``` Reproduced with `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B` (INC-int4, head unquantized) as target and `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` as drafter, TP2 on dual RTX 3090. Both classes are unquantized and their `apply()` dispatches the same unquantized GEMM, so the guard now accepts either, and the error names the offending method. Also types the `config` parameter as `Qwen3Config` to match the base class signature. ## Why this is not a duplicate #52816 introduces the DFlash2 architecture; this PR only fixes the LM-head guard in the code that PR adds, on top of its head. No other open PR touches this path. ## Test plan - `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` on the touched file → clean. - Startup with the INC-int4 target above; drafts k=7, measure acceptance. - (to be filled with exact commands + results) ## Test Result (to be filled) ## Note AI assistance (pi coding agent) was used for the fix and this description; every changed line was reviewed and tested by the submitter.

signal.title: [Spec Decode] perf: precompute draft-to-target index mapping in eagle/dflash models
signal.text: ## Purpose find some potential perf issue when I go through code. ask copilot provide a fix. Avoid recomputing torch.arange + draft_id_to_target_id on every compute_logits call by caching the result in _draft_targets (an nn.Parameter with requires_grad=False). The mapping is computed once in load_weights after weights are loaded and reused for all subsequent forward passes. Affected models: deepseek_eagle3, llama_eagle3, qwen3_dflash, qwen3_eagle3 ## Test Plan ## Test Result --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signal.title: [XPU][MoE] Resize batched Triton MoE tiles and change grid order
signal.text: # Purpose Two changes to the expert-batched Triton MoE (`BatchedTritonExperts`): - Grid order. `batched_triton_kernel` is launched with the expert id as the fastest-varying grid axis, so consecutive programs walk different experts' weights. `batched_triton_kernel_swapped` puts the tile index on axis 0 instead, so consecutive programs share an expert's weight tile. Same tiles computed, only the program-to-tile assignment changes. It is selected on XPU only, because the reorder costs up to 5.5% decode throughput on H200, so CUDA and ROCm keep the original kernel and the original grid. - Tile sizes. `try_get_optimal_moe_config` gains an optional `default_config_func`, consulted after the config override and the tuned-JSON lookup, so tuned configs still win wherever they exist. `BatchedTritonExperts` passes `get_default_batched_config`, which narrows `BLOCK_SIZE_N`/`BLOCK_SIZE_K` to 32 on XPU. The shared heuristic sizes tiles for one large `[M, K] x [K, N]` GEMM, but the batched layout runs `E` small GEMMs of at most `max_num_tokens` rows, where wide N/K tiles are mostly masked-off work. Blockwise-quantized shapes keep the shared config's K because `moe_mmk` derives scale-group offsets from it, and configs without `num_warps` (batch-invariant, wna16) pin their own tiles. `batched_triton_kernel` keeps its source and its position in the file, so its Triton cache key is unchanged and CUDA compiles the same kernel it does today. `batched_triton_kernel_swapped` differs from it by exactly the two `tl.program_id` assignments. `default_config_func` has exactly one caller, so no other config path changes. ## Testing XPU: 2× Intel Arc Pro B70, TP=2, DeepSeek-V2-Lite bf16, `moe_backend=batched_triton`, base = merge-base `bca7bea24`. | metric | base | this PR | |---|---|---| | serving throughput, `--dataset random` (output tok/s) | 110.98 | 184.61 | | offline throughput (tok/s) | 128.81 | 170.29 | | latency, batch size 32 (s) | 105.48 | 79.62 | | GSM8K, 400 questions, 5-shot | 0.3500 | 0.3450 | The GSM8K delta is −0.0050 against a one-sigma band of 0.0238, i.e. no measurable accuracy change, with identical total generated tokens. H200: 2× H200, dp2 with `--enable-expert-parallel --all2all-backend deepep_low_latency`, which is the CUDA configuration that routes through `BatchedTritonExperts`. Decode is ISL 128 / OSL 512 at concurrency 32, base = vLLM main. | model | base | this PR | reorder ungated | |---|---|---|---| | Qwen3-30B-A3B, eager | 321.2 | 320.0 | 304.0 | | Qwen3-30B-A3B, cudagraphs | 320.7 | 319.8 | 303.2 | | Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, eager | 275.4 | 275.1 | 269.5 | | Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B, eager | 227.0 | 230.0 | 226.2 | Output tok/s. The third column is the first revision of this PR, which applied the reorder on every platform: it costs 5.4% and 5.5% on the two Qwen3-30B configs and 2.1% on Qwen3.5-35B, which is what the XPU gate is there to avoid. With the gate, CUDA decode is within 0.4% of main on every config, prefill is flat, and GSM8K returns the same answers in all three arms. <details> <summary>Full perf detail, kernel-level isolation and test commands</summary> Latency at batch size 1 is flat (50.18s → 49.63s), as expected, since one token per expert leaves the kernel launch-bound either way. `bench serve` on sharegpt improves 90.12 → 159.67 output tok/s, but that workload measured ±15% run-to-run on this node (same build twice: 159.67 → 138.38), so the random-dataset and offline numbers above are the ones I would rely on. Isolating the grid order alone on XPU, with the same tensors, the same tiles and the same warp count, changing only the program-to-tile assignment: | shape | expert-first | tile-first | speedup | |---|---|---|---| | E=32, M=256, N=1408, K=2048 | 1359.8 µs | 676.9 µs | 2.01x | | E=64, M=256, N=1408, K=2048 | 3633.9 µs | 1024.0 µs | 3.55x | | E=64, M=256, wide 128/64 tiles | 6436.4 µs | 1181.4 µs | 5.45x | | E=64, M=3072, N=1408, K=2048 | 30476.8 µs | 5951.2 µs | 5.12x | Output was bitwise identical in every case. `batched_triton_kernel.cache_key` is the same on this branch as on `main`, so an existing Triton cache still hits on CUDA. H200 decode cells are means over repeated runs: 5 reps for base and the ungated reorder on Qwen3-30B eager, cudagraphs and Qwen3.5-35B; 3 reps for this PR on Qwen3-30B eager and Qwen3.5-35B; single runs for Qwen3-Next-80B and for this PR under cudagraphs. Spread across the 5-rep cells is about 1.5%, so the 5% gap the ungated reorder shows is well outside it. Running the arms in the opposite order reproduces it (302.3 output tok/s over 3 reps, against 304.0 in the original order), so it is not a warmup or thermal artifact. H200 prefill, ISL 2048 / OSL 8 at concurrency 64, total tok/s: | model | base | this PR | |---|---|---| | Qwen3-30B-A3B, eager | 15127 | 15122 | | Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, eager | 17684 | 17704 | | Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B, eager | 8227 | 8249 | | Qwen3-30B-A3B, cudagraphs | 14885 | 14916 | The Qwen3.5-35B row drops the first rep in both arms: for that model the first prefill run is compile-dominated (13856 base, 13877 this PR) and every later rep sits at 17.7k in both arms. H200 GSM8K, 200 questions, 8-shot, correct answers out of 200: | model | base | this PR | reorder ungated | |---|---|---|---| | Qwen3-30B-A3B, eager | 184 | 184 | 184 | | Qwen3-30B-A3B, cudagraphs | 188 | 188 | 188 | | Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, eager | 23 | 23 | 23 | | Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B, eager | 85 | 85 | 85 | Identical counts, which is what should happen on CUDA given that this PR runs main's kernel with main's grid there. The low absolute score on Qwen3.5-35B is a prompt-template mismatch in my eval harness rather than a model or PR problem, and it is the same in all three arms. ``` pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_batched_moe.py \ -k "swapped or blockwise_quant_k_tile or td_matches_plain or td_zero_expert \ or backend_mapping or supports_current_device or batched_experts_end_to_end" ``` → 13 passed, 768 deselected. ``` pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_batched_moe.py -k test_batched_mm ``` → 103 passed, 96 skipped on XPU, which covers the swapped kernel through `invoke_moe_batched_triton_kernel` on the fp8 and blockwise paths as well as bf16. ``` pre-commit run --files <changed files> pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --files <changed files> --hook-stage manual ``` → ruff-check, ruff-format, typos, mypy-3.10, mypy-3.12 all Passed. `test_batched_mm_swapped_grid` runs the swapped kernel on whatever device is present and compares it against `native_batched_masked_quant_matmul`, which pins the tile→(expert, m, n) mapping to an independent reference and checks no row past an expert's token count is written. It targets the swapped kernel specifically because `test_batched_mm` goes through `invoke_moe_batched_triton_kernel` and so only covers the kernel the running platform selects. I confirmed it is not vacuous by transposing the in-kernel `pid_m`/`pid_n` decode, which fails 2 of its 3 shapes; the third is `max_tokens_per_expert=1`, where `randint(low=0, high=1)` gives every expert zero tokens and the kernel early-exits. A mutation that merely permutes the tile order does not fail, which is expected since a permutation is what this PR does. `test_swapped_kernel_matches_original_source` compares the two kernels line by line, ignoring the `def` line and the `tl.program_id` assignments, so a change that lands in only one copy fails on CUDA too, where the swapped kernel is never launched. Adding `+ 0` to one copy's `num_pid_n` fails it. </details> ## AI assistance AI assistance (Claude) was used here: for the benchmark and A/B harnesses, the accuracy and perf runs, and for drafting the test and comments. I reviewed everything.

signal.title: [Model] Fix GLM-OCR MTP weight loading
signal.text: ### Summary - recognize `model.language_model.layers.*` as a valid MTP checkpoint prefix - add regression coverage for all supported MTP layer prefixes - preserve the existing behavior when the model has no MTP layers ### Why Fixes #49856. The current `zai-org/GLM-OCR` checkpoint stores its appended MTP layer under `model.language_model.layers.16.*`. `GlmOcrMTP.load_weights()` calls `get_spec_layer_idx_from_weight_name()` before `_rewrite_spec_layer_name()` removes the `language_model` wrapper. The classifier previously recognized only `model.layers.*` and `layers.*`. Consequently, every nested GLM-OCR MTP weight was classified as a non-MTP weight and skipped before its name could be rewritten, leaving eight draft parameters uninitialized. This change teaches the common classifier about the nested language-model prefix. Keeping the handling in the classifier also makes `skip_spec_layers()` apply the same classification when loading the target model. ### Validation Hardware and software: - NVIDIA RTX 4090 - Python 3.12 - PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130 - original reproduction source commit `833483f3578a2c4766977d0fe431bd32a01ce250` - repeated post-fix validation on rebased PR head `c23502a49f58533131b8baaf2a075197ba43984c` - `zai-org/GLM-OCR` revision `ca5d8b3e287e52589e37c28385d9655ee4372f9d` Before the change: ```text ValueError: Following weights were not initialized from checkpoint: model.layers.16.enorm.weight model.layers.16.hnorm.weight model.layers.16.eh_proj.weight model.layers.16.shared_head.norm.weight model.layers.16.mtp_block.input_layernorm.weight model.layers.16.mtp_block.post_attention_layernorm.weight model.layers.16.mtp_block.post_mlp_layernorm.weight model.layers.16.mtp_block.post_self_attn_layernorm.weight ``` After the change: - the MTP drafter loads successfully - `/health` becomes ready - an OpenAI-compatible multimodal request completes successfully - an image containing `vLLM MTP smoke test 49856` is transcribed exactly End-to-end server command: ```bash vllm serve zai-org/GLM-OCR \ --served-model-name glm-ocr \ --max-model-len 4096 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \ --max-num-seqs 8 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \ --enforce-eager \ --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}' curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8000/health ``` The OCR response contained: ```json { "content": "vLLM MTP smoke test 49856" } ``` Tests and checks: ```text .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/models/test_utils.py 12 passed .venv/bin/python -m ruff check \ vllm/model_executor/models/utils.py tests/models/test_utils.py All checks passed! .venv/bin/python -m ruff format --check \ vllm/model_executor/models/utils.py tests/models/test_utils.py 2 files already formatted git diff --check No errors. ``` After rebasing onto `upstream/main` at `14617c2b`, the focused tests and end-to-end GPU validation were repeated on PR head `c23502a49f58533131b8baaf2a075197ba43984c`. With the default V2 runner, the MTP drafter loaded successfully without the eight uninitialized-parameter error, and startup proceeded to the unrelated CUDA graph capture failure tracked by #51966. With `--enforce-eager` to bypass that independent graph-capture path, `/health` and `/v1/models` returned HTTP 200, and the multimodal OCR request completed with the exact output `vLLM MTP smoke test 49856`. ### Duplicate-work check Before opening this PR, searches for #49856, GLM-OCR MTP loading, and `model.language_model.layers` plus `get_spec_layer_idx_from_weight_name` found no open PR implementing this fix. Another contributor posted an intent to investigate shortly before this PR was opened, but no implementation or PR was available; this PR comes from an independently completed reproduction and validated fix. ### AI assistance disclosure AI assistance was used for issue triage, root-cause analysis, drafting the regression tests, and organizing the validation. signal.title: fix(security): widen int32 pointer arithmetic to int64 in CUDA kernels
signal.text: ## Summary - Widen 32-bit integer pointer offset arithmetic to 64-bit in CUDA kernels to prevent cross-user data disclosure when `num_tokens * stride` overflows `2^32` - Applies the established fix pattern from `451227cb3f` (activation_kernels.cu): cast `blockIdx.x` to `int64_t` before multiplying by stride/dimension - Covers LayerNorm, LayerNorm-quant (FP8), MoE routing, and AllSpark W8A16 GEMM kernels ## Affected kernels | Kernel | File | Risk | |---|---|---| | `rms_norm_kernel` | `layernorm_kernels.cu` | High -- confirmed exploitable with PoC | | `rms_norm_static_fp8_quant_kernel` | `layernorm_quant_kernels.cu` | High -- FP8 quantized path | | `fused_add_rms_norm_static_fp8_quant_kernel` (both specializations) | `layernorm_quant_kernels.cu` | High | | `moeSoftmax` / `moeSigmoid` / `moeTopK` | `topk_softmax_kernels.cu` | Moderate | | AllSpark W8A16 GmemTile / ComputeTile | `allspark_qgemm_w8a16.cu` | Low (defense in depth) | ## Root cause CUDA built-in `blockIdx.x` is `unsigned int` (32-bit). When multiplied by a 32-bit `hidden_size` or stride, the product wraps at 2^32, causing a kernel block to read/write another user's hidden state within the same batch. With `hidden_size = 8192`, the overflow triggers at ~524,288 tokens. ## Fix pattern ```cpp // Before (32-bit overflow) scalar_t* out_row = out + blockIdx.x * hidden_size; // After (64-bit safe) const int64_t token_idx = blockIdx.x; scalar_t* out_row = out + token_idx * hidden_size; ``` For host-side code, `int input_stride` is widened to `int64_t input_stride` to match the kernel parameter change. ## Test plan - [x] Pre-commit hooks pass (clang-format, typos, etc.) - [ ] Existing LayerNorm kernel tests pass - [ ] Existing MoE kernel tests pass - [ ] CI build succeeds on CUDA targets Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

signal.title: Add separate post-thinking sampling parameters
signal.text: ## Summary This PR adds support for using a separate set of sampling parameters after a model finishes its `<think>...</think>` reasoning block. The primary motivation is models such as **Qwen 3.8 27B**, where the optimal sampling parameters for reasoning differ substantially from the optimal parameters for the final answer. In testing, Qwen 3.8 27B benefits from a relatively high temperature (`~0.9–1.0`) during reasoning. Lower temperatures can cause the reasoning process to become repetitive or enter loops. However, keeping that same temperature after `</think>` noticeably reduces the reliability and precision of the final response, including normal chat output and tool calls. This PR allows those two phases to use different sampling configurations. For example: ```json { "temperature": 0.9, "top_p": 0.95, "top_k": 20, "post_thinking": { "temperature": 0.2, "top_p": 0.95, "top_k": 20 } } ``` With this configuration: * while inside an open `<think>` block, the normal sampling parameters are used; * after `</think>`, the `post_thinking` sampling parameters are used; * if a model opens another `<think>` block later in the same generation, sampling switches back to the primary parameters; * fields omitted from `post_thinking` inherit their values from the primary sampling configuration. This makes it possible to use sampling parameters appropriate for exploratory reasoning without carrying that randomness into the final answer. ## Motivation Reasoning models do not necessarily benefit from a single sampling configuration throughout the entire generated sequence. For Qwen 3.8 27B specifically, I have found the following configuration to work well: * **Thinking:** `temperature=0.9` * **Final output:** `temperature=0.2` The higher temperature keeps the reasoning process healthy and avoids repetitive reasoning loops, while the lower temperature after `</think>` produces substantially cleaner and more reliable final output. Using `temperature=0.9` for the entire response allows reasoning to work correctly, but makes the final answer more error-prone. Using `temperature=0.2` for the entire response improves the final answer, but can negatively affect the reasoning process. Allowing the sampler to change state at the reasoning boundary provides the benefits of both. Initial testing with Qwen 3.8 27B shows significantly fewer errors in generated answers while preserving the behavior of the thinking section. ## API The PR adds a `post_thinking` sampling configuration. Example generation configuration: ```json { "temperature": 0.9, "top_p": 0.95, "top_k": 20, "min_p": 0, "post_thinking": { "temperature": 0.2, "top_p": 0.95, "top_k": 20 } } ``` Any parameter not explicitly provided under `post_thinking` inherits the corresponding primary sampling parameter. For example: ```json { "temperature": 0.9, "top_p": 0.95, "top_k": 20, "post_thinking": { "temperature": 0.2 } } ``` is effectively equivalent to: ```json { "temperature": 0.9, "top_p": 0.95, "top_k": 20, "post_thinking": { "temperature": 0.2, "top_p": 0.95, "top_k": 20 } } ``` ## Sampling behavior The sampler tracks whether generation is currently inside a reasoning block. Conceptually: ```text <think> primary sampling parameters </think> post_thinking sampling parameters ``` The state transitions are: ```text <think> -> primary sampler </think> -> post_thinking sampler <think> -> primary sampler ``` The final transition is not expected to be relevant for Qwen 3.8 27B, but supporting it keeps the behavior consistent if a model produces multiple reasoning sections. The `post_thinking` configuration applies to everything following the reasoning block, including: * normal assistant content; * structured output; * tool calls; * other generated content after `</think>`. If `post_thinking` is not supplied, generation behaves exactly as it does today. ## Server configuration The feature can be configured as a server default through the generation config. Recommended/tested Qwen 3.8 27B configuration: ```bash vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 \ --override-generation-config '{ "temperature": 0.9, "top_p": 0.95, "top_k": 20, "min_p": 0, "post_thinking": { "temperature": 0.2, "top_p": 0.95, "top_k": 20 } }' ``` The important difference here is the temperature transition from `0.9` during reasoning to `0.2` after reasoning completes. ## Per-request configuration It can also be specified on individual requests: ```python client.chat.completions.create( model="qwen/qwen3.8-27B", messages=[ {"role": "user", "content": "..."} ], temperature=0.9, extra_body={ "post_thinking": { "temperature": 0.2, "top_p": 0.95, "top_k": 20, }, }, ) ``` This allows applications to tune the two phases independently without changing server-wide defaults. ## Backward compatibility The feature is opt-in. When `post_thinking` is not specified, sampling behavior remains unchanged. Existing requests, generation configurations, and model behavior should therefore continue to work as before. ## Results So far I have primarily tested this with **Qwen 3.8 27B**. The initial results are encouraging: * reasoning behavior remains effectively unchanged; * reasoning loops remain avoided with the higher thinking temperature; * final answers contain noticeably fewer errors; * final output is more deterministic and coherent; * tool-call generation benefits from the lower post-thinking sampling temperature. More systematic evaluation would be useful, particularly across additional reasoning models. ## Why implement this in vLLM? It is possible for a client to approximate this behavior by stopping generation after `</think>` and issuing another request with different sampling parameters. However, doing so introduces unnecessary complexity and can interfere with normal continuous generation, request state, KV-cache reuse, tool-call generation, streaming, and model-specific chat templates. The reasoning boundary already exists within a single generation. Allowing the sampler configuration to change at that boundary lets vLLM support this use case directly without splitting one logical model turn into multiple requests. ## Reference implementation The current implementation is available here: ```text https://github.com/mdierolf/vllm-fork/tree/feat/post_thinking_sample_settings ``` This is still a work in progress, and I am interested in feedback on both the API shape and where the state transition should live within vLLM's sampling architecture.

signal.title: [ROCm] Add per-call decode budget to sparse-MLA indexer
signal.text: ## Purpose The ROCm AITER sparse-MLA indexer decode path allocates a fresh fp32 logits tensor on every call to `rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits`: `(heads, B*next_n, max_model_len)` on the stage1 3D path, or `(B*next_n, max_model_len)` on the gfx942/gfx950 fused 2D path. With long context and a large running batch the per-call working set is multi-GiB; across ~60 layers per decode forward the caching allocator fragments and OOMs. Prefill had the same problem and got `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB` plus chunking in #36178. This is the decode mirror. Two pieces, decode-only, ROCm-only: - the fp32 logits buffer is now drawn from a per-process workspace keyed by (device, shape) and refilled with `-inf` between calls, so no per-layer alloc/free of multi-GiB tensors; - `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_DECODE_MAX_MB` (default 4096) bounds the per-call working set. When a single call would exceed the budget the batch is split into sub-batches that fit and copied into the full output. The aiter kernel does not consume `schedule_metadata` on ROCm, so the metadata doesn't need to be re-derived per chunk. Set to 0 to restore the legacy unbounded behaviour. Prefill is not touched. The CUDA path is not touched (this file only runs on ROCm via the AITER sparse-MLA backend). Both `_ON_GFX942` and `_ON_GFX950` are covered, plus the stage1 3D else-branch that older arches still hit. Related: #36178 is the prefill-side mirror (same shape of fix, opposite forward-pass phase). #41002 is in flight in the same area, happy to rebase on top of it after it merges. ## Test Plan 1. Numeric equivalence test added at `tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_sparse_decode.py`. Skipped on non-ROCm and when the AITER `paged_mqa_logits` module is not importable, so it sits with the rest of the ROCm-only kernel tests. On a ROCm gate it asserts the chunked path returns bit-identical logits to the full-batch call. ```bash pytest -s -v tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_sparse_decode.py ``` 2. Synthetic micro-bench on a single MI355X (gfx950), 60 back-to-back calls into `rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` with a pre-allocated paged kv at `B=1024, next_n=1, heads=64, head_dim=128, block_size=64, max_model_len=131072`. Stress shape, picked so the 3D per-call working set is well above any reasonable budget. Measured peak `torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated()` minus the paged-kv baseline, sweeping `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_DECODE_MAX_MB` against the legacy code. 3. End-to-end re-run of the GLM-5.1-FP8 customer repro that motivated this: ```bash vllm bench serve --random-input-len 1 --random-output-len 2 --num-prompts 1024 \ --ignore-eos --temperature 0 --seed 0 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 -tp 8 --enforce-eager ``` ## Test Result Indexer working set at the high-water mark, 60-layer loop: | setting | indexer working set @ peak | | -------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------: | | legacy (no patch) | 33792 MiB | | `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_DECODE_MAX_MB` unset (= 4096) | ~4160 MiB | | `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_DECODE_MAX_MB=2048` | ~2080 MiB | | `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_DECODE_MAX_MB=1024` | ~1040 MiB | The 33.8 GiB legacy delta is exactly `heads * B * next_n * max_model_len * 4` bytes for the 3D stage1 buffer; chunking brings it down to `chunk_b * heads * next_n * max_model_len * 4` plus a one-shot 2D accumulator. Wall time across all four settings stays between 1.09 and 1.24 s for the 60-call loop, the only overhead is one `copy_` per chunk into the persistent output buffer. End-to-end on GLM-5.1-FP8, the decode-time HIP OOM that originally fired at ~24 GiB per layer no longer occurs; 1017/1024 prompts succeed, the 7 remaining failures are bench-client side ("never received a valid chunk") and clear with `--max-concurrency 256`.
