signal.title: [Perf][ROCm] Dual-stream decode with hipgraphs
signal.text:
## What's new since reverted in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52024 TLDR: changes since this PR was reverted: [here](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52033/changes/b25620205d5529e8e36ca143050770ce31969428..1b7ff2c22beb1fddbebaed5c08ef62367e986528). **Context:** Re-opened https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48223 after it failed CI due to poor gsm8k acc for Qwen3.5 with DP2EP. **Root cause of failure:** Qwen3.5 uses the same tensor for hidden state and shared expert inputs, and never creates any copies of either tensor throughout the MoE. This causes a race condition during multi-stream. Specifically, it uses the same tensors because it's **not quantizing the routed experts' input**. When quantizing the input (as in DSv3) a copy is "implicitlly created" and hence the two buffers are different. **Fix:** **Disable dual-stream if not quantizing the routed experts' input**. To retain Nvidia behavior, we only do this check on ROCm. This (1) ensures Qwen3.5 does not have a race condition, and hence accuracy is preserved (but multi-stream is off), and (2) DSv3 uses multi-stream. **Validation:** Get traces for both DSv3 and Qwen3.5 when running DP, and re-run gsm8k with this config: ```bash vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B \ --max-model-len 4096 \ --data-parallel-size 2 \ --enable-expert-parallel \ --trust-remote-code \ --disable-uvicorn-access-log ``` ### **Qwen3.5**: mulistream overlap **disabled** automatically. No overlap: This is because its MoE layer is using **unquantized GEMMs**: Accuracy OK! |Tasks|Version| Filter |n-shot| Metric | |Value | |Stderr| |-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:| |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.8453|± |0.0100| | | |strict-match | 5|exact_match|↑ |0.8332|± |0.0103| ### **DSv3**: proper multi-stream overlap for DPA+TP8 (with no extra copies) This works because it's using quantized (fp8) fmoe: --- _From original PR:_ ## Purpose Fixes #48111. Enables (1) dual-stream decode for CUDA-like platforms with proper overlap (2) make them hip/cudagraph compatible. Only enabled on ROCm when using DP, as we observed [performance regression under TP](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48223#issuecomment-4993855510). Mutually exclusive with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS`. Disable with `VLLM_DISABLE_SHARED_EXPERTS_STREAM=1` as usual. **Gain:** About -3-4% TPOT on 1k/1k and 8k/1k when using DPA vs default. **Note:** When Fused Shared experts (FSE) can be used, it provides even better TPOT than dual-stream. However, FSE cannot be used everywhere (like with MoRI a2a kernels). ### Technical details - Simply allowing `MULTI_STREAM_OVERLAPPED` for CUDA-like platforms is not sufficient for performant dual-stream decode (on ROCm, at least), because the shared expert was launched on the aux stream only _after_ the routed experts had completed. That leads to a sequential launch with no overlap: - Instead, we need to launch the shared expert in the aux stream _before_ the dispatch. #### After this PR we get the following traces - Pure decodes: properly overlapped - Mixed batches: no aux stream - Pure prefills: no aux stream ## Test Plan Tested on 8xMI300. 1. Run DSv3 with DPA+TP: ```bash export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm bench deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3-0324 \ --data-parallel-size 8 \ --tensor-parallel-size 1 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 \ --max-model-len 16K ``` 2. Bench serve sweep, 1k/1k and 8k/1k ISL/OSL - 10x as many prompts as the concurrency level; 2x number of warmups. - Comparing to nightly `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-a16dbd5b8572d4128be9f10b9dcff4999b594b25` with fused shared experts ```bash vllm bench serve \ --backend vllm \ --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3-0324 \ --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 1024 \ --random-output-len 1024 \ --host localhost \ --port 8000 \ --ignore-eos \ --ready-check-timeout-sec 6000 \ --seed 5678 \ --max-concurrency 128 \ --num-prompts 1280 \ --num-warmups 256 ``` 6. GSM8k accuracy non-regression ```bash lm_eval \ --model local-completions \ --model_args model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3-0324,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,tokenized_requests=False,trust_remote_code=True,num_concurrent=256 \ --tasks gsm8k \ --num_fewshot 5" ``` ## Test Result - Couple % improved TPOT ### 1k/1k (P50's only) | Concurrency | Variant | QPS | TTFT (ms) | TPOT (ms) | % TPOT improved | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | this branch | 0.04 | 232.57 | 23.67 | **+4.24%** | | 1 | nightly | 0.04 | 273.16 | 24.72 | - | | 2 | this branch | 0.08 | 258.38 | 24.16 | **+4.58%** | | 2 | nightly | 0.08 | 298.14 | 25.32 | - | | 4 | this branch | 0.15 | 397.90 | 25.52 | **+7.03%** | | 4 | nightly | 0.14 | 366.23 | 27.45 | - | | 8 | this branch | 0.25 | 602.93 | 30.84 | **+3.41%** | | 8 | nightly | 0.24 | 664.92 | 31.93 | - | | 16 | this branch | 0.44 | 1268.65 | 35.02 | -6.77% | | 16 | nightly | 0.46 | 851.06 | 32.80 | - | | 32 | this branch | 0.71 | 1830.04 | 42.03 | **+2.75%** | | 32 | nightly | 0.70 | 1698.74 | 43.22 | - | | 64 | this branch | 1.34 | 3228 | 43.51 | **+4.71%** | | 64 | nightly | 1.29 | 2528 | 45.66 | - | | 128 | this branch | 2.15 | 4487.07 | 53.85 | **+1.86%** | | 128 | nightly | 2.10 | 4543.42 | 54.87 | - | | 256 | this branch | 3.46 | 6554.86 | 65.74 | **+3.12%** | | 256 | nightly | 3.37 | 6386.54 | 67.86 | - | Note: TTFT numbers seems highty variable. Ran 64 concurrency yet another time, and then I got 1902 ms TTFT @ 1.37 QPS, substantially better than the first time. This PR should not affect prefills anyhow so not focusing too much on TTFT here anyways. ### 8k/1k | Concurrency | Variant | QPS | TTFT (ms) | TPOT (ms) | % TPOT improved | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | this branch | 0.04 | 1868.16 | 25.22 | **+3.59%** | | 1 | nightly | 0.04 | 1860 | 26.16 | - | | 2 | this branch | 0.07 | 2034.06 | 25.42 | **+5.47%** | | 2 | nightly | 0.07 | 2014.35 | 26.89 | - | | 4 | this branch | 0.11 | 3800.62 | 31.35 | **+2.82%** | | 4 | nightly | 0.11 | 3687 | 32.26 | - | | 8 | this branch | 0.19 | 4105.90 | 37.01 | **+5.54%** | | 8 | nightly | 0.18 | 4122.95 | 39.18 | - | | 16 | this branch | 0.31 | 6355 | 45.37 | -3.07% | | 16 | nightly | 0.31 | 6321 | 44.02 | - | | 32 | this branch | 0.45 | 9616.31 | 60.48 | **+11.44%** | | 32 | nightly | 0.41 | 9173.59 | 68.29 | - | | 128 | this branch | 0.85 | 15579.93 | 131.24 | -3.71% | | 128 | nightly | 0.89 | 13966.30 | 126.55 | - | ### GSM8k This branch: |Tasks|Version| Filter |n-shot| Metric | |Value | |Stderr| |-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:| |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.9416|± |0.0065| | | |strict-match | 5|exact_match|↑ |0.9409|± |0.006| Nightly: |Tasks|Version| Filter |n-shot| Metric | |Value | |Stderr| |-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:| |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.9484|± |0.0061| | | |strict-match | 5|exact_match|↑ |0.9492|± |0.0060| ---

signal.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Inherit target KV cache scales in Gemma4 MTP draft layers
signal.text: Gemma4 MTP draft layers share the target's physical KV cache (kv_sharing_target_layer_name), but their Attention objects keep their own _k_scale/_v_scale, which stay at 1.0 because assistant checkpoints carry no KV scales. On targets with calibrated FP8 KV scales (e.g. unsloth/gemma-4-31b-it-nvfp4), the drafter dequantizes the shared cache with the wrong scale (k_scale ~0.003 read as 1.0) and MTP acceptance collapses from ~65-77% to ~34-46%, costing ~30% decode throughput. Output quality is unaffected (rejection sampling), so the bug is silent. Fix - to copy the target layer's q/k/v/prob scales onto each KV-sharing draft layer after the mapping is wired; a no-op for scale-free targets. ## Purpose Fix a silent MTP acceptance-rate collapse (~30% decode throughput loss) when a Gemma4 target with calibrated FP8 KV-cache scales is served with speculative decoding. Draft layers share the target's physical KV cache but keep _k_scale/_v_scale at 1.0 (assistant checkpoints ship no scales); with calibrated-KV targets served --kv-cache-dtype fp8 the drafter reads a lot different K/V and per-position acceptance decays 0.86/0.71/0.55/0.42 -> 0.71/0.42/0.21/0.10. The problem was both reproduced: * on new unsloth/gemma-4-31b-it-nvfp4 (https://unsloth.ai/docs/basics/nvfp4) with added FP8 KV cache calibration and using original "google/gemma-4-31b-it-assistant" model for speculative decoding. * on self quantized nvfp4 models based on "google/gemma-4-31B-it-qat-q4_0-unquantized" using "google/gemma-4-31B-it-qat-q4_0-unquantized-assistant" for speculative decoding - comparing models with baked KV cache calibration and without. Fix: copy _q/_k/_v/_prob_scale + float mirrors from the target layer after process_weights_after_loading has populated them. ## Test Plan A/B of two byte-identical modelopt NVFP4 exports differing only in baked KV scales, served with MTP on RTX PRO 6000 (SM120), production workload (in our case, but could be any workload actually); ## Test Result mode | acceptance length | decode tok/s no KV calibration baked) | 3.4 - 4.1 | 163.1 calibrated-KV before fix | 2.35 - 2.69 | 114.3 calibrated-KV after fix | 3.66 - 3.75 | 162.5 (~parity) --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signal.title: Fix Transformers modelling backend `RMSNormFuser.fuse` performance
signal.text: #50128 identified that `RMSNormFuser` was taking an excessively long time at startup tracing every norm module in `fuse` bypassing the caching efficiency in `match`. This PR determines and caches the attribute to read the `eps` from at in `match` so we no longer need to trace in `fuse`. Measured on the Transformers-backend fuser path: `Fusers(model, vllm_config)` (per-class matching, cold cache) plus `fuse()` on every matched instance, which is the work `recursive_replace` does. | Model | Norms | Before | After | Speedup | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` | 113 | 998 ms | 50 ms | 20.1x | | `google/gemma-3-4b-it` | 206 | 6050 ms | 105 ms | 57.8x | | `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B` | 33 | 261 ms | 45 ms | 5.8x | | `allenai/OLMoE-1B-7B-0924` | 65 | 548 ms | 83 ms | 6.6x | | `mistralai/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1` | 65 | 679 ms | 84 ms | 8.1x | Split by phase, since the two changes pull in opposite directions: | Model | match (per class) | | RMSNorm `fuse` (per instance) | | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | | before | after | before | after | | `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` | 43 ms | 37 ms | 944 ms | 2.0 ms | | `google/gemma-3-4b-it` | 112 ms | 95 ms | 5931 ms | 2.4 ms | | `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B` | 27 ms | 35 ms | 224 ms | 0.6 ms | | `allenai/OLMoE-1B-7B-0924` | 88 ms | 80 ms | 458 ms | 1.3 ms | | `mistralai/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1` | 72 ms | 81 ms | 605 ms | 1.2 ms | `fuse` no longer traces at all, so per-instance cost collapses (350x-2500x).

signal.title: [Bugfix] Load reasoning parser plugins before headless engine config
signal.text: ## Purpose Fixes #53072. Headless serving currently constructs the engine config before loading `--reasoning-parser-plugin`. `VllmConfig` resolves the requested parser during config initialization, so a custom parser raises `KeyError` before its module has a chance to register itself. This change loads the plugin before `AsyncEngineArgs.from_cli_args` and `create_engine_config`, matching the existing API server startup order. It also adds a regression test that checks the import has happened when engine config construction begins. I searched the open vLLM pull requests by issue number and relevant keywords and found no duplicate implementation. No documentation update is needed because this restores the existing CLI option in headless mode. Codex assisted with investigation and drafting. I reviewed and understand every changed line and ran the validation below locally. ## Test Plan - Run the new headless CLI regression test together with the related CLI suites. - Run the repository pre-commit hooks against both changed files. ## Test Result Before the fix, the new regression test fails because the plugin import call count is zero when engine config construction starts. After the fix: ```text VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/entrypoints/cli/test_serve.py tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_launch_cli.py tests/entrypoints/openai/test_cli_args.py 43 passed, 16 warnings in 10.76s ``` ```text .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/entrypoints/cli/serve.py tests/entrypoints/cli/test_serve.py All applicable hooks passed. ``` --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, including the issue it resolves. - [x] The test plan, including the commands used. - [x] The test results, including before/after behavior. - [x] Documentation impact was considered; no update is required for this bug fix. </details>

signal.title: [Feature] Support `extract_hidden_states` on Model Runner V2
signal.text: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch ### Feature Add Model Runner V2 support for `extract_hidden_states`, so the existing hidden-state extraction path works when MRv2 is enabled (ideally via an `ExtractHiddenStatesSpeculator` registered in `init_speculator()`), with the same core semantics as Model Runner V1: - extract configured intermediate-layer `aux_hidden_states` - write them into `HiddenStateCache` through the cache-only extract model - remain compatible with hidden-states KV connectors (e.g. `ExampleHiddenStatesConnector`) - return sampled tokens as draft tokens so verification always accepts ### Motivation `extract_hidden_states` is already supported on Model Runner V1 (`ExtractHiddenStatesProposer`) and documented for draft-model data generation / analysis. MRv2 is becoming the default path for more models, but today MRv2 `init_speculator()` does not register extract and raises: ```python NotImplementedError(f"{speculative_config.method} is not supported yet.") ``` ### Pitch Porting extract to MRv2 would: 1. keep feature parity with MRv1 as MRv2 adoption grows 2. avoid long-lived out-of-tree forks just to preserve an already-supported speculative method 3. reuse the existing extract model / cache-spec / connector stack, mainly adding the missing MRv2 Speculator wiring ### Alternatives 1. **Maintain an out-of-tree / backend-specific MRv2 Speculator** Unblocks local users quickly, but risks divergence from upstream semantics and higher maintenance cost. 2. **Build a separate non-speculative hidden-state export API** Cleaner long-term API maybe, but much larger scope than porting the already accepted extract method to MRv2. 3. **Do nothing / wait without tracking** Leaves a growing MRv1/MRv2 feature gap with no clear roadmap signal for downstream projects. ### Additional context #### Current status on recent `main` - **Model Runner V1**: supported in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py` via `ExtractHiddenStatesProposer`, with `use_aux_hidden_state_outputs = True`. - **Model Runner V2**: `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/__init__.py` `init_speculator()` currently registers only `dflash` / `dspark` / Gemma4 MTP / `mtp` / eagle-family (`use_eagle()`). Other methods, including `extract_hidden_states`, fall through to `NotImplementedError`. - There is no `ExtractHiddenStatesSpeculator` (or equivalent) under `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/`. So with MRv2 enabled, a config like: ```python speculative_config = { "method": "extract_hidden_states", "num_speculative_tokens": 1, "draft_model_config": { "hf_config": { "eagle_aux_hidden_state_layer_ids": [1, 2, 3, 4], }, }, } ``` fails at speculator initialization instead of using the existing V1 extract path. #### Related prior art I searched existing issues/PRs for an MRv2 port of `extract_hidden_states` and did **not** find a dedicated tracking issue/PR. Closest related work: - Original RFC: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/33118 - Initial feature: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/33736 - Docs: `docs/features/speculative_decoding/extract_hidden_states.md` - Follow-up MRv1 / connector / hybrid work (not MRv2 port), e.g.: - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39949 - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43869 - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49301 There are active MRv2 speculative-decoding efforts (Eagle/MTP/draft-model, etc.), but none appear to cover `extract_hidden_states` specifically. #### Why this matters As MRv2 becomes the default for more models, lacking extract support creates a feature gap for draft-model data generation and for out-of-tree backends that are migrating users to MRv2 while still needing hidden-state export. #### Questions for maintainers 1. Is it correct that MRv2 does not support `extract_hidden_states` yet? 2. Is there already a tracking issue/PR that I missed? 3. Is there a rough priority or timeline for an MRv2 port (e.g. an `ExtractHiddenStatesSpeculator`)? Happy to help prototype or review an in-tree MRv2 implementation if that matches upstream direction. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signal.title: [Feature][Model Runner V2] Support extract_hidden_states speculation
signal.text: ## Purpose Fixes #49562. `extract_hidden_states` is supported by the existing model runner, but Model Runner V2 currently rejects the configuration and has no speculator for forwarding the sampled token while caching the target model's auxiliary hidden states. This PR: - allows the `extract_hidden_states` speculative method with Model Runner V2; - requests auxiliary hidden-state outputs from the target model; - adds a Model Runner V2 `ExtractHiddenStatesSpeculator` that forwards sampled tokens and caches the selected hidden states through the existing `ExtractHiddenStatesModel`; - adds focused configuration, dispatch, cache, and failure-path tests. Duplicate-work check on 2026-07-25: - #49562 was open with no assignee or comments; - searching open PR bodies for `49562` returned no results, and this fork head had no existing PR; - #46399 concerns dynamic speculative decoding for fixed-K proposers, while #46788 concerns DeepSeek auxiliary-layer indexing. Neither implements Model Runner V2 support for this method. AI assistance was used to help implement and validate this change. The submitter reviewed every changed line and understands the change end-to-end. ## Test Plan The final patch was reapplied to upstream main `33ef67e9fb5f3f9c2dfe1aa95e9880d5ecd7b38b`, then checked with: ```bash git diff --check ruff check \ tests/test_config.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_extract_hidden_states_speculator.py \ vllm/config/vllm.py \ vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py \ vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/__init__.py \ vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/extract_hidden_states.py ruff format --check \ tests/test_config.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_extract_hidden_states_speculator.py \ vllm/config/vllm.py \ vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py \ vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/__init__.py \ vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/extract_hidden_states.py mypy vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/extract_hidden_states.py python -m pytest \ tests/test_config.py::test_v2_model_runner_supports_extract_hidden_states \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_extract_hidden_states_speculator.py \ tests/v1/spec_decode/test_extract_hidden_states.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2_eplb.py -q ``` The predictable-model GPU E2E was run on one RTX 3090 with driver `580.65.06`, PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`, and the CUDA 13 toolkit: ```bash CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda-13.0 \ VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 \ VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 \ CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ python -m pytest \ tests/v1/kv_connector/extract_hidden_states_integration/test_extraction.py::test_extract_hidden_states_with_predictable_dummy_model \ -v -s ``` `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0` avoids compiling the unrelated FlashInfer sampling JIT during this feature test. A validation-only tokenizer fixture adjustment used the data-disk Hugging Face cache and `AutoTokenizer`; it was reversed immediately after the run and is not present in the commit. ## Test Result - `git diff --check`: passed. - Ruff: `All checks passed!`. - Ruff format: `6 files already formatted`. - Direct Mypy check for the new production module: `Success: no issues found in 1 source file`. - Related regression tests: `19 passed, 14 warnings in 5.52s`. - Predictable-model Model Runner V2 GPU E2E: `1 passed, 16 warnings in 64.39s`; the engine log explicitly reported `Using V2 Model Runner`. - The final commit contains exactly six files: 293 insertions and 2 deletions. The changed-file Mypy wrapper still returns nonzero because upstream `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py` has five existing errors at lines 514, 586, 1141, 1315, and 1585. These locations are outside this PR's only `model_runner.py` hunk (around line 198). The new module and both test files pass their Mypy groups. The Git pre-commit hook bootstrap could not complete because fetching the `ruff-pre-commit` environment from GitHub timed out. The scoped Ruff, format, Mypy, diff, and pytest commands above were run manually, and the commit was created with `--no-verify`. Earlier validation on the preceding main snapshot also completed a full CUDA 13 CMake/Ninja build and a custom-op numerical check with `max_abs_error=0.0`. Qwen3.5 hybrid and two-GPU tensor-parallel smoke tests each passed there. Those two model smoke tests were not rerun in this publish turn; the two intervening upstream commits do not overlap this PR's six files. No accuracy or performance benchmark was run. This change wires existing hidden-state extraction behavior into Model Runner V2; the GPU E2E validates sampled-token generation, hidden-state export, layer values, chunked prefill, and per-request output options. --- <details> <summary>Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist</summary> - [x] The purpose and resolving issue are included. - [x] The test plan includes the commands used. - [x] The test results and limitations are included. - [x] Documentation impact was considered; no user-facing configuration or model-support documentation changes are required. </details>

signal.title: [Model] Route the Qwen3.5 vision tower through the UVA offloader
signal.text: ## Purpose When I try to deploy Qwen3.8-27B to my system with vision tower offloaded to CPU DRAM, it silently fails. After investigation, it turns out that `--cpu-offload-params visual` on Qwen3.5 multimodal models was a **silent no-op** for the vision tower. The tower is constructed directly in `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration.__init__` (not via `make_layers`), so it never reaches `get_offloader().wrap_modules` and the offloader's segment matching never saw a single `visual.*` parameter — no warning, no error, just `Total CPU offloaded parameters: 0` (actually no log line at all, since the summary is only printed when bytes > 0). This PR routes the vision tower through the UVA offloader so that `--cpu-offload-params visual` genuinely offloads the tower weights (0.86 GiB on Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4) to CPU memory. ### How it works - `_maybe_offload_visual_tower()` wraps the tower in a throwaway container so its parameters carry the `visual.` name segment (`visual.blocks.0.attn.qkv.weight`), which the offloader's exact-segment matching (`f".visual." in f".{name}."`) requires. Passing the bare tower would expose names like `blocks.0.attn.qkv.weight` with no `visual` segment and would silently match nothing. - Only the UVA backend is wired up: `PrefetchOffloader.wrap_modules` asserts it is called exactly once (already done by `make_layers`), and the prefetch backend is layer-stack-scoped by design. - Applies to both `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` and `Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration`. ## Why this is not a duplicate Searched `vllm-project/vllm` issues and PRs (open and all states) for: `cpu-offload-params visual`, `vision tower offload`, `wrap_modules visual`, `UVA offload vision`, `offload visual encoder`, `qwen3.5 offload`. No existing issue or PR requests offloading vision-tower *weights* via `--cpu-offload-params`. Related but distinct work, explicitly not duplicates: - **#41891** (open): offloads multimodal *feature tensors* to CPU after HF processor runs (`_call_hf_processor` → `.to("cpu")`), freeing transient GPU memory. Different problem: runtime features vs. resident tower *weights*. - **#48468 / #51462** (open/closed): wire up the weight offloader in the V2 model runner (the runner never called `set_offloader`). Different root cause — in this checkout the V2 runner already installs the offloader (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py:329`, from #51413); this PR targets a *model-side* gap. - **#43453** (open): skip per-tensor scale parameters inside the UVA offloader. Independent offloader-internal change. ## Test Plan ```bash # Unit tests .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/test_qwen3_5_visual_offload.py -v .venv/bin/ruff check vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_5.py tests/models/test_qwen3_5_visual_offload.py ``` ## Test Result - **Unit tests**: `4 passed` (noop backend passthrough, UVA routing + `visual.` segment naming, prefetch untouched, segment matching). - **Lint**: `All checks passed!` (ruff), formatted. - **End-to-end on `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4`** (architecture `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`, 27B NVFP4, single GPU): - Launch: `--cpu-offload-gb 2 --cpu-offload-params visual` - Log: `INFO [uva.py:58] Total CPU offloaded parameters: 0.86` (matches the 0.86 GiB vision tower). - GPU memory: model load dropped from **21.34 GiB → 20.49 GiB** (~0.85 GiB, consistent with the tower being offloaded). - **Image understanding** (vision tower resident on CPU via UVA zero-copy): correctly described the test image ("A red square and a blue circle ... white background ... 'TEST' ..."). - **Multi-turn chat**: correct arithmetic follow-up (391 + 9 → 400). - No errors, no fallback, `finish_reason: stop` on both modalities. ## Notes - Documentation for the flag's scope remains as-is; the offloader docstring ("Unmatched parameters are not offloaded") is already the user-facing contract, and this PR makes the *vision tower* reachable by that contract. - AI assistance was used in preparing this change (implementation, tests, and this description); the submitting human has reviewed every changed line and run the tests above. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR. - [x] The test plan, providing test commands. - [x] The test results (unit + e2e on real hardware). - [x] Why this is not a duplicate of existing PRs. - [x] AI-assistance statement (per AGENTS.md). </details>

signal.title: [Bugfix] Fix hybrid attention cache miss due to eagle drop
signal.text: ## Purpose This PR fixes an unexpected prefix cache miss bug in hybrid sparse attention models. ## Bug Setup: - Kimi K3, TP8 B300 - Block size: 1536 - Prefix-match unit (PMU): 128 - Cache retention interval: 0 (only cache at prompt boundary) Turn 1: prompt_length=24576, cache_hit_length=0 [expected] Turn 2: prompt_length=50000, cache_hit_length=23040 [expected] Turn 1: prompt_length=24577, cache_hit_length=0 [expected] Turn 2: prompt_length=50000, cache_hit_length=0 [unexpected - full miss] The cause: Mamba caches state at two prompt-boundary positions: - the last block-aligned position for `prompt_length - 1`; and - the last PMU-aligned position, registered as a partial block entry. With `prompt_length=24576` those are 23040 and 24576. With `prompt_length=24577` both collapse to 24576. Full attention is cached up to 24576. The current prefix cache implementation requires Eagle to match one block (128 in this case) past the candidate and then dropping it. The `23040` mamba checkpoint in case 1 satisfies a cache hit where `23040 + 128` is cached in full attention. But in case 2 there is no mamba checkpoint that can satisfy it, and thus leads to a full miss. ## Fix The PR fixes by moving the mamba/SWA cache state position forward when using eagle so that it can match an extra unit/block of full attention cache to drop. ## Test Plan ## Test Result --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details> **BEFORE SUBMITTING, PLEASE READ <https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/contributing>** (anything written below this line will be removed by GitHub Actions)

signal.title: [Frontend][Core] Add release_kv_cache_memory() API
signal.text: ## Motivation Sleep level 2 releases KV cache memory, but it also discards model weights. This is unnecessarily expensive when a framework only needs temporary GPU headroom while keeping the same model instance resident. One concrete use case is model weight update in RL training. The workaround in [verl#7373](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7373) uses `sleep(level=2)` followed by `wake_up(tags=["weights"])` before updating the standalone model. Releasing only the KV cache reduces peak GPU memory and can avoid OOM during the update, without discarding and remapping weights. ## Summary This PR adds `release_kv_cache_memory()` as a dedicated KV-only partial-sleep operation. It discards KV cache allocations, keeps model weights resident, and pauses scheduling until the released memory is restored with the existing `wake_up()` API. ## Implementation ### Call flow The offline and server entry points converge on the same engine path: ```text LLM.release_kv_cache_memory() -> LLMEngine ---------\ -> EngineCore POST /release_kv_cache_memory -> EngineClient ------/ | v Executor.discard(("kv_cache",)) | v Worker -> SleepModeBackend | v CuMem/XPU allocator.discard(tags) ``` `EngineCore` first pauses the scheduler and clears the prefix cache. Depending on the selected pause mode, it either handles existing requests immediately or waits for in-flight requests to finish before asking all workers to discard KV cache allocations. The scheduler remains paused after release; a discard failure also fails closed instead of resuming scheduling with potentially partially unmapped memory. At allocator level, only mapped allocations tagged `kv_cache` are unmapped and released, without a CPU backup. Per-allocation mapping state prevents duplicate unmap or map operations when release, sleep, and wake-up calls are mixed. ### Interaction with sleep levels `release_kv_cache_memory()` is treated as a KV-only partial sleep. A later `sleep(1)` or `sleep(2)` can upgrade that state to a full sleep: | Current state | Operation | Result | | --- | --- | --- | | Fully awake | `release_kv_cache_memory()` | KV cache discarded, weights resident, scheduler paused | | KV-only sleeping | `sleep(1)` | Weights offloaded, KV cache remains discarded | | KV-only sleeping | `sleep(2)` | Weights discarded, KV cache remains discarded | | KV-only sleeping | `wake_up(["kv_cache"])` | KV cache remapped and scheduling resumed | | Full sleep | `wake_up(["kv_cache"])` | Only KV cache remapped; weights remain sleeping and scheduling stays paused | | Full sleep | `wake_up()` | All allocations restored and scheduling resumed | The executor tracks the exact internal state with `sleeping_tags`. Scheduling is resumed only after no sleeping tags remain. ### Logging and observability This PR reuses the existing sleep-state logger instead of adding a dedicated `kv_cache_released` Prometheus state. After KV release, the existing metrics report `awake=0`, `weights_offloaded=0`, and `discard_all=0`: the engine is not available for scheduling, but it is not in sleep level 1 or 2. The precise resource state remains available internally through `sleeping_tags`. There is currently no requirement to monitor KV-only release separately. If that becomes useful, a dedicated Prometheus state and its transition logic can be added in a follow-up change. ## Scope The public API intentionally supports only KV cache release. Existing sleep levels already cover the other current cases: - `sleep(1)` offloads weights and discards KV cache memory. - `sleep(2)` discards all managed GPU memory. A generic public tag API would also need to define whether each tag is discarded or offloaded, increasing the API surface and overlapping with existing sleep semantics. More fine-grained public memory management can be discussed when a concrete additional use case appears; the internal `discard(tags)` path remains extensible. ## Related work - [vLLM#42658](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42658) explores generic tag-level sleep management. This PR instead provides a smaller, explicit end-to-end API for the known KV-only use case. - [vLLM#46438](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46438) contains related allocator-level selective-discard work. - [verl#7373](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7373) demonstrates the downstream model-update use case and its current sleep/wake workaround. This PR does not duplicate the generic public API proposed in #42658; its scope and semantics are intentionally narrower. ## Tests ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/v1/executor/test_executor.py::test_discard_records_sleep_state_after_worker_failure \ tests/v1/executor/test_executor.py::test_sleep_after_kv_cache_discard \ tests/v1/engine/test_sleep_lifecycle.py \ -q -o addopts='' ``` Result: `5 passed`. GPU-dependent end-to-end coverage is also included for offline `LLM.release_kv_cache_memory()` and the development server endpoint and metrics. ```bash pre-commit run ``` Result: passed. Model evaluation is not applicable because this change does not affect model outputs or accuracy. ## AI assistance AI assistance was used to review the implementation and draft this description. The submitter reviewed the resulting changes and test scope.

signal.title: [Bug]: GLM-5.2 MTP accepts 0% of drafts on MI355X (gfx950); disabling expert parallelism hits hipErrorIllegalAddress
signal.text: ### Your current environment `collect_env.py` output isn't available (the nodes were tied up); details taken from the container image and run logs: ``` vLLM : 0.27.1+rocm723 PyTorch : 2.11.0+gitd0c8b1f ROCm : 7.2.3 Container : vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.27.1 GPU : 8x AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950) amdgpu : 6.16.13, kernel 6.8.0-137-generic Model : amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 (quark MXFP4) MoE backend: aiter ``` ### 🐛 Describe the bug GLM-5.2 MTP starts fine on MI355X and then accepts **zero** draft tokens. Speculative decoding is pure overhead — it drafts at ~40-230 tok/s and accepts none of it. ```bash export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 vllm serve /models/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 \ --served-model-name amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 \ --trust-remote-code \ --async-scheduling \ --distributed-executor-backend mp \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --enable-expert-parallel \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.80 \ --max-model-len 262144 \ --max-num-seqs 2 \ --moe-backend aiter \ --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \ --tool-call-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \ --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' ``` Startup resolves as expected — target `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`, draft `DeepSeekMTPModel` — then: ``` SpecDecoding metrics: Mean acceptance length: 1.00, Accepted throughput: 0.00 tokens/s, Drafted throughput: 37.80 tokens/s, Accepted: 0 tokens, Drafted: 378 tokens, Per-position acceptance rate: 0.000, 0.000, 0.000, Avg Draft acceptance rate: 0.0% ``` What I tried: | # | change | result | |---|---|---| | A | as above | `acceptance length 1.00`, per-position `0.000, 0.000, 0.000` | | B | `num_speculative_tokens: 1` | `acceptance length 1.00`, per-position `0.000` | | C | `--kv-cache-dtype auto` | `acceptance length 1.05`, per-position `0.046, 0.000, 0.000` | | D | drop `--enable-expert-parallel` | crashes, see below | B rules out the startup warning's explanation: ``` WARNING [speculative.py:912] Enabling num_speculative_tokens > 1 will run multiple times on same MTP layer, which may result in lower acceptance rate ``` Position 0 is 0.000 at `num_speculative_tokens=1` too, so re-running GLM-5.2's single nextn layer isn't what's breaking this — the very first draft token is never accepted. C says fp8 KV contributes but isn't the cause: bf16 KV lifts position 0 from 0.000 to ~0.05, still far from usable. D, without expert parallelism, dies during memory profiling instead: ``` terminate called after throwing an instance of 'c10::AcceleratorError' Search for `hipErrorIllegalAddress' in https://rocm.docs.amd.com/projects/HIP/en/latest/index.html Exception raised from ~CUDAGraph at /app/pytorch/aten/src/ATen/hip/HIPGraph.cpp:302 ``` I also checked whether the unquantized nextn layer is being mis-handled by the quark loader — it isn't, as far as I can tell. Layer 78 is genuinely unquantized in this checkpoint (789 `.weight`, 0 `.weight_scale`, 781 entries in `quantization_config.exclude`), but `DeepSeekMTPModel` sets `mtp_start_layer_idx = num_hidden_layers` and names it `model.layers.78`, which is what the exclude patterns match on. So the exclusions should apply. For reference, SGLang on the same node with the same checkpoint gets a working draft: ``` Decode batch, #running-req: 1, ..., accept len: 3.00, accept rate: 0.67, cuda graph: True ``` This may be the same root cause as #48568 (MI300X / gfx942), which points at MTP's `mtp_block` reduce-scattering under `--enable-expert-parallel` with TP>1 while the predictor layer doesn't restore full tokens. Filing separately because the symptom here is different in a way that matters: on gfx950 there's no hang and no error — it silently produces a 0% acceptance rate, so a benchmark run looks healthy and just reports worse numbers. Disabling EP also fails differently (illegal address rather than working around it). Happy to run further diagnostics on gfx950 if that helps. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] I have searched for similar issues and read the [documentation](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/).

signal.title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Refuse block-FP8 in MarlinFP8.can_implement
signal.text: ## Summary Refuse block-FP8 layers in `MarlinFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel.can_implement` so the dispatcher falls through to the next supported kernel (typically `TritonFp8BlockScaledMMKernel`). ## The bug `csrc/quantization/marlin/marlin.cu` TORCH_CHECKs `b_scales.size(1) == size_n` for the 2-D scales path. Block-quantized FP8 layers ship `weight_scale_inv` of shape `[N_blocks_n, N_blocks_k]` — e.g. DSv4-Flash's `compressor.fused_wqa_wkv` at `[12, 32]` for `(1536, 4096)` weight with block `[128, 128]`. Marlin's per-channel kernel-side expectation is `[K/group, size_n]`. The check fires. This is reachable in production today because: 1. Consumer-Blackwell operators set `VLLM_TEST_FORCE_FP8_MARLIN=1` to keep NVFP4-MoE alive on SM 12.0 (no other NVFP4 MoE backend currently lights up on RTX PRO 6000). 2. With the env var set, `MarlinFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel.is_supported` returns True for SM ≥ 89. 3. Marlin is at priority 4 in `_POSSIBLE_FP8_BLOCK_KERNELS[CUDA]`, ahead of `TritonFp8BlockScaledMMKernel`. 4. `CompressedTensorsW8A8Fp8.apply_weights` → `Fp8LinearOp` → dispatcher picks MarlinFP8 for block-FP8 layers → `b_scales` shape mismatch. Symptom: `RuntimeError: b_scales dim 1 = 32 is not size_n = 1536` at `profile_run`. Reproducible with `canada-quant/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4-FP8-MTP` on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell. ## The fix `can_implement` is the canonical place to refuse layers a kernel can't actually serve. Per-group activation quant scales is the dispatch-side signal for block-quantization (see `init_fp8_linear_kernel` at `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py:521`). ```python @classmethod def can_implement(cls, c) -> tuple[bool, str | None]: try: if c.activation_quant_key.scale.group_shape.is_per_group(): return False, "MarlinFP8 cannot serve block-FP8 layers; ..." except Exception: pass return True, None ``` Defensive try/except because the config shape can vary across schemes; if introspection fails, we keep the prior permissive behavior. ## Validation Verified on `canada-quant/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4-FP8-MTP` (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, SM 12.0, TP=4) with `VLLM_TEST_FORCE_FP8_MARLIN=1`: - **Before**: `RuntimeError: b_scales dim 1 = 32 is not size_n = 1536` at `profile_run` (3-frame trace pinned to `attention.py:454 attn_gemm_parallel_execute` → `fused_wqa_wkv` → `compressed_tensors.py:851 scheme.apply_weights` → `marlin_utils_fp8.py:69 apply_fp8_marlin_linear` → `marlin.cu:701`). - **After**: dispatcher picks `TritonFp8BlockScaledMMKernel`, engine init completes (43.4 GiB / 33.8s weight load, MTP shared embeddings, profile_run + cudagraph capture succeed), `"Application startup complete"` reached, smoke completion `"The capital of France is" → " Paris, which is located in the Île-de"` (10 tokens, coherent). ## Risk - 19-line change in one file, no behavior change for any layer that isn't per-group-activation-quantized (i.e. tensor / channel / token strategies are unaffected). - The `try/except` on config introspection means even if a future scheme's quant_key doesn't have `.scale.group_shape`, we keep the prior permissive return. - The dispatcher's existing fallback chain handles the actual block-FP8 serving — Marlin was never the right kernel for these layers; this just stops it from claiming it can. ## Adjacent - `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/attention.py:377` directly reads `self.wo_a.weight_scale_inv` — but only `MarlinFP8.process_weights_after_loading` renames `weight_scale` → `weight_scale_inv`. Once this PR routes the layer to a non-Marlin kernel, the bare read AttributeErrors. Follow-up commit / PR adds a `getattr` fallback. - Closes one strand of #43564 (the load-time crash on consumer Blackwell). The numerical-correctness concern documented in that issue is orthogonal to this PR and remains under investigation. Disclosure (per [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/AGENTS.md#accountability)): authored with AI assistance; the code path was traced end-to-end from the runtime trace, the fix shape was confirmed by reading the dispatcher (`vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py:502+`) and the kernel selection priority list, and the patch was tested on a downstream venv built from `jasl/vllm@a02a3778f` against the canada-quant artifact. Mainline-build verification is in progress; will report results on this PR. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signal.title: [Bug]: `find_mm_placeholders` may return an incorrect position for `PromptInsertion`
signal.text: ### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Description When `PromptInsertion` inserts tokens that overlap with adjacent tokens in the original prompt, `find_mm_placeholders` may locate an earlier occurrence instead of the tokens inserted by the prompt update. For example: - Original prompt contains `[32000]` at index 3. - The insertion target is `[32000]`. - The inserted placeholder tokens are `[32000, 32000]`. After applying the update, the resulting sequence around the target is: ```text [..., 32000, 32000, 32000, ...] original inserted ``` The inserted placeholder starts at index 4. However, `find_mm_placeholders` scans the resulting prompt for `[32000, 32000]` and finds the sequence starting at index 3, which includes one token from the original prompt. ## Expected behavior The placeholder position should refer to the tokens inserted by `PromptInsertion`, so `start_idx` should be 4. ## Actual behavior `find_mm_placeholders` reports `start_idx=3`. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signal.title: [Core][Multimodal] Skip redundant placeholder scan when token match succeeds
signal.text:
## Purpose CLOSE #52924 `_apply_prompt_updates` first calls `_apply_token_matches`. If any token match fails, it falls back to `_apply_text_matches`. The current code always calls `_find_mm_placeholders` after matching, even when all token matches succeed. This call scans for placeholders again through the following path: `_find_mm_placeholders` → `find_mm_placeholders` → `_iter_placeholders` → `prompt[start:end] == content_tokens`. The table below shows the placeholder scan time at different image resolutions with 2,500 input text tokens: | Function | 480p | 720p | 1080p | 3k | | ----------------------------- | -------- | -------- | --------- | --------- | | `_apply_prompt_updates` | 5.126 ms | 9.542 ms | 23.728 ms | 75.347 ms | | `_find_mm_placeholders` | 4.556 ms | 8.950 ms | 23.074 ms | 74.241 ms | | `find_mm_placeholders` | 4.513 ms | 8.908 ms | 23.030 ms | 74.198 ms | | `_iter_placeholders` | 4.328 ms | 8.710 ms | 22.781 ms | 73.965 ms | | slice compare | 2.934 ms | 7.150 ms | 20.977 ms | 71.419 ms | | slice compare / total | 57% | 75% | 88% | 95% | Each function in the scan path takes almost as long as `_apply_prompt_updates`. This shows that placeholder scanning takes most of the total time. The `slice compare` row measures `prompt[start_idx:end_idx_full] == content_tokens_full`, which is the main bottleneck. As image resolution increases, this comparison grows from 2.934 ms to 71.419 ms and from 57% to 95% of the total `_apply_prompt_updates` time. When all token matches succeed, token matching already knows each placeholder position. The code does not need to scan the prompt again. This PR collects placeholders during token matching and returns early when all matches succeed. It therefore skips `_find_mm_placeholders`. If any token match fails, the code still uses the existing text fallback path. The following benchmarks compare `_apply_prompt_updates` before and after this change. The first benchmark fixes the image resolution and varies the input text length. The second fixes the input text length and varies the image resolution. 1. Input text length comparison (fixed image resolutions: 720p and 3k)

Image resolution comparison (fixed input text length: 2,500 tokens) | resolution | baseline | this PR | speedup | | ---------- | --------- | -------- | ------- | | 480p | 5.126 ms | 0.601 ms | 8.5× | | 720p | 9.542 ms | 0.725 ms | 13.2× | | 1080p | 23.728 ms | 0.944 ms | 25.1× | | 3k | 75.347 ms | 1.712 ms | 44.0× | As the input text grows, the speedup increases from 2.6× to 13.9× at 720p and from 2.9× to 50.9× at 3k. With 2,500 input text tokens, the optimized `_apply_prompt_updates` takes 0.601–1.712 ms across the tested image resolutions. This gives an 8.5×–44.0× speedup. Both benchmarks skip `_find_mm_placeholders` when all token matches succeed. ## Behavior Token-matching path: the code returns early only when every token match succeeds across all modalities (`update_idx is not None`). The unit tests show that the new path produces the same `new_token_ids` as the old path for general token-matching cases. `_apply_token_matches_with_placeholders` collects placeholders directly and removes empty modality lists. Text fallback path: if any token match fails, the code still calls `_apply_text_matches` and `_find_mm_placeholders`. This PR does not change the fallback path. For typical `PromptReplacement` updates, direct collection and rescanning return the same placeholder positions. For `PromptInsertion`, inserted tokens may match adjacent tokens in the original prompt. A rescan can then select an earlier range that includes an original token. Direct collection records the exact range inserted by the update. The issue below tracks this case. ## Related work and performance ### Related issue Related to [#52924](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52924). This issue describes how `find_mm_placeholders` can return the wrong start position when tokens inserted by `PromptInsertion` overlap with adjacent tokens in the original prompt. This PR records the inserted token position directly. It does not treat an adjacent original token as part of the placeholder. ### Related PR Merged PR [#51774](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51774) also improves multimodal prompt updates, but it targets a different bottleneck. This PR builds placeholders directly when all token matches succeed and skips the redundant `_find_mm_placeholders` scan. The results below measure this PR on top of #51774. In the tables, `#51774` is the baseline after that PR merged. `#51774 + This PR` adds this PR. 1. **10,000 placeholders synthetic benchmark** The setup matches #51774. It uses 1,000,000 input tokens and 10,000 image placeholders. Each placeholder expands to 50 tokens, so the updated prompt contains 1,490,000 tokens. This PR reduces average latency by 45.0%. | Function | Version | Run 1 | Run 2 | Run 3 | **Average** | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | `_apply_prompt_updates` | #51774 | 466.451 ms | 462.842 ms | 462.278 ms | **463.857 ms** | | `_apply_prompt_updates` | #51774 + This PR | 255.581 ms | 255.501 ms | 254.922 ms | **255.335 ms** | 2. **3k image with 2,500 input text tokens** We measured 64 requests with one 1728×3072 image and 2,500 input text tokens. Average latency drops from 3.432 ms to 1.409 ms. Maximum latency drops from 13.749 ms to 1.481 ms, an 89.2% reduction. The new maximum is only 5.1% above the average. The standard deviation drops from 2.587 ms to 0.024 ms, which shows more stable latency. | Function | Version | Requests | **Average** | **Maximum** | Std | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | `_apply_prompt_updates` | #51774 | 64 | **3.432 ms** | **13.749 ms** | 2.587 ms | | `_apply_prompt_updates` | #51774 + This PR | 64 | **1.409 ms** | **1.481 ms** | 0.024 ms | ## Test Plan This PR adds `test_apply_token_matches_with_placeholders`. The test reuses the five tokenized cases from `test_find_update_tokens` and covers: - `PromptInsertion` and `PromptReplacement`; - multimodal item counts of 0, 1, and 2; - matching `new_token_ids` against manually constructed expected output when token matching succeeds; - matching directly collected `PlaceholderFeaturesInfo` fields (`modality`, `item_idx`, `start_idx`, and `tokens`) against manually constructed expected output; - keeping failed token matches on the existing text fallback path. We also keep the refactored `test_find_update_tokens` to verify that existing token-update results do not change. We run `test_apply_matches_many_shared_targets_scales_linearly` to verify that the new helper still uses the linearly scaling prompt-update planner. ```bash pytest tests/multimodal/test_processing.py::test_apply_token_matches_with_placeholders \ tests/multimodal/test_processing.py::test_find_update_tokens \ tests/multimodal/test_processing.py::test_apply_matches_many_shared_targets_scales_linearly \ -q ``` ## Test Result ```text 11 passed, 2 warnings in 6.30s ```

signal.title: [Bugfix] Pick KV cache block size from all attention backends
signal.text: ## Purpose Fixes #48286. `Platform.update_block_size_for_backend()` only consulted the first non-SSM attention backend when auto-picking the KV cache block size. Models that mix a permissive main backend with a stricter secondary one — e.g. DSA models whose `DeepseekV32IndexerBackend` only supports block size 64 — kept the default of 16 and crashed later in `select_common_block_size()`: ``` ValueError: No common block size for 16. ``` This change collects all distinct non-SSM backends and takes the largest preferred block size, so the indexer's requirement is honored no matter which layer registers first. Not a duplicate: no open or closed PR addresses #48286 (checked issue timeline and recent PRs). AI assistance was used for this PR; the change was reviewed and tests were run before submitting. ## Test Plan ``` pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py::test_update_block_size_for_backend_honors_strictest_backend ``` The new test fails on main (`assert 16 == 64`) and passes with this change. Also verified against the real backend on CPU: ```python select_common_block_size(16, [DeepseekV32IndexerBackend]) # reproduces the reported ValueError Platform.update_block_size_for_backend(cfg) # with an indexer layer present cfg.cache_config.block_size # -> 64 ``` No GPU available locally, so no e2e serving run of a DSA model; the sibling `select_common_block_size` unit tests and `pre-commit run` (ruff, mypy) pass. ## Test Result ``` $ pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py -k block_size -q 5 passed, 30 deselected in 1.97s ``` (4 pre-existing block-size tests plus the new one.)

This mismatch violates the block count assertion and causes the process to abort. I printed `local_num_tokens` and `remote_num_tokens` on the decode side and found a discrepancy: `local_num_token` = `remote_num_tokens` + 1. If `remote_num_tokens % block_size == 0`, then the `num_blocks` in the decode will be 1 more than `remote_blocks`, leading to a fatal error. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signal.title: [Bugfix][DeepSeek V4] Handle trailing system messages in prompt rendering
signal.text: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Purpose Co-authored-by: laolaoPlayer <2584941823@qq.com> Address the DeepSeek V4 trailing-system prompt-rendering edge case reported in [#40854](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/40854#issuecomment-4864596205) and [#46256](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/46256) and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/11951. When the final message has the `system` role, `render_message` leaves the prompt at a bare system-message boundary instead of appending the assistant transition. Generation can then stop immediately and return empty content. This change appends the existing assistant/thinking transition only when the `system` message is truly the final message. Existing `user` and `developer` behavior is unchanged, and no transition is inserted before a later `user`, `assistant`, or `latest_reminder` message. Open PR #43937 addresses the same symptom with an unconditional `system` allow-list entry. That broader condition changes existing `system -> latest_reminder` golden fixtures. This PR uses a trailing-only guard to preserve those prompts. The difference was documented in [#46256](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/46256#issuecomment-5204237778). No documentation update is needed because this fixes existing tokenizer behavior without adding an option or API. ## Test Plan - Add a regression test for `system -> user -> system`. - Add a non-regression test for `user -> assistant -> system -> user`. - Run the complete DeepSeek V4 tokenizer test file: ```bash VLLM_PLUGINS="" \ PYTHONPATH=/workspace/vllm-cpu-test-bootstrap-pr:/workspace/vllm-pr-c14a568e2 \ /workspace/vllm-pr-c14a568e2/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ -p no:cacheprovider \ --confcutdir=/workspace/vllm-pr-c14a568e2/tests/tokenizers_ \ /workspace/vllm-pr-c14a568e2/tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v4.py ``` - Run Ruff check, Ruff format check, and `git diff --check`. - Reuse the completed real-environment validation through the production router. ## Test Result - Before the fix: `1 failed, 1 passed`; the trailing-system prompt was missing `<｜Assistant｜></think>`. - Focused regression tests after the fix: `2 passed`. - Complete `tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v4.py`: `28 passed in 14.57s`. - Ruff check: `All checks passed!`. - Ruff format check: `2 files already formatted`. - `git diff --check upstream/main..HEAD`: passed. - Real environment: four scenarios were each run three times after deploying the source patch to all four nodes and restarting the cluster. All 12/12 requests passed. The target case returned `"4"` instead of an empty response, with no regression in the other scenarios. See the [full report](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51262#issuecomment-5204365444). - No additional NPU run was performed after rebasing because the source patch was unchanged. ## AI Assistance AI assistance was used to inspect the renderer control flow, implement the regression coverage and fix, compare related open work, and prepare validation. The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests listed above. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose and related issues are documented. - [x] The unit-test and static-check commands are provided. - [x] Unit-test, static-check, and real-environment results are recorded. - [x] Documentation impact was considered; no documentation change is needed. </details>

signal.title: [Bugfix][KV Cache] Fix incremental multimodal block hashing
signal.text: ## Purpose `Request.append_output_token_ids()` computes block hashes incrementally when a new full block is completed. If that block overlaps multiple multimodal features, the existing incremental path starts from only the final feature and can omit an earlier feature in the same block. The resulting hash then differs from a freshly constructed request with identical tokens and multimodal input. This change starts multimodal hashing from the first feature overlapping the new block, using the existing `get_mm_features_in_window()` helper. It adds a regression test for both supported hash functions and checks that incremental and fresh construction produce identical block hashes. Addresses the multimodal hashing subproblem identified in #49377 and #49448. The prior investigation and patch direction in #49448 are credited to @edwardlong-ctrl, who is also attributed in the commit trailer. This does not duplicate an open PR: - #49448 was closed unmerged by its author. - #49619 rehashes after streaming-session token replacement; it does not change the ordinary `append_output_token_ids()` path fixed here. - #50114 skips no-op hasher calls before a full-block boundary; it retains the last-feature assumption addressed here. - Searches for `49377 in:body` and multimodal block-hash keywords found no open PR implementing this fix. AI assistance was used in developing this PR. ## Test Plan The repository uv environment is denoted by `<venv>` below. ```bash <venv>/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py \ -k 'incremental_append_with_multiple_mm_features' <venv>/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py \ -k 'request_block_hasher or hash_tokens_different_mm_input' <venv>/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py ruff check vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py \ tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py ruff format --check vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py \ tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py git diff --check origin/main...HEAD ``` An additional seeded local differential test compares incremental hashing with fresh hashing across randomized multimodal layouts and block boundaries. ## Test Result - New regression: 2 passed, 77 deselected. - Neighboring request block-hasher tests: 8 passed, 71 deselected. - Randomized differential check: 500 layouts and 1,147 completed block boundaries; every incremental hash list matched fresh construction. - Ruff checks, formatting checks, and `git diff --check`: passed. - Complete test file: 61 passed, 18 failed. All 18 failures occur while `ModelConfig` attempts to access Hugging Face in the network-restricted test environment; they do not reach the modified block-hashing path. - Model evaluation: not applicable; this changes cache-key construction and does not change model execution or generated outputs.

signal.title: turboquant decode attetnion optimization
signal.text: ## Purpose This work optimizes the TurboQuant decode path in vLLM while preserving compressed KV-cache semantics. It introduces three related changes: 1. A page-local KV-cache ABI shared by cache store, decode, dequantization, and continuation-prefill paths. 2. Fused store kernels that quantize, pack, and write directly to the new ABI without an intermediate layout conversion. 3. An optimized fused decode-attention operator. ## Support matrix The new page-local ABI is fully integrated across the TurboQuant cache lifecycle. All cache producers and consumers—including the MSE and FP8 store paths, decode attention, full dequantization, and continuation-prefill—use the same layout. The runtime contains neither a legacy-layout branch nor an ABI conversion operator. The table below describes only the coverage of the optimized decode-attention operator: | Capability | Supported range | |---|---| | Attention | Full causal self-attention, `q_len = 1` | | Query/output dtype | BF16 | | Head dimension | 64, 128, 256 | | Head geometry | MHA and GQA | | Page size | 16, 32, 64, 128 | | Cache preset | K4V4-NC | | Attention scale | `1 / sqrt(head_dim)` | | Execution mode | Eager and CUDA Graph | | GPU | NVIDIA H100 / SM90 | Unsupported fast-path configurations continue to use the existing compressed TurboQuant implementation.

signal.title: [Perf] Scale num_warps with tile size in Triton reshape-and-cache kernels
signal.text: ## Purpose Both CUDA launch sites in `triton_reshape_and_cache_flash.py` hardcode `num_warps = 16` (512 threads) regardless of tile size. When the tile is smaller, the surplus warps hold thread slots without doing work, which limits how many blocks stay resident on an SM. `_reshape_cache_per_token_head` in the same file already derives the count from the shape — `min(16, max(1, head_size_padded // 32))` — and so does the CUDA version (`dim3 block(std::min(num_heads * head_size, 512))`). This applies that rule at the two remaining sites. Only the launch geometry changes; the kernels write the same bytes to the same slots. Tiles of 512 elements or more still get 16 warps, so the shapes the original benchmarks covered are unaffected. ROCm and XPU take a separate branch and are untouched. ## Test plan ``` pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py -k diffkv python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_reshape_and_cache_flash.py --implementation triton --mode cudagraph --num-heads 2 --head-size 64 ``` The DiffKV kernel had no direct coverage, so the new test checks against a PyTorch reference that key and value land in their own halves of the packed cache row — three `(head_size_k, head_size_v)` pairs, three block sizes, two dtypes, both cache dtypes — and that padded tokens leave the cache untouched. `--num-heads 8 --head-size 64` gives n = 512, where both versions launch identically, so that row is the control. ## Test result 18 tests pass on an A100 on both the patched and the unpatched kernel (18 more skip below SM89, where the Triton fp8 path is unsupported). Kernel latency on an A100-SXM4-80GB, median of 5 repetitions alternating patched and unpatched, CUDA graph mode. Negative means faster. Rows are labelled by `n = num_kv_heads * head_size`, which sets `TILE_SIZE`. | config | 1024 tok | 4096 | 16384 | 65536 | |---|---|---|---|---| | n=512 (control) | −0.6% | +0.2% | +0.3% | −0.05% | | n=256 | −11.2% | −26.0% | −33.5% | −45.1% | | n=128 | −10.6% | −29.6% | −50.9% | −67.7% | | n=64 | −9.2% | −27.3% | −49.1% | −73.0% | | DiffKV 192/128 (MiMo-V2 shape) | −29.8% | −40.9% | −44.6% | −47.1% | | DiffKV 256/256 | −31.9% | −41.5% | −45.2% | −46.2% | Below ~1000 tokens there are fewer blocks than the GPU has SMs, so nothing overlaps and there is no effect. Above that the gain grows with the token count, as more blocks fit per SM and more stores are in flight. Repeated three times across two A100 variants: the control stayed within 0.08% and varying the DiffKV cache strides or slot pattern moved results by under 0.15 points. End-to-end, gpt-oss on A100 (sinks need FA3/4, so Triton is the only backend vLLM can pick on sm80). `n` is per rank, so TP is what brings gpt-oss into range: 512 at TP=1 (unchanged), 256 at TP=2, 128 at TP=4. Each cell is the mean of 3 runs of `llm.generate()` over 128 prompts of 2048 token ids, `max_tokens=1`, prefix caching off, order alternating. | config | `num_warps = 16` | scaled | delta | |---|---|---|---| | gpt-oss-20b, 2×A100, TP=2, 16384-token steps | 7.2094 s | 7.1951 s | −0.198% | | gpt-oss-120b, 4×A100, TP=4, 16384-token steps | 6.7100 s | 6.6816 s | −0.424% | | gpt-oss-120b, 4×A100, TP=4, 65536-token steps | 6.5420 s | 6.5191 s | −0.349% | Every scaled run beat every `num_warps = 16` run. Larger steps do not help: the per-call saving is superlinear in tokens (25.1 µs at 16384, 171.4 µs at 65536) but the step count falls by the same factor. The DiffKV path has no e2e number — MiMo-V2-Flash does not fit in 4×A100. `ncu` at three shapes confirms the change does what it claims and nothing else: `launch__block_size` and `waves_per_multiprocessor` scale exactly as `min(16, TILE_SIZE // 32) * 32` predicts (unchanged at the control, −75% at n=128, −50% for DiffKV), while DRAM bytes move 0.1% and global store sectors are identical. Correctness rests on the new test rather than those counters, which is also why I ran no accuracy evals. ## Notes Developed with Claude Code. I reviewed every line and ran the tests myself. Duplicate check: no open or merged PR changes `num_warps` at either site. #46060 rewrites the capability check in both launch blocks of this file — I will rebase if it lands first. #47535 adds an opt-in CUDA DiffKV op and keeps Triton as the default, which is the path this speeds up.

signal.title: [ROCm][Perf] Kimi-K3 Fused kernels for KDA prefill
signal.text: ## Purpose On ROCm, Kimi-K3's KDA prefill chunk path currently runs a pipeline of nine Triton kernels. This PR adds a fusion path for ROCm that fuses these operations based on the characteristics of their workloads: **Prologue**: The kernel that prepares the chunks leading up to the recurrent state update. It normalizes `q` and `k`, cumsum gate into `g` and `beta`, builds `Aqk` in each chunk, inverts the transition `Akk`, and produces w and u. Each 64-token chunk can be processed in parallel, so it is dispatched in `(chunk, head)` grids for parallelism. **Chunk recurrence**: This does the remaining recurrence state update. For each sequence, the state update is sequential, and dispatching workgroups on the number of sequences can lead to low CU occupancy. This path breaks a sequence down into groups of chunks where the number of groups is determined by device capability, and takes a two-pass approach to increase parallelism within sequences: - Pass 1: Each group walks a recurrence from a zero state and records how it transforms an incoming state - Perform a scan across groups from a sequence to recover each group's true initial state - Pass 2: Re-walks each group from the correct start to produce outputs The fusion chain is ~2x faster than the Triton chain, especially in the chunk recurrance stage. E2E tests shows this reduces TTFT by ~4%. | tokens / seqs | Triton chunk stage | fused chunk stage | speedup | Triton chain | fused chain | speedup | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1024 / 1 | 117.4 µs | 60.7 µs | 1.93× | 139.2 µs | 79.1 µs | 1.76× | | 4096 / 1 | 301.1 µs | 113.7 µs | 2.65× | 330.5 µs | 143.0 µs | 2.31× | | 4096 / 2 | 232.7 µs | 110.0 µs | 2.12× | 278.0 µs | 154.7 µs | 1.80× | | 4096 / 8 | 192.5 µs | 84.5 µs | 2.28× | 256.6 µs | 145.2 µs | 1.77× | | 16384 / 1 | 1174.2 µs | 335.9 µs | 3.50× | 1232.4 µs | 393.5 µs | 3.13× | The fusion path is packed into two pytorch interfaces that serve as a replacement for the original Triton chain. An additional engine argument option `--kda-prefill-backend=fused` is added to enable this fused path, and it's set as the default when it is supported. The kernels have only been tested on gfx950 at the moment, so its build and dispatch is guarded on gfx950 for now. ## Test Plan Unit tests for the fused kernels lm_eval with gsm8k on MI355X Server command ``` VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \ VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2_A8W4=1 \ AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 \ VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 \ vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \ --trust-remote-code \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \ --load-format auto \ --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \ --max-num-seqs 128 \ --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \ --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","custom_ops":["+fused_rms_norm_gated"]}' \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --kda-prefill-backend ["fused" | "triton"] ``` Benchmark ``` vllm bench serve --model moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --backend vllm --trust-remote-code --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 --max-concurrency "$CONC" --num-prompts $((CONC * 4)) --temperature 0 --ignore-eos ``` lm_eval ``` lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --model_args "model=moonshotai/Kimi-K3,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=64,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False,max_gen_toks=8192,timeout=3600" --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 20 --apply_chat_template --fewshot_as_multiturn --seed 1234 ``` ## Test Result gsm8k on MI355X |Tasks|Version| Filter |n-shot| Metric | |Value | |Stderr| |-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:| |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 20|exact_match|↑ |0.9765|± |0.0042| | | |strict-match | 20|exact_match|↑ |0.9773|± |0.0041| E2E benchmark | ISL/OSL | Conc | Config | Total tokens/s | Delta (%) | Total reqs/s | Delta (%) | Output tokens/s | Delta (%) | mean TTFT (ms) | Delta (%) | mean TPOT (ms) | Delta (%) | mean ITL (ms) | Delta (%) | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 8192/1024 | 16 | baseline | 4009.6 | — | 0.4351 | — | 445.5 | — | 2275.4 | — | 33.6 | — | 33.6 | — | | 8192/1024 | 16 | fused | 4053.2 | +1.1 | 0.4398 | +1.1 | 450.4 | +1.1 | 2174.8 | -4.4 | 33.3 | -0.9 | 33.3 | -0.9 | | 8192/1024 | 32 | baseline | 6239.1 | — | 0.6770 | — | 693.2 | — | 3419.0 | — | 42.7 | — | 42.7 | — | | 8192/1024 | 32 | fused | 6323.0 | +1.3 | 0.6861 | +1.3 | 702.6 | +1.3 | 3267.1 | -4.4 | 42.2 | -1.1 | 42.2 | -1.1 | | 8192/1024 | 64 | baseline | 8309.7 | — | 0.9017 | — | 923.3 | — | 5712.0 | — | 63.3 | — | 63.3 | — | | 8192/1024 | 64 | fused | 8498.2 | +2.3 | 0.9221 | +2.3 | 944.2 | +2.3 | 5460.5 | -4.4 | 62.1 | -2.0 | 62.1 | -2.0 | | 8192/1024 | 128 | baseline | 10251.1 | — | 1.1123 | — | 1139.0 | — | 10471.0 | — | 101.1 | — | 101.1 | — | | 8192/1024 | 128 | fused | 10559.0 | +3.0 | 1.1457 | +3.0 | 1173.2 | +3.0 | 10023.7 | -4.3 | 98.3 | -2.8 | 98.3 | -2.8 | --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signal.title: [Bug] Streaming completions end with no finish_reason / no [DONE] — xgrammar "Failed to advance FSM" is one logged trigger, but some drops are fully silent (no engine error)
signal.text: ### Summary While serving a Qwen 3.8 27B NVFP4 checkpoint with `--enable-auto-tool-choice` (xgrammar FSM backend for tool-call constrained decoding), the engine logs a `Failed to advance FSM` ERROR for some requests, and the HTTP SSE stream for those requests terminates **without a final `finish_reason` chunk and without the `data: [DONE]` sentinel**. Downstream clients (e.g. an OpenAI-compatible SDK consumer) receive only partial content and cannot distinguish a normal completion from a truncated one. Importantly, the "no `finish_reason` / no `[DONE]`" symptom is **broader than the logged FSM error**: on the same instance we also observed client-visible mid-stream drops where the engine logs **nothing** — no `Failed to advance FSM`, no ERROR, no disconnect, no abort — while the engine is healthy and actively serving. The API-server layer logs no error, warning, or client-disconnect event for the affected request in either case. So the missing terminal chunk is the real user-facing bug; the FSM failure is one observed (logged) trigger, and a clean-engine occurrence suggests the failure path can be silent. Per the FSM error message itself ("Please file an issue"), filing here. ### Environment - vLLM: `0.26.1rc1.dev298+g1ea84d74b.d20260803` (pip inside container) - Image: `eugr/spark-vllm:latest` (sha256:1d335d4fb3d1c5dce6e79f87a4019a04e98fa9ceb7b894d50d413159382ab6c6) - Hardware: NVIDIA GB10 (Grace Blackwell, sm_121a), CUDA 13.x (eugr image) - Model: Qwen 3.8 27B NVFP4, `served-model-name qwen3.8-27b` - Single node, TP=1 ### Launch command ``` vllm serve /model \ --served-model-name qwen3.8-27b \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \ --trust-remote-code \ --tensor-parallel-size 1 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.45 \ --max-model-len 262144 \ --max-num-seqs 4 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}' ``` ### Observed engine logs (timestamps UTC) ``` (EngineCore pid=304) ERROR 08-18 23:06:09 [backend_xgrammar.py:162] Failed to advance FSM for request chatcmpl-ab4973be9a4cd69e-86178720 for tokens 271. Please file an issue. (EngineCore pid=304) ERROR 08-18 23:10:38 [backend_xgrammar.py:162] Failed to advance FSM for request chatcmpl-803065810e03ac9d-8173c9f7 for tokens 271. Please file an issue. ``` Additional distinct requests with the same error signature were observed within a 48 h window on the same instance (request IDs available on request): 2 further occurrences, all at token 271 or nearby. Note: both FSM failures reported "for tokens 271" — the FSM advance failure appears reproducible at a specific token position, which may indicate a particular token id / grammar state combination. ### Symptoms 1. Client receives a partial stream of content deltas, then the connection ends cleanly (no HTTP error, no 5xx). 2. No final chunk with `finish_reason`, no `data: [DONE]`. 3. Engine continues serving subsequent requests normally (KV cache ~4–6 %, 0–2 running requests, no preemptions, no OOM, no crash). 4. **Two observed variants**, both producing the identical client symptom: - (a) Logged trigger: the single `Failed to advance FSM` ERROR above, nothing else. The API server logs no error/warning/disconnect. - (b) **Silent trigger**: no engine log line at all — no FSM error, no ERROR, no disconnect, no abort — while the engine is healthy and actively serving (e.g. 00:43 and 00:48 UTC 2026-08-19, `Running: 1 reqs`, ~15–20 tok/s generation, clean 00:40–00:50 UTC window). ### Impact Clients cannot distinguish this from a benign early stop. An agent framework treating "no finish_reason + partial text" as an error will surface it as a truncated/incomplete response, causing user-visible failures and wasted retries. Frequency observed: ~18 client-visible drops over ~2 days on a moderately loaded single-node box (plus 2 more on 2026-08-19, one of which was the silent variant), and several of the affected completions were ordinary text turns (not tool calls). Because the silent variant logs nothing, operators cannot currently correlate a client-side truncation with any server event. ### Questions / hypotheses (for maintainers) - Is there a known fix for FSM advance failure in the xgrammar backend (the line in question: `vllm/v1/.../backend_xgrammar.py:162`)? - Should a failed FSM advance degrade gracefully (e.g. fall back to unconstrained decoding for the remainder of the sequence) and still emit a terminal `finish_reason` so clients get a clean stream end? - Is the "for tokens 271" repeat a clue to a specific grammar state (e.g. a token that is valid per the tokenizer but invalid in the FSM)? - **What causes the silent variant** — a `finish_reason` / `[DONE]` terminal chunk being dropped with no server-side error at all? Is there any code path where the API server closes the SSE stream for a healthy in-flight request without logging, and could a WARN/DEBUG be added so this is diagnosable? ### Minimal repro status No minimal prompt-level repro yet; the failure correlates with specific request content during normal chat/tool-call traffic. Happy to capture the full request payload for a failing request ID if maintainers want it (data contains private content — will redact or share via a secure channel).

signal.title: [Bugfix] Allocate packed outputs in fused_q_kv_rmsnorm so q_b_proj keeps its low-latency GEMM path at decode
signal.text: ## Purpose Fix a silent performance bug: `fused_q_kv_rmsnorm` allocates its outputs with `torch.empty_like(qr)`, but `qr`/`kv` are column slices of the fused `qkv_a` projection output. PyTorch preserves the strides of size-1 dims, so at `num_tokens == 1` (single-sequence decode) `empty_like` returns a tensor carrying the **parent buffer's row stride** — e.g. `(2112, 1)` for a `[1, 1536]` `q_c` slice: ```python >>> qkv = torch.empty(1, 2112) >>> q = qkv[:, :1536] >>> torch.empty_like(q).stride() (2112, 1) # is_contiguous() is True, but not packed row-major ``` The Kimi-K3 low-latency GEMM dispatch (`low_latency_gemm._is_packed_row_major`, which requires `stride == (shape[1], 1)`) then rejects `q_c`, and `q_b_proj` silently falls back to `F.linear` → cuBLAS on **every decode step**, even though `(2304, 1536)` is listed in `KIMI_K3_PROJECTIONS`. `num_tokens >= 2` happens to produce packed strides, so only decode is affected — which is why this never showed up in prefill or batched benchmarks. The fallback is not just a missed fusion. On one SM103 machine (148 SMs) the cuBLAS heuristic picks `nvjet_sm103_tst_16x64_64x16_2x1_v_bz_TNN` at ~10.9 µs/call for this `[1,1536]×[1536,2304]` GEMM, vs 4.5 µs (in-graph) for the intended `dsv3_fused_a` kernel — ~150 µs per decode step across Kimi-K3's 24 MLA layers at TP8. On another SM103 machine (152 SMs) the heuristic happens to land on a faster kernel (~3.1 µs), so the cost of this bug is machine-dependent and easy to miss. Fix: allocate packed row-major outputs explicitly. Packed outputs are strictly better for every downstream consumer of these tensors. ## Test Plan ```bash pytest tests/kernels/core/test_fused_q_kv_rmsnorm.py ``` Adds `test_fused_q_kv_rmsnorm_outputs_are_packed`, which feeds column slices of a fused buffer (the real call pattern from `mla.py`) at `num_tokens ∈ {1, 16}` and asserts packed output strides plus numerical correctness. The `num_tokens == 1` case fails before this change (`stride (768, 1) != (192, 1)`) and passes after. End-to-end A/B on Kimi-K3, TP8, single 8×GPU SM103 node (`--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, isl 128 / osl 32, torch-profiled serving, identical config except this one file): ## Test Result Unit tests: 13 passed (8 correctness, 3 grid-cap, 2 new packed-stride).
